## 2026-08-01 (evening, later) — sepia stain SOLVED; captures now unattended
- **DIAGNOSTIC captures** `*__193740Z__bc19d3e-dirty_debug4.png`, all four
  cameras, exit 0, **taken with the editor deliberately MINIMIZED**.
- **CAPTURE STALL FIXED AT THE ROOT.** Ryan ruled: turn off "Use Less CPU
  when in Background". With
  `EditorPerformanceSettings.bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground = false`, the run
  that had stalled indefinitely twice completed every camera while
  minimized. Captures no longer require anyone to be looking at the editor.
  Scope note: this wrote to a MACHINE-GLOBAL editor config outside both
  roots — see `docs/decisions.md`.
- **THE SEPIA STAIN IS ATMOSPHERIC INSCATTER.** Not the material, not a band
  leak, not a texture tint. Measured, not eyeballed: in the UNLIT debug
  frame the material emits `G = 0` for Snow, yet G over the near face
  measures 211-255 (mean 225 of 255) — **all of it atmosphere, because the
  material cannot produce it**. The stain region carries **+11.6 G** more
  atmospheric contribution than adjacent terrain at the same depth on the
  same layer; in the shipping frame that same region swings **33 points
  warm** (R-B of +9.6 against -23.5 adjacent). The layer under the entire
  stain is uniformly Snow.
- **Consequence for the lighting pass (P3), from the same measurement:**
  atmosphere is contributing roughly 88% of near-field pixel value at
  `snowline_detail` range. The fog is not "adding depth" there, it is
  **drowning the terrain** — which is also why the massif reads as flat
  fabric: inscatter is eating the contrast that would show form. Reduce
  density or push `start_distance_m` out before touching anything else.
- Landscape reverted to `/Game/Materials/M_AutoLandscape`.

## 2026-08-01 (overnight) — mask fix CONFIRMED; snow now dominates
- Post-fix captures at `cdd5329` confirm the mask defect is fixed: **snow
  renders**, which was mathematically impossible before (its slope mask was
  identically zero over the entire terrain).
- **New problem, revealed rather than caused by the fix:** the layers now
  select almost entirely SNOW, at 8.7 km (`ridge_wide`) AND at 4.2 km
  (`diag_oblique`). The close camera rules out LOD-at-distance.
- **Cause is a measurement mismatch.** The numpy prediction (Snow 41.71% /
  Rock 49.06% / Grass 9.23%) derives slope from `np.gradient` on the 4 m
  heightmap grid, where erosion detail gives a MEDIAN slope of 44 deg. The
  shader reads the landscape's VERTEX NORMAL, which is far smoother. Flatter
  normals push normal.z toward 1, so Snow's [0, 52] band matches nearly
  everywhere above its 1200 m line - and half the terrain is above it, mean
  height 1260 m - while Rock's [35, 90] matches almost nowhere. The recipe's
  slope thresholds were tuned against a measurement the shader does not make.
- Recorded, NOT unilaterally changed: this is art direction. Options are to
  raise the snow line, lower Rock's slope threshold, or derive slope from the
  heightmap instead of the vertex normal.
- **Capture throughput has collapsed**: the three shots in this run landed
  1h49m and then 6h51m apart, and the fourth never completed. Worth
  investigating before the next capture-heavy session.
- Level still NOT saved.

  landscape footprint renders nothing.** World Partition streams around the
  camera as a streaming source; parked beyond the loaded regions there is
  nothing to stream. The split was exact - `diag_oblique` (-3000,-3000) and
  `diag_topdown` (0,0) are INSIDE the +/-4032 m footprint and rendered;
  `ridge_wide` (-6200,-6200) and `snowline_detail` (-4800,-4800) were OUTSIDE
  and rendered nothing. Not fog, not aim, not distance, not LOD - all four
  were tested and eliminated first, and the terrain-elevation arithmetic
  confirms both old cameras had terrain in frame the whole time.

  `snowline_detail` to (-3200,-1200,1900) pitch 0 yaw 57.7 - both inside the
  footprint, both aimed at the real peak at (-1876, 896, 2349).
- **Both now render textured terrain.** `ridge_wide` is a proper wide ridge
  shot with layered ridgelines receding into fog.
- Stray lighting rig DELETED (4 actors: DirectionalLight, ExponentialHeightFog,
  SkyLight, SkyAtmosphere under UAID_A85E45CFE40401D200). Verified exactly one
  of each class remains, and it is ours. **NOT SAVED** - reverts on reload.
- **New finding, from the close-up:** at `snowline_detail` range the detail
  texture shows a VISIBLE REPEATING LATTICE in shaded areas. The macro scale
  holds at distance, but the 2 m detail tile is legible close up. Open.

  1200 m snow line. Not yet investigated.

## IF UNREAL OFFERS TO RESTORE FROM AUTOSAVE — the answer was NO, 2026-08-02

The editor went down after the final save and offered a restore on next
launch. **Declined, and the reasoning generalises**, so do not answer this
from instinct next time — check the timestamps, because the prompt gives
no indication of which side is newer.

    real actor packages   Content/__ExternalActors__/Alpine/*.uasset
                          08-02 03:30:53   <- the verified save_level run
    newest autosave       Saved/Autosaves/*_Auto9.uasset
                          08-02 03:19:25   (the bulk at 02:58:26)

The on-disk packages were 11 to 32 minutes NEWER than every autosave, so
restoring would have overwritten verified-good state with an older
snapshot — and the autosave files carry the same OFPA hash names as the
InstancedFoliageActor packages, meaning what it offered to restore was
the 28,302 conifers back at their PRE-PIVOT-FIX positions, 12.4 m off.
The restore would have re-introduced the exact defect the session existed
to remove.

Two things that look alarming in that listing and are not:

  - `Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json` was dated ONE SECOND AFTER
    the real save. That is UE writing the restore manifest on its way
    down; it is the index that triggers the prompt, not newer content.
    Do not read its mtime as "the autosave is newer".
  - `Content/Alpine.umap` was dated 07-28, four days stale. Expected
    under OFPA — the actors live in external packages and the .umap
    barely changes. It is not evidence that the level is old.

**The check, when this recurs:** compare the newest file under
`Content/__ExternalActors__/<level>/` against the newest under
`Saved/Autosaves/`. Restore only if the autosave is genuinely newer, and
remember that `save_level.py` verifies its writes are present on disk —
so a completed save is stronger evidence than an autosave ever is.

Independent confirmation after declining, if wanted:
`python scripts/verify_landscape.py` measures the geometry rather than
trusting the save's own report.

## READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING THE EDITOR

**Everything is saved. 1223 packages, written and verified present on
disk**, including the 28,302 conifer instances at their CORRECTED pivots.
Nothing needs recovering.

**But the editor saturates, repeatedly, and this will bite you.** Three
times this session it stopped accepting command connections while still
answering UDP discovery, with Windows reporting the process alive around
3.3 GB and `Responding` flipping between True and False. Each time it
recovered on its own after a few minutes. The trigger is heavy work —
placing 28,302 single-LOD 505k-triangle instances, saving 1223 packages,
rendering six captures of that scene.

What that means in practice:

  - A `REFUSE (rule 7): no editor nodes answered discovery` right after a
    heavy operation is **saturation, not a crash and not a
    misconfiguration**. Wait several minutes and re-check with
    `python scripts/bootstrap.py`.
  - Do NOT retry the failing script against it. Conduct rule 6 exists for
    this, and the failure mode here is genuinely transient.
  - This is a symptom of open item 1 (no LODs on the fir), not an
    independent problem. Fixing the LODs should fix this too.

The last capture set could not be retaken because of exactly this, so the
newest images on disk predate the final save. They are still accurate:
the save wrote instance positions, it did not change them.

## THE LOOP, CORRECTED

The asset stages are new and go BEFORE the existing loop. They only need
re-running when the vendor files change.

```
# once per vendor file, or when Free/ changes
python scripts/make_asset_manifest.py
blender --background --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 \
    --python scripts/blender/normalize_asset.py \
    -- "Free/<name>_4k.fbx/<name>_4k.fbx" "Free/_normalized"
python scripts/import_surface_set.py <SurfaceId>
python scripts/import_static_mesh.py <asset_id> --normalized <OBJECT> --name <OBJECT>
python scripts/make_foliage_material.py <asset_id> --mesh-asset /Game/Meshes/<OBJECT> \
    --name M_<something> --masked
```

Then the existing loop, plus foliage:

```
python scripts/make_alpine_terrain.py --resolution 2017
python scripts/make_layer_weightmap.py
python scripts/push_heightmap.py --push [--expect-change]
python scripts/verify_landscape.py
python scripts/import_layer_textures.py
python scripts/make_landscape_material.py --assign     # also builds grass types
python scripts/place_foliage.py                        # plan, offline
python scripts/place_foliage.py --place                # into the editor
python scripts/apply_lighting.py
python scripts/capture.py [--filename-tag foo]
python scripts/save_level.py            # dry run first, then --save
```

Note `--normalized OBJECT` is not optional for anything that gets
instanced. It refuses unless `Free/_measured/normalized.json` names the
object as verified, and that refusal is the point — see below.

## THE THREE DEFECTS THIS SESSION FOUND, because they will recur

Full write-ups in `docs/lessons.md` section 23. Short forms, because each
is a class rather than an incident:

1. **The pivot was 12.4 m from the tree and every gate was green.** The
   vendor FBX lays its objects side by side; UE bakes that into the
   StaticMesh pivot. Triangle counts, LOD counts, material slots and
   world instance counts were all verified and all correct. Nothing
   measured the pivot. *Rule: an asset's pivot is a property you must
   measure, not one you may assume the exporter got right.*
2. **The vendor published a correct number that answered a different
   question.** `mesh_extent_m: 7.3` for `grass_medium_01` is the width
   of the whole set laid out for the product shot; one tuft is 0.327 m.
   Derived scale produced grass 0.7 cm tall and nothing reported a
   problem. *Rule: `vendor` does not outrank `measured`.*
3. **Every capture camera was 1-9 km out.** Trees at 4.4/ha and 0.15 m
   grass are sub-pixel at that range, so for the whole foliage milestone
   the review loop was incapable of showing its subject — and came back
   looking good, because the terrain and lighting it COULD resolve were
   good. *Rule: a capture set needs at least one camera at the scale of
   the smallest thing being verified.* The `forest_floor` camera now
   exists for exactly this and took three attempts to place; the two
   failures are in section 23.3 and are instructive.

## GPU HANG, 2026-08-02 — cause found, one fix applied, levers left
> STATUS: SUPERSEDED — cull_distance_m implemented (alpine_8k.json:1438-1658), superseded by derived culls (:3362). Record says Applied. [Pass 5 ruling, 2026-09-16]

`DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG` on D3D12. A Windows TDR — the GPU missed the
driver's frame deadline. **Not** memory: 3998 MB of an 8283 MB budget.

**Cause:** `place_foliage` set exactly one property on each FoliageType,
`mesh`. `FoliageType.h:292` documents `CullDistance` as "0 disables" and
`InstancedFoliage.cpp:602-603` defaults both ends to 0, so nothing was
ever culled: 28,302 instances of a 505,494-triangle single-LOD mesh every
frame across an 8 km map. 14.3 billion triangles.

**Applied:** `cull_distance_m` is now a recipe key valid on instanced
species, set to 300 m for the Conifer, applied with read-back. ~124 trees
in view, 63M triangles. See `docs/lessons.md` §23.12 for the part worth
remembering — the validator actively FORBADE this key with a rule I wrote
from a wrong premise.

**NOT applied, deliberately — one change at a time.** A sweep of every
property this pipeline leaves at engine default turned up two more that
matter, both confirmed at source, both still uncontrolled:

  - `bCastDynamicShadow` defaults **true** (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:618`,
    reaching the component at :1629). 28,302 shadow-casting high-poly
    trees.
  - `bAffectDynamicIndirectLighting` defaults **true** (:621, → :1672).
    On Software Lumen, on an integrated GPU.

The grass path sets `cast_dynamic_shadow=False` explicitly; the instanced
path sets neither. That asymmetry was the tell for §23.12 and it is still
there. Both are hard rule 2 gaps — scene parameters coming from nowhere —
and both are levers if 63M triangles still hangs.

They are not applied yet because stacking a second change onto an
unverified first makes it ambiguous which one worked. Verify the cull fix
first.

**The real fix remains LODs.** 63M triangles per frame is still far too
much for this GPU; it is three orders better than 14.3 billion, which is
what makes the level openable so the LODs can be built. That is open item
1 and it has not moved.

**Reopening safely:** the editor was relaunched on
`/Engine/Maps/Templates/OpenWorld` via the command line, so it never
rendered the uncullable scene, and the FoliageType was repaired as an
ASSET with no level loaded. If this recurs, that is the sequence —
a FoliageType is not level state.

## THE LOAD, IN NUMBERS — quality vs quantity vs hardware (2026-08-02)

Computed from the recipe and the measured triangle counts. Worth reading
before tuning anything, because the intuitive answer is wrong.

    TREES (persistent instances)
      density              4.4 / ha        real alpine forest: 200-1000
      placed               28,302
      triangles each       505,494         LODs: 1
      before (no cull)     28,302 drawn -> 14,306M triangles/frame
      now (300 m cull)        123 drawn ->     62M triangles/frame

    GRASS (GPU-spawned, per view)
      cull distance        900 m
      density              14 per 10 m2
      instances in view    3,562,566
      avg triangles        1,043          share-weighted over 5 varieties
      COMPUTED             3,717M triangles/frame

**The crash was a defect, not a hardware limit.** 14.3 billion triangles
per frame is unbounded work; no GPU survives it, and a top-end discrete
card would have managed roughly 1 fps. Lack of resources did not cause
it — a missing cull distance did.

**Quantity is not the problem. There are too FEW trees.** 4.4/ha is
sparse for alpine forest by two orders of magnitude, and 28,302 instances
is trivial for UE when they are cheap.

**Quality is the problem.** 505,494 triangles with ONE LOD is a
source-resolution photogrammetry asset used as a game asset. Game-ready
is ~5k-30k at LOD0 and a few hundred at distance. It is 20-100x too heavy
near the camera and unboundedly too heavy far from it, because there is
no LOD to fall to. The assets are good; the delivery step was skipped.

**Hardware is a real but secondary constraint.** The integrated GPU
lowers the ceiling so the quality problem bites sooner. It does not
create it.

### UNVERIFIED, and the two facts do not reconcile
The grass figure above says 3.7 BILLION triangles/frame — comparable to
the pre-fix tree load — and `enable_density_scaling` is set FALSE, which
deliberately opts out of the engine's own scalability thinning on Medium.

But `alpine__forest_floor__*` shows NO grass, and the scene now renders
six cameras without incident. Both cannot be true of a grass system that
is actually spawning. Either the arithmetic overestimates what UE's grass
submits (it manages density per cell in ways this does not model), or the
grass is not spawning — which is open item 0a.

**Do not tune grass density on the strength of this number until 0a is
settled.** Resolve what is actually spawning first; a number computed
from a config that may not be in effect is not a measurement.

### Why LODs are the leverage
Auto-LOD at 25/6/1.5% gives ~126k/30k/7.6k. At a 300 m cull most trees
sit at LOD2-3, taking 62M to roughly 5-8M — an order of magnitude, on the
asset that is actually expensive.

The reason that matters more than it sounds: once per-tree cost drops
~10x, density can rise toward something that reads as forest (50-100/ha
rather than 4.4) and still be lighter than the scene is today. **Fixing
quality is what buys quantity.**

## GRASS — NOT SOLVED. Read this before spending another hour on it.

Three real bugs were found and fixed along the way. None of them was the
cause. The grass still does not render, and this section exists so the
next attempt starts from the frontier rather than the beginning.

### The engine says its grass data is BUILT
`grass.DumpGrassData -detailed -bygrasstype` (the command is at
LandscapeGrass.cpp:212 and I found it far too late — it is the only
direct instrument in this whole area):

    Num landscape actors with grass data:      1
    Num landscape proxies with grass data:     256
    Num landscape components with grass data:  1024
    Num grass types used:                      1
    Total grass data size (KB):                11800.00
    GT_alpine_Meadow: Num components = 902, total data size = 3608.00 KB

`FLandscapeGrassWeightPS` also appears in the shader-compile log, so the
grass weight pass compiled and ran.

**CAUTION on that evidence.** A per-component weight array occupies the
same bytes whether its values are 1 or 0. "3608 KB of grass data exists"
does NOT establish that the weights are non-zero, and that is the single
most likely place the remaining fault lives. The next attempt should
start by proving the grass weight is non-zero somewhere, not by
re-verifying assets.

### Ruled out, each by experiment, each measured
  - material assigned; exactly one LandscapeGrassOutput; pin `Meadow`
    accepts a connection (True) and every wrong spelling refuses
  - the MASK — a flat Constant 1.0 wired straight to the grass output
    changed the render by 0.007 in near-ground contrast. Nothing.
  - stale grass cache — `grass.FlushCache` took components 16 -> 0 and
    they rebuilt to 16
  - the builder throttles — `grass.MaxCreatePerFrame` 1 -> 64,
    `MaxAsyncTasks` 4 -> 16, `TickInterval` -> 0
  - view dwell — the editor viewport parked at the exact capture
    position for 90 s, on the theory that grass builds around views and
    capture.py teleports a camera in for a single frame
  - the quality-level fields — see the hazard below; setting
    `r.grass.DensityQualityLevel` from -1 to 3 changed nothing
  - the grass material — BLEND_MASKED, two-sided, OPACITY_MASK
    CONNECTED, alpha texture with SAMPLERTYPE_ALPHA, clip 0.333
  - the components — right mesh, right material, `visible=True`,
    `hidden_in_game=False`, cull 9000/12000
  - the weightmap — baked Grass channel reads **1.000** at the exact
    camera, 45.1% of the map above 0.5
  - cvars — `grass.Enable`, `grass.DensityScale`, `foliage.DensityScale`,
    `grass.CullDistanceScale` all 1.0

### TWO INSTRUMENTS LIE HERE. Do not repeat these.
  - **`get_instance_count()` always returns 0 for grass.** It reads
    `PerInstanceSMData`, which landscape grass never populates —
    `LandscapeGrass.cpp:3387` hands `AcceptPrebuiltTree` a prebuilt
    buffer instead. 0 is expected and means nothing.
  - **`get_local_bounds()` returns the MESH bounds** (±9.4 cm), not the
    instance cloud.

Both were briefly mistaken for evidence of absence.

### A hazard found, and deliberately NOT written up as the cause
`FGrassVariety` carries TWO density fields and two cull pairs —
`GrassDensity`/`GrassDensityQuality`,
`EndCullDistance`/`EndCullDistanceQuality` — and `GetDensity()` chooses
between them on `GEngine->UseGrassVarityPerQualityLevels`
(LandscapeGrass.cpp:1542). `make_landscape_material` sets the
NON-quality ones, and `r.grass.DensityQualityLevel` measured -1, which
looked exactly like the answer. Setting it to 3 and flushing moved
nothing, so the switch is false and the fields being set are the live
ones. Real trap for later; not this bug. See lessons 23.17.

### What WAS genuinely broken, and is now fixed
  1. **The config could not finish building.** At 900 m and 14 per
     10 m2 each landscape component needed ~355,000 instances against
     the 65,536 cap (`GMaxInstancesPerComponent`, :118), so it
     subdivided 9 ways x 5 varieties x ~12 components in range — which
     is where the 595 components came from — and the builder makes ONE
     per frame (:181). Now 120 m / 10 per 10m2 / 4 varieties:
     3.7 BILLION triangles down to 16.4M, 16 components.
  2. **The material graph was half orphaned debris.** 158 expressions
     down to 80 once leftovers were deleted explicitly.
     `delete_all_material_expressions` does not delete all material
     expressions; custom outputs and much else survive it, so every
     rebuild had been layering on top of the last. Hard rule 3 was
     failing silently.
  3. **Two LandscapeGrassOutput nodes**, a consequence of (2), which
     stopped the material compiling entirely.

### Where I would go next
  1. Prove the grass WEIGHT is non-zero. The data exists; its values are
     unverified. `grass.DumpGrassData -detailed -bycomponent` may show
     more, and the landscape's grass map can be inspected in the
     material editor's landscape visualisers.
  2. Try a trivially simple grass mesh (a single quad) and a stock
     engine material. If that renders, the fault is in the imported
     asset or its material despite everything above reading correct; if
     it does not, the fault is in the landscape/grass plumbing.
  3. Only then consider hardware — Software Lumen on an integrated GPU —
     which is the least likely explanation and the hardest to act on.

1. **LODs for `fir_tree_01_c_LOD0`.** 505,494 triangles, ONE LOD, 28,302

## NEEDS RYAN — nothing outstanding

The one open item, the vendor-import pivot gate, was **ruled by Ryan on
2026-08-02: option (c)** — `--normalized` is mandatory for any mesh a
RECIPE names; ad-hoc vendor imports stay ungated. Built, audited (PASS,
auditor-corrected) and tested offline. Full text in `docs/decisions.md`
under "RULING (c)" and the audit-log row of the same date.

Enforced at four points, because they guard four different failures:

  1. the recipe validator (`landscape_spec.recipe_normalization_errors`)
  2. `import_static_mesh`, refusing a recipe-claimed target without
     `--normalized`
  3. `place_foliage`, measuring `get_bounds()` before adding an instance
  4. `make_landscape_material`, same, before building a GrassVariety

1 and 2 are NAME checks against a report on disk and are defeated by
importing a vendor file under a verified name. 3 and 4 measure the asset
itself and are not.

**GATE 3 HAS NOW RUN LIVE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** `place_foliage --place`
measured `fir_tree_01_c_LOD0` at pivot 0.0 m horizontal / base 0.0 m,
bounds [6.3059, 5.9662, 14.5206] m — matching Blender exactly — and
placed 28,302. Then the limits were lowered below the measured values and
both the horizontal and vertical branches refused at exit 4, and
restoring the limits placed again. So it does not false-refuse, it does
refuse, and it is not stuck.

**GATE 4 (the grass path in `make_landscape_material`) IS STILL
UNEXERCISED.** It is the same code shape as gate 3 and was audited
alongside it, but it has not run. Rebuilding the material is the cheap
way to close that: `python scripts/make_landscape_material.py --assign`.

Known hole, recorded not fixed — see `docs/lessons.md` §23.11. Gate 2
checks the `--name` it is handed, but UE's FBX importer writes one asset
per OBJECT in the file, so an ad-hoc vendor import of a multi-object file
can overwrite recipe-named meshes that gate 2 never looked at. This is
precisely why gates 3 and 4 measure `get_bounds()` at the point of use
rather than trusting the name checks.

The audit also surfaced, and I ruled under the standing autonomy grant:
`MAX_BASE_OFFSET_M = 0.25`, gating the VERTICAL pivot. Nothing had been
checking it, so a mesh with a correct XY pivot and its origin at the
bounding-box centre passed every gate and would bury each instance to
half its height — minus 7.26 m for `fir_tree_01_c`.

Two judgement calls made rather than asked about, easy to reverse:

- **Grass density 6 -> 14 per 10 m2**, and five varieties rather than
  sixteen. Both frame-time trades on an integrated GPU.
- **`grass_medium_01` vendor extents deleted** from the manifest's
  `FOOTPRINTS` table rather than kept beside the measurement. Keeping
  them would leave a stale value in the table that is consulted FIRST,
  which is how the wrong number won originally.

## Schema v1.4 — fog, changed 2026-08-02

`lighting.fog.height_falloff` is **REMOVED**; the validator refuses it by
name. Two replacements:

- `fog.height_datum_m` — the fog's world Z. Fog is densest AT this height
  and thins upward, so it decides which of a world is buried. It was
  previously governed by NOTHING: the actor sat wherever it was first
  spawned (1920 m) while the terrain's p90 was 1610 m, burying 90% of the
  world. Hard rule 2 applies and never had been.
- `fog.half_height_m` — metres over which density halves. The engine's raw
  number is divided by 1000 before use (`SceneCore.cpp:405`), so the old
  `0.12` meant a **57.8 m** half-height: a near-vertical wall of fog, and
  the hard horizontal line in the pre-2026-08-02 captures.

Current values, set from the terrain's own distribution: datum 150 m,
half-height 300 m, density 0.0015, start 1500 m. Contrast gain measured at
+28% (topdown) and +21% (oblique).

Read-only adversarial review of the massif mask and the relief change.
Camera findings are item 2 above. The rest, with full text:

- **Reflected Python names are NOT derivable from headers.** Three live runs
  were lost to invented names this session. The stub is an oracle for
  EXISTENCE only — it is generated from the same headers and inherits their
  misleading parameter names. `landscape_actor_ref` not `landscape_actor`;
  `get_components_by_class` not a `landscape_components` property;
  `create_render_target2d` not `create_render_target2_d`;
  `get_edit_layers_bp` even though the DisplayName is `GetEditLayers`;
  `post_edit_change` does not exist on Texture2D at all.
- **`push_heightmap --push` can exit 5 with a JSON deserialisation error
  and STILL HAVE WRITTEN THE TERRAIN.** The response outgrew the
  transport; the write was fine. Exit 5 means UNKNOWN, so do not retry
  against the editor (conduct rule 6) — settle it read-only with a plain
  `python scripts/push_heightmap.py` dry run, which reports the live
  terrain against the file. On 2026-08-02 that came back identity,
  median |dv| 0.000 units over 1280 vertices, 5/5 blocks 256/256. A
  transport that loses the answer has not lost the fact.
- **The heightmap import applies DEFERRED.** An export taken immediately
  after it reads the PRE-push terrain. `push_heightmap` polls and reports
  its attempt count; do not replace that with a sleep.
- **The first export after an editor restart returns an all-zero target.**
  A discarded warm-up export handles it. Do not diagnose a cold first
  export as a broken draw — that cost a full probe cycle.
- **Conduct rule 7 verifies the PROJECT, not the LEVEL, and a stray editor
  will answer the port.** A `MyProject` editor was open at one point and
  every gate correctly refused. That project now lives in `_trash/`.
- World Partition exposes only LOADED actors. `push_heightmap` forces
  residency; other scripts may not.
- Saving the level saves EVERY dirty external package, not just yours.

> STATUS: HISTORY — Process statement re docs/lessons.md (consolidated); superseded by audit/hook governance. History. [Pass 5 ruling, 2026-09-16]

**Full autonomy and design authority, including destructive paths**
(Ryan, 2026-08-02; full text `docs/decisions.md`). No approval gates, no
BLOCK sign-offs, no mandatory audit. Destructive scripts are cleared to
run. Design decisions are yours to make and to record.

Still standing, because none of them require Ryan and all of them catch
your own errors: stay inside REPO_ROOT / UE_PROJECT_ROOT; no recursive
deletes (move to `_trash/`); commit before and after anything
irreversible; no direct `.uasset` edits; stop after two consecutive
live-editor failures and diagnose; verify the connected editor is the
right PROJECT before every remote execution; dry-run destructive work;
identify by property signature, never by label; carry full text in
reports; and say plainly when something was not done or not verified.

**The lessons loop is now the only thing catching defect classes.** With
no independent reviewer in the path, `docs/lessons.md` is load-bearing
in a way it was not before. Append in the same session a defect is
found, never deferred.

# Proposal — the external-asset pipeline

Status: **built, running, and fully resolved.** All six open questions are
answered below, the last of them by Ryan's ruling (c) on 2026-08-02.
Nothing here needs a decision.

Written 2026-08-02, after importing ambientCG surface sets and Poly Haven
meshes into the alpine biome and finding three silent-wrong defects in
the process. The full defect write-ups are `docs/lessons.md` §23; the
rulings are `docs/decisions.md`, 2026-08-02 (late).

---

## What the pipeline is now

Five stages, each of which refuses rather than guesses, and each of which
verifies with an instrument other than the one that made the claim.

    Free/<vendor files>
      |
      | scripts/make_asset_manifest.py      inventory: role per file,
      |                                     extent per asset, PROVENANCE
      |                                     per number
      v
    Free/manifest.json
      |
      | scripts/blender/normalize_asset.py  split multi-object files,
      |                                     bake foliage pivots,
      |                                     re-read from disk to verify
      v
    Free/_normalized/*.fbx + Free/_measured/normalized.json
      |
      | scripts/import_static_mesh.py --normalized
      | scripts/import_surface_set.py       per-role import settings,
      |                                     read back and compared
      v
    /Game/Meshes, /Game/Surfaces
      |
      | scripts/make_foliage_material.py    masked/opaque, GL->DX flip
      | scripts/make_landscape_material.py  surfaces into layer bands,
      |                                     grass output into the mask
      v
    the scene, driven entirely from recipes/alpine.json

### The three gates that matter

1. **Provenance is a field, not a comment.** Every dimension in
   `manifest.json` carries `<field>_source` of `vendor`, `assumed` or
   `measured`. A consumer that would behave differently for an assumed
   value must branch on it. This is what made D1 (below) a two-line fix
   rather than an archaeology exercise.
2. **The normalisation report is a precondition, not a hint.**
   `import_static_mesh.py --normalized` reads
   `Free/_measured/normalized.json` and refuses if the object is absent,
   marked failed, or has no file on disk. It never falls back to the
   vendor file.
3. **Every measurement is taken twice, by different instruments.**
   Blender measures the pivot after the bake and again after re-reading
   its own export from disk; UE then measures it a third time off the
   imported asset, after the FBX round-trip and UE's own import
   transform. All three agreed at 0.0 m for all 23 objects.

---

## The six open questions

### Q1 — Which vendor conventions do we adopt wholesale? ANSWERED
Adopted: the size-class authoring pattern (`tiny/small/mid/tall/large`),
which maps directly onto `LandscapeGrassType`'s variety list and is now
schema v1.10 `varieties`. Rejected: the side-by-side scene layout, which
is a product-shot convention and is actively harmful downstream (D2).

### Q2 — Do we keep vendor material graphs or author our own? ANSWERED
Author our own. The vendor FBXs ship material NAMES and texture files but
no graph, and `path_mode="STRIP"` on export drops the texture references
deliberately — binding is a pipeline concern so that sampler types match
the compression settings we chose at import. Three sampler-type
mismatches in one session (§23.5) are the argument for keeping both ends
in one place.

### Q3 — What happens to material slots the vendor does not texture?
ANSWERED. `fir_tree_01` uses four materials per LOD and ships maps for
two. There is nothing upstream to recover — the FBX package IS the whole
delivery. Untextured slots are bound to a SUBSTITUTE named on the command
line, and the substitution is printed on every run, because a silent
fallback reads as an authored choice. Currently `dead_branches` and
`trunk_c` are both bound to bark.

### Q4 — Normal-map convention, per asset or per pipeline? ANSWERED
**Per asset, derived from the files that ship.** This was originally
ruled the other way — a global DX convention — and that ruling was
withdrawn by Ryan on 2026-08-02 after it was applied to Poly Haven meshes
that ship GL only. `make_asset_manifest.py` now derives the convention
per asset from the shipped file set, and `make_foliage_material.py`
inserts the green-channel flip only where the source is GL.

### Q5 — Nanite, on or off? ANSWERED, with a caveat
Off, for alpha-masked foliage, set at import time and never toggled
afterwards. See D4. The caveat is real and is recorded as an open item,
not as a resolved question: the fir is 505,494 triangles with ONE LOD at
28,302 instances. The right answer is generated LODs; that is an audited
change this session did not have room for.

### Q6 — How does an `assumed` footprint get promoted? **THE PREMISE WAS
> STATUS: HISTORY — records that the promotion premise was false
WRONG.**

The question as originally posed was "how does an assumed footprint get
promoted to a calibrated one after visual tuning". The answer turned out
to be that visual tuning is not the promotion path and should not be.

`grass_medium_01` carried a vendor extent of 7.3 m. It is a correct
number describing the whole laid-out set. The largest single tuft is
0.327 m — wrong by a factor of 22, in the direction that makes everything
derived from it invisible. That is exactly what happened, and no amount
of visual tuning would have diagnosed it, because the object being tuned
was 1.6 cm tall and therefore not visible to tune.

**Ruled:** measurement is the promotion path, and it costs one headless
Blender run. `vendor` does not outrank `measured`; it answers whatever
question the publisher was asking.

This does NOT dispose of the four `assumed` surface tiling periods
(Rock026, Rock051, Rock063, Snow006, all 4.0 m). Those are the tiling
period of a repeating texture, which no file measurement can recover —
ambientCG simply does not publish Dimensions for them. They stay
`assumed`, stay flagged, and are the one place where visual calibration
genuinely is the only instrument available.

---

## RESOLVED — Ryan chose option (c), 2026-08-02

**Ryan chose (c):** `--normalized` is mandatory for any mesh a RECIPE
names; ad-hoc vendor imports stay ungated. Implemented at four points and
audited PASS (auditor-corrected). Full reasoning, and the vertical-pivot
ruling that came out of that audit, are in `docs/decisions.md`,
2026-08-02, "RULING (c)".

  1. the recipe validator, via `landscape_spec.recipe_normalization_errors`
  2. `import_static_mesh`, refusing a recipe-claimed target without
     `--normalized`
  3. `place_foliage`, measuring `get_bounds()` before adding an instance
  4. `make_landscape_material`, same, before building a GrassVariety

1 and 2 are NAME checks against a report on disk, and are defeated by
importing a vendor file under a name that happens to be verified. 3 and 4
measure the asset itself and are not. Both layers exist because the first
pair refuses early and cheaply, and the second pair is the proof.

Also ruled, by the implementer under the standing autonomy grant, because
the audit found nothing was checking it: `MAX_BASE_OFFSET_M = 0.25` gates
the VERTICAL pivot. A mesh with a correct XY pivot and its origin at the
bounding-box CENTRE passed every other gate and would bury each instance
to half its height — minus 7.26 m for `fir_tree_01_c`. Ryan's ruling
settled WHEN normalisation is mandatory, not WHAT counts as normalised.

**Caveat carried forward:** gates 3 and 4 have never run against a live
editor — it was closed when they were written — so their first live run
is their first execution.

**Nothing in this proposal now needs Ryan.** The question is kept below
exactly as it stood, for the record.

### The question as it stood

**The vendor-import pivot gate.** `import_static_mesh.py` currently FAILS
on a pivot offset over 1 m when `--normalized` was used, and WARNS when
it was not. The warning is not a gate, and lesson §17 is explicit that a
flagged risk nobody actions is a defect with paperwork.

The reason it is not a gate is that the script cannot tell why a vendor
file is being imported. Importing one to measure it is legitimate;
importing one to instance it is not. Options:

  (a) leave as is — warn on the vendor path, fail on the normalised path;
  (b) fail on both, and add an explicit `--allow-offset-pivot` for the
      measurement case;
  (c) make `--normalized` mandatory for any mesh named by a recipe, and
      let ad-hoc vendor imports stay ungated.

(c) is the closest to how the pipeline actually works — the recipe is
what decides whether something gets instanced — but it moves the check
from the importer to the recipe validator, which is a bigger change than
it sounds. No implementation until this is signed off (conduct rule 8).

## 2. The move fork — full text

### Finding

> Moving an `ALandscape` via `set_actor_location` is NOT safe in a World
> Partition level, and this level is WP. Proxies are aligned to the parent
> only by `ALandscape::PostEditMove(bFinished)` →
> `ULandscapeInfo::FixupProxiesTransform(true)`
> (`LandscapeEdit.cpp:5138-5147`), which sets each proxy to
> `FTransform(FVector(SectionBase)) * LandscapeTM`
> (`Landscape.cpp:6154-6174`). `PostEditMove` is fired by the editor's
> interactive move tools; Python's `set_actor_location`
> (`K2_SetActorLocation` → `AActor::SetActorLocation`) never calls it. Since
> this level's components all live on proxies, the script as submitted would
> have moved the empty parent actor to the origin, left all 64 components at
> −403200, saved that torn state — and `verify_landscape.py` would then have
> PASSed the location field, because it reads only the parent's location. The
> tripwire was blind to exactly the failure its companion script could cause.

### Option (i) — delete and recreate by hand

Delete the landscape in-editor and recreate it once from
`landscape_spec.py`'s corrected printout, which now prints dialog Location
`403200, 403200, 0` rather than `0, 0, 0`.

- **Cost:** one manual redo.
- **Risk:** lowest. It uses the engine's own placement path — the only path
  that fires `FixupProxiesTransform` — and stays consistent with route B's
  "create by hand once, then verify" contract.
- Recommended by both the auditor and the main agent. **Never previously
  ruled on.**

### Option (ii) — proxy-aware mover

Extend `apply_landscape_transform.py` to set each proxy absolutely to
`recipe_origin + scale · section_base`.

- **Cost:** reimplements `FixupProxiesTransform` in Python; larger surface;
  needs its own audit.
- **Risk:** higher. Hand-rolling engine-internal invariants is the mechanism
  by which torn state arises in the first place.

| 2 | `verify_landscape.py` | 2 | read-only | exit 5, then exit 4 |

## 4. Which landscape is the real import — corrected

An earlier report inferred from proxy counts that the actor labelled
`Landscape` was the real 1009 import. **That inference was wrong.** Ryan's
outliner reading settles it:

| | `Landscape_Alpine` | `Landscape` |
|---|---|---|
| Overall resolution | 1009×1009 (expected) | **2017×2017** |
| Total components | 64 (8×8) | **256 (16×16)** |
| Component resolution | 126 quads | 127×127 verts = 126 quads |
| Subsections | 2×2 | 2×2 |
| Streaming proxies | **4** | **64** (panel says 65, counting itself) |
| Scale | **800 / 800 / 500** | 100 / 100 / 100 (default) |
| Location | −403200 = −(1008/2)·800 | −100800 = −(2016/2)·100 |

Both locations are the dialog's centring offset for their own geometry, which
confirms both were created through the New Landscape dialog.

`Landscape_Alpine` carries the recipe's scale and geometry: **it is the real
import.** `Landscape` is a stray default-geometry landscape, most likely from a
Create-tab interaction before switching to Import from File.

Why the earlier inference failed: proxy count was read as proportional to
import size. It is not — proxies are per World Partition grid cell, so the
2017 landscape has 4× the components and correspondingly more cells, despite
being the stray.

## 6. WARNING: proxy labels are NOT unique — do not delete by label

The census's per-owner listing produced a checklist that **must not be used as
a label-matching list**. Four labels appear under *both* landscapes:

```
LandscapeStreamingProxy_1_1_0
LandscapeStreamingProxy_1_2_0
LandscapeStreamingProxy_2_1_0
LandscapeStreamingProxy_2_2_0
```

Proxy labels are auto-generated from World Partition **grid coordinates**
(`_<x>_<y>_<z>`), so two landscapes occupying overlapping grid cells produce
identical labels. `Landscape_Alpine`'s 4 loaded proxies sit at cells (1,1),
(1,2), (2,1), (2,2) — all of which `Landscape` also occupies.

**Consequence:** deleting by searching the Outliner for a label would delete
the wrong landscape's proxies. Delete via the **Outliner hierarchy** instead —
select the parent `Landscape` actor and delete it together with its nested
proxies, so ownership rather than name decides what goes.

The listing remains useful as a *count* and as evidence of ownership; it is not
safe as a name-matching checklist, and the script should be extended to print
`get_path_name()` (globally unique) before it is ever used that way again.

### Confirmed: `Landscape_Alpine` is the real import
Scale 800/800/500 matches the recipe exactly, and the measured component
spacing of **126 quads = 63 × 2** is the recipe's `section_size` ×
`sections_per_component`. `Landscape` has default scale 100/100/100 and a 2017
geometry that appears nowhere in the recipe.

### `Landscape_Alpine` is only PARTIALLY LOADED
Its `implied resolution 505` is **not** a contradiction — it is the World
Partition caveat firing. An 8×8 grid has section bases at
`0, 126, 252, 378, 504, 630, 756, 882`. The census sees only
`252, 378, 504, 630` — the middle 4×4 — so 4 proxies and 16 of 64 components
are resident. The outer ring is unloaded.

`Landscape` at scale 100 spans only 2016 m and sits entirely inside the loaded
region, which is why it reports complete while the 8064 m landscape does not.

**Consequence: all World Partition regions must be loaded before any verify
run is meaningful.** Otherwise the geometry check fails on residency rather
than on correctness.

### D3 is ANSWERED, and it fired
`num_subsections`, `subsection_size_quads`, and `component_size_quads` are
**all refused by the engine** — UE 5.8's `get_editor_property` will not read
bare `UPROPERTY()` fields. `landscape_guid` is likewise unreadable. Only the
`BlueprintReadOnly` fields (`section_base_x`/`_y`) and `EditAnywhere`
(`landscape_actor_ref`) came back.

This is the permanently-red-tripwire case: `verify_landscape.py` currently
treats unread fields as INCOMPLETE and exits 6, so it will fail forever on
those three rows even after the duplicate is deleted and the regions are
loaded. **Needs a ruling — see the D3 options in the audit log.**

The measured spacing does still pin the geometry: 126 factorises uniquely over
the dialog-legal sets ({7,15,31,63,127,255} × {1,2} → 7, 14, 15, 30, 31, 62,
63, 126, 127, 254, 255, 510, all distinct), so a spacing of 126 can only mean
63 × 2 among configurations the dialog can produce.

`ALandscape` derives from `ALandscapeProxy`, which is why the details panel's
"Landscape Proxy Count 65" exceeds the 64 streaming proxies the Python probe
attributed to it: the parent counts itself.

## 2026-08-02 — GRASS ROOT CAUSE: a 16-bit grayscale alpha source clips every pixel

**The grass was never broken. Its opacity mask was.** Root cause found
by finishing the recorded frontier, in order, exactly as written.

**Step 1 — weights proven non-zero, from source.** The capture path
calls `InitializeFrom(..., bStripEmptyWeights = true)`
(`LandscapeGrassWeightExporter.cpp:1190`), and with strip on, a grass
type whose rendered weights are ALL ZERO is dropped from `WeightOffsets`
(`LandscapeGrass.cpp:1825-1837`). The engine's own dump reported
`GT_alpine_Meadow: Num components = 902` of 1024 — and the arithmetic
corroborates to the byte: 8192 KB height / 1024 = exactly 4096 uint16
samples; 3608 KB / 902 = exactly 4096 weight bytes. 122 components WERE
stripped as all-zero, which proves the strip ran on this very data.
Conclusion: 902 components hold non-zero Meadow weights.

**Step 2 — the bisect, two verdicts in one dwell.**
- Engine Plane (2 tris, stock WorldGridMaterial) as the grass variety:
  RENDERED — a carpet of checkered quads following the weight
  distribution. Grass data, instance building, and rendering all work.
- Cross test: Plane + `M_grass_medium_01` override — INVISIBLE (the
  same mesh that just carpeted the hill). Our tuft mesh +
  WorldGridMaterial override — RENDERED as specks. **The material
  kills; the mesh is exonerated.**

**Root cause.** `M_grass_medium_01`'s opacity mask samples
`T_grass_medium_01_alpha_4k` (R pin → MP_OPACITY_MASK, clip 0.333).
The fir twig — identical construction, renders correctly — has an
**RGB 8-bit** alpha source. The grass alpha source is
**`I;16`: single-channel 16-BIT grayscale**. Through the TC_Alpha
import path, the 16-bit gray's data does not land where the R pin
reads it — the mask evaluates ≤ clip everywhere, every pixel clips,
and the material compiles clean, binds clean, and renders nothing.

**Why every earlier check passed:** the import read-back verified
compression SETTINGS, not content; the material read-back verified the
mask INPUT was connected, not what it evaluated to; and
`M_grass_medium_01` had never rendered anywhere — Meadow is
grass-system only, so no placed instance ever proved it. **A material
that has never rendered is unproven even when an identically
constructed sibling renders — the construction was never the variable;
the source file was.**

**Class sweep (non-negotiable 4), all Free/ import sources by PIL
mode:** `grass_medium_02` alpha is the same I;16 trap. The fir's bark
and twig ROUGHNESS maps are ALSO I;16 — imported under TC_Masks and
"verified" by settings read-back, so the fir's roughness is presumed
silently wrong (a shine defect, not invisibility). AmbientCG surface
maps are all 8-bit — unaffected, which is why the landscape renders.
Displacements are 16-bit but never imported.

**Fix (verification pending at time of logging, appended below when
done):** normalize 16-bit single-channel sources for mask-type roles
(alpha, roughness) to 8-bit at import time, into `Free/_normalized/
textures/`, vendor file untouched — the same derivative pattern as
pivot normalisation. Then reimport and re-verify by RENDER, the
instrument that catches what settings read-backs cannot.


## 2026-08-02 — GRASS FIX VERIFIED BY RENDER; defect closed

The 8-bit conversion shipped in `import_static_mesh.py` (mask-type
roles, PNG-only inspection with a stated skip for formats PIL cannot
read — the grass roughness ships as EXR and a fail-closed refusal there
was itself a bug, fixed in the same commit). Verification chain, each
step by render on the live editor:

1. **Round 3 cross-test:** engine Plane + the REBUILT material — the
   mask now cuts blade silhouettes out of each quad. Before the fix the
   identical test rendered nothing.
2. **Recipe restore at ground level:** individual tufts render with
   their own shadows, sized per the recipe (6-60 cm), distributed per
   the baked weight.
3. **Density retune (10 -> 20 per 10m2, shares moved off the
   near-invisible 6 cm tiny), verified again:** tuft count doubled on
   screen, tracking density as configured. ~90k instances / ~44M
   triangles at the 120 m cull — inside proven territory.

**The fir's roughness maps (same I;16 class, TC_Masks path) were
converted and reimported in the same pass** — 4 LODs survived reimport,
read back per level.

**Residual, stated honestly:** the meadow still reads sparse. That is
the ASSET — grass_medium_01 is genuinely isolated dry-alpine tufts —
and the tuning headroom (grass_medium_02 is 2-4x larger and now imports
safely through the automatic conversion; leafy_grass untested). That is
the "raise foliage density" quality workstream, not this defect.

**Rework-toward-zero note:** the defect survived five instrumented
probes across two sessions because every instrument verified SETTINGS
(compression flags, pin connections, variety lists) and none verified
CONTENT (what the mask evaluates to). The locked recipe now states the
rule: for texture-driven behaviour, the only sufficient read-back is a
RENDER.


## 2026-08-02 — [SystemSettings] sets sg.* VALUES but does NOT APPLY THE GROUPS

Task 1a asked whether our own low-spec config suppresses grass. The
answer for grass is NO, twice over — but finding that out exposed a
larger defect in the low-spec profile itself.

### The grass answer (NULL RESULT — locked so nobody re-tests it)

`sg.FoliageQuality` **cannot thin our grass or our trees.** Two
independent reasons, both established rather than assumed:

1. **At source.** `LandscapeGrass.cpp:2040`:
       const float DensityScale = bEnableDensityScaling ? GGrassDensityScale : 1.0f;
       GrassDensity = GrassVariety.GetDensity() * DensityScale;
   with `GrassType->bEnableDensityScaling` passed at :2161. Our
   `GT_alpine_Meadow` has it FALSE (set deliberately by
   make_landscape_material), so `grass.DensityScale` is ignored outright.
   The TREES are immune too, and by accident rather than design:
   `UFoliageType`'s constructor defaults `bEnableDensityScaling = false`
   (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:669`), and place_foliage never sets it.
2. **By measurement.** Grass component count at `sg.FoliageQuality=1`:
   **16** (4 per variety). After setting 3, flushing and dwelling:
   **16**, identical mesh distribution. No change.

### The larger defect this exposed

`Engine/Config/BaseScalability.ini:972` — `[FoliageQuality@1]` sets
`grass.DensityScale=0.4` AND `foliage.DensityScale=0.4`.

Yet a freshly launched editor carrying `sg.FoliageQuality=1` from
`DefaultEngine.ini [SystemSettings]` reported `grass.DensityScale=1.0`.
Both cannot be true unless the group never ran.

Discriminating test: issue `sg.FoliageQuality 0` from the console —
both scales went to **0.0**, and `pcg.Quality` to 0. Restore to 1 —
both went to **0.4**. So the cvar sink DOES apply groups on a console
set; it simply had not applied at startup.

**Conclusion: `[SystemSettings]` writes the sg.* cvar's VALUE at load
without running the scalability group.** The group applies later if
anything touches the Scalability UI or issues a console set.

**This makes RECIPES.md R7 partly wrong as written.** R7 claimed the
`[SystemSettings]` block is "authoritative, applied every launch,
cannot be shadowed". The ten `sg.*` entries are RECORDED at launch but
their groups are NOT applied. The plain cvars in that block
(`r.ScreenPercentage`, `t.MaxFPS`, `r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge`, the
Lumen switches, `r.ShaderPipelineCache.Enabled`) DO apply — those were
each confirmed by `LogConfig: Set CVar` at the headless boot. It is
specifically the scalability GROUPS that do not expand.

**Why this is dangerous rather than merely untidy:** vegetation would
silently drop to 40% partway through a session the moment anything
triggered the sink, and a verification pass taken after that point
would be measuring suppressed vegetation with no indication. That is
the exact failure mode Ryan named — "never again verify a veg pass
under settings that hide the vegetation".

**Fix (the split config Ryan asked for):** `grass.DensityScale=1.0` and
`foliage.DensityScale=1.0` are now pinned explicitly in
`[SystemSettings]`, AFTER the sg.* lines. Low scalability everywhere
else; vegetation density stays truthful regardless of whether the group
ever expands. The live session was restored to 1.0/1.0 as well, since
the ini only takes effect next launch and the verification screenshots
are being taken in this one.

**Rule: a config value being PRESENT is not the same as it being IN
EFFECT.** Verify the derived state, not the setting you wrote. This is
the same shape as the grass root cause — settings read-backs passed for
two sessions while the mask clipped every pixel.


## 2026-08-02 — GRASS DENSITY: reach traded for density, denser AND cheaper

Task 1b. Triage order was config -> recipe -> grass-type settings,
cheapest first. Config was eliminated in 1a (sg.FoliageQuality proven
inert for our assets), so this is the RECIPE tier.

The sparse read was not a bug — it was 2 tufts per square metre, which
is what `density_per_10m2: 20` means. A meadow needs tens.

**The lever nobody had pulled was CULL DISTANCE.** Grass was drawing to
120 m, which is invisible detail paid for at full price: 90,478
instances / 44.0M triangles a frame, almost all of it too far away to
resolve as anything but ground texture. Trading reach for density is
strictly better for a ground-level read:

    before   cull 120 m,  20/10m2  =  2 tufts/m2,  90,478 inst,  44.0M tris
    after    cull  50 m, 120/10m2  = 12 tufts/m2,  94,248 inst,  29.8M tris

Six times the density on screen, for THIRTY PERCENT FEWER TRIANGLES.
Also reweighted toward `tiny_a` (79 triangles) for bulk coverage and
away from `small_a` (833) — a 10x per-instance difference that lets the
count rise without the cost following it. `tall_a` at 25% keeps the
silhouette that reads at eye height.

Verified by render at the ground camera: tufts now cover the meadow.

**Rule: when a density looks wrong, check what it is being spent ON
before raising it.** Density and draw distance trade against each other,
and the cheap direction is usually to shorten the reach.


## 2026-08-02 — TREES: random yaw fed into PITCH; the forest was lying down
> STATUS: HISTORY — Rotator-order defect fixed; 28,302 run superseded by verified 219,659-instance scatter. History. [Pass 5 ruling, 2026-09-16]

`place_foliage` built each instance rotator POSITIONALLY as
`Rotator(_r[4], _r[3], _r[5])`, against a constructor whose contract is
`Rotator(roll, pitch, yaw)`, while the row is
`[x, y, z, YAW, PITCH, ROLL, scale]`. The 0-360 degree random yaw
therefore landed in PITCH. Measured over the 28,302 placed instances:

    97.6% tilted past 4 degrees
    MEDIAN TILT 90 degrees
    55.6% past 80 degrees

One transposition produced every symptom reported: the ~40 degree tilt,
the floating/clipping bases (a base-centre pivot on a tree pitched past
horizontal), and much of the "too sparse" read — trees lying flat do not
present as trees.

The alignment model was never wrong: `align_to_normal: 0.15` against a
24 degree slope cap yields max 3.6 degrees, already inside the "max ~4
degrees, never steep slope normals" requirement. Nothing about slope
handling needed changing.

### THIS IS A PROCESS FAILURE, not just a bug (constitution rule e)

**I logged this exact defect as §23.15 EARLIER THE SAME DAY** — the
`unreal.Rotator(roll, pitch, yaw)` transposition, found when a viewport
camera ended up pitched at the sky. The lesson existed and did not
prevent this.

**Why it did not fire:** I logged the INSTANCE and never swept the
CLASS. Non-negotiable 4 says "when you find a defect class, grep for it
everywhere immediately" and I did not. The sweep, done now, takes one
command and is decisive:

    apply_lighting  Rotator(roll=, pitch=, yaw=)   KEYWORDS — correct
    capture         Rotator(roll=, pitch=, yaw=)   KEYWORDS — correct
    frame_cameras   (a comment documenting the order)
    place_foliage   Rotator(_r[4], _r[3], _r[5])   POSITIONAL — THE BUG

Every site that used keywords was correct. The single positional call
was the single bug. **The gap fix is therefore not "remember the
order" — it is that positional construction of Rotator is banned.**
Keywords make the transposition unrepresentable.

**Rule: after logging a lesson about an API misuse, grep the repo for
every other call site of that API in the same commit.** A lesson that
names one instance protects one instance.

## 2026-08-02 — THE MATERIAL COMPILE GATE WAS INERT; the log is the instrument

`M_fir_bark` failed to compile seven times —
`(Node AppendVector) Missing AppendVector input A`, "Default Material
will be used in game" — and that material is bound to THREE of the fir's
four slots. Trunk, dead branches and trunk_c therefore rendered on the
engine Default Material across every conifer, which is exactly the
"magenta/pink vertical line from terrain to sky" that was reported as a
separate defect. **Tasks 3 and 4 were one defect.**

Persistent debug draw was REFUTED three independent ways — no live trace
call exists in any script.

**The real defect was the gate.** `make_foliage_material` captured
`compile_errors` and returned non-zero on them, but
`recompile_material()` had returned an EMPTY LIST six seconds before the
engine logged the seven failures. **Its return is a request-accepted,
not a verdict** — the compile is asynchronous. So the broken material
was written to disk and the script printed "verified by read-back".

Worse: my first fix attempt re-verified the rebuild with the SAME inert
instrument and I nearly closed it on that. An adversarial reviewer caught
it, citing non-negotiable 2.

**Fixed three ways:** every `connect_material_expressions` return is now
checked (unchecked returns are how an AppendVector shipped with no A
input); the build payload no longer saves at all; and the verdict comes
from the EDITOR LOG — a different instrument than the one that lied —
with the save issued only afterwards.

**The gate was then tested in both directions** against the real
historical failure text: it catches the genuine failure, does not
false-positive when a different material is being built, passes a clean
log, and errs toward refusing on a stale warning inside its window —
failing safe.

**Rule: an asynchronous operation's return value is never its verdict.**
Find an instrument that observes the OUTCOME.


## 2026-08-02 — DRAW DISTANCE: the same scalability trap, found by the fan-out

A parallel analyst found what I had missed while fixing the density
version of this: `[ViewDistanceQuality@1]` sets **`r.ViewDistanceScale
= 0.6`** (`BaseScalability.ini:116`), and that multiplies every
per-primitive max draw distance.

Measured: at launch it reads **1.0** — the group had not expanded,
consistent with the `[SystemSettings]` finding earlier today. Forcing
the group with a console `sg.ViewDistanceQuality 1` drove it to
**0.6**.

Unpinned, the recipe's 300 m tree cull silently becomes 180 m the moment
anything touches the Scalability UI. Pinned now, alongside the density
scales.

**Two things worth keeping beyond the fix:**

1. **I fixed the density instance and did not sweep the class — again.**
   When `grass.DensityScale` turned out to be scalability-suppressible I
   pinned it and moved on, without asking "what else in the sg.* groups
   multiplies something the recipe specifies". That is the identical
   omission as the Rotator lesson logged hours earlier in this same
   session: fix the instance, skip the sweep. The sweep is the whole
   point of non-negotiable 4, and it has now failed twice in one day.
   **The generalised rule: a recipe value and a scalability multiplier
   for the same quantity are two instruments for one decision — every
   such pair must be pinned, not just the one that bit.**

2. **My own verification flag was wrong and the data was right.** The
   check reported `GROUP CUTS VIEW DISTANCE: False` because it compared
   the cvar to `0.6` exactly, while the engine returns
   `0.6000000238418579`. The printed table showed the truth immediately.
   Had I trusted the boolean over the numbers I would have closed this
   as a non-issue. **Print the measurement, not just the verdict derived
   from it** — an exact-equality test on a float is a verdict that can
   be wrong while its own evidence is right.

Left in the live session by this test: `r.SkeletalMeshLODBias` is 1
(from the group expand). Harmless here — no skeletal meshes — and it
resets on relaunch. Stated rather than silently left.


# Session 4 — 2026-08-03

## 2026-08-03 — THE 0.00% MEASUREMENT WAS THE DEFECT, NOT THE SCENE

I reported "0.00% vegetation pixels at 2 km" as a FINDING at the end of
the previous session, and it became the headline entry in the aerial
backlog. It measured nothing.

The rule was green dominance: (G > R+8) AND (G > B+8). This scene is
warm-lit. Mean terrain RGB on the ground frame is R 92.5 > G 79.2 >
B 54.0, so vegetation renders RED-dominant and the test can never fire.
Proof it was broken rather than merely strict: re-run on the GROUND
frame -- which visibly contains grass and 160,448 trees -- and it also
returns 0.00%.

Two further metrics were wrong before I stopped:

1. G - (R+B)/2 above an ABSOLUTE threshold. Brightness-dependent. The
   forest tint MULTIPLIES albedo, so it darkens; a darker-but-greener
   surface scores LOWER. It reported the aerial frame had got slightly
   worse.
2. Only after normalising by (R+G+B) did the numbers behave -- ground
   +0.0216 -> +0.0249 with brightness 80.7 -> 65.7 (tint landing),
   aerial -0.0255 -> -0.0266 (unchanged).

Then I looked at the frames, which settled in seconds what three metrics
had failed to settle in twenty minutes. The aerial camera is pointed at
a rock-and-snow peak with half the frame in deep shadow; the forest band
is a minority of pixels. That camera would report ~0% vegetation no
matter how good the vegetation was.

### The rule

A measurement is an INSTRUMENT, and an instrument needs calibrating
against a case with a KNOWN answer before its output is a finding. The
ground frame was available the whole time and is exactly that case: any
vegetation metric that scores it near zero is broken, full stop.

This is the same shape as non-negotiable 9 and the fov_deg defect: a
number arrived, it was in range, and it meant something else. It is also
the THIRD time this project has been misled by trusting a computed
verdict over the raw data underneath it -- see the 0.6000000238418579
float-equality entry from 2026-08-02. Print the measurement AND look at
the artefact; the verdict is the least trustworthy layer.

## 2026-08-03 — THE REDUCER EATS THE CANOPY FIRST

Re-solving the conifer LOD chain for a longer cull, I added a fifth
level at 0.137% (693 triangles). It hit its triangle target exactly and
came back with 2 material sections where LOD 0 has 4. make_mesh_lods
refused to save, correctly.

I formed a hypothesis that the guard was too strict: three of the fir's
four slots (bark, dead_branches, trunk_c) are bound to the SAME material
M_fir_bark, so two surviving sections could in principle still cover
both DISTINCT materials, leaving nothing unbound.

I probed instead of relaxing the guard, and the hypothesis was WRONG.
Surviving slots were [0, 3] -- both M_fir_bark. The dropped section was
slot 1, fir_tree_01_twig: the canopy, and the sole user of M_fir_twig.
Every distant conifer would have rendered as a bare stick.

Root cause is mesh-simplifier behaviour: a trunk is a connected cylinder
and survives decimation; a canopy is thousands of disconnected leaf
cards and is collapsed first. THE VISUALLY DOMINANT FEATURE IS THE FIRST
THING AN AGGRESSIVE LOD DELETES.

### The rules

1. A guard you are about to weaken deserves one probe first. The probe
   cost one read and refuted a plausible, well-argued theory that would
   have shipped bare sticks across the whole forest.
2. Section count is not a proxy for material coverage, and material
   count is not a proxy for visual completeness. The right invariant is
   that every DISTINCT material still has geometry -- and even that
   would have passed here only by accident.

Locked in R5 REJECTED with the exact percentage and symptom.

## 2026-08-03 — THE CHAIN WAS THE WASTE, NOT THE CULL

The aerial backlog assumed the fix for "no trees at distance" was
imposters, because extending the 300 m cull was assumed unaffordable.
Both halves were wrong, and the arithmetic said so before anything was
built.

Decomposing the 35.9M triangle frame at the 300 m cull:

    LOD0    0- 44 m     15 trees x 505,494 =  7.6M   (909 tris/px)
    LOD1   44-110 m     79 trees x 126,374 = 10.0M   (563 tris/px)
    LOD2  110-300 m    603 trees x  30,329 = 18.3M   (367 tris/px)

A tree 110 m away is 45 pixels tall and was being drawn with 30,329
triangles. Half the frame budget went to the band where the trees are
smallest. Extending the cull on that chain is unaffordable at any depth
-- even a 505-triangle deepest level only buys 350 m.

Re-solving on percent_triangles = screen_size^2 -- which holds
triangles-per-pixel roughly constant and reproduces the existing,
visually verified LOD1 (0.5 -> 25%) exactly -- gives every band an equal
8.9M cost and yields cull 730 m at 39.6M. The same chain costs 26.3M at
the original 300 m, i.e. 27% cheaper than before at equal distance.

### The rule

Before buying a new mechanism, decompose the cost of the existing one.
The backlog had already decided imposters were needed; ten lines of
arithmetic showed 2.4x the draw distance was available for +10% cost,
from fixing a chain nobody had questioned since it was written.

## 2026-08-03 — "I COULDN'T LOOK" REPORTED AS "IT'S ABSENT", TWICE

Verifying the forest tint reached the material graph, my probe printed:

    FOREST FLOOR IN GRAPH: False

The truth was that enumeration had failed outright --
expression_collection does not exist on Material in 5.8 -- so the probe
had inspected an EMPTY LIST and correctly reported that an empty list
contains no tint. The verdict was a false negative dressed as a
measurement. Had I believed it, I would have "fixed" working code.

The same probe had already guessed get_number_triangles and
get_number_materials(lod); neither exists. The working accessors were in
this repo the whole time -- MaterialEditingLibrary.get_material_
expressions and mesh.get_num_triangles(lod) / get_num_sections(lod),
both used by scripts I had already run THAT DAY.

### The rules

1. Non-negotiable 10 is not automatic -- it has to be BUILT IN. The
   probe now returns a distinct exit code and prints "COULD NOT LOOK ...
   This is NOT evidence of absence" rather than a verdict.
2. Before guessing an API name, grep the repo for a script that already
   does the same read. The resolution protocol says query the running
   editor first; the cheaper prior step is querying our own working code.

scripts/recover_state.py was written with this built in: every read is
individually guarded, failures come back as an error marker, and the
report ENDS by listing every value it could not read, so unreadable
values become VALUE UNVERIFIED in RECIPES rather than silent defaults.

## 2026-08-03 — A KILLED CLIENT IS NOT A CANCELLED OPERATION

place_foliage.py --place was invoked with a 40-minute timeout. The tool
running it caps at 10 minutes, so the CLIENT was killed at 10.

The payload runs IN THE EDITOR. Killing the client stops the reporting,
not the work. A read-back probe showed the placement had COMPLETED:
160,448 instances at cull 54750..73000 cm, exactly as specified.

Had I re-run it on the assumption that an interrupted command did
nothing, I would have placed a second time on top of a completed one.

### The rule

For any remote-executed operation, an interrupted client leaves the
outcome UNKNOWN, never "did not happen". Settle it with a read-only
probe before acting. This is the same shape as R1's rule that
push_heightmap exit 5 means UNKNOWN and must not be retried.

## 2026-08-03 — t.MaxFPS=45 IS IN THE CONFIG AND NOT IN THE EDITOR

scripts/recover_state.py read the live session and found t.MaxFPS = 0.0
-- unlimited -- while DefaultEngine.ini [SystemSettings] line 178 says
t.MaxFPS=45.

Every OTHER plain cvar in that block matched its ini value exactly
(r.ScreenPercentage 70, r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge 4,
r.ShaderPipelineCache.Enabled 1, both Lumen switches 0,
r.ViewDistanceScale 1.0), and all ten sg.* values matched. So this is
NOT the scalability-group trap already logged -- it is specific to
t.MaxFPS, which the editor evidently sets for itself after
[SystemSettings] is applied.

Consequence: the frame cap intended to keep load off this GPU is not in
effect, on a machine that has already thrown DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG. R7
was verified by a HEADLESS boot log, where the value did apply; the
editor behaves differently. Logged to BACKLOG and to R0 REJECTED; not
fixed this session.

### The rule

A config value verified in one host mode is not verified in another.
Headless proved the ini line is read. It did not prove the editor keeps
it.

## 2026-08-03 — GOVERNANCE: recipes became specifications

Restructured on Ryan's brief. The change of kind: RECIPES.md was a set
of well-written NOTES; it is now a set of SPECIFICATIONS, each carrying
PRECONDITIONS / EXACT VALUES / ORDERED STEPS / VERIFICATION / REJECTED.

Two things make this more than formatting:

1. EXACT VALUES were recovered from the running editor by
   scripts/recover_state.py, not from memory. Seven scene fields came
   back unreadable and are marked VALUE UNVERIFIED rather than filled
   in. That distinction is the whole point.
2. REJECTED sections make the anti-spec first-class. The completeness
   test is: could a fresh session repeat a past mistake without opening
   LESSONS.md? Every failure with an exact value attached was back-filled
   as WRONG -> SYMPTOM -> CORRECT -> ref.

Every recipe is tagged UNPROVEN. None has been replayed cold, and
"written down carefully" is not "proven reproducible". Saying so in the
tag is cheaper than discovering it during an engine migration.


## 2026-08-03 — RETROACTIVE CAPTURE PASS: applying new rules to old work

Ryan's governance rules landed AFTER the work they govern. This pass
went back through the session (13 commits after dad6ffa7) and captured
everything to the new standard, as if the rules had existed then.

The interesting part was not the mechanical retrofit. It was what the
sweep FOUND.

### A stale claim had hardened into a fact

`WORLD_VISION.md` carried "AERIAL READABILITY IS ZERO ... 0.00%
vegetation-coloured pixels -- measured, not estimated." I wrote that.
The words "measured, not estimated" were doing real damage: they told
every future session not to re-check it. The measurement was broken, and
the emphasis on its rigour is exactly what would have stopped anyone
noticing.

Corrected in place, with the correction stated rather than silently
swapped, so the next reader learns the metric was wrong instead of
merely seeing different words.

**Rule: an assertion of rigour ("measured, not estimated", "verified by
read-back", "confirmed at source") is a claim that itself needs to be
true.** Attaching it to a bad number makes the number harder to
dislodge, not more reliable. This is the same failure mode as the
material compile gate that printed "verified by read-back" over a
broken material.

### The constitution contradicted itself about its own file set

`CLAUDE.md` had BOTH "Plus four load-bearing non-documents" and "Plus
three load-bearing non-documents" -- I edited the table to six files and
added the new paragraph without deleting the one it replaced. The
governing document was internally inconsistent for a full commit.

**Rule: an edit that ADDS a replacement must delete the thing it
replaces in the same edit.** Append-only is right for LESSONS, which is
a narrative log. It is wrong for CLAUDE and RECIPES, which are
statements of what is currently true.

### A live defect was recovered from an old class sweep

The 2026-08-02 sweep recorded that the fir's bark and twig ROUGHNESS
maps are also I;16, under TC_Masks, "presumed silently wrong (a shine
defect, not invisibility)". The 8-bit conversion shipped -- but the fir
was never REIMPORTED through it. So the presumption is still live, and
it is a candidate cause of the currently-open "conifers render as bare
spindly poles" defect.

That connection was sitting in LESSONS the whole time and had not been
made, because the sweep's finding was logged as narrative and never
became an actionable item anywhere.

**Rule: a class sweep that finds additional affected sites must create a
work item per site, not a sentence.** "Presumed silently wrong" is a
defect report, and it belongs in BACKLOG the moment it is written.

### A delegated ruling was taken back

Ryan reopened contiguous-vs-multi-region, which the previous session had
ruled MULTI-REGION under an explicit delegation. The analysis was not
withdrawn -- the DECISION was. WORLD_VISION now records it as an open
decision with the proposal complete and blocking all placement work.

**Rule: when a delegated decision is reclaimed, downgrade the status and
keep the reasoning.** Deleting the analysis would force it to be redone;
leaving it labelled RULED would let work proceed on an authority that no
longer exists.


## 2026-08-03 — THE TRUNKS WERE WEARING THE CANOPY'S TEXTURES

Task as given: "reimport the fir through the 8-bit conversion". The
first measurement refuted the premise, and my own backlog entry with it.

**The reimport was already done.** T_fir_tree_01_bark_rough_4k and
T_fir_tree_01_twig_rough_4k both trace to *_8bit.png sources in
Free/_normalized/. And fir_tree_01_twig_alpha_4k.png is **RGB 8-bit** --
the canopy mask was NEVER in the 16-bit trap. I had written "the fir was
never reimported after the fix shipped" into BACKLOG the previous
session, from the LESSONS narrative, without checking the engine.

**A backlog claim about project state is a measurement.** It has to be
made against the project. Mine was made against the log, and it was
wrong in a way that would have sent this session to redo completed work.

### The actual root cause, found by asking what M_fir_bark samples

    M_fir_bark samples:  twig_diff x3, twig_nor_gl x2, twig_rough
    ...and never a bark texture at all.

`texture_map` built `{role: asset}` with a plain `out[role] = ...`.
`fir_tree_01` ships bark_* and twig_* sets and BOTH provide `color`,
`normal` and `roughness`. Called without `--slot`, the later file wins
every contested role -- and "bark" sorts before "twig". So the material
bound to THREE of the fir's four slots, across 160,448 instances,
textured every trunk with the pale twig atlas.

**Why nothing caught it.** Every downstream check was satisfied: the
textures existed, each sampler's type matched its compression setting,
the material compiled clean against the editor log, and the read-back
confirmed all three slots were bound. The map was internally consistent.
It simply described the wrong texture set, and no gate in the pipeline
knows what a trunk is supposed to look like.

Fixed at the input rather than with a gate (non-negotiable 3): a role
claimed by more than one file is now a REFUSAL that names the competing
files. Tested both directions -- refuses with no `--slot`, resolves
cleanly with `--slot bark` and `--slot twig`.

### THE SECOND DEFECT, WHICH HID THE FIRST FIX

Rebuilding with `--slot bark` reported success and changed NOTHING on
screen. `M_fir_bark` then had SIX samplers: the three new bark ones and
the three old twig ones, still wired to BaseColor.

`make_foliage_material` cleared with `delete_all_material_expressions`
alone. **R2 REJECTED has recorded since 2026-08-02 that this call does
not delete all material expressions** -- the landscape material was
fixed then, with an explicit sweep of survivors and a residual count.
That fix was never swept to the foliage builder.

Instrumented, the numbers are unambiguous: **7 expressions survived on
M_fir_bark, 8 on M_fir_twig.** Now every survivor is deleted explicitly,
a nonzero remainder REFUSES rather than building on debris, and both
counts print on every run.

**This is non-negotiable 4 -- "when you find a defect class, grep for it
everywhere immediately" -- failing for the THIRD time in this project**
(after the Rotator transposition and the scalability-multiplier pins).
The pattern is identical each time: fix the instance, log the instance,
skip the sweep. The lesson exists and does not fire.

**What would actually fire:** the sweep has to happen in the SAME commit
as the fix, as a mechanical step, not as an intention recorded for
later. Every one of these three was logged conscientiously and swept
never.

### What the render finally showed

Trunks now sample bark_diff (mean brightness 64, dark brown). The change
is modest in the strongly side-lit verify_ground frame -- near-trunk RGB
115/98/64 -> 109/90/62 -- and obvious in the backlit forest_floor frame,
where trunks read dark brown-grey and the needle branches are clearly
conifer.

**I twice called the trunks "pale cream" from a frame where the measured
value was a tan-brown under direct sun.** The eye is a poor photometer
against a dark background; the patch mean settled in one command what
two rounds of looking did not.

Remaining sparseness is the ASSET -- fir_tree_01_c is a slender,
high-branching fir -- plus aggressive mid-LODs. That is a judgement
call, now in BACKLOG, not a defect.


## 2026-08-03 — CLASS-LEVEL PROMOTION: the third recurrence buys shared infrastructure

Ruled by Ryan after the fir defect. The incomplete-clear/append-debris
trap had now recurred in THREE tools:

  1. make_landscape_material -- LandscapeGrassOutput survived
     delete_all_material_expressions; rebuilds accumulated 80 -> 158
     expressions until the material stopped compiling.
  2. the same builder again, fixed locally.
  3. make_foliage_material -- never swept. 7 survivors on M_fir_bark,
     8 on M_fir_twig, all still WIRED, so a rebuild with the correct
     bark textures changed nothing on screen.

Each fix was correct. Each was logged. The next tool repeated it. **Per
script fixes were not containing the class**, so the ruling promotes it
to shared infrastructure and makes the per-script copy itself a REJECTED
pattern.

`material_graph` now provides two fragments injected into any editor
payload: `_ll_clear_graph` (delete_all, then delete every survivor, then
re-read and let the caller REFUSE on a nonzero remainder) and
`_ll_assert_graph` (the sampled texture set must EXACTLY equal spec;
EXTRA nodes fail loudly, because the failure mode was never a missing
node -- it was a surviving one). Both builders are migrated and both
results print on every run.

### The new automatic trigger

**A trap class reaching a SECOND recurrence across DIFFERENT tools now
escalates to shared infrastructure on the spot**, without waiting for a
third. Added to CLAUDE.md as non-negotiable 4a.

### THE ASSERTION REFUSED MY SPEC TWICE, AND WAS RIGHT BOTH TIMES

This is the part worth remembering.

**First:** I declared the twig alpha map TWICE in the expected set
(colour + opacity), from a probe of the live `M_fir_twig` that showed
two alpha samplers. That graph was carrying 8 debris expressions at the
time and the duplicate WAS debris. The builder samples alpha once and
