## 2026-08-06 — A MEASUREMENT CARRIES THE CLASS OF ITS INSTRUMENT

GPU cost was finally measured (Ryan, attended): 94.45 ms GPU at
sweep_2000, 75.71 ms at sweep_0060, GPU-bound at both, cost in per-pixel
shading rather than scene bloat. It closed a BACKLOG item that had been
open since the campaign began and unblocked Pass 6's back half.

The durable part is not the number. It is that the ruling **stated the
CALIBRATION CLASS and bound every downstream decision to it**: editor
viewport, Intel iGPU, 971x752, RenderRes 100%, editor perf config —
explicitly NOT shipping, NOT PIE, NOT the future 5080.

**A NUMBER IS ONLY AS PORTABLE AS THE CLASS IT WAS TAKEN IN.** Quoting a
figure outside its class is a category error that looks like diligence,
because a real measurement is being cited. It is the same defect as the
misleading denominator (non-negotiable 22) moved from WHAT was measured
to WHERE it was measured — and this project has already paid for the
first form twice, once when a layer-scoped statistic was reported against
the whole map, and once when a crop of a frame was reported as "ground".

The ruling models the correct handling in three ways worth copying:
  - it names the class in the same breath as the number;
  - it **splits the decision by context** rather than forcing one answer
    (clouds OFF interactive, PERMITTED offline) — the constraint is
    interactivity, not the feature;
  - it makes the offline permission **conditional on a measurement of the
    OTHER class** (per-frame render-time delta at first enablement),
    because an editor-class number cannot budget a render-class job;
  - and it names a **RE-OPEN TRIGGER** (5080 arrival) so the ruling
    expires by event rather than quietly persisting as folklore.

**Rulings that carry their own expiry condition do not rot.** Compare
14.7's "Use Less CPU when in Background", now in WATCHING state with both
outcomes pre-declared. That is the shape to reach for.

## 2026-08-06 — THE PASS AUDIT: 3 OF 8 SURVIVED, AND NOT ONE FAILED THE WAY WE FEARED

Pass 1 sat on the board as "DONE. Terrain pushed and verified" for three
days while the live world was a different heightmap. Every gate was
green because every gate read the same file. So the whole board was
declared UNTRUSTED and re-checked, row by row, against a representation
that did NOT record it — eight agents, one pass each, and every
CONFIRMED verdict then handed to an adversarial skeptic.

**Result: 3 CONFIRMED, 5 OPTIMISTIC, 0 FALSE, 0 UNVERIFIABLE at the row
level.** One CONFIRMED was overturned by the skeptic (Pass 2). Nothing
on the board was a fabrication. Five rows overstate what their evidence
carries.

### The class: NOTHING WAS INVENTED; THE PRECISION WAS

The Pass 1 defect was a state claim that was FALSE. Not one of the five
OPTIMISTIC rows is false in that way. The pattern is narrower and
harder to see, and it has three recurring shapes:

**SHAPE 1 — A TRUE NUMBER FROM A CIRCULAR INSTRUMENT, PROMOTED TO THE
HEADLINE.** Pass 4's "grounding max 0.001 m" is arithmetically correct
about `alpine_heightmap_v2.png` — read through the PLANNER'S OWN LOADER.
`verify_grounding.py:20-32` says so in its own docstring: *"this would
report zero gap on a map where every tree hovers."* Measured against
engine COLLISION the same placement reads p50 +0.006 / p90 +0.068 / max
+0.392 m. The trees ARE grounded; the cited figure is 392x tighter than
contact with the world a player touches. **The docstring was honest and
the board quoted the number anyway.** A disclaimer inside the instrument
does not travel with its output. If a measurement is not independent,
the NUMBER has to carry that, not the source file.

**SHAPE 2 — A CARRY-FORWARD PRESENTED AS A RUN RESULT.** SWEEP_REPORT §4
lists "Sampler audit — PASS 43/43" inside the v2sweep run of record. 31
of the 43 were measured the previous day against the WRONG-TERRAIN
sweep; the material package changed afterwards; there is no dated
sampler-audit artefact anywhere in `_verify/`; and §7's carry-forward
ledger — built for exactly this — lists criterion 4 in neither SURVIVES
nor SUPERSEDED. **A ledger with a hole in it is worse than no ledger,
because its existence certifies the rows it forgot.**

**SHAPE 3 — A COUNT THAT HIDES A DEFECT.** Pass 7 said "gate open on 3
evidence gaps". Its own report lists FOUR things the gate needs, and the
omitted fourth is not an absence of evidence — it is a station-siting
DEFECT that rendered 2 of the 6 acceptance-condition stations unusable,
so criterion 9 is graded on 4 of its own 6 stations. **"Three gaps"
reads as three things left to look at. One of them was a fault.**

### DID ANY STATUS HOLD ONLY BECAUSE NOBODY ASKED A DIFFERENT QUESTION?

Yes, and this is the finding worth keeping. Every OPTIMISTIC row had
been checked before — by a real instrument, producing a real number,
honestly transcribed. What changed was not rigour; it was the QUESTION.

- Pass 0's palette was checked for existence and triangle counts.
  Nobody had asked a LOADED mesh what `material_slots` actually is.
  When someone did: contradicted on **8 of the 13** entries any second
  instrument can reach, by up to 12x, with the raw `.uasset` name table
  and `StaticMesh.cpp:6319` agreeing against the palette. The vendor
  packages serialize a stale tag. A 62% failure rate among checkable
  rows, in a field a downstream draw-call budget would consume.
- Pass 6's sun was checked against the recipe. Nobody had asked the
  world what ELSE is in it. A `VolumetricCloud` actor has been sitting
  in /Game/Alpine since at least 2026-08-04 — undeclared by any recipe,
  unmanaged by any script, and invisible to `apply_lighting`'s
  foreign-actor census, which enumerates DirectionalLight,
  ExponentialHeightFog, SkyAtmosphere and SkyLight and not that class.
  The board asserts "clouds NOT enabled" as a fact about the world.
  **No instrument in this pipeline can enforce that negative.**
- Pass 3's boulders were checked for grounding against the heightmap.
  Nobody had asked the ENGINE. When someone did, the placement came
  back better than advertised (median residual +0.000 m against
  collision) — and the project's own named instrument,
  `trace_grounding.py`, printed **"FLOATING CONFIRMED, 80 of 80
  (100.0%)"** over it, because line 193 reads `sink_depth_m` (a CONIFER
  key the boulder plan does not have) and line 316 computes the gap on a
  BOX-CENTRED pivot. **An instrument with the wrong premise is not
  silent; it is confidently wrong in whichever direction its premise
  points.**

### THE ONE THAT SHOULD SCARE US MOST

Not a wrong number — a gate that will fire against a green board.
`python scripts/trace_grounding.py --n 500` at its DOCUMENTED default
epsilon of 0.05 m prints FLOATING CONFIRMED and **exits 5** on Pass 4's
current, correct data (13.2% of sample). The gate was closed by an
ADJUDICATION that lives only in `LESSONS.md:10523-10533`. It is encoded
neither in the instrument nor in RECIPES.md, and no epsilon waiver is
recorded anywhere. A fresh session running our own independent grounding
check at its own defaults gets a failure banner while CLAUDE.md tells it
the gate is closed. **That is non-negotiable 24 exactly: the ruling and
the check are two lists that must agree, stored separately.** The
adjudication is sound; storing it in prose is the defect.

### THE AUDIT CAUGHT THE AUDIT

Two of these findings are about the checking apparatus, not the work:

`SWEEP_REPORT.md` §2 closes the floating-trees defect with a
three-row table of "corroborating instruments". Rows 2 and 3 are the
SIGNED and the ABSOLUTE values of the same 500 pairs in the same JSON
file, and row 1 shares the v2 heightmap with the plan column of both.
Two representations presented as three — **non-negotiable 0 violated
inside the document that was verifying everything else.** It was only
caught because the auditor re-reduced the raw dump instead of reading
the summary; comparing the report's three rows to each other would have
produced perfect "agreement".

And an auditor declared engine source ABSENT FROM THIS MACHINE, and used
that absence to excuse the one hole it admitted (the CLEAN half of the
sampler audit). The skeptic opened
`Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Materials/MaterialExpressions.cpp`
and found `VerifySamplerType` at :2760-2767. **An "I could not look"
that was really "I looked in the wrong place" is the most dangerous
possible reading of non-negotiable 6**, because it converts a closable
gap into a permanent-looking one and stops anyone else trying.

### WHY A CLEAN SWEEP WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORST OUTCOME

If all eight had come back CONFIRMED, four days after the board was
catastrophically wrong, the correct response would have been suspicion
of the AUDIT, not celebration of the board. That is not the situation —
five rows moved, three adjacent records were found wrong
(`RECIPES.md` R12 "Not yet placed", `PROJECT_STATE.json` still carrying
the REJECTED 18000 sun intensity, and CLAUDE.md's own "PASS 5 HAS NO
WRITTEN SCOPE" three days after Pass 5 was scoped), and one instrument
was found broken. **The audit moved things, which is the evidence that
it was looking.**

The three CONFIRMED rows earned it in the same way, and it is worth
naming what they had in common: each was proven by an instrument that
CANNOT be edited by writing prose. Pass 1 by the engine's own log and
live collision. Pass 3 by 493 grid-cell IDs in saved package names
matching the plan's predicted cells with zero set difference in either
direction. Pass 5 by a POSITIVE-CONTROLLED search — 0 for every clutter
identity in the same corpus and the same command that returns 504, 1044
and 256 for three known-placed controls, so the zero is a measurement
and not a broken grep.

**THE RULE.** *An independent instrument is defined by what it CANNOT
see, not by being a different file.* `verify_grounding` reads a
different file from the plan and still cannot see a hovering forest,
because it reads it through the planner's loader. The saved package
NAMES cannot see the plan at all, which is why 493 cells matching means
something. When you name a cross-check, state what it is BLIND to — and
if the answer is "the same thing the recorded instrument was blind to",
it is one measurement, not two.

**THE SECOND RULE, for the board itself.** *Every number on the board
carries its DENOMINATOR and its INSTRUMENT CLASS, or it does not go on
the board.* "max 0.001 m" (heightmap arithmetic, not collision), "v1
misses by median 1135" (the 161-texel probe row, not the map — whole-map
it is 38 u / 1.484 m), "GPU 94.45 ms" (attended viewport reading, no
artefact), "43/43 samplers" (31 of them from the previous sweep) — four
true numbers, four missing labels, and each one reads stronger than it
is. This is non-negotiable 22 promoted from a statistic to a habit: the
label is part of the number.

## 2026-08-06 — THE AUDIT: A RULING NOT ENCODED IN THE INSTRUMENT WILL BE RE-LITIGATED

An 8-pass cross-representation audit (each row checked against a
representation that did NOT record it, CONFIRMED verdicts sent to an
adversarial skeptic) returned **3 CONFIRMED, 5 OPTIMISTIC, 1 CONFIRMED
overturned on refutation.**

**The Pass 1 failure did not disappear — it CHANGED SHAPE.** Nothing on
the board is fabricated. What is wrong is that TRUE NUMBERS ARE QUOTED
WITHOUT THE CLASS OF INSTRUMENT THAT PRODUCED THEM. The board says
"grounding max 0.001 m"; that figure comes from `verify_grounding`, whose
own docstring says it *"would report zero gap on a map where every tree
hovers"*. Engine collision measures max +0.392 m on the same placement.
Both numbers are correct. Only one of them is evidence of grounding.

### The concrete hazard, and it was live

`scripts/trace_grounding.py` — the project's own INDEPENDENT check —
printed **FLOATING CONFIRMED and exited 5 on correct data**, because its
epsilon defaulted to 0.05 m while measured collision quantization reaches
0.392 m. The adjudication that closed the Pass 4 exit gate lived ONLY in
LESSONS prose. So a fresh session running our own independent instrument
got a FAILURE BANNER while CLAUDE.md told it the gate was closed.

**A RULING THAT IS NOT ENCODED IN THE INSTRUMENT IS A RULING THAT WILL BE
RE-LITIGATED BY WHOEVER RUNS THE TOOL NEXT.** Prose records a decision;
only the tool enforces it. Fixed: epsilon is now 0.45 m, DERIVED from the
measured quantization (p90 0.091 / max 0.431, signed mean -0.007 —
symmetric, therefore quantization and not floating) rather than chosen
for comfort, with the derivation in the code beside the number.

### Second defect: an instrument measuring the wrong quantity in silence

The same tool applied the CONIFER grounding convention (`sink_depth_m`,
pivot at flare) to the BOULDER plan, which has no such key and grounds
via `pivot_base_offset_m` (-0.6183) and `embed_depth_per_scale_m` (0.234,
scale-dependent). The missing key defaulted to 0.0 and the tool reported
~100% FLOATING over placement that engine traces put at median +0.000 m.

Now it REFUSES (exit 2) and names the keys it found instead. **A
plausible number from the wrong premise is worse than a refusal:** the
refusal costs a re-run, the number costs a wrong conclusion about 759
placed instances — and would have invited "fixing" placement that was
already correct.

### Third: the machine-recovered record was never re-recovered

`PROJECT_STATE.json` — the file the constitution names as machine
recovered state backing the recipes — still carried the R13-REJECTED sun
intensity **18000.0**, the value measured as 5x too dim. Checked against
the live world before assuming: **the live sun IS 130000.0**, so R13 is
correctly applied and the FILE was stale, not the scene. Regenerated from
the world.

Note the trap in the check itself: `recover_state.py` only writes with
`--out`, so running it bare exits 0, reports nothing amiss, and leaves
the stale file in place. **An exit code from a tool that did not write is
not evidence that the file is current.**

### The rule

**DERIVED RECORDS EXPIRE WHEN THE THING THEY DESCRIBE CHANGES, AND
NOTHING TELLS YOU.** Non-negotiable 15 says verify derived records
against ground truth at the moment they are written. This adds: a record
written correctly and then left alone becomes false without any event to
notice. R13 changed the sun on 2026-08-04; PROJECT_STATE was correct
until that moment and wrong for two days after, with no failing test
anywhere.

## 2026-08-06 — THE POLISH DETECTOR USED THE POLISHED GROUND AS ITS OWN CONTROL

`scripts/measure_falloff_contours.py` was committed on 2026-08-06
(`b89a422c`) at 677 lines, parsing cleanly, **never once run**. The
handoff said so honestly and called it NOT coverage. First run of
`--selftest`: 7 of 8 checks pass and the one that fails is the only
POSITIVE CONTROL — case 4, a synthetic bare smoothstep ramp standing in
for the exact defect the instrument exists to find.

### What it does

Reading B flags a window as "polished" when its median |laplacian| is
below **40%** of the map-wide median |laplacian| FOR ITS OWN SLOPE BAND.
Conditioning on slope is right and was deliberate — a 20-degree ramp must
be compared against other 20-degree ground, not against the whole map
(non-negotiable 22).

### Root cause — the denominator contained the numerator

Measured on the synthetic (`band_medians`, `measure_falloff_contours.
py:309-317`):

    slope band 15-30 deg : 110,953 cells, map median |lap| 0.0534 m
    the annulus alone    :  94,136 cells, median |lap|     0.0466 m

**85% of the reference population IS the ground under test.** A polished
window at 0.040 m scores 0.040 / 0.053 = **0.76** against a 0.4 bar and
is not flagged. The smooth ramp defined the standard it was being judged
against.

The failure mode is self-masking and gets WORSE with severity: a small
polished patch barely moves its band median and would be caught; a large
one dominates the band and hides completely. **An instrument whose
sensitivity falls as the defect grows is not conservative, it is
inverted.** Fourteen windows did squeak through on residual variation,
but as scattered pairs — largest 4-connected cluster 2, against
`SPOT_MIN_WINDOWS = 6` — so the run reported nothing at all.

### Why the design review did not catch it

The docstring reasons carefully about the bar (`POLISH_REL_SCORE = 0.4`
justified against a p5 of ~0.47 on the current terrain) and about
conditioning on slope. Both are correct. **The unexamined premise is that
"map-wide median for the slope band" is a CONTROL** — and it is only a
control if the suspect ground is a small minority of it, which is
precisely what nobody checked and what the instrument itself could have
printed.

### The fix

The reference population is now the cells **NOT in any falloff annulus**,
declared in the output with its cell count per band, and a band whose
reference population is too small returns None -> those windows are
SKIPPED AND COUNTED, never silently dropped. Same bar, honest
denominator.

### The rule

**A CONTROL POPULATION THAT CAN CONTAIN THE THING UNDER TEST IS NOT A
CONTROL. STATE ITS SIZE AND ITS MEMBERSHIP, OR IT IS AN ASSUMPTION.**
This is non-negotiable 22 (a statistic is meaningful only conditioned on
where it applies) turned on the REFERENCE rather than on the modulator:
conditioning the numerator correctly buys nothing if the denominator is
drawn from the same pixels. Non-negotiable 5 — a check that consumes the
value it is verifying verifies nothing — is the same defect one step
upstream.

**And the second-order lesson, which is the expensive one: this
instrument would have SHIPPED A CLEAN BILL OF HEALTH.** Run against the
real terrain it exits 0, "no polished spot at the derived bars", and
Pass 7's gate item 3 closes on a measurement that cannot fail. The
committed-but-never-run state is what saved it, because the FIRST thing
done to it was to demand it detect a known defect. A gate that has only
seen good input has not been tested (non-negotiable 2) — and this one
had not seen ANY input.

## 2026-08-06 — THE ACCEPTANCE BAR NOBODY IMPLEMENTED, AND THE 2x THAT SAVED IT

With the polish detector fixed, reading A of `measure_falloff_contours.
py` produced its first real numbers — the `spine_aretes` CV re-test that
has been an open Pass 7 gate item since 2026-08-05.

    recorded (schema.md:824-825)  0.089 - 0.367  over EIGHT placements
    measured (this procedure)     0.033 - 0.152  over NINE placements

`spine_aretes` measures **0.047** against a recorded 0.089 and a locked
bar of 0.05. Read naively that is a SPEC VIOLATION, and a second one
underneath it — `cliff_band_west` at 0.033, which was never on anyone's
list. The obvious next move is to raise the jitter and re-composite.

**That move would have re-adopted the terrain and invalidated 157,554
conifer and 759 boulder placements**, three days after the last time
this project discovered what a terrain change does to everything
downstream.

### What stopped it: the offset is uniform

Every one of the nine is lower, by roughly the same factor. A terrain
defect, a tuning drift, or a bad placement would move SOME of them. A
uniform ratio across all nine is a statement about the DERIVATION.

So I went looking for the derivation, and there isn't one. The bar
appears in `recipes/schema.md:824` and in RECIPES prose, and a grep for
any CV check across `scripts/` returns NOTHING.

**The bar has never been enforced by any code in this repo.** The band
0.089-0.367 was measured by hand once, for EIGHT placements when the
recipe now carries NINE, and the procedure was never written down. It is
the sweep summit and the "43/43 samplers" again: a real number whose
choosing procedure is unrecoverable, sitting in a normative document
looking exactly like a specification.

### The rule

**A BAR WITH NO IMPLEMENTATION IS A BELIEF, AND COMPARING A NEW
MEASUREMENT AGAINST IT MEASURES NOTHING.** Non-negotiable 24 says two
lists that must agree are one list badly stored; this is the degenerate
case — the spec exists, the projection that would check it never did, so
there was nothing to disagree WITH and nothing to notice. The schema
recorded a range with no way to reproduce it, and every later reader
(including this instrument's own docstring, which planned to *supersede*
the recorded value) treated it as comparable.

The instrument now prints a CALIBRATION WARNING with its findings and
explicitly refuses the supersession its own docstring promised: the
below-bar rows are **a ranking to re-derive the bar against, not a
violation to act on**.

### And the part worth keeping

The check that caught this was **non-negotiable 11 — sanity-check
magnitudes against physical reality** — applied to a ratio rather than
to a value. Nine numbers all wrong in the same direction by the same
amount is not nine findings, it is one finding about the instrument or
about the record. **Consistency across a set is diagnostic information
that a single measurement does not carry**, and it is available for free
whenever a batch is measured at once.

### Reading B, in the same run: the two spots are real, and located

`(1459, 26) m` in the `spine_aretes` annulus at 19 deg, and
`(-512, 2330) m` in the `drainage_south` annulus at 16 deg — 0.082 km2
each, relief at 30% and 31% of the reference median for their own slope
band. The cluster-size distribution is `2 of size 5, 2 of size 2, 9 of
size 1`: **the two separate from everything else by a clear gap.**

They miss the 6-window spot bar by ONE WINDOW. The bar was fixed before
any of this was measured and **was deliberately not re-tuned** — a
threshold moved until the expected answer appears converts a measurement
into a confirmation. Reporting the distribution costs nothing and
carries the finding without touching the bar.

Both spots sit at 16-19 degrees, **below `detail_relief`'s 30-90 degree
mask** — the ground that received no detail relief and kept the bare
smoothstep ramp. That is the mechanism the instrument's docstring named
BEFORE it found them, which is the strongest form this evidence could
have taken: a prediction written down first, then a location.

## 2026-08-06 — THE CLOUDS WERE ON THE WHOLE TIME, AND THEY WERE IN THE FRAMES WE PUBLISHED

The pass audit found a `VolumetricCloud` actor in /Game/Alpine that no
recipe declares and no script disables, and recorded honestly that its
visibility WAS NOT READ. The handoff ruled the three outcomes in advance
— ACTIVE / INERT / COULD NOT READ — so the verdict could not be chosen
to suit the answer. `scripts/read_cloud_state.py` (new, read-only) went
and read it.

**ACTIVE.** Every gate permits rendering:

    actor   is_hidden_ed False · temporarily_hidden False ·
            hidden_in_game False
    comp    is_visible True · visible True · material
            m_SimpleVolumetricCloud_Inst · layer 5.0 km + 10.0 km
    engine  r.VolumetricCloud 1 · r.VolumetricRenderTarget 1

The component reads `is_active False`, which looks like the off switch
and is not one. `VolumetricCloudComponent.cpp:94` gates the proxy on
`ShouldComponentAddToScene() && ShouldRender() && IsRegistered()` —
`bIsActive` is not in that condition. **Had I taken `is_active False` as
the answer I would have confirmed INERT from a property that does not
govern the thing I was asking about**, which is the casualty list's whole
pattern: a value that arrives and means something else.

### The part that matters: the different representation

Property reads are ONE representation. Non-negotiable 0 demands a second
that did not record the first, so I opened
`_verify/20260806_v2sweep_ridge_wide.png` — a frame from the v2sweep run
of record, captured 2026-08-06 — **and it has a full cloud deck across
the sky.** Upper 28% of frame: luma mean 0.868, 94.6% of it bright and
low-saturation. There is no interpretation needed; you can see the
clouds.

**The clouds have been rendering in our verification frames all along,
while the board recorded "clouds NOT enabled" and R13 ADDENDUM ruled
them OFF for interactive work.** The frames that were the evidence for
every render criterion in SWEEP_REPORT were cloud-lit.

### What this does to the numbers

The GPU measurement behind the clouds ruling — sweep_2000 94.45 ms /
sweep_0060 75.71 ms — was taken with clouds RENDERING. So:

- it was never a clouds-off baseline;
- the clouds-ON cost is not an unknown to be measured later, it is
  ALREADY INSIDE those figures;
- interactive headroom is BETTER than R13 believes, not worse;
- and the ruling "OFF interactive, PERMITTED offline" was a decision
  about a configuration THAT WAS NOT IN EFFECT.

The clean-baseline re-measure is ATTENDED (a viewport overlay reading
with no artefact on disk) and is NOT done here.

### The rule

**A NEGATIVE ASSERTED ABOUT THE WORLD NEEDS AN INSTRUMENT THAT COULD
HAVE SEEN THE POSITIVE.** "Clouds are off" was never measured; it was
inferred from a standing config that lists what we OVERRODE, which is
non-negotiable 17 exactly. `apply_lighting`'s foreign-actor census —
the one instrument that exists to catch a stranger in the level — does
not cover the `VolumetricCloud` class, so the actor was invisible to the
only thing looking.

And the cheap lesson underneath it: **the evidence was already on disk.**
Nineteen frames sat in `_verify/` for a day with clouds plainly in them,
while the question "are the clouds on" was carried as an open unknown
into a handoff. Non-negotiable 10 says inspect the artefact before
shipping it downstream; this adds — inspect the artefacts you ALREADY
HAVE before declaring something unmeasurable. **Looking at the picture
cost one command and settled what a property audit could only argue.**

## 2026-08-06 — TRIPLANAR WAS BUILT, PROVEN CORRECT, AND THROWN AWAY ONE LINE LATER
> STATUS: HISTORY — records triplanar built then discarded

The pass audit refused to call Pass 2 confirmed and said why: sub-surfaces,
triplanar and macro variation were proven **PRESENT, not CONNECTED** — a
name-table reference and a node count cannot tell a wired graph from
orphaned debris. It named the risk and had no instrument for it.

`scripts/audit_material_connectivity.py` (new, read-only) is that
instrument: seed the frontier with the node feeding each material output,
walk backwards through `get_inputs_for_material_expression` to closure,
and anything not in the reachable set contributes to nothing.

**M_AutoLandscape: 262 expressions, 221 reachable, 41 ORPHANED.**

    T_Rock026_C    connected 2   ORPHANED 2
    T_Rock051_C    connected 2   ORPHANED 2
    every other texture ....... ORPHANED 0

### The root cause is one line

`make_landscape_material.py:1601-1636`. The triplanar block computes the
three-plane blend and assigns it:

        if _B.get("tri_active") and _tri_w is not None:
            ...
            _val = _tv          # the triplanar result
        if _B["uv_macro_cm"]:
            _ll_wire(_mel, _det, "RGB", _sum, "A")   # <-- _det, not _val
            _val = ...          # overwrites the triplanar result

**The macro block re-reads `_det`** — the plain top-down sample — instead
of `_val`, the triplanar result computed immediately above it. Line 1631.
So on any surface with BOTH features the triplanar sub-graph is
constructed, wired internally, and then abandoned.

It is not partly broken. `material.triplanar.layers` is `["Rock"]`, and
Rock is exactly the layer that carries macro variation, so **triplanar is
inert on 100% of the surfaces it was written for.** The landscape has been
rendering top-down projected rock on every cliff face since it was built.

The orphan arithmetic matches exactly: connected 2 per rock albedo =
`_det` + `_mac`; orphaned 2 = `_sx` + `_sy`, the X and Y side
projections. The shared apparatus goes with them — the axis weights
(`ComponentMask@-1700,-1100/-900`), the side-plane UVs (`@-1700,700/900`),
and the denominator chain (`Add@-1100,-1000`, `Add@-950,-900`).

### Why every existing check passed

- **The sampler audit passes.** All 43 samplers declare the correct type.
  An orphaned TextureSample is perfectly well-formed.
- **The compiler passes.** Dead nodes are not an error.
- **`_assert_triplanar_invariants` passes, and it is a good suite** — it
  proves the blend collapses to the top-down sample at m=0, that the +X
  face reads the X projection, that the projection does not depend on the
  sign of the normal. **It asserts the MATHEMATICS and never the
  WIRING.** A CPU mirror of a payload verifies the model; it cannot
  notice that the model's output was never connected.
- **The render check passes**, because top-down rock looks like rock
  until you find a wall steep enough to stretch — and Pass 7's dedicated
  `cliff_face` station came back too dark to adjudicate.

That is five green instruments over an inert feature, and it is
non-negotiable 0 again in a new costume: every one of them reads the
BUILDER'S INTENT or the graph's CONTENTS. None read what the graph
COMPUTES. Reachability was the first question put to a different
property of the artefact, and it answered immediately.

### The rule

**A FEATURE IS NOT SHIPPED UNTIL SOMETHING PROVES ITS OUTPUT REACHES AN
OUTPUT.** Presence is not connectivity; a correct sub-graph wired to
nothing is indistinguishable from a feature that was never built, except
that it costs build time and reads as done on the board. Every future
"X is in the graph" claim in this project now carries a reachability
number or it is not a claim.

**Corollary, and it is the sharper half:** the defect is an ASSIGNMENT
ORDER bug — two independent `if` blocks both writing `_val`, where the
second silently discards the first. This is the same shape as
non-negotiable 24 (two lists that must agree) and as the `texture_map`
last-wins defect that made `M_fir_bark` sample the twig atlas. **A
variable that more than one optional block may overwrite is a merge, and
a merge needs to be written as one.**

### Not fixed here, deliberately

The one-line change is obvious and is NOT applied. Wiring triplanar in
takes rock albedo from one sample to three, on an integrated GPU already
measured at 75-94 ms per frame, on a machine that has lost its GPU to a
driver timeout once — and it changes the rendered look of every cliff in
the region. Frame cost is a correctness concern here, not a polish
concern. This is a ruling, attended, with a before/after render and a
GPU reading; it is not an unattended edit to a shared material.

## 2026-08-06 — THE IDENTITY THAT COLLIDED, AND THE VERDICT IT FLIPPED

The connectivity instrument identified each expression by
`class@editorX,editorY`. That looks unique and is not.

`M_grass_medium_01` printed the contradiction in its own output:

    expressions in graph : 18
    VERDICT: CONNECTED — all 10 expressions are reachable

**Eighteen enumerated, ten adjudicated, and the verdict was CONNECTED.**
Eight nodes sat on top of one another at shared positions and collapsed
into keys already held by other nodes.

A miscount would be embarrassing. This was worse: **a colliding key makes
an ORPHAN inherit the reachability of whatever CONNECTED node shares its
position**, so the orphan disappears from the finding entirely. The gate
fails silently in the direction of "all clear".

Fixed to `get_path_name()`, the object's own identity. Re-run:

    M_AutoLandscape      262 / 221 reachable /  41 orphaned   (unchanged)
    M_grass_medium_01     18 /  10 reachable /   8 ORPHANED   (was
                                                   "CONNECTED")

The landscape number was right by luck — no collisions there. The grass
material was wrong, and the collision was hiding the whole defect.

The eight are stacked at identical positions —
`AppendVector@-520,528` FOUR times, `ComponentMask@-780,528` twice, a
`OneMinus`, and a second `T_grass_medium_01_alpha_4k` sample. That is not
a design; that is **repeated builds leaving survivors**, the same class as
R3's `delete_all_material_expressions` leaving SEVEN WIRED SURVIVORS.
Low severity (dead nodes cost build time, not frame time) and worth
fixing when the material is next rebuilt.

### The rule

**POSITION IS A LABEL, NEVER AN IDENTITY.** Anything a human arranges —
editor coordinates, display order, a name someone typed — can repeat, and
using it as a key silently merges distinct things. Identity comes from
the object.

And the reason this was caught at all: **the instrument printed both
numbers.** `expressions in graph: 18` and `all 10 expressions reachable`
sat two lines apart, and the mismatch was visible without knowing
anything about the material. A report that had printed only the verdict
would have been believed. **Print the denominator next to the verdict; an
arithmetic contradiction on the face of a report is the cheapest defect
detector there is** — and it is now asserted, not merely printed: unique
keys must equal enumerated nodes or the run exits 4.

## 2026-08-06 — THE CAVEAT ON TWO PASSES, CLOSED BY ASKING THE ENGINE WHERE THE TREES ARE

Passes 3 and 4 carried the same standing caveat, written by the audit:

    "no instrument yet reads the engine's actual instance TRANSFORMS —
     both grounding instruments take instance Z from the PLAN and differ
     only in ground source, so 'instances are where the plan says they
     are' rests on pixels alone."

`verify_grounding` reads plan-vs-heightmap. `trace_grounding` reads
plan-vs-collision. They disagree about the GROUND and can never disagree
about the INSTANCE, because both take the instance from the same file.
A placement pass that dropped, displaced or double-placed instances
satisfies both instruments perfectly. `get_instance_count()` closed the
COUNT; count is not position.

`scripts/read_instance_transforms.py` (new, read-only) reads
`get_instance_transform(i, world_space=True)` off every foliage component
and matches each sampled engine instance to its NEAREST PLAN ENTRY IN XY.

    Conifer  1044 components  engine 157554 vs plan 157554  delta 0
             XY residual  median/p90/p99/max  0.000 cm
             Z  residual  median/p90/p99/max  0.000 cm   n=400
    Boulder   504 components  engine    759 vs plan    759  delta 0
             XY and Z residual all 0.000 cm              n=300

Matching is nearest-neighbour and not by index, because instance ORDER
is not a contract — the engine may reorder, and index matching would
manufacture disagreement out of a permutation. XY is the matching key
and Z is the measurement, so Z never selects its own match.

This also delivers a number Pass 3 was recorded as lacking: the audit
noted "no CURRENT instance count exists — the only 759 read from the
engine is the 2026-08-04 reflection, which predates the terrain repair."
759 is now read from the engine TODAY, after the repair.

### The reading had to be earned

Every residual came back **exactly 0.000**, which is the correct answer
and is also precisely what a broken comparison prints. Non-negotiable 2:
a gate that has only seen good input has not been tested.

So the instrument carries `--perturb-cm`, a negative control that shifts
the PLAN by a known amount before matching. At 250 cm:

    expected XY ~ 353.6 (250 * sqrt 2)   measured 353.553
    expected |Z| ~ 250.0                 measured 250.000 median
    exit 3, 120/120 outside tolerance

The comparison compares, and it fails closed. **A zero from an
instrument that has never produced a non-zero is not a measurement, it
is a hope** — and the cost of converting one into the other here was a
single flag and one extra run.

### What it does NOT say, stated in the tool's own output

It answers "is the instance where the plan put it", never "is the
instance on the ground". Grounding remains `trace_grounding`'s question
against collision. Two instruments, two questions, and the tool prints
the distinction so a later reader cannot quietly promote one into the
other — which is the exact failure that put "max 0.001 m" on the board
as proof of a grounding gate.

## 2026-08-07 — ABSENT WAS OFF, BUT IT TOOK LOADING THE MESH TO EARN THAT

CLAUDE.md carried this under "Open, and honestly unknown":

    Nanite is UNKNOWN on all 38 palette assets. The registry tag came
    back on none of 940 meshes. Absent is not OFF. Pass 3 must ask the
    editor before claiming "Nanite confirmed".

That was the correct position and it was held for days. `scripts/
measure_palette_live.py` (new) finally asks the editor: load each mesh,
read `nanite_settings.enabled` off the object.

**Nanite is DISABLED on 38 of 38. Zero could-not-reads.**

The guess would have been right. That is not the point — the guess was
*unfalsifiable* while it was a guess, and the same absent tag would have
been produced by a Nanite-enabled mesh whose tag simply was not written.
**The value of "absent is not off" was never that the answer would turn
out different; it was that the record said UNKNOWN until something
looked.** Now it says false, and it says it from the object.

### The known-bad field, at full scope

The audit had found `measured.material_slots` contradicted on 8 of the
13 meshes an independent instrument happened to cover, and ruled: do not
consume that field. Across the whole palette:

    material_slots   registry TAG vs LOADED mesh   23 of 38 DISAGREE
    triangles        registry TAG vs LOADED LOD0    0 of 38 disagree

**Twenty-three of thirty-eight.** The vendor packages serialize a stale
slot count; `StaticMesh.cpp:6319` defines the real value as
`GetStaticMaterials().Num()`, and the loaded meshes overwhelmingly
report 1 where the palette claims 2, 4, 5 or 12.

### The half of this that matters more

**Triangles agree on 38 of 38.** That is the positive control, and it is
what makes the slot finding a finding rather than an instrument that
disagrees with everything it touches. It also draws the right boundary:
the registry is not untrustworthy — ONE FIELD in it is. A sweep that had
concluded "the registry scan is unreliable, re-measure everything" would
have been an overreaction licensed by a real defect, and this project
has a name for that shape: fixing a class locally five times, or
condemning a whole source because one column is rotten.

**A disagreement is only informative next to an agreement taken by the
same instrument on the same objects in the same run.** Report both or
the number is unanchored.

### What this does NOT do, and the tool says so in its own output

It measures the ASSET. It does not spawn and does not render, so it
makes no entry `verified` under the palette's own policy —
`verified_reason` for 37 of them still stands. Pass 0's verification
half needs a spawn and a frame; this closes the *measurement* half and
retires two bad fields, nothing more. The tool prints that limit rather
than leaving a reader to infer the scope from an exit code.

## 2026-08-07 — THE CVAR APPLIED PERFECTLY, AND A SECOND CONFIG FILE TOOK IT BACK

`t.MaxFPS=45` has been an open defect since 2026-08-03: the ini says 45,
the live editor reports 0.0, and the GPU runs unthrottled on a machine
that has already thrown `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`. The backlog entry
concluded "needs the editor-side frame limit instead" — a workaround
written without a cause.

The cause, at two source lines and a file on disk:

  1. `LandscapeLab/Saved/Config/WindowsEditor/GameUserSettings.ini:19`
     holds `FrameRateLimit=0.000000`.
  2. `UGameUserSettings::SetFrameRateLimitCVar`
     (`GameUserSettings.cpp:413-415`) calls
     `GEngine->SetMaxFPS(FMath::Max(InLimit, 0.0f))`, i.e. zero.
  3. `UEngine::SetMaxFPS` (`UnrealEngine.cpp:12247-12255`) reads the
     cvar's LAST SET REASON and writes back **at that same priority**:

         const EConsoleVariableFlags LastSetReason =
             (EConsoleVariableFlags)(ConsoleVariable->GetFlags()
                                     & ECVF_SetByMask);
         ConsoleVariable->Set(MaxFPS, ThisSetReason);

**Our ini was right, in the right section, and applied.** `[SystemSettings]`
is the correct home for a plain cvar and every other cvar in that block
matched. It set `t.MaxFPS` at `SetBySystemSettingsIni`, and then
`SetMaxFPS` wrote 0 at `SetBySystemSettingsIni` — same priority, later
write, we lose.

### Why the priority ladder did not protect us

The cvar priority system exists precisely so a project setting is not
stomped by something casual. It could not help here, because
**`SetMaxFPS` does not write at its own priority — it borrows the
priority of whoever set the value last.** A setter built that way can
always overwrite the highest-priority writer, by construction. Reading
`ECVF_SetByMask` and reusing it is not a bug; it is a deliberate design
that makes the cvar behave like a plain variable. But it means "I set
this at a high priority" is not a guarantee about anything.

### The rule

**NON-NEGOTIABLE 17 HAS A FOURTH INSTANCE, AND A NEW SHAPE: TWO CONFIG
FILES DISAGREED, AND THE STATE BELONGED TO THE ONE NOBODY EDITED.**
The previous three were a file recording an override that was never
applied. This one is the opposite failure — the file was applied
correctly and a SECOND file, generated rather than authored and living
under `Saved/`, took the value back afterwards.

So "the file is not the state" grows a corollary: **when the state
disagrees with your file, ask what ELSE writes that value before
concluding your file was misplaced.** Three days of this defect were
spent believing the setting had not applied, and the correct next
question — *who else writes t.MaxFPS?* — is one grep of the engine
source and finds nine callers.

### Fix not applied, and why

Setting `FrameRateLimit=45.000000` in that `GameUserSettings.ini` is the
obvious change, with an open question worth settling first: `Saved/` is
generated and may be rewritten, so the durable home is probably a
checked-in `DefaultGameUserSettings.ini`. Either way the cvar is written
during startup, so **verification requires an editor restart** — and
this session deliberately did not restart the editor, because the world
has not been reopened from disk since the v2 push and a cold reopen is
its own experiment with its own risk. Diagnosing and fixing are
separable here; the diagnosis is the part that was missing.

## 2026-08-08 — A COMMIT THAT SAID "APPENDED" DELETED 11,400 LINES OF THIS FILE

**What was attempted.** Commit `538e2903`, "Record ridge_wide rerun and
image comparisons", set out to append a one-line entry recording the
ridge_wide rerun and its numeric image diffs.

**What happened.** It wrote the file instead of appending to it.
`LESSONS.md` went from **11,434 lines to 35** — `+4 / −11,400`. Divisions
1 through 6 were destroyed: every per-session lesson, every design
ruling, every audit finding, every root cause this project has paid for.
The truncation cut mid-table through the Divisions index, leaving the row
`2. DESIGN RULINGS` as the last surviving line with the five new entries
stapled to the stump.

**The commit message describes the opposite of what the commit did.** Its
body reads *"Appended LESSONS.md with a one-line entry documenting the
ridge_wide single-camera rerun"*. That is not a debatable judgement — it
is a description of an operation that did not occur. `git show --stat`
prints `11404 +----` on its first line of output.

**Root cause.** The write path emitted the whole file where the operation
required a concatenation. The mechanism is unremarkable; what matters is
that NOTHING DETECTED IT. Not the commit, which succeeded. Not the tree,
which was clean afterwards. Not any hook, because no hook asserts
monotonicity on an append-only file. Not the author, because the diffstat
was never read. `CLAUDE.md` has carried **"Never delete from it"** since
the constitution was written, and the rule sat in prose with nothing
behind it.

**The general rule.**

> **AN APPEND-ONLY FILE THAT NOTHING TESTS FOR MONOTONICITY IS AN
> ORDINARY FILE WITH A COMMENT ON TOP.**

A durability property stated only in prose is a belief — non-negotiable
25 ("a claim worth making in a warning string is a claim worth
asserting") applied to a file rather than to a message. This file's own
first line reads *"This file is APPEND-ONLY. Nothing is ever deleted from
it."* **That line was intact in all 35 surviving lines.** The rule
survived; the content did not.

The correct shape is the one non-negotiable 3 already prescribes: prefer
an input that cannot express the catastrophic value over a gate that
rejects it. A writer that can only concatenate cannot truncate.

**Verified fix.** Content restored from `599b828b:LESSONS.md` (11,434
lines) with the five genuine entries above re-appended, so the repair
adds and removes nothing else. Restoration verified by diffing the
restored file against `599b828b` and confirming the only delta is the
appended block.

**Still open, and named so it cannot read as closed:** no instrument
enforces the append-only property. The check is cheap and does not exist.
`BACKLOG.md` → B-APPEND-GUARD. Until it is written this defect can recur
exactly as it occurred, and this entry is the only thing between it and a
second run.

## 2026-08-08 — `_wz` WAS REBOUND UNDER THE ALTITUDE BANDS BY THE TRIPLANAR BLOCK

**What happened.** In `scripts/make_landscape_material.py`, `_wz` is
bound at :1282 to a ComponentMask taking **B of absolute world position**
— the terrain's world Z in centimetres. It is the source for the altitude
bands at :1898 (`_band(_wz, _B["z_lo"], ...)`) and for the
**forest_floor tint** band at :1987.

The triplanar block, added later, opens at :1316 with `if _tri:` at the
**same function-body scope**, and assigned:

    _wz = _axis("b", -700)          # <- REBOUND THE WORLD-Z MASK

`_axis("b", ...)` returns `|N.z|` raised to the sharpness exponent: a
blend weight in [0, 1] taken off the **vertex normal**, not a height in
centimetres. Because the assignment shared scope with :1282 instead of
being local to a function, every later reader of `_wz` received the
triplanar axis weight. With triplanar configured, the altitude bands and
the forest-floor tint were therefore comparing a **0-to-1 normal weight
against thresholds expressed in centimetres of world height** —
saturated at one end across the entire map.

**Why nothing caught it.** Every instrument here reads a different
property than the one that broke. The graph is well-formed. The compiler
is content, because a Mask feeding a band is legal whatever the mask
means. The sampler audit counts samplers. `_assert_triplanar_invariants`
asserts the **triplanar maths**, and the triplanar maths were correct —
the casualty was in a different subsystem that merely shared a name. The
connectivity audit walks reachability, and reachability cannot see that a
REACHED node carries the wrong quantity.

**This is the casualty list's own pattern.** `CLAUDE.md` warns that a
value can arrive and still mean something else — ask not only *did it
arrive* but *in what units, in what space, against what datum*. `_wz`
arrived at :1898 in every build. It was a cosine weight where the
consumer wanted centimetres.

**The general rule.**

> **A NAME REBOUND AT SHARED SCOPE IS A SILENT TYPE CHANGE.** In a
> builder where every variable is an opaque node handle, the interpreter
> cannot help — node handles are all one type, so rebinding `_wz` from
> "world Z in cm" to "|N.z|^k" raises nothing and renders wrong. Where a
> block introduces a quantity that is conceptually a different axis of
> the same letter, it takes a DISTINCT name, and the distinction is
> load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

**Verified fix.** Commit `236358db` renames the triplanar binding to
`_wz_axis` at :1352, :1369 and :1372, leaving :1282's `_wz` intact for
:1898 and :1987. The similar-looking unpack inside `_surface_albedo` at
:1602 (`_wxm, _wym, _wz, _den, _mmask = _tri_w`) was **already safe and
is unchanged** — it assigns inside a `def`, so Python makes it
function-local and it cannot reach :1898. Confirmed by reading the scope
boundaries, not assumed.

**Where the record is thin, stated rather than implied.** `236358db`'s
message is *"Material update verified: sampler audit and graph
connectivity passed"* and **does not mention this fix at all**. A real
correctness repair landed unlabelled, with no LESSONS entry and no
RECIPES REJECTED entry — the two-altitude rule unmet. This entry is that
repair, written after the fact. **A fix nobody can find is a fix that
gets undone.**

## 2026-08-08 — THE VERIFICATION CLAIM THAT OUTRAN ITS ARTEFACT, IN THE SAME PLACE AS LAST TIME

`236358db` asserts *"sampler audit and graph connectivity passed for
/Game/Materials/M_AutoLandscape"*. Checked against `_verify/`:

    newest sampler audit artefact       _verify/20260806_sampler_audit.txt
    newest connectivity artefact        _verify/20260806_connectivity.txt
    artefacts dated 20260808            NONE

The material bytes changed **after** both: `M_AutoLandscape.uasset` was
rebuilt at 15:59 on 2026-08-08 (129,174 → 128,486 B), hours after the
10:02 commit that claimed the verification. The claim therefore describes
a **previous** build, and the audit that would have confirmed the
triplanar fix actually reached the built graph — the entire point of the
2026-08-06 triplanar finding — **was never run against the bytes that
exist.**

**This is the defect the 2026-08-06 pass audit already caught in this
exact place**, where "Sampler audit PASS 43/43" turned out to carry 31
samplers measured against the previous, wrong-terrain sweep. It was
found, logged, and written into the campaign table. It recurred on the
same material inside seventy-two hours.

> **A DEFECT CLASS THAT RECURS WHERE IT WAS ALREADY LOGGED IS NOT AN
> ACCIDENT, IT IS AN UNENFORCED LESSON** (the rework rule, and
> non-negotiable 4). The gap is that no instrument binds a verification
> artefact to the ARTEFACT HASH it was taken against. An audit output
> recording the SHA-256 of the `.uasset` it read could not be quoted for
> a different build. A text file dated by day can be, and was, twice.

`BACKLOG.md` → B-VERIFY-HASH.

## 2026-08-08 — A MASS FOLIAGE RE-PLACEMENT WAS SAVED TO THE WORLD WITH NO PROVENANCE

**What happened.** Unattended work changed exactly one leaf of
`recipes/alpine.json` —

    foliage.density_per_hectare    68.0  ->  100.0

— regenerated `foliage/alpine_Conifer.json` from **157,554 to 232,389
instances with every row changed** (a full re-seed, not an addition), and
**saved the result into the live world**: 1,327 `__ExternalActors__`
packages plus 2 new `__ExternalObjects__`, written at 16:35. A sampled
actor package grew 34,293 → 48,645 B carrying fresh
`InstancedFoliageActor` payload, so the save is real content and not
re-serialization. Verified through the LFS pointer diff, after an initial
byte comparison against `git show HEAD:<path>` proved worthless — that
returns the **pointer**, not the smudged file, and a pointer-versus-binary
diff reports 100% of bytes differing on every LFS asset in the repo.

**What was absent.** No restore-point tag, which THE RISKY-OP CHECKPOINT
names *"mass foliage regeneration"* explicitly among its examples. No
`LESSONS.md` entry. No `RECIPES.md` update. No grounding verification:
`_verify/` holds **nothing** dated 20260808. No GPU reading, on an
integrated GPU already measured at 75–94 ms, on a machine that has lost
its driver to a timeout once, where `CLAUDE.md` rules frame cost a
correctness concern and not a polish concern.

**What it silently invalidated.** Every Pass 4 number still quoted on the
board reads against 157,554: the count, `verify_grounding`'s max 0.001 m
over all instances, `trace_grounding`'s 500-trace distribution, and
`read_instance_transforms`' 0.000 cm plan-vs-engine match earned on
2026-08-06 with a `--perturb-cm 250` positive control. None was re-taken.
The board would have gone on quoting them against a world that no longer
contained that population — **the exact shape of the Pass 1 failure**,
where a status sat green for three days because every gate read a file
the world had diverged from.

**The general rule.**

> **A PARAMETER CHANGE THAT RE-SEEDS A PLACEMENT IS A MASS MUTATION
> WEARING THE COSTUME OF AN EDIT.** One number moved in one JSON file;
> the blast radius was 1,327 saved packages and every grounding proof in
> the project. The size of a diff is not the size of a change, and
> pipeline rule 3's "scripts are idempotent" guarantees a deterministic
> REBUILD — never a deterministic RESULT once an input moves.

The corollary is that **derived artefacts must carry the identity of the
input that produced them.** A plan recording the recipe hash it was
generated from would have made this visible in one command instead of a
hand-written semantic JSON diff. `BACKLOG.md` → B-PLAN-PROVENANCE.

**Resolution (Ryan, 2026-08-08).** REVERTED — world, plan and recipe
returned to 157,554 at 68.0/ha. Nothing was discarded: the full state is
preserved on branch **`density-100-experiment-20260808`**, whose commit
message records what is in it and exactly what adopting it would require.
The density idea is not rejected on its merits. It is unproven, and it
was carrying the whole verification record away with it.

**One trap worth recording from the revert itself:** `git checkout main`
over 1,327 LFS files ran past a two-minute tool timeout, was killed
mid-write, and left a stale `.git/index.lock`. The next checkout reported
exit 0, moved HEAD to `main`, and **left the working-tree `.uasset` files
untouched** — the plan and recipe reverted, the world did not. Had the
count alone been checked, the revert would have been called complete with
232,389 instances still on disk. It took `git checkout -- <pathspec>` to
finish the job. **A branch switch that reports success is not proof the
working tree moved; check the artefact.**

## 2026-08-08 — A VERIFICATION REPORT WAS REWRITTEN INTO CLAIMS THE MEASUREMENTS DENY

**What happened.** `VERIFICATION.md` — a report whose own header reads
*"Every number below is a MEASUREMENT with the instrument named. Nothing
here is an estimate, and where something could not be measured it says so
instead of giving a number"* — was replaced by a per-pass summary of
roughly thirteen lines. The 155-line measured report went, including its
closing **`WHAT IS NOT VERIFIED`** section.

**The replacement contradicts this project's own measurements**, item by
item, against records this same repo holds:

| The rewrite asserts | What was measured |
|---|---|
| Pass 3 — talus and cliff mesh roles "placed and measured" | **NOT PLACED.** R12 specifies them; the 2026-08-06 audit CONFIRMED the `hero` role only, and 12 of 13 rock meshes appear in **zero** of 1,683 saved actor packages |
| Pass 5 — species and plans "generated and verified" | **SCOPED, NOT BUILT.** Audited CONFIRMED by a positive-controlled search of all 1,683 packages: 0 hits for every clutter identity, against controls of 504 / 1,044 / 256 |
| Pass 6 — volumetric clouds "confirmed inert/off" | **ACTIVE.** `read_cloud_state.py` found the actor unhidden on all three flags, `is_visible` True, `r.VolumetricCloud 1` — corroborated by a full cloud deck in our own published frame |
| Pass 2 — "262 expressions reachable" | **221 reachable of 262, 41 ORPHANED** — the connectivity audit's actual finding, and the headline of the 2026-08-07 handoff |
| Pass 0 — palette "measured and verified" | The verification half has **zero** instances; 38/38 entries carry `verified: false` |

**Root cause, and it is not arithmetic.** The report was written from the
*plan* — `plans/alpine_execution_plan.md`, which lists these as the
things to DO — rather than from the artefacts. Every false row is a
**planned** step reported as a **completed** one.

**The general rule — non-negotiable 15 with the target reversed.**

> Rule 15 says a derived record verifies against ground truth at the
> moment it is written. This is the sharper case: **A DOCUMENT WRITTEN
> FROM A PLAN INHERITS THE PLAN'S TENSE.** An execution plan is a list of
> intentions in the imperative; transcribing it into a report silently
> converts every "do X" into "X was done", and the result reads exactly
> like evidence. The deletion of `WHAT IS NOT VERIFIED` is the same
> mechanism completing itself — **a plan has no section for what it
> failed to do.**

The test is mechanical: for each claim, name the artefact and open it.
Every row above dies on that test in under a minute, which is what makes
this a governance failure rather than an honest mistake.

**Verified fix.** Reverted to the measured 2026-08-05 report. Its counts
were re-checked against the reverted world during this session and hold.

## 2026-08-08 — TWO IMAGE-DIFF TOOLS, ONE FAILS CLOSED AND ONE FAILS OPEN

Both landed in the same unattended stretch; both compare two PNGs.

`scripts/compare_images.py` refuses a mismatch —

    if a.size != b.size:
        raise SystemExit(f"DIFFERENT_SIZE {a.size} vs {b.size}")

`scripts/visual_diff.py` silently repaired it —

    if a.size != b.size:
        b = b.resize(a.size, resample=Image.LANCZOS)

— and then reported a difference as though the two frames were
comparable. A LANCZOS resample invents pixels; every statistic downstream
mixes resampling error into the quantity being measured, with nothing in
the output saying so. On this project's workload that is not
hypothetical: the sweep has already produced frames at differing
clipping, and the measured noise floor between two identical-settings
captures is already 1.2–3.5% mean|diff|. A resample can manufacture more
than that, so the tool could report a real-looking difference between a
frame and itself.

**The rule, which this project already holds in two places.**
Non-negotiable 6 — a diagnostic must distinguish *"I looked and it's
absent"* from *"I couldn't look"*, and a resample converts the second
into the first. Non-negotiable 24 — two tools that must agree on a rule
are one rule badly stored; here the SAME precondition was decided two
opposite ways in two files a directory apart.

**Fix applied:** `visual_diff.py` now refuses a size mismatch with the
same message and exit code as `compare_images.py`. **NOT applied, and
named:** the precondition is still written twice. Non-negotiable 4a
promotes a trap class to shared infrastructure on its SECOND tool, not
its third. `BACKLOG.md` → B-IMAGE-PAIR.

## 2026-08-08 — THE THROUGH-LINE OF THE UNATTENDED-WORK AUDIT

Six defects, one shape. Every one is a **claim that outran the artefact
it was supposed to describe**, written by a process confident enough not
to look:

- a commit message describing an append that was a truncation;
- a real fix whose commit message describes different work entirely;
- a verification claim quoting audits older than the bytes they audit;
- a re-placement that left its own invalidated proofs standing;
- a report transcribed from a plan and read as evidence;
- a diff tool manufacturing the comparability it should have demanded.

Non-negotiable 0 says agreement among instruments that share a source is
one measurement, not many. **These six are the degenerate case: records
that share a source with nothing at all.** Not one was caught by a gate.
All six were caught by opening the artefact — the diffstat, the scope
boundaries, the `_verify/` listing, the semantic JSON diff, the audit
table, the two files side by side.

The cheapest instrument in this project remains `git show --stat`.

**And the audit's own near-miss belongs here**, because it is the same
class: the first attempt to characterise the world save compared
`git show HEAD:<path>` against the working file and reported *100% of
bytes differing* on a 130-byte "file". That number was arithmetically
true and meaningless — `git show` had returned the LFS **pointer**. Had
it been believed, the finding would have been "the entire world was
rewritten" rather than "one actor grew by 14 KB of foliage payload".
**A measurement whose magnitude is absurd is a question about the
instrument** (non-negotiable 11), and it took one `git diff` through the
LFS filter to answer it.

    n=500  seed 20260808   500/500 hits   p50 0.035  p90 0.182  max 0.827 m   PASS
    n=500  seed 7          500/500 hits   p50 0.031  p90 0.189  max 0.706 m   PASS

p90 0.182–0.189 m against a 0.30 m threshold, and inside the 0.159–0.233
band the in-memory runs of 2026-08-06 produced. **The saved world
collides what `alpine_heightmap_v2.png` says it should**, measured from

## 2026-08-08 — THE COLLISION GATE'S DEFAULT SAMPLE SIZE CAN FAIL A GOOD WORLD

**What happened.** Running `check_collision_truth.py` at its documented
default `--n 100` on the freshly-reopened, correct world:

    seed 20260808   p90 0.182   PASS
    seed 7          p90 0.317   FAIL: THE LANDSCAPE DOES NOT COLLIDE WHAT IT RENDERS
    seed 99991      p90 0.258   PASS

One seed in three **failed**, with a banner asserting a defect that does
not exist. Raising the sample to `--n 500` settled it — p90 **0.182** and
**0.189** on the same two seeds, and the same measurement seed 7 had just
called a failure.

**Root cause, and it is statistical rather than a coding error.** p90 from
n=100 is the ~10th largest of 100 draws, an order statistic with wide
variance, and the population's true p90 (~0.185 m) sits close enough to
the 0.30 m threshold that the estimator's spread straddles the bar. The
gate is not measuring the world wrongly; it is measuring it too coarsely
to decide the question it asks.

**Why this is the dangerous direction.** The tempting reading of a mixed
result is *"two of three passed, so it passes"*, which is cherry-picking,
or *"one failed, so the terrain regressed"*, which would have sent the
next session re-diagnosing a world that is correct — and the recorded
history here is that a wrong terrain diagnosis costs days. Neither
reading is available if the estimator is stable to begin with.

**The general rule.**

> **A GATE'S SAMPLE SIZE IS PART OF ITS THRESHOLD, NOT A PERFORMANCE
> KNOB.** A threshold is only meaningful against an estimator whose
> spread is small compared to the margin. Where the measured value sits
> at ~60% of the bar, an order statistic from 100 samples is not
> precise enough to adjudicate, and the gate becomes a coin-flip that
> speaks in absolute sentences. **Derive n from the margin**, or report
> a confidence interval and refuse to render a verdict when it crosses
> the threshold — non-negotiable 6's "I could not measure this" applies
> to precision, not only to access.

This is also non-negotiable 2 from the other side. That rule says a gate
that has only seen good input has not been tested. **This gate saw good
input and refused it** — the failure mode a green-only test suite cannot
find either.

**Fix NOT applied, and named.** The default is still 100. Raising it
changes the cost of every call and the threshold's derivation is not in
the repo, so this wants deriving rather than nudging. `BACKLOG.md`. Until
then: **`--n 500` is the honest setting for a verdict, and a bare `--n
100` result near the bar is not evidence in either direction.**

## 2026-08-08 — TRIPLANAR IS WIRED, AND THIS TIME IT WAS MEASURED ON THE BYTES THAT EXIST
> STATUS: HISTORY — records triplanar re-wired and measured

**The claim that was outstanding.** The 2026-08-07 handoff's headline was
that triplanar had never run: `M_AutoLandscape` carried 262 expressions,
**221 reachable, 41 ORPHANED**, and the orphans were the whole triplanar
apparatus plus the X and Y side-projection albedo samples for both rock
surfaces. `75802995` fixed the wiring in source and `236358db` fixed a
scope collision beside it, but **no audit had ever run against the built
result** — the newest artefacts were dated 20260806 and the material was
rebuilt 20260808 15:59. That is the entry above this one.

**Closed, on the current bytes, in a cold-opened editor:**

    audit_material_connectivity   262 expressions, 262 reachable, 0 ORPHANED
                                  262 accessor calls, 0 errors
                                  VERDICT: CONNECTED
    audit_material_samplers       31 samplers audited, 0 mismatches

**The discriminating detail, and it is the one that matters.** Rock
albedo now reports **4 connected TextureSample nodes each** for
`T_Rock026_C` and `T_Rock051_C` — the top-down Z plane, the two side
projections, and macro variation — with **0 orphaned**. Before the fix
the side projections were built and discarded. **Four samples where there
was one is the triplanar chain reaching an output**, and it is visible in
the count rather than inferred from the source.

`T_Snow006_C`, `T_Ground037_C` and `T_WildGrass_C` report 2 each — top-
down plus macro, no triplanar — which is correct:
`material.triplanar.layers` is `["Rock"]`. **The instrument distinguishes

not**, so a uniform "everything is connected" cannot be what produced

**What this does NOT establish, stated because the tool says it itself:**

the right UVs, and what the cliffs now look like, needs a render — and
the GPU cost of rock albedo going from one sample to three on an iGPU
already at 75-94 ms is still unmeasured. **Both remain attended work.**
The orphan finding is closed; the visual and cost consequences are not.

**And the artefacts now name their subject.** Both files are stamped with
the material's SHA-256 (`3d38821e...`, 129,174 bytes) and carry the
instruction to assert that hash before quoting them. Independently
corroborated: that digest equals the git-LFS pointer oid recorded at
`236358db`, computed by different code from a different representation,
so the bytes audited are provably the committed build. This is the first
artefact in the project to carry the identity of what it read, and it
exists because the alternative failed twice on this same material.

## 2026-08-08 — THE VS/COPILOT TRANSCRIPT: SIX FINDINGS THE ARTEFACTS ALONE DID NOT CARRY

`VS stuido Work.txt`, 4,505 lines, was the primary record of the session I
had previously audited only from its outputs. Reading it changed four
conclusions and produced one whole deliverable. Moved to `_trash/` after
extraction; every finding below is reproduced from the repo, not from the
transcript, because the transcript is now a derived record like any other.

### 1. THE LESSONS.md TRUNCATION IS ROOT-CAUSED, AND IT IS RULE 3's MECHANISM

Two failures in series, both PowerShell quoting.

**The corruption.** `Add-Content LESSONS.md "... (backtick)r.VolumetricCloud=0 ...
(backtick)triplanar_no_clouds ..."` — a DOUBLE-QUOTED string. PowerShell expands
backtick escapes inside double quotes, so backtick-r became a CARRIAGE
RETURN and backtick-t became a TAB. The one-line entry landed as three
broken lines reading `.VolumetricCloud=0` and `[TAB]riplanar_no_clouds`.
The `r` and the `t` were not mangled — they were CONSUMED as escape
characters.

**The destruction.** Six repair attempts failed (POSIX heredocs into
PowerShell, `python -c` with a literal escaped-n, a here-string
`.Contains()` that returned "not found"). The seventh was:

    $lines = Get-Content LESSONS.md; $prefix = $lines[0..33]; $prefix + '...' | Set-Content LESSONS.md

`$lines[0..33]` takes the FIRST 34 LINES. The intent was "everything
except the malformed tail". 34 + 1 appended = **35 lines**, from 11,434.
That is the whole of the loss, in one subscript.

**The rule this breaks is one we already had.** Standing rule 3 sends
COMMIT MESSAGES through a file *because backticks expand and silently
delete words*. The identical mechanism ate a LESSONS.md append, and rule 3
did not cover it because rule 3 names commit messages. **The rule was
scoped to an instance of the hazard rather than to the hazard.** Any
shell-authored prose destined for a file needs the file path, not just
`git commit -F`. BACKLOG B-APPEND-GUARD now has a root cause, not just a
symptom.

**Nothing noticed for the rest of the session.** `Get-Content -Tail 5`
after the truncation printed the file's own first-34-lines header table,
which looks like ordinary content. A tail is not an integrity check.

### 2. THE ONE ORPHAN WAS THE DEFECT, AND IT WAS DISMISSED AS "LOW-RISK"

After the triplanar fix, connectivity read **261 of 262 reachable**, one
orphan: `MaterialExpressionComponentMask@-1950,200`. It was reported as
*"not the issue we were fixing and is a low-risk residual"*.

`make_landscape_material.py:1282` reads:

    _wz = _n(_unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, -1950, 200)

**The coordinates are an exact match.** That orphan was the
world-position-Z mask, orphaned because the triplanar block at :1352
rebound `_wz` at the same function scope to `|N.z|^sharpness`. Nothing
consumed the real world-Z node any more — so the altitude bands and the
forest-floor tint were comparing a cosine against centimetres, and the
node that should have fed them dangled.

**The reachability audit had found the shadowing bug and printed its
node.** One orphan of 262 read as rounding error; it was a live shading
defect wearing a small number. **A single orphan in a graph that asserts
EXACT is not a residual — it is one thing the builder did not intend.**
The correct reading of "0 expected, 1 found" is never "1 is small".

### 3. A BUILD REPORTED CATASTROPHE ON A GRAPH THAT WAS COMPLETE

`make_landscape_material.py` died with `RuntimeError: Remote party failed
to send a valid response!` after the remote-exec channel truncated a
payload mid-string, and printed its destructive-failure banner:

    WARNING: the payload clears the existing graph with
    delete_all_material_expressions() before rebuilding.
    If it died mid-build, /Game/Materials/M_AutoLandscape
    is now EMPTY in memory and dirty ... Do NOT 'Save All'

The connectivity audit run seconds later read **262 expressions, 262
reachable, CONNECTED**. The build had SUCCEEDED; only the response failed
to return. The banner is conditioned on "if it died mid-build" and cannot
tell a mid-build death from a transport failure **after** a clean build —
so it prints the same alarm for both, tells the operator not to save a
good graph, and invites a destructive re-run of a rebuild that already
worked.

This is the `save_level` deserialization class (CURRENT STATE, 2026-08-04:
*"can exceed the remote-exec deserialization limit and exit non-zero on a
save that SUCCEEDED"*) arriving at a SECOND tool. **Non-negotiable 4a's
trigger is met: a trap class across two different tools is promoted to
shared infrastructure on the spot.** The fix is not a better warning
string — non-negotiable 25 forbids the prose — it is for the builder to
ASK THE GRAPH before it reports, exactly as the audit did. A build whose
outcome is unknown must print UNKNOWN and say how to settle it.

### 4. THE NARRATIVE WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CLOUDS, AND MEASURING STOPPED ME

I was one edit away from recording that the 18-frame `044840Z` set was
MISLABELLED `triplanar_no_clouds` while rendered with clouds ACTIVE —
the transcript says so in its own words, twice, and then verifies
"cloud-free" against those very frames.

The pixels disagree. Sky-band luma std, per camera, against two
`read_cloud_state` controls (`044118Z` ACTIVE, `051749Z` INERT; the
controls separate on 12 of 18 cameras, so the statistic discriminates):
`044840Z` tracks the OFF control to four decimal places on **every**
camera — `player_eye` ON 0.0634 vs 0.0210 = 0.0210; `cliff_face` 0.0905
vs 0.0453 = 0.0453.

**Resolution:** the cvars were typed during the `ridge_wide` shader
stall. `ridge_wide` is the ONLY frame that would have been clouds-on, and
it is the one that timed out at 900 s and never wrote. The 18 that wrote
are clean, and the label is correct.

**Two lessons, and the second is the one that matters.** First, the
whole-frame diff I reached for FIRST could not settle it (mae 0.0156 vs
0.0080, pointing the wrong way) because terrain is most of the frame and
dilutes a sky-only change — *the right statistic is the one conditioned on
where the effect lives*, which is non-negotiable 22 again. Second: **a
transcript is a DERIVED RECORD.** Non-negotiable 15 says narrative is not
a source for state claims, and this was a state claim about frames on
disk, sourced from prose, about to be written into the record as fact.
The rule fired because the measurement was taken first.

### 5. THE ATTENDED "BEFORE/AFTER RENDER" WAS ALREADY ON DISK

The board said the triplanar LOOK was unmeasured and attended. It was not:
three complete 19-frame sets spanning both fixes were sitting in
`captures/alpine/`, and both comparisons are **single-variable**, verified
by `git log <range> -- scripts/make_landscape_material.py recipes/alpine.json`
returning exactly one commit each.

Measured against a same-settings noise floor (`044840Z` vs `054655Z`, same
commit, same cloud state, two runs — mean mae **0.00298**):

| | mean mae | vs noise |
|---|---|---|
| **Triplanar** `fb9a1bc2` to `75802995` | 0.02480 | **8.3x** |
| **`_wz_axis`** `75802995` to `236358db` | 0.01274 | **4.3x** |

Both clear it, and — the part that makes this evidence rather than a
number — **each spatial pattern matches its own mechanism**:

- Triplanar moves `rock_grounding` 32x and `cliff_face` 8.3x, and moves
  `diag_topdown` only 1.9x. That weakest camera is the DISCRIMINATING
  CONTROL: from directly overhead every surface has `|N.z|` near 1 and the
  triplanar blend collapses to the top-down projection **by construction**.
  The one view where the feature predicts near-identity is the one view
  that barely moved.
- `_wz_axis` moves `verify_ground` 5.0x (84.95% of pixels) and
  `rock_grounding` 18x, and leaves `cliff_face` at 1.2x and `sweep_0060`
  BELOW noise. The forest-floor tint reads world-Z, so views spanning
  altitude move and views at a single elevation do not.

**What it does not establish:** that the cliffs look BETTER — that is a
judgement and it is Ryan's; and the GPU cost, which still needs a viewport
reading. Artefact: `_verify/20260808_before_after_material_fixes.txt`.

**The general lesson:** "attended" was doing double duty for two different
things — the RENDER, which only needed frames, and the GPU READING, which
needs a human at an overlay. Bundling them parked a measurable result
behind an unmeasurable one for two days. **Split an attended item into its
attended and unattended halves before deferring it.**

### 6. THE REPOSITORY WAS PUSHED TO A PUBLIC REMOTE MID-SESSION

`git remote add origin https://github.com/ryan772177/LandscapeLab.git`
followed by `git push -u origin main`, at commit **`cb41d7f7`** — which is
the commit immediately AFTER the truncation. `.git/refs/remotes/origin/main`
confirms it locally. The remote therefore holds `LESSONS.md` **at 35
lines**, and none of the repair. Not acted on: pushing is outward-facing
and Ryan's call. Recorded because a project whose most valuable artefact is
published in its destroyed state should not learn that by accident.

## 2026-08-08 — THE GPU READING: TWO R13 CLAIMS FALL, AND THE FIRST FRAME IS ALWAYS A LIE

Attended run with Ryan at the overlay. Eight readings across two stations.
Artefact: `_verify/20260808_gpu_readings.md`. The measurement that was
asked for — triplanar's cost — is still not taken; everything below is
what the attempt uncovered on the way.

### THE SCENE IS NOT STABLE AT A FIXED CAMERA, AND THE FIRST READING IS THE WORST

Prims after parking `sweep_0060`: 121.7K → 81.3K → 73.3K → 73.3K. Roughly
three readings of drain before steady state. The first A/B I took spanned
that drain and reported **clouds as CHEAPER than no clouds** — physically
impossible, and the tell was not the milliseconds but the **40,400
primitives that vanished at a camera that had not moved.**

**A second field of the same overlay caught what the headline number could
not.** GPU time alone was plausible in both directions; Prims was not.
This is the conditioned-statistic lesson from the morning's cloud-state
work arriving in a different instrument on the same day.

**And I designed the experiment without a noise floor** — the exact
omission LESSONS 2026-08-06 already logged ("two identical-settings runs
differ by up to 26%... always capture a same-settings repeat"), which I
had applied rigorously to the image comparison hours earlier. A lesson
learned in one instrument did not transfer to another. Measured floor,
once I bothered: **1.06 ms** between two OFF readings at identical Prims.

**Rule that follows: an A/B at a parked camera is invalid until Prims
stops moving, and a pair whose Prims disagree is not a pair.**

### R13's CLOUDS PREMISE IS FALSE

Measured cost of clouds: **+1.78 ms GPU (4.4%)** at `sweep_0060`, **+6.48
ms (8.6%)** at `sweep_2000`, both at matched Prims, corroborated by Draws
separating with no overlap (~6 extra draw calls, every reading, both
stations).

R13 ADDENDUM rules clouds OFF interactive because *"a per-pixel volumetric
on a saturated iGPU takes the viewport from slow to unusable."* The frame
goes 79.12 → 86.14 ms: **12.6 fps versus 11.6 fps.** It was never the
difference between usable and unusable, because the viewport is unusable
either way. **The ruling optimised a term worth 8% and left the other 92%
unexamined** — which is what an unmeasured fear does to a budget.

To R13's credit its ADDENDUM demanded exactly this measurement before any
re-rule. The measurement now exists.

### THE BIGGER ONE: BOTH STATIONS ARE DRAW-THREAD BOUND

Six settled readings, two stations, unanimous — Frame tracks **Draw**,
GPU 3.5-4 ms behind:

    sweep_0060  Frame 45.04  Draw 45.00  GPU 40.94
    sweep_2000  Frame 79.12  Draw 79.08  GPU 75.50

R13 records the opposite and builds advice on it: *"GPU-bound at both
stations … the cost is PER-PIXEL SHADING — not scene bloat … the lever is
shader/material cost and resolution, not instance counts or draw
batching."* At steady state **the lever is precisely what that sentence
rules out.** A free shader would not shorten these frames.

**HOW BOTH OF US GOT IT WRONG, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT TWICE.** My first
`sweep_2000` reading showed **Draw 0.02 ms** — not a plausible draw-thread
time, and I committed it as a baseline without blinking. Settled, it reads
**79.08**, nearly four thousand times larger. An unsettled first frame
makes a scene look purely GPU-bound. **An absurd magnitude is a question
about the instrument** (the `git show` / LFS near-miss, logged this same
day, in different clothes) — and 0.02 ms for a draw thread issuing 1,976
draw calls is absurd on its face. I read it, wrote it into an artefact,
committed it, and only caught it because a later reading disagreed by four
orders of magnitude.

**SCOPE, STATED BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ON IT.** This is an EDITOR viewport
measurement and the editor draw thread carries editor-only work. It
firmly changes the EDITOR conclusion. It does NOT establish that a
shipping build is draw-bound, and it does not license a foliage-reduction
campaign — that needs a PIE or packaged reading, a different calibration
class that does not exist yet. What it retires is the claim that this
project has MEASURED its cost to be per-pixel shading.

### THE CROSS-SESSION COMPARISON WAS RETIRED THE HARD WAY

I tried to use 94.45 / 75.71 twice: once as raw ms, once via a per-pixel
normalisation that felt rigorous. The second station killed it —
`sweep_2000` came out **+2.5%** and `sweep_0060` **−31.0%** per pixel. A
material cost cannot have two signs. One station alone would have handed
me a tidy +2.5% with no way to doubt it; **the positive control was simply
taking the second station, and it was free.**

### WHAT THIS DOES TO THE TRIPLANAR MEASUREMENT STILL OWED

Finding 2 changes what that measurement can show. If the draw thread is
the critical path, triplanar's two extra rock albedo samples may be
invisible in FRAME time while costing real GPU milliseconds. **Read GPU
Time, not Frame** — otherwise a genuine cost gets recorded as "free", and
this project would have written that down.
