## 2026-08-14 (later still) — THE TREE PACKS ARE SKELETAL, AND THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION DID NOT APPLY

The conifer intake ran. Both headline findings are about the SPEC being wrong
for these assets, not about the assets being bad.

**1. ALL EIGHT TREE VARIANTS ARE `SkeletalMesh`.** Discovered by a refusal, not
by a check I had thought to write: `measure_rock_meshes`' payload came back
with `lod_count: None` and
`StaticMeshEditorSubsystem: Failed to convert parameter 'static_mesh'`. The
bounds read fine (SkeletalMesh has `get_bounds` too) and `nanite_enabled` read
True, so seven of nine fields looked like a successful measurement.
`find_assets` filtered to `StaticMesh` under `/Game/Megaplant_Library` with
name `Tree_` returns **zero rows**; only the `Instances/` parts are static.
**The foliage system instances StaticMesh only**, so neither pack can join the
153,796-instance forest as shipped. This is the blocking fact for any
re-scatter and it was invisible from the store page, the file listing and the
asset count alike.

**2. NEITHER FOLIAGE MATERIAL IS ALPHA-MASKED.** `MI_Norway_Spruce_Foliage_01`
and `MI_Baltic_Pine_01_Foliage` both carry `bOverride_BlendMode: true` with
`blendMode: BLEND_Opaque`, parented to
`/ProceduralVegetationEditor/.../MA_Foliage_Trees`. The needles are geometry.
**So `conifer_asset_spec.md` section 2.3 — ">= 45% atlas opaque coverage", its
"single most important criterion" — does not apply to these assets at all.**
The incumbent's 24.02% is a fact about ALPHA-TESTED CARDS. Against opaque
geometry it is not a smaller number, it is an answer to a different question.

**AND MY OWN TOOL PRINTED A NUMBER THAT WAS NOT A MEASUREMENT.** The first run
reported `T_Baltic_Pine_Foliage_CA` at **100.00% opaque** and I nearly read it
as a spectacular result. The atlas's alpha channel is **255 everywhere — one
distinct level**. There is no mask in it; the exporter did its job. "100%
opaque" was the ABSENCE OF A MASK being rendered as full coverage, which is
non-negotiable 6 wearing a number, produced by an instrument I had written
twenty minutes earlier and had not fed a negative control.

**What caught it was the magnitude, not a gate.** 100.00% and a clip spread of
exactly 0.00 are both absurd on their face for a foliage atlas (NN11), and the
rule that says look at the pixels before running a statistic (NN10) is what
turned an absurd number into the alpha histogram that explained it. The tool
now FAILS CLOSED on both conditions — constant alpha, and a consuming material
that is not `BLEND_Masked` — and reports `coverage_applicable: false` with the
reason instead of a percentage.

**A THIRD, QUIETER DEFECT IN THE SAME TOOL.** `albedo_rgb_where_opaque` selects
texels with alpha >= 0.5. When alpha is constant that selects EVERY texel, so
Baltic Pine's `[137, 129, 101]` is the mean of the whole atlas including
padding — not the needle colour. Same arithmetic, different question, and it
would have been quoted as a needle albedo. The output now states its
denominator explicitly (NN22).

**THE CLIP-SPREAD TEST IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS, and this is worth keeping.**
Norway Spruce reports spread 0.00 and I labelled it "effectively binary". It
has **78 distinct alpha levels** — but every intermediate one is >= 179, so
clip 0.1 and clip 0.5 select the identical texel set and the spread vanishes.
The conclusion happened to be right; the test cannot distinguish "hard binary"
from "soft fringe entirely above both thresholds". The distinct-level count is
now reported alongside so the difference is visible.

**WHAT THE MEASUREMENTS DO SAY, and it is good news on the axis that matters.**
Heights 6.47-26.84 m (Spruce) and 11.39-28.69 m (Pine) against the incumbent's
14.52 m: the mature variants sit inside the spec's 18-35 m band, where
`fir_tree_01` never did. Pivots are at the trunk base to within 4-10 mm on all
eight. Horizontal pivot offsets run 0.121-0.373 m; the worst, Norway Spruce A
at 0.373 m, approaches the 0.419 m that got `vegetation_debris` REFUSED — but
that refusal was for a 1.03 m-wide object sweeping a 0.84 m circle under random
yaw, and this is a 6.63 m-wide tree. **The rule needs re-deriving as a RATIO
before it is applied here**, not copied across as an absolute.

## 2026-08-14 (later still) — THE LOD CHAIN HIT ITS TRIANGLE TARGETS EXACTLY AND DESTROYED THE CANOPY

R5's chain was applied to the eight baked Megaplants conifers. Every level
landed within **0% of its requested triangle count** — and every reduced
level collapsed from **3 material sections to 1**, on all eight meshes.

    LOD 0 :   125,321 triangles, 3 sections
    LOD 1 :    31,330 triangles, 1 sections   wanted ~31,330  (0% off)
    LOD 2 :     5,527 triangles, 1 sections   wanted ~5,526   (0% off)
    LOD 3 :       964 triangles, 1 sections   wanted ~964     (0% off)

**This is R5's own REJECTED entry, arriving two levels earlier than it ever
did before.** On `fir_tree_01` the simplifier only dropped a section at a
FIFTH LOD of 693 triangles; here it drops two sections at **LOD1, screen
size 0.5** — near field. The mechanism is the one R5 names: the simplifier
eats disconnected foliage cards before a connected trunk. A tree whose
canopy section vanishes at half screen size renders as a bare stick at
almost any distance, which is precisely the defect the whole conifer
replacement exists to fix.

**THE TRIANGLE TARGET WAS A PERFECT SCORE ON THE WRONG EXAM.** "0% off" at
every level reads as a flawless result and would have been reported as one
by any gate counting triangles. R5's acceptance criterion is SECTION COUNT
AT EVERY LEVEL, and it is the only thing that caught this. Written down
in 2026-08-03 after one asset, it fired correctly on a different asset,
from a different vendor, produced by a different pipeline, eleven days
later.

**AND THE FAILURE PATH LEAVES A LIVE HAZARD, which the tool says out loud:**
nothing was saved, but all eight meshes are DIRTY IN EDITOR MEMORY with the
rejected chain applied, and saving a level saves every dirty external
package. An unrelated save would silently persist a chain that was
explicitly rejected. The tool prints this; the operator has to act on it.
Restarting the editor is the clean discard.

## THE TOOL CONFLATED "BUILD A CHAIN" WITH "DECLARE A SPECIES"

Getting this far required fixing `make_mesh_lods.py`, whose only input was
`foliage.species`. Anything needing an LOD chain had to pretend to be a
placement declaration and was then judged by the FOLIAGE validator, which
refused all eight for two reasons that were both correct and both
irrelevant:

  * no VERIFIED row in the Blender normalisation report — true by
    construction, since these are baked in-engine and never went through
    `normalize_asset.py`. That gate is exactly right about PLACEMENT (never
    place a mesh of unknown provenance) and says nothing about decimation.
  * `weight_share` summing to 4.8 over the Grass layer — a complaint about
    a placement property of eight things that were never going to be
    placed, produced entirely by my staging file copying a template.

Added `lod_targets`: a top-level list saying what it means — build a chain
on this mesh — validated NARROWLY (path shape, chain monotonic, percentages
in range) and never read as a placement declaration. The foliage path is
untouched, and the foliage validator now runs only when the recipe actually
declares foliage, so a pure `lod_targets` file is not refused for lacking a
block it does not use.

**The narrow validator was proven in both directions before use** — the
LOD-0 index trap (`percent_triangles: 1.0`), a percentage above 1, a chain
that does not reduce, ascending screen sizes and a non-numeric value are
each refused with a specific message, against a positive control that is
accepted.

## NANITE FOLIAGE IS THE ROUTE AROUND THIS, AND IT IS EXPERIMENTAL

Nanite clusters per material section, so it cannot drop the foliage section
the way the simplifier just did, and it removes the need for a discrete
chain at all. Two facts make these unusually good candidates: both foliage
materials measured **`BLEND_Opaque`** — real geometry needles, no alpha test
— and Nanite's historic weakness is masked foliage.

`r.Nanite.Foliage` is real (`NaniteResources.cpp:117-121`), defaults **0**,
and is **`ECVF_ReadOnly`** — settable only at startup, so config plus a
restart is the only route. It is backed by a `UPROPERTY` on
`URendererSettings` (`RendererSettings.h:1550-1553`,
`ConsoleVariable = "r.Nanite.Foliage"`), which is why
`[/Script/Engine.RendererSettings]` is the correct section for it even
though every other `r.Nanite.*` pin in this project lives in
`[SystemSettings]`. **Maturity tier: EXPERIMENTAL** — the DisplayName is
"Nanite Foliage (Experimental)".

Also note the standing ruling "Nanite stays OFF on vendor foliage meshes"
does NOT apply: its stated reason is that vendor meshes are gitignored so
the flag vanishes on re-download. These bakes are ours and tracked.

**Unmeasured, and it is the next measurement:** GPU cost at the
`forest_floor` station against the recorded 8.14 ms with 154,018 conifers.

**AMENDMENT, same day — `r.Nanite.Foliage` IS BROADER THAN ITS NAME.** The
entry above called it the switch for Nanite foliage support. A second,
wider search of the engine source found three more consumers, and two of
them are other features entirely:

    RenderUtils.cpp:1369-1376  NaniteAssembliesSupported()
                               return bAllowNaniteFoliage || bAllowAssemblies
    RenderUtils.cpp:1378-1385  NaniteVoxelsSupported()
                               return bAllowNaniteFoliage || bAllowVoxels
    TemporalSuperResolution.cpp:499-502
                               return bNaniteFoliageEnabled
                                      || ThinGeometryDetection != 0

So setting it to 1 also enables **Nanite Assemblies**, **Nanite Voxels**
and **TSR thin-geometry detection** — three separately-gated experimental
features that would otherwise each need their own opt-in. On a machine that
has already lost its GPU to a driver timeout, the blast radius of a flag is
part of its cost.

**AND IT BREAKS THE PLANNED A/B.** The recorded 8.14 ms at `forest_floor`
with 154,018 conifers was measured with this flag OFF. Comparing a
Nanite-foliage run against it would conflate Nanite foliage with a TSR
path change. The fix is cheap because Nanite is PER-MESH: run the control
with the flag ON and the trees still non-Nanite, then flip only the meshes.
**The variable has to be the thing under test, not the thing that was
convenient to change.**

Every one of those reads is a `static const bool` initialised on first
call, which independently corroborates the `ECVF_ReadOnly` startup-only
behaviour rather than resting on the flag alone — two mechanisms, same
conclusion.

*Method note: the narrow grep that answered the original question was
correct and incomplete. The broad one had been dispatched first, timed out
into the background, and its result arrived after the conclusion was
already committed. Reading it anyway is what caught this.*

## 2026-08-14 (end) — THE BAKE IS FAITHFUL AND THE SOURCE IS NOT A WHOLE TREE

A scratch look-test level answered the question thumbnails could not, and the
answer is worse than "the canopy is thin".

**UNDER REAL LIGHTING, ALL EIGHT BAKED TREES ARE BARE WOODY SKELETONS.**
Trunk and branch structure in fine detail; **not one needle**. The frame is
tonally valid — sRGB mean 0.7781, std 0.1208, 0.000% blown, 0.003% black —
so this is not the empty-world black-frame trap, and it is not the dark
thumbnail either.

**THE MECHANISM, established by a second representation rather than
inferred.** `Twig_Norway_Spruce_01`, one of the `Instances/` parts, renders
as a dense green needle cluster. The needles ship as SEPARATE StaticMesh
assets — `Twig_*` for the spruce, `Needle_*` for the pine — and the
Procedural Vegetation Editor assembles them onto the woody armature. **The
SkeletalMesh `Tree_*_01_A..D` is the armature only.**

So the 125,321–331,779 triangles are BRANCHES, and every verification the
bake passed was true:

    bounds     match the source to under a centimetre
    materials  3 carried in order, correctly named
    vertices   identical on all four spruces, within 0.1% on the pines

**The bake is a faithful copy of its source. The source is not a whole
tree.** Every gate was measuring fidelity-to-source, and fidelity-to-source
was never the question anyone cared about.

**THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE NIGHT'S OTHER TWO DEFECTS.** The MCP server
logged "Starting" before its socket bound. Fab reported a file list it read
from a manifest rather than from disk. Here, eight bakes verified against
the thing they were copied from while nobody had checked that the thing
copied from was the thing wanted. **Success reported from the INTENT rather
than from the ARTEFACT** — three times, in three different systems, in one
session.

**AND THE THUMBNAIL "NEAR-MISS" WAS NOT A MISS.** Hours earlier I nearly
reported "bare poles" from a 256×256 unlit thumbnail, caught myself on the
331,779-triangle magnitude, and ruled the instrument invalid. **The
instrument WAS invalid and the reading was RIGHT.** Being right for a bad
reason is not being right, and the correction still stands — a dark
thumbnail could not have distinguished "no needles" from "needles I cannot
see", which is exactly why the lit render was necessary. But it is worth
recording that discarding a true signal is the cost of that discipline, and
that the cost was one scratch scene.

**WHAT THE LOD SECTION-COLLAPSE WAS ACTUALLY TELLING US.** Earlier the
simplifier reduced every level from 3 material sections to 1, and it was read
as "the canopy will vanish at distance". Re-read now: there is no canopy in
the mesh to lose. The Foliage section is present but carries almost nothing,
which is why the reducer discarded it first. **A symptom read correctly can
still be attributed to the wrong cause.**

### THE FORK, unresolved and Ryan's

1. **Assemble via PVE, then bake.** `PVE_Norway_Spruce_01`,
   `PVE_Preset_Norway_Spruce_01` and `PVE_*_Data` ship with each pack and the
   Experimental `ProceduralVegetationEditor` plugin is now enabled. If it can
   emit an assembled mesh, `bake_skeletal_to_static.py` takes it from there
   unchanged. **UNVERIFIED — whether PVE exposes a bake/export is the next
   thing to establish.**
2. **Place PVE actors directly.** Almost certainly not viable at 150,000
   instances, and unmeasured.
3. **Use these as hero trees only** and keep the existing fir/Scots-pine for
   the forest.

Nothing has been scattered and `/Game/Alpine8K` is untouched.

## 2026-08-15 — PVE EXPORTS A REAL TREE. OPTION 1 WORKS.

`_verify/20260815_pve_export_vs_armature_bake.png` settles it. Same variant,
same lighting, same camera, one variable: **left** is
`SM_Tree_Norway_Spruce_01_A`, the SkeletalMesh armature baked by
`bake_skeletal_to_static.py` — a bare pole with branch stubs. **Right** is
`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`, the same tree exported from the PVE editor as a
**Static Mesh** — a full Norway spruce with needles, a conical crown and a
real cast shadow. Frame tonally valid: sRGB mean 0.7707, std 0.1288, 0.000%
blown.

**THE ONE SETTING.** The PVE editor's Export Settings had
`Export Mesh Type: Skeletal Mesh` — the vendor's own choice, and the entire
reason the packs ship skeletal. Changing it to `Static Mesh` and pressing
Export produces the assembled tree. Everything upstream of that — the
armature bake, its LOD chain, the section-collapse — was solving a problem
created by one dropdown.

**MEASURED, and one number needs its caveat.** The export reports LOD0 at
**2,335 triangles**, which is NOT the tree: Nanite replaces LOD0 with a
reduced fallback, exactly as recorded for `boulder_medium_01` (4,136 ->
1,796). The real geometry is Nanite data. The PVE viewport's own readout for
this tree is **147,746 triangles, 76,337 vertices, 25 unique foliage assets,
215 foliage instances** — and "Unique Foliage 25 / Foliage Instances 215" is
the direct statement that the needles live in the PVE assembly, not in the
skeletal source.

    height        29.31 m   (armature bake of the same variant: 26.85 m)
    materials     3, NAMED by PVE: Bark_01, Foliage_01, Decorations_01
    nanite        enabled, Create Nanite Foliage was ticked in the dialog
    on disk       3.80 MB

The height difference is itself evidence: the PVE tree is 2.46 m taller
because foliage extends past the branch tips the armature ends at.

### THREE OPERATIONAL FACTS WORTH KEEPING

**MCP TOOL CALLS RUN ON THE GAME THREAD.** Clicking Export opened a modal
("Modify Export Settings") and the Click call never returned; the MCP client
gave up after 300 s of silence and reported the tool FAILED. Nothing had
failed — a dialog was waiting for input, and MCP cannot answer it because
MCP is blocked by it. **An MCP timeout is not evidence about the editor.**
Diagnose from outside: process CPU, the log, and a Win32 window enumeration.

**CPU RATE DISCRIMINATED WAITING FROM WORKING.** While the dialog waited,
the editor drew ~0.4 cores. Once Export was pressed it went to ~4 cores
sustained for 18 minutes. Same "no output" from the log in both phases; the
rate is what separated them.

**THE ASSET EXISTED BEFORE IT WAS ON DISK.** The export finished at 00:10
and `Content/Meshes/Trees/` stayed empty, because the package was created
DIRTY IN MEMORY. The tell was an autosave line naming a package that had
never existed:
`Moving '.../SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A_Auto27BD....tmp' to '.../Autosaves/Game/Meshes/Trees/...'`.
Polling the destination folder would have waited forever.

### TWO OF MY OWN TOOLS TOLD THE TRUTH BADLY

`scratch_tree_scene.py --replace` claimed a capability it did not have:
`new_level()` returns False when the asset exists, so the flag only skipped
the script's own refusal and then died on a bare "new_level returned False".
Fixed to swap to an empty map and delete first. **A flag that names an
outcome it cannot deliver is worse than no flag.**

And the export dialog was captured at two-thirds size, because
`GetWindowRect` returns VIRTUAL units while `CopyFromScreen` reads the
PHYSICAL buffer — the same 1.5x DPI factor that has now been paid for three
times tonight in three different tools. Scale the ORIGIN and the SIZE.

### WHAT IS NOT DONE

Seven trees remain skeletal-only. The export dialog has a **Batch** tab
listing all four variants of a pack with checkboxes, so a pack is plausibly
one operation rather than four — untested. Each export took ~18 minutes of
4-core work, so the remaining seven are hours, not minutes.

Nothing is scattered. `/Game/Alpine8K` is untouched. `bake_skeletal_to_static.py`
and R-BAKE are now superseded for THIS pack but remain correct for any
genuinely skeletal source, and R-BAKE's REJECTED entries stand.

All four Norway Spruce variants are now Static Meshes with needles:

    SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A   29.31 m   3.80 MB
    SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_B   23.64 m   3.47 MB
    SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_C   18.09 m   1.83 MB
    SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_D    8.02 m   1.71 MB

Frame `_verify/20260815_pve_spruce_four_variants.png`, tonally valid at sRGB
mean 0.7682, std 0.1293, 0.000% blown. Spot-checked `_C`: three named
material slots (Bark_01, Foliage_01, Decorations_01) and Nanite enabled.

**THE EXPORT SETTINGS ARE PER NODE, AND FINDING THAT OUT COST ONE CLICK
INSTEAD OF AN HOUR AND A RE-DOWNLOAD.** The Batch tab's tooltip is "Batch
export all output nodes" and ticking it checks all four. The right-hand
Export Settings panel still shows ONE set of values, which reads as global.
It is not: clicking node B showed B's own settings, and they were the
vendor's —

    Content Browser Folder : /Game/Megaplant_Library/Tree_Norway_Spruce/...
    Export Mesh Type       : Skeletal Mesh
    Asset Replace Policy   : Replace

My earlier edits had only ever touched node A. **Pressing Export at that
moment would have written skeletal re-exports over the vendor source assets,
inside gitignored content — where git cannot restore them and only a Fab
re-download could.** The disambiguating test was to select a different node
and look at whether the panel changed. One click.

**AND THE 0.3-CORE SIGNATURE CAUGHT THE SECOND STALL.** After pressing
Export the log printed `Export Started`, then `FlushAsyncLoading(2771): 1
QueuedPackages`, then nothing for eleven minutes. The tempting reading is a
deadlock in the flush. CPU said otherwise: ~0.3 cores, the WAITING
signature, against the ~4 cores this export draws when it is really running.
A window enumeration found `WARNING: Assets will be overwritten` — the
Replace policy asking to confirm, because `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`
already existed from the first run.

**The warning dialog is also a gate worth reading rather than dismissing.**
It lists exactly which assets it will destroy. Here it listed one —
`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` under `/Game/Meshes/Trees/`, ours and committed.
Had the per-node settings not been fixed, that same list would have named
the vendor assets, and it would have been the last chance to notice.

**THE ASSET-EXISTS-BEFORE-IT-IS-ON-DISK PATTERN REPEATED EXACTLY.** After
the batch finished, `Content/Meshes/Trees/` still showed only the one file
from the previous run. `find_assets` returned all four. They were dirty in
memory; `save_assets` put them on disk. **Polling the destination folder is
the wrong instrument for "did the export finish" — ask the asset registry.**

### STILL OPEN

Four Baltic Pine variants remain skeletal-only, and their PVE asset has its
own four nodes with the same vendor defaults. The procedure is now known and
the per-node trap is documented; the cost is ~18 minutes of 4-core work per
variant.

## 2026-08-15 — FOUR DESIGN RULINGS, MADE BY THE FABLE MODEL UNDER RYAN'S DELEGATION

**Provenance, stated first because it matters.** Ryan went to bed having
said: *"you have full authority while im away ask the fable model if you
need any guidance it will act as the decision maker for me while im away"*.
The four rulings below were made by a Fable-model agent given the measured
evidence, and are recorded as **model rulings under delegation — NOT as
Ryan's own words.** Anything destructive to `LESSONS.md` or `RECIPES.md`
still waits for him; these are all additive.

### D1 — CAMERA RE-SITING: fix the four buried stations by Z-ONLY LIFT, hold the other fifteen

Four ground stations measure BELOW the terrain — `sweep_0060` −4.38 m,
`sweep_0350` −3.30 m, `trunk_base` −2.71 m, `lod_far` −1.19 m — because 19
of 20 cameras were inherited byte-identical from a 4 m/vertex recipe.

The ruling's load-bearing distinction: **a camera inside the hill has no
baseline worth preserving**, so the "re-siting resets the A/B baseline"
objection does not apply to those four. It applies fully to the stations
that measure fine — above all `forest_floor` at +1.93 m, which carries the
8.14 → 7.76 ms GPU series and both canopy A/Bs. Those stay byte-identical.

Z-ONLY, not a mask re-site: keep XY and bearing, set Z from the engine line
trace plus eye height. That preserves each station's SUBJECT — the defect is
burial, not siting. `lod_far` especially must keep its XY because it pairs
with `lod_near` 13 m away, and that pair geometry is the station's whole
purpose.

A full deliberate re-site becomes a named `camera_epoch` AFTER the D4
re-scatter, so every frame can state which station set it belongs to.

### D2 — TREES: import `PN_interactiveSpruceForest`; the Baltic Pine exports are DEFERRED

The decisive argument is not cost, it is which gap gets closed. PN ships
`MA_Imposter` plus 21 baked 4096² atlases, and BACKLOG's aerial-readability
item calls imposters *"the only way real forest reaches airship altitude
past the 730 m cull"*, against a WORLD_VISION ruling that makes aerial
readability first-class. **Option (b) closes the project's largest recorded
gap; four more Baltic Pine variants close none** — Scots pine already covers
that role.

Also: the forest has no sapling tier at all, and PN's 0.56–16.9 m range
provides one. Its 10.5–16.9 m mature trees are botanically closer to a
treeline stand than the 29.31 m spruce now placed.

And the hazard asymmetry: the PVE export path was one click from writing
skeletal meshes over gitignored vendor sources git cannot restore. Spending
~72 minutes of 4-core compute through a fail-open path to buy marginal
variety is the wrong side of *prefer an input that cannot express the
catastrophic value*.

FOUR CONDITIONS, and the third is the interesting one: wind is EDITED OUT
for a static first import (`PN_GlobalUpdater` is a runtime Blueprint
dependency; wiring it would violate single-variable measurement and pipeline
rule 1); and **`LODGroup=None` on the 14 big trees makes explicit screen
sizes and cull distances MANDATORY BEFORE PLACEMENT, encoded as a REFUSAL in
the gate rather than a checklist item** — non-negotiable 3, an input that
cannot express the bad state beating a gate that must remember to check.

### D3 — UNDERSTORY: blueberry only, on the GRASS system, not instances

Blueberry is the dominant spruce-forest understory to treeline in the Alps;
blackberry and raspberry are montane-below-treeline and stay on disk. The
484 MB demo ground texture stays behind.

**Grass system rather than instances is precedent, not a new call** — the
2026-08-08 ruling "carpet density on the grass system, instances only for
sparse landmarks" is exactly this case. 19–178 cm carpet plants through the
instance path would burn tens of thousands of the shared 250k ceiling that
D4 needs for trees; through GrassOutput they cost zero instances.

Two gates first: `uncorrected_pivot_errors()` on each mesh (the grass system
corrects nothing and buries a box-centred pivot 50% by construction), and
the landscape-material rebuild discipline, attended. Abort bar +1.5 ms GPU
over the 7.76 ms baseline.

### D4 — DENSITY: rise to ~220,000 instances as a CLOSURE GRADIENT, never uniform 70%

WORLD_VISION already answers whether sparse is intended — it records foliage
density as *"two orders of magnitude below reality"* and raising it as *"the
next visible-quality step"*.

But **70% cover was a reference-class error**: that is a managed lowland
forestry number. Subalpine spruce near treeline is naturally patchy, 20–50%
and gap-structured. **The defect is as much UNIFORMITY as count** — 23.28/ha
spread evenly reads as thin everywhere instead of dense-here-open-there. The
fix is structure: dense stands low on the arc thinning to krummholz at the
640 m band top, which also makes WORLD_VISION's foothill→peak gradient
visible.

~220,000 is chosen to leave a **30k reserve under the shared 250k ceiling**,
because that ceiling is ONE budget for rocks and vegetation by construction
and the rocks are absent by ruling, not permanently. The ceiling is not
raised: it was derived for this hardware, and 7.76 ms is an editor-viewport
floor, not a shipped cost.

ONE re-scatter combined with D2's mix, not two — every mass re-scatter
re-rolls every position, so sequencing them separately would invalidate all
positions twice for an intermediate state with no measurement value. Abort
bar **11 ms GPU** at `forest_floor`.

### SEQUENCING, which binds all four

D1's Z-fix first (cheap, restores the instruments), then D2 import plus
scratch-scene measurement, then D3's material rebuild, then the single D4
re-scatter, then the D1 epoch re-site and a fresh sweep. Every step leaves
`/Game/Alpine8K` recoverable by tag.

## 2026-08-15 — D2 INTAKE: A GATE THAT WOULD HAVE THROWN AWAY THE REASON THE PACK WAS CHOSEN

Measuring `PN_interactiveSpruceForest` before importing it produced three
findings, and two of them contradict something that was written down as
established.

### 1. THE RULING'S PREMISE ABOUT LOD GROUPS WAS WRONG, AND MEASURING IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS CAUGHT

The D2 ruling states `LODGroup=None` on the 14 big trees, and builds a
condition on it: explicit screen sizes and cull distances become a gate
REFUSAL *because* the meshes supply no defaults.

Measured: **15 of 21 carry `SmallProp`, 6 carry `NAME_None`**, inconsistently
— the same tree at `high` and `low` quality differs from itself. The ruling's
premise is false for most of the pack.

`measure_rock_meshes.py`'s shared payload did not read `lod_group` at all, so
the field had never been measured by anything. It was added this session
before the run, specifically because the ruling made the value load-bearing.
**A design that rests on an unmeasured property gets that property measured
before it is built on** — the ruling was right to name it, and wrong about
its value, and only one of those matters once you look.

The conclusion survives in a stronger form: the meshes' declared screen sizes
must be treated as authoritative, and cull distance still has to be declared
explicitly, because nothing in the pack supplies one.

### 2. AN ENGINE COMMENT THAT SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF THE CODE BENEATH IT

`SmallProp` is `NumLODs=4` (`BaseEngine.ini:2685`). Every big tree has **5**
LODs, and **LOD4 is the imposter**.

`UStaticMesh::SetLODGroup` (`StaticMesh.cpp:5605-5607`):

    // Set the number of LODs to at least the default. If there are already
    // LODs they will be preserved, with default settings of the new LOD group.
    int32 DefaultLODCount = GroupSettings.GetDefaultNumLODs();
    SetNumSourceModels(DefaultLODCount);

The comment promises preservation. `SetNumSourceModels`
(`StaticMesh.cpp:5944-5974`) does the opposite when shrinking: for every LOD
above the new count it calls `ClearMeshDescription()`, empties the
`MeshDescriptionBulkData`, strips both section-info maps, then
`SourceModels.SetNum(Num)`.

**So assigning any 4-LOD group to these meshes deletes the imposter.**

The dangerous part is not the engine bug — it is that **the obvious tidy-up
is the destructive act.** Finding "15 meshes carry an inconsistent LOD group"
invites normalising it, and normalising it destroys the imposters on all 14
big trees. The pack was chosen *for* those imposters. A future session will
find the same inconsistency and feel the same urge, which is why the ruling
NOT to normalise is recorded in the artefact and here rather than left as a
judgement someone has to re-make.

This is the project's own prose-claims-rot rule (non-negotiable 25) appearing
in engine source: a comment asserting a guarantee that nothing re-checks when
the code below it changes.

### 3. OUR OWN TOOL RETURNED A CONFIDENT WRONG VERDICT ON CORRECT CONTENT

`measure_lod_materials.py` exited 4 on all 14 big trees with:

    LOST MATERIAL(S): branch, leaf, trunk
    This LOD cannot render what LOD0 renders...
    ...the fix is to stop the chain before the loss, or to rebuild that LOD.

That advice, followed, **discards the imposter LOD** — the entire reason D2
selected this pack over four more pine variants.

Root cause is a missing distinction, at `measure_lod_materials.py:181`. The
tool computed `lost = base - used` and never computed `gained = used - base`.
Two different facts were collapsed into one:

- **LOSS** — materials disappear and nothing replaces them. The simplifier
  dropped geometry; the mesh renders as strictly less of itself. A defect.
- **SUBSTITUTION** — materials disappear *and* a material LOD0 never had
  appears. The LOD is a deliberate replacement representation: a billboard or
  octahedral imposter standing in for the whole tree.

**Every imposter LOD ever authored trips the loss test by construction.** The
tool had only ever been pointed at generated chains (R5's conifers) where a
final LOD is always a reduction, so it had never seen a substitution — which
is the project's own rule that a gate which has only seen one kind of input
has not been tested.

Fixed by classifying on `gained`, and the section-count check now indicts only
a LOD that lost without gaining. Verified both directions on real meshes: the
imposter LOD reports SUBSTITUTION and passes, while a genuine finding the same
run surfaced — every tree drops its `_branch` material at LOD2 or LOD3, before
the imposter — still exits 4. **The fix had to keep a real defect loud while
silencing a false one, and that is the test it was held to**, not merely
"does the imposter stop failing".

### THE SHAPE OF ALL THREE

Each came from asking the artefact a question nobody had asked it: the LOD
group (never read by any tool), the group's effect on LOD count (read at
source rather than assumed from a comment), and what a LOD *gained* rather
than only what it lost. None was catchable by re-reading the plan, and the
plan was confidently wrong about the first.

## 2026-08-15 — THE WIND WAS ALREADY BLOWING, AND THE MEAN NEARLY HID IT

The D2 ruling said to edit the wind out because `PN_GlobalUpdater` is a
runtime Blueprint dependency and wiring it would breach pipeline rule 1.
Before authoring ~73 material instances on that reasoning, the cheaper
question was asked first: **is the wind even live without the Blueprint?**

Three `highres_shot` frames, one parked camera, ~5 s apart, nothing touched
between them, in a scratch level containing no Blueprint of any kind.

    frames      mae      vs 0.00298 floor   px >2%   max local
    1 vs 2    0.00611        2.05x           4.36%     0.7333
    1 vs 3    0.00410        1.38x           3.66%     0.6824
    2 vs 3    0.00561        1.88x           4.27%     0.7255

**Read as a mean, 1.4-2.1x a noise floor is the kind of number this project
has correctly dismissed before.** It is roughly what the ScreenPercentage
A/B produced when the honest conclusion was "this lever is minor". Stopping
at the mean would have concluded the wind was inert and moved on.

Conditioned on WHERE it happens, it is not minor at all: 2.4% of the frame
changes by more than 10%, local differences reach **0.73**, and the change
is stratified by row band — canopy 10.32% of pixels, flat ground plane
1.04%.

**The diff image settled it in one look.** Amplified 6x it is a clean
silhouette of the tree: canopy saturated, the bare lower branches picked out
individually, sky and the flat untextured ground plane black. A static scene
re-rendered twice gives TAA jitter spread along edges everywhere; this is
confined to exactly the geometry that moves under wind and absent from the
two large regions that physically cannot. The spatial pattern matches the
mechanism, so it is evidence rather than a number.

### THE MEAN WAS A MISLEADING DENOMINATOR, IN THE ONE PLACE THE RULE IS EASY TO FORGET

Non-negotiable 22 was written about a layer-scoped selector reported against
the whole map. This is the same defect wearing frame coordinates: a change
occupying 2.4% of the pixels, averaged over 100% of them, reads as noise.
**Whole-frame mae is a layer-scoped statistic whenever the subject does not
fill the frame** — and a tree on a plain never does. The instrument that
answered the question was the one that stated its denominator.

### THE RULING'S REASON WAS WRONG AND ITS CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT

`PN_GlobalUpdater` is not required: the material drives the animation from
engine Time by itself. So the stated justification — a runtime Blueprint
dependency — does not apply.

The conclusion survives on a better ground that nobody had stated. **An
animating canopy makes every pixel comparison non-deterministic.** This
project's entire method is single-variable frame A/B against a floor
measured in the third decimal place. A forest that moves between the
"before" and the "after" does not raise the floor a little; on a
vegetation-filled frame it removes the instrument.

Worth separating clearly, because the two are easy to conflate: **frame
COST is unaffected.** That is a timing measurement, not a pixel one, so the
8.14 -> 7.76 ms result stands.

### AND THE REMOVAL IS CHEAP, WHICH ONLY MEASURING REVEALED

Wind is carried on STATIC SWITCH parameters — `Level 1/2/3 Wind` and the
three `Bending` siblings — on `MA_Summer`, `MA_Winter` and `MA_Imposter`.
A static switch set false in a child Material Instance COMPILES THE BRANCH
OUT rather than zeroing an amplitude, so it costs nothing at runtime.

That matters beyond convenience. The pack is gitignored with **0 tracked
files**, so any edit to the vendor masters is unrecoverable on re-download —
the Fab-boundary rule's own worked example. Child MIs in a tracked folder
leave every vendor byte identical. **The safe route existed the whole time
and was only visible after reading the parameter list**, which is the same
shape as the LOD-group finding earlier the same session: the artefact was
never asked.

### THE PART THAT REACHES BACKWARDS, RECORDED RATHER THAN CHASED

The 153,796 trees already standing in `/Game/Alpine8K` are Megaplants/PVE
content whose materials have never been tested for this. If they animate,
every PIXEL comparison taken on that world since the spruce adoption sits on
an inflated floor. The check is one park and three shots and it is NOT done,
because that world is expensive to load and it does not block D2. Stated
here so it is a known gap rather than a silent one.

Related: **the 0.00298 floor was derived on bare terrain**, before this
project had any animated foliage. Quoting it against a vegetation-filled
frame is a calibration-class error of the kind R13 already labels for GPU
figures.

## 2026-08-15 — THE FIX WAS SEVEN DAYS OLD, FORTY LINES AWAY, AND ON THE WRONG BRANCH

D2's ruling made explicit cull distances a gate REFUSAL before the PN trees
could be placed. Checking whether that gate already existed found that it
half did, on the wrong half.

`import_heightmap._validate_foliage`, before today:

    if "cull_distance_m" in sp:
        v = sp["cull_distance_m"]
        if not _is_num(v) or not 0.0 <= v <= 100000.0:

Three catastrophic inputs passed in silence — the key **absent** (so
FoliageType's engine default of 0 applies), the value **0.0**, and
**100000.0**, a 100 km cull on an 8.128 km map. Measured against the live
validator rather than read: all three returned zero errors.

**And the comment DIRECTLY BELOW that block already said what the first two
cost**, in this project's own words:

> Every instanced species was left on the engine default of 0, which
> `FoliageType.h:292` documents as "0 disables", so 28,302 505k-triangle
> trees were submitted every frame across an 8 km map until the GPU missed
> the Windows TDR deadline and returned `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`.

Forty lines further down, the GRASS branch requires the key, bounds it to
(0, 250], and carries a comment dated 2026-08-08 explaining the requirement
— whose closing sentence is *"That lesson was written about the INSTANCED
path and never applied to the grass path beside it."*

**So the sweep ran exactly one hop and stopped.** The lesson originated on
the instanced path, was applied to the grass path, and was never applied
back to the path it came from. For seven days the branch that actually hung
the GPU was the only one that did not enforce the fix, in a file that
contains a paragraph explaining why it must.

This is non-negotiable 4 in its purest form — *"NaN-passing-range-checks was
fixed five times because it was fixed locally each time"* — and it is worth
noting what did NOT catch it. Not the gate suite: `prove_gates` had four
probes for the grass cull and none for the instanced cull, so it proved the
half that was already correct. Not a review of the file: the narrative is
right there and reads as though the work were done. What caught it was
asking the validator a question and reading its answer, rather than reading
the prose around it.

**Fixed with the interval OPEN at zero** — `0.0 < v <= 5000.0` and the key
required — so the disabling value is no longer expressible rather than
merely rejected (non-negotiable 3). The bound is 5000 to MATCH
`_validate_rock_species`: rocks and trees are the same instanced path with
the same cost mechanism, and one physical constraint gets one number rather
than a second free to drift (non-negotiable 24).

**Proven both directions, positive control FIRST**, because a gate that
refuses everything is not a gate: the shipped recipe still validates with
zero errors, 1.0 m and exactly 5000.0 are accepted, and 5000.1, 0.0,
100000.0, a string and the missing key are all refused. Four permanent
probes added to `prove_gates.py` beside the grass four, so the two halves
can no longer drift apart. Whole suite exit 0, dead-gate sweep clean over 51
checkers, and every recipe in `recipes/` re-validated with no new failures.

### THE PART WORTH CARRYING FORWARD

A comment explaining why a rule exists is evidence the rule was UNDERSTOOD,
not evidence it was ENFORCED. This file had the incident, the source
citation and the mechanism written down beside a branch that did not check
it. **When a lesson names a path, grep that path** — the grass comment
literally named "the INSTANCED path" as the origin of the defect, and that
sentence was the map to the remaining hole.

## 2026-08-15 — THE FOREST DOES NOT MOVE. THE FLOOR DOES.

The question was whether the 153,796 trees standing in `/Game/Alpine8K`
animate the way the PN spruce does. The answer is no, and the run found two
things worth more than the answer.

### THE ANSWER, FROM TWO SOURCES THAT SHARE NOTHING

`MA_Foliage_Trees` (the Megaplants conifer master) declares 38 scalars, 19
switches and 20 vectors, **every one of them shading or colour**.
`ScotsPine_01_Leaves_Mat` declares three scalars and no switches. Not one
wind, wobble, bending, phase or time parameter between them, against a PN
master carrying twelve. And removing the grass left frame-to-frame variance
unchanged, 0.011745 -> 0.012122.

### FINDING 1 — THE NOISE FLOOR IS A PROPERTY OF A SCENE, NOT OF A PROJECT

`/Game/Alpine8K` at `forest_floor` re-renders itself at **mae 0.0117, 3.94x
the 0.00298 this project quotes everywhere**, across 23% of the frame, with
the grass off and zero shader compile workers running. It is renderer
temporal accumulation, not motion.

0.00298 was measured on `/Game/Alpine` — 2017², before Lumen, before the
capable-GPU profile, before volumetric fog. **It has been carried across a
new world, a new resolution, a new lighting model and a new quality profile
as though it were a constant.** Every pixel A/B judged against it on
Alpine8K has been over-crediting differences by about 4x.

This is the CALIBRATION CLASS rule that R13 already applies to GPU
milliseconds, unapplied to the one number that gates every visual verdict.
The fix is not a better floor; it is that a floor must be RE-DERIVED with
its scene and its settings, and quoted with them attached.

### FINDING 2 — A CVAR THAT READS BACK CORRECTLY AND DOES NOTHING

The vegetation-off control was `foliage.CullAll 1` + `grass.Enable 0`. Both
read back. `render_condition` printed CONDITION SET AND READ BACK ON EVERY
CVAR. **The trees stayed on screen.**

Caught by measuring the thing the control was supposed to change rather than
trusting that it had: the upper half of the frame is canopy and sky, so
culling trees must collapse its dark coverage. It fell 62.73% -> 53.92%,
while the grass half fell 56.52% -> 41.55%. **The half that was supposed to
change most changed least.**

`foliage.CullAll` is declared in `HierarchicalInstancedStaticMesh.cpp:63-67`
— the HISM culling path. `r.Nanite.Foliage` is 1 and the placed spruce is
Nanite, so it never enters that path. The cvar is not broken; it is scoped
to a renderer the foliage no longer uses.

**This is exactly the protocol's own warning — a value can arrive and still
mean something else — landing on a cvar rather than on an API argument.**
"Set and read back" proves the variable holds the number. It proves nothing
about whether the subsystem reading that variable is the one drawing the
picture.

**And it reaches backwards.** CURRENT STATE records the 2026-08-14
decomposition as vegetation ON 8.14 / CULLED 5.86, delta +2.28 ms,
attributed to "154,018 conifers plus grass". If `r.Nanite.Foliage` was
already 1 for that run, that 2.28 ms was **grass alone**. Not resolved here,
because resolving it needs the cvar's value at that run and not a guess —
but recorded, because the figure is on the board as a conifer cost.

### THE SHAPE

Both findings are the same shape as the session's earlier ones: a number
inherited from a context it no longer describes, and a control believed
because it reported success. The floor was true of a different world. The
cull was true of a different renderer. Neither announced that it had stopped
being true, and in both cases the only thing that surfaced it was measuring
the artefact the claim was about — the frame's own variance, and the dark
coverage of the half that should have emptied.

**A null result is only evidence when the instrument could have produced a
non-null one.** The grass control passed that test — removing grass moved
20.9x the floor — so "grass is not the cause" is a real finding. The tree
control failed it, so "trees are not the cause" rests on the material
probes, and the write-up says so rather than banking both as one result.

## 2026-08-15 — THE BUILDER, THE VALIDATOR AND TWO AUDITS ALL PASSED A CLAIM THAT WAS FALSE

D3 put the blueberry understory on the grass system. It landed, it costs
nothing measurable, and it produced the clearest example this project has of
a claim surviving every gate it had.

### THE CHAIN THAT AGREED, AND WAS WRONG

`MA_Blueberry` carries the same wind system as the PN trees. The grass system
gives no per-instance correction and the vendor pack must not be edited, so
the only route is `GrassVariety.override_materials` (PythonStub :121628).

That was declared in the recipe. The **validator accepted it**. The **payload
handled it**, including a fail-closed branch for an override that will not
load. The **builder reported success**. **Connectivity** passed 298/298 with
0 orphans. **Samplers** passed 37/37.

All eight varieties read back **`overrides: NONE`** off the saved asset.

Root cause at `make_landscape_material.py:2932`: the recipe's variety dicts
never reach the payload. They are transformed into
`{mesh, density, smin, smax}` first, and `override_materials` was dropped in
that transform. **The payload was correct about a field it never received.**

### WHY EVERY EXISTING GATE WAS BLIND, WHICH IS THE POINT

Not one of those instruments was broken, and not one was asking the question.
A grass type with no material overrides is a **perfectly well-formed grass
type**. Connectivity asks whether nodes are reachable. Samplers ask whether
declared types match. The builder asks whether its own calls returned. None
of them can distinguish "the override is absent because nobody wanted one"
from "the override is absent because it was silently dropped in transit".

**Agreement among instruments that share a source is one measurement**
(non-negotiable 0), and here they shared more than a source: they shared an
ASSUMPTION, that a field declared in the recipe reaches the thing that
consumes it. The transform between them was invisible to all of them.

What caught it was a new instrument that reads the SAVED asset and shares no
code with the builder — `scripts/read_grass_type.py` — with
`--expect-all-overridden` written as a **REFUSAL** rather than a printed
observation. A tool that prints "overrides: NONE" and exits 0 is a tool that
would have been skimmed past.

### THE SECOND FINDING: I HAD BROKEN THE GATE THE RULING NAMED, EARLIER THE SAME DAY

The ruling required `uncorrected_pivot_errors()` per mesh — the grass system
puts the mesh's PIVOT on the surface and a box-centred pivot buries 50% by
construction.

`recipe_normalization_errors` merges two registries into one "verified" map,
then does `if ok: continue`. Adding the engine-derived registry to that map
this morning meant **registering a mesh as engine-derived exempted it from
the pivot gate entirely.** The two registries never carried the same
guarantee:

    BLENDER-NORMALISED   pivot is AT THE BASE by construction
    ENGINE-DERIVED       somebody MEASURED it; the pivot is where the
                         vendor left it

Blueberry is a grass species built from vendor `.uasset` meshes — precisely
the combination the hole was shaped for, found one working day after the hole
was made. Fixed by tagging provenance at merge time. Proven both directions,
positive control first.

**The general shape: a widening that looks like a convenience is a
weakening when the two things being merged carry different guarantees.** The
merge was written to stop a Fab rock being refused for lacking a Blender row
it can never have — a real and correct fix — and it silently took a second
check with it.

### AND A NULL COST THAT HAD TO BE DISPROVED BEFORE IT COULD BE BELIEVED

Frame cost came back GPU 7.74 against a 7.75 baseline: -0.01 ms, against a
+1.5 ms abort bar. **A zero delta is also exactly what "the grass never
spawned" looks like**, and this project has shipped invisible grass for two
sessions before. It was not accepted until the understory was on pixels at
the same station. The arithmetic then agrees: ~7,634 instances at ~500
triangles is ~3.8M against a 29.8M grass budget, which belongs under the
noise of a 300-frame mean. Recorded as "under the measurement floor", not as
"free".

## 2026-08-15 - D4: A BAND IS NOT A GRADIENT, AND ONE RAMP IS NOT A FOREST

The height band was a HARD window. Inside [120, 640] m every elevation was
equally likely, so the forest ran at uniform density to the top edge and
stopped dead. WORLD_VISION's complaint was UNIFORMITY as much as sparseness,
and no amount of raising density_per_hectare addresses that - it makes the
same flat forest thicker.

### THE PRIOR THAT SCALES, AND WHY THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT

placement_priors.centred_bias REDISTRIBUTES: wet ground gains exactly what
dry ground loses, mean preserved, because flow says WHERE trees prefer to
stand. Closure is a different KIND of fact. A subalpine stand genuinely thins
toward treeline - fewer trees, not the same trees moved uphill - and ends in
open krummholz. So closure_ramp SCALES, and the caller's count falls with
it.

That distinction had to be argued explicitly in the code, because the two
functions now sit side by side in the same module and look interchangeable.
Anything that preserved the mean here would describe a forest that does not
exist.

### ONE RAMP WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A SMALLER COPY OF THE SAME DEFECT

The instinct is a single closure ramp shared by every species. That thins all
four tiers together and yields a scale model of the uniform forest - the same
composition everywhere, just less of it.

Real stands change composition with elevation: the big crowns drop out first
and the last thing standing is stunted regeneration. So the falloff is
per-tier - canopy 1.00->0.15, sub-canopy ->0.30, saplings ->0.55 - and the
top of the band ends SAPLING-DOMINATED rather than empty. The acceptance
rates confirm it landed: 22.4% for the canopy against 30.0% for saplings,
from one shared mask and four different ramps.

### THE COUNT HAD TO BE RE-DERIVED, NOT CARRIED

A multiplier that scales cannot leave the density alone. Measured: at the
unchanged 68/ha, closure alone takes the plan from a uniform 153,796 to
111,079. 135/ha then gives 219,659 - the ruling's ~220,000 with a 30,341
reserve under the shared 250,000 ceiling. Deriving the density from the ramp
rather than guessing at it took one dry run, because the planner prints
counts before it places anything.

### AND A GATE THAT REFUSED THE WORLD, NOT THE WORK

save_level.py defaults to 
ecipes/alpine.json. Run without --recipe it
refused with exit 7 - "recipe targets '/Game/Alpine' but the editor has
'/Game/Alpine8K' open". That is not pedantry: the tool carries a package
ALLOW-LIST derived from the recipe, so it would have saved 219,659 instances
under a list scoped to a different world. The gate that looks like
bureaucracy on every green run is the one that matters on the red one.

+65,863 instances for +0.18 ms GPU, against an 11 ms abort bar and a 7.92 ms
reading. Cheap because the new tiers are light and carry imposter LODs -
which is the D2 intake paying for the D4 budget, and the reason the two were
ruled as one re-scatter.

## 2026-08-15 — THE FIRST PIE FRAME THIS PROJECT HAS EVER MEASURED, AND THREE THINGS THAT RETURNED SUCCESS WHILE DOING NOTHING

PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 1 asked for one PIE capture, on the grounds that every
performance number this project owns is editor-viewport class and four
variables change sign the moment a player exists. It is done, at three
stations, with two artefacts on disk. What it found about the WORLD is one
paragraph. What it found about INSTRUMENTS is most of this entry.

### THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE INSTRUMENT WAS BUILT

The whole design rests on Python remote execution continuing to answer while
a game world is ticking, and nothing in this repo recorded whether it does.
If it did not, an instrument built on it would not fail loudly - it would
HANG, which is the exact shape of the 2026-08-10 capture that ran fifteen
minutes with a live process and zero output.

So `probe_pie` asked that one question in isolation first. It answers: remote
exec responds during PIE with a 0.0 s round trip. Cheap, and it meant the
600-line instrument was written against a measured premise rather than a
hoped-for one.

### A GREP THAT COULD NOT MATCH, READ AS AN ANSWER

Searching the generated Python stub for the play API with the patterns
`editor_play`, `request_play` and `end_play` returned exactly one function:
`editor_play_simulate`. Read as an answer, that says **5.8 Python cannot
start real PIE, only Simulate** - and Simulate has no PlayerController and no
player camera, so every number would have belonged to a class nobody asked
for.

`editor_request_begin_play` (PythonStub 606201) matches none of those three
patterns. It was found by READING THE LINES AROUND THE HITS rather than
trusting the hit list.

This is the `LandscapeNanite.cpp` near-miss again, in a different container.
There the path did not exist; here the pattern could not match. **Both
produce a zero that reads as "looked and absent" when it is "could not
look"** - non-negotiable 6. The general form worth carrying: *a negative
result from a search is only evidence if the search could have found the
thing.*

### THE STATION SEQUENCE WAS WRONG IN TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, AND THE GATES
### CAUGHT BOTH

First run, all three stations refused. Neither refusal was a bug in the
gates; both were real.

**1. TRACING FOR GROUND BEFORE MOVING THE PAWN CAN NEVER HIT.** World
Partition streams around the PAWN. The pawn spawns at the world origin (the
level has no PlayerStart), and the station is 4.8 km away, so the region was
never loaded and the top-down collision trace hit nothing across a 6 km
span. **"Not streamed" and "there is no terrain here" produce the identical
answer**, and the tool correctly reported the raw fact - no hit - rather than
a Z it had invented. Fix: teleport to a perch first, wait for streaming, then
trace, then move to the real height.

**2. THE VIEW POINT READ BACK AS THE ORIGIN, AND IT WAS TELLING THE TRUTH.**
`get_player_view_point` returned [0,0,0] while the pawn's own location read
back exactly on target. `APlayerController::GetPlayerViewPoint` returns the
camera manager's CACHED point, gated on `GetCameraCacheTime() > 0` with the
engine's own comment *"Whether camera was updated at least once"*. Read in
the same payload as the teleport, it returns the cache from before the move -
the origin, where the pawn spawned. Fix: read it on a later tick.

**And this is precisely why the read-back is worth having.** The pawn's
location is the field the setter wrote; reading it proves only that the value
landed. The view point is a DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT - non-negotiable 8 - and it
is the one that would have caught a frame measured somewhere other than where
the station was declared. It fired on its first real use, on my own error.

### THE PLAN'S OWN CONSOLE COMMAND IS A SILENT NO-OP

PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 1 prescribes `CsvCategory VSM 1` and `CsvCategory
GPUScene 1` to turn on the default-off diagnostic categories. Run exactly as
written, across three stations, **every VSM column was absent from the CSV**
- and the tool reported them ABSENT rather than as zeros, which is the only
reason the difference was visible at all.

Root cause at `CsvProfiler.cpp:1138-1148`. `HandleCSVCategoryCommand`
compares the second argument against the literal words `enable` and
`disable`. `"1"` matches neither, so `bIsOperationValid` goes false and the
command falls through to a usage error **without enabling anything**. The
console command still returns normally. The correct form is
`CsvCategory VSM enable`.

Note also `:1152-1153`: with the argument OMITTED the command **toggles**. So
the bare form is not idempotent and a second run would switch the category
back off. The explicit word is required for pipeline rule 3, not only for
correctness.

Re-run with `enable`: all five VSM columns record.

**Three no-ops in one session - a grep that could not match, a trace that
could not hit, a command that could not enable - and all three returned
success.** The thing that made each one visible was refusing to print a
number the instrument had not actually obtained.

### WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT THE WORLD

Tag `pie001`, categories off, which is the clean cost run:

    station              GPUTime   GameThread   RenderThread   RHI
    forest_floor           7.816       7.198          5.309    2.779
    canopy_250m            5.082       7.084          5.198    2.765
    airship_1500m          3.404       7.022          5.055    2.523

**The control reproduces.** 7.816 ms against the editor series' 7.92 at the
same camera - inside the plan's +/-0.2 ms acceptance - even though the two
classes differ in streaming (4 resident landscape proxies against 256
force-resident), in FOV (90 in PIE against the recipe camera's 75) and in
having gameplay ticking. That agreement is worth more than it looks: it says
the GPU cost at this station is dominated by what is in frame and not by the
residency difference.

**GPU HALVES WITH ALTITUDE AND THE GAME THREAD DOES NOT MOVE.** 7.82 -> 5.08
-> 3.40 against 7.20 -> 7.08 -> 7.02. The game thread is a FIXED cost here,
and it is already 7 ms with **zero gameplay**: no AI, no enemies, one dynamic
instance. PHASE2_PLAN's headline risk was that the game thread binds before
the GPU. On this evidence it does, and the plan's own figure of 8.0 ms for AI
perception plus EQS at engine defaults would land the frame around 15 ms of
game thread against a 16.67 ms budget, before one enemy exists.

**Stated as a limit, because it changes what the number means:** PIE runs
inside the editor process, so this game thread carries editor overhead a
cooked build would not. **7 ms is an upper bound on the shipping figure, not
the shipping figure.** The decomposition needs a cook, which this project has
never produced and which is additionally mis-pointed - `GameDefaultMap` is
still Epic's template world.

### THE PAGE-POOL QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE PLAN NAMED THE WRONG FIELD

The plan says the discriminating field is `VSM/SinglePageCount` +
`VSM/FullCount` against the 2048-page pool, because page saturation and a
large instance count produce the same frame time and lead to opposite work.
The reasoning is right and the field is one step off: those two count shadow
MAPS, not pages (`VirtualShadowMapArray.cpp:2619-2620` wrap
`GetNumSinglePageShadowMaps` and `GetNumFullShadowMaps`). The direct measure
is `VSM/FreePages`, `VirtualShadowMapCacheManager.cpp:685`.

Measured, tag `pie002`: FreePages 1820 / 1978 / 2024 of
`r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages` = 2048. **Peak usage is 228 pages of
2048 - 11%.** Virtual shadow map pages are NOT the constraint at any of the
three stations, and no work should be aimed at them.

### THE DIAGNOSTIC CATEGORIES ARE NOT FREE, SO THE TWO TAGS ARE NOT ONE SERIES

Same station, same camera, same session, categories the only difference:

    forest_floor   GPUTime 7.816 (pie001)  ->  8.338 (pie002)   +0.52 ms

**Turning on the instrumentation costs about half a millisecond of GPU.** So
`pie001` is the cost measurement and `pie002` is the diagnostic measurement,
and a number may not be lifted from one into the other. This is R13's
calibration-class rule arriving one level down: the INSTRUMENT's own settings
are part of the class.

### ONE COLUMN THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE, AND IS THEREFORE NOT YET EVIDENCE

`SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances` read **284,424 at all three stations** in
`pie001`, and **284,424 / 4,264 / 4,264** in `pie002`. Same stations, same
order, same session. A statistic that disagrees with itself across two runs
is not a measurement of the world yet, whatever it is measuring.

**It is recorded here and deliberately NOT quoted as a finding.** The
plausible mechanism - it is declared `ECsvCustomStatOp::Accumulate`
(`SceneCulling.cpp:2676`), so what it means depends on how many times the
update ran in a frame - is an inference, and the honest position is that this
column needs its own single-variable run before anyone leans on it. Named so
that a later session does not discover the inconsistency by trusting it.

## 2026-08-15 — UNIT 2: A METRIC THAT DOES NOT MEASURE WHAT IT SOUNDS LIKE, AND A BAR WITH NO DENOMINATOR

PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 2 asked for one number: the fraction of the mount-profile
mask whose 1 m neighbour rise exceeds `MaxStepHeight` = 45 cm. The number is
**19.87%**. It is also close to meaningless, and the arithmetic that says so
is one line.

### THE METRIC CONFLATES RAMPS WITH LEDGES

    a 45 cm rise over a 100 cm cell is atan(0.45) = 24.23 degrees

The mount profile admits everything up to **35 degrees**, which is **70 cm of
rise per cell**. So every slope between 24.23 and 35 degrees trips the metric
**while being entirely walkable**. A character walks UP a walkable slope; it
does not step onto it. `MaxStepHeight` governs impacts with surfaces steeper
than the walkable floor, not the gradient of a ramp.

**And at 1 m per vertex the heightmap cannot express a step at all.** A step
is a rise over a SUB-METRE horizontal distance, and sub-metre horizontal
detail is below this map's Nyquist limit by construction. Every transition
this heightmap can represent is a ramp of some angle. So 19.87% is a
restatement of the slope distribution wearing a step-height label.

**Consequence worth carrying:** `MaxStepHeight` is not a TERRAIN constraint on
this world at this resolution. It becomes one only for PLACED geometry —
rocks, roots, stairs, a settlement's thresholds. Note also that Nanite
displacement (+/-0.4 m peak) does NOT create steps in collision: landscape
collision is the heightfield, not the displaced surface.

This is the same shape as the `Height 2500.0` trap and the misleading
denominator: **a number that is arithmetically correct and answers a question
nobody asked.**

### THE FINDING THAT MATTERS CAME FROM THE METRIC NOBODY ASKED FOR

Running `traversability()` alongside, because slope and connectivity are what
actually bind:

    profile  crossable      largest    regions      reachable
    walk        75.94%       72.03%      77479         94.84%
    mount       60.67%       17.75%     219828         29.26%
    climb       99.54%       99.51%       1523         99.97%

`recipes/alpine_8k.json` declares `world.primary_movement_mode: "mount"` and
`world.min_connected_frac: 0.8`. **Mount reads 29.26% — a FAIL by a factor of
nearly three, on the PRIMARY movement mode, across 219,828 disconnected
regions.** That is precisely the "a thousand isolated shelves" case
`traversability()`'s own docstring exists to catch.

### AND THEN THE CONTROL SAID IT WAS MOSTLY THE INSTRUMENT

219,828 regions is a suspicious number — it has the shape of salt-and-pepper
fragmentation, where isolated steep cells punch holes in a mask and
connected-component labelling counts every hole as a boundary. So the same
computation was repeated on box-reduced copies:

    cell        crossable    largest      regions    reachable
    1 m            60.67%     17.75%       219828       29.26%
    2 m            64.17%     21.36%        64546       33.28%
    4 m            68.57%     51.16%        14225       74.61%
    8 m            72.83%     68.75%         2340       94.39%

**Reachability goes 29% -> 94% and regions collapse 219,828 -> 2,340, on the
SAME TERRAIN.** The fragmentation is overwhelmingly an artefact of sampling
slope per 1 m cell, not a fact about the world.

**So the FAIL is withdrawn as a claim about the terrain** — and it must not
be re-raised by a later session reading only the first table.

### THE REAL DEFECT IS THAT THE BAR HAS NO DECLARED SCALE

`min_connected_frac: 0.8` is a threshold with **no stated cell size**, and it
was written for `recipes/alpine.json`, whose world is **4 m per vertex**. The
8K recipe inherited the number and not its denominator. At 4 m the same
terrain reads 74.61% — near the bar; at 1 m it reads 29.26% — nowhere near.
**Same world, same bar, opposite verdicts, and nothing in the recipe records
which one the bar meant.**

This is non-negotiable 22 (always state the denominator) meeting R13's
calibration class: **a threshold is only meaningful conditioned on the scale
it is evaluated at**, and a scale-free threshold silently changes meaning the
moment the map's resolution changes. The 8K re-terrain moved four
resolution-dependent parameters that "only ever had one value"; this is a
fifth, and it was missed because it lives in a BAR rather than in a
generator.

### THE PRINCIPLED FIX, RECOMMENDED AND NOT TAKEN UNILATERALLY

**The evaluation scale should be a physical property of the AGENT, not a
choice.** A mount occupies roughly 2-4 m of ground; slope sampled at 1 m is
finer than the agent can resolve, so evaluating rideability there asks
whether a horse can stand on a dinner plate. That makes the scale a
pass-independent physical quantity, which is exactly what non-negotiable 19
says must be declared once and read by every consumer — beside
`MOVEMENT_PROFILES`, not beside the bar.

Not applied unilaterally because it changes a gate's verdict, and a gate
whose bar moves to make a failing number pass needs the reasoning ratified
before the number, not after. **The number to beat is recorded here so the
ratification cannot be graded against a moving target.**

### THE CORRIDOR HALF WAS NOT MEASURED, AND SAYS SO

Unit 2's acceptance also wants the figure "restricted to the inter-massif
corridor". **The corridor has no spatial definition anywhere in this repo.**
`WORLD_VISION.md:304` defines it in prose as *"the primary traversal route"*
and gives no coordinates, no mask, no endpoints; nothing in `recipes/`
declares one. Inventing a rectangle and calling it the corridor would make
every number computed against it unfalsifiable, so it is reported as **I
COULD NOT LOOK** — which is not a pass. Closing it is one ruling from Ryan,
and it is the same open item as `WORLD_VISION.md:322`.

## 2026-08-15 — UNIT 3: 63,981 TREES THAT SAY "BlockAll" AND COLLIDE WITH NOTHING

PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 3 exists to check one thing before unit 6 spends a
session on it: do the scattered meshes actually carry simple collision. The
answer for three of the four instanced species is yes. For the largest one it
is no, and the way it is no is worse than absence.

    species         system      simple prims   nanite   tris LOD0
    Conifer         instanced        0          True       2335
    ConiferPine     instanced        2 sphyl    False     27824
    SpruceSub       instanced        1 sphyl    False     20695
    SpruceSapling   instanced        1 sphyl    False      2604

**`Conifer` is `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` at 63,981 instances — the largest
species in the world, and the 29.31 m hero spruce the whole forest was
re-adopted for on 2026-08-15.**

### THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY CHECK THAT WOULD BE RUN

Read straight off the loaded asset:

    body_setup            present          <- NOT null
    agg_geom box/convex/sphere/sphyl/tapered/levelset   0 0 0 0 0 0
    collision_profile     BlockAll         <- it already claims to block
    collision_trace_flag  CTF_USE_DEFAULT  <- simple and complex kept separate
    nanite                true

So: the mesh **has** a BodySetup. Its profile **already says BlockAll**. Unit
6 would set `QUERY_ONLY` + `BlockAll` on it, and every property read-back
would confirm the setting landed — because it did. And a line trace would go
straight through the trunk, because there is no geometry to hit.

This is "a value can arrive and still mean something else", in its purest
form. The setting is correct, present, and about nothing.

### AND THE PLAN'S OWN GUARD DOES NOT CATCH IT

PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 3 says that if the meshes have no simple primitive,
`CreateAllInstanceBodies()` returns early and unit 6 silently does nothing.
The citation is real and I opened it — `InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:2877-2882`:

    UBodySetup* BodySetup = GetBodySetup();
    if (!BodySetup) { UE_LOGF(... "unable to create InstanceBodies!"); return; }

**But that guard fires on a NULL BodySetup, not on an EMPTY one.** This mesh
has a BodySetup, so it sails past, bodies ARE created, and the engine logs
nothing at all. The plan expected a warning in the log that will never
appear.

So the question to ask an asset is not *"does it have a BodySetup"* but
**"how many elements are in its agg_geom"**. One is a pointer check the
engine does for you; the other is the fact you actually need. The tool asks
the second.

### WHY THIS ONE AND NOT THE OTHER THREE

It is the only Nanite mesh in the list, and the only one this project
EXPORTED rather than received. The other three ship from vendors with
author-made capsules. `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` came out of the
skeletal-to-static PVE export on 2026-08-15 (R-BAKE), and **that path does
not author simple collision.** Nothing in R-BAKE's verification asks whether
it did — the bake's gates all measured fidelity-to-source, which is exactly
the shape of the original armature defect the same export path produced.

**Generalisable:** an asset this project GENERATES has no vendor doing the
unglamorous parts. Every property a vendor would have authored is a property
our intake must check for, and the intake currently checks appearance.

### THE GOOD NEWS FOR THE FIX

`git check-ignore` says the mesh is **not** vendor content: it is ours and
tracked. So the capsule can be authored at source and committed, with none of
the Fab-boundary problem that makes a vendor edit vanish on re-download.

**NOT DONE, deliberately.** Authoring collision is unit 6's work, it mutates
an asset, and the capsule dimensions belong in a recipe declaration rather
than in my judgement. The plan is already explicit that the answer is one
authored capsule per trunk and **never** `UseComplexAsSimple` — which would
put a 2,335-triangle trimesh in the query scene for each of 63,981
instances.

### A STEP OF UNIT 3 THAT HAD NO TARGET

Unit 3's acceptance says `collision_prims` in the recipe "is superseded by it
with a note, exactly as `material_slots` was". There is nothing to supersede:
`collision_prims` appears only in `recipes/alpine.json`, the superseded 2017
recipe, and **zero of those entries name any of the four live meshes**.
`recipes/alpine_8k.json` declares no collision field on any species at all.

Recorded because "supersede X" quietly becoming "X was never there" is the
kind of step that gets ticked off rather than noticed.

## 2026-08-15 — UNIT 4: THE SKELETON WAS PROBED, AND THE HEADLINE ASSET COUNT SHRANK BY 60%

PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 4 re-runs the characters domain, whose first attempt
returned one sentence and let three other briefs fill the vacuum
incompatibly. Deliverable: `plans/characters_brief.md`. New instrument:
`scripts/probe_skeleton.py`, artefact `Free/_measured/skeletons.json`.

### THE PROBE CONFIRMED A RULING AND RETRACTED A RECORD

    asset                                bones  UE5 markers  verdict
    UE4_Mannequin_Skeleton                  68     0 of 4     UE4
    SK_Mannequin (/Game/Mannequin/)         68     0 of 4     UE4
    SK_Mannequin (GV pack)                 161     4 of 4     UE5
    SKM_Manny    (GV pack)                 161     4 of 4     UE5

Controls `pelvis` and `hand_l` pass on all four, which is what makes the
zeros a real absence rather than a broken probe.

`ASSETS.md` "UE template content" gives `Content/Mannequin` the role
*"mannequin is the retarget target for GASP"*. It is the **UE4** skeleton and
cannot be. Corrected by appending to `ASSETS.md`, not by editing the row —
the intake-time belief is part of the record.

**The mitigating detail is worth naming too:** that row's `verified` column
always read **NO**. The register was honest about its own confidence; what
was wrong was a role claim nobody had checked. A `verified: NO` row is a
promise to check, and this is the check arriving late.

### WHY A NAME IS NOT AN IDENTIFICATION

Both candidates are called some variant of "Mannequin", and the folder
literally named `Mannequin` is the UE4 one. Nothing in the naming
distinguishes them. The bone list is what animations actually bind to, and a
retarget aimed at the wrong skeleton fails **after** the animation budget has
been written against it.

Same class as `material_slots` and `collision_prims`: **a field that reads
like a measurement and was never one.**

### THE COUNT THAT SHRANK, AND THE EIGHT ASSETS FILED UNDER THE WRONG WEAPON

PHASE2_PLAN.md §3 advertises "~110 animations" as a headline reason
characters cost acquisition nothing. Measured on disk: **102 assets, 42.6 MB**
— and the composition matters far more than the count:

    Rifle     39    weapon-specific
    Pistol    29    weapon-specific
    Unarmed   28    usable
    Death      6    usable

**68 of 102 are shooter animations.** This is a melee and mounted RPG, so the
usable set is **42**, not 102 — a 60% haircut on the headline.

**And the 8 hit reacts are inside `Anims/Rifle/HitReact/`.** They are
upper-body reactions with nothing to do with rifles, but a session told "take
the Unarmed folder" misses all eight. Recorded because that is exactly the
shape of an instruction that gets followed correctly and still loses content.

What IS free and complete: 4 melee attacks (3-hit plus charged), 8-way walk,
8-way jog, jump/fall/land/dash/walljump, idle, a blendspace and an AnimBP.
Genuinely absent and named: **any mounted animation at all**, which matters
because `WORLD_VISION.md` ruling 2b sizes POI spacing against mounted speed.

### THE IN-PROJECT UE5 MANNY HAS NO PHYSICS ASSET, AND A BROKEN LOD CHAIN

    SKM_Manny (GV pack)   LOD  0        1        2       3
                        verts  48,779   48,779   14,962   7,525
                        physics asset: NONE

**LOD0 and LOD1 are identical.** A four-entry chain whose first reduction
reduces nothing is a three-entry chain paying for a fourth — and the first
step is normally the most valuable, because it fires soonest over the most
screen area.

**No physics asset means no ragdoll.** The only physics asset in the project
is bound to the **UE4** skeleton — which is the asset the `physics` brief's
P4 ragdoll design was built on, and it is the wrong skeleton by this probe.
So the ragdoll design was doubly wrong: wrong skeleton, and the right
skeleton has nothing.

**Both problems are solved by choosing the source rather than by fixing
anything.** The engine template set carries `PA_Mannequin`, three Control
Rigs, `SKM_Manny_Simple` and all 102 animations under the engine EULA. The
brief rules for migrating it. The LOD check must then be **re-run against
`SKM_Manny_Simple`** — the 48,779/48,779 result belongs to a mesh we are not
adopting and must not be carried forward as a fact about the one we are.

### A TRAP THE FIX CREATES

After migration the project holds **two** UE5 mannequin skeletons, both 161
bones, both plausibly named `SK_Mannequin`. Animations bound to one do not
play on the other, and the failure mode is a silent T-pose rather than an
error. Identical bone counts are **not** identity. `probe_skeleton` prints the
resolved skeleton path per mesh, which is the discriminating field;
`Skeleton.compatible_skeletons` (PythonStub 255051) is the mechanism if both
must exist. Preferred: do not keep both.

### AND ONE NUMBER DELIBERATELY NOT INVENTED

Unit 4's acceptance asks for a *proposed measurable* per-character cost. No
millisecond figure is given, because PHASE2_PLAN.md ruling 12 already records
that every per-domain allocation in the original briefs was PROPOSED and read
like a ruling. Adding a forty-third proposed millisecond would repeat exactly
the defect the plan called out.

Instead the brief specifies the experiment, and names the premise that must
be settled first: **Python's spawn functions target the EDITOR world, not the
PIE world** (`EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_class`, PythonStub
641645), and there is no reflected spawn into a running game world. Whether
transient editor-world actors are duplicated into PIE is unknown and decides
the whole approach — the same shape as `probe_pie` settling remote execution
before `measure_pie_cost` was written on top of it.
