# 2026-08-16 (night) — UNIT 6: NOTHING IN THIS WORLD COLLIDED BUT THE LANDSCAPE

**Session goal:** `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 — "trees stop him". It passes; the
route there found four defects the board did not know about, and one of them
is the same shape as the Pass 1 failure that started this project's whole
verification doctrine.

## THE BOARD SAID ONE MESH WAS BROKEN. FOURTEEN WERE.

`R-COLLIDE` and the campaign table both record unit 3's finding:
`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` — 63,981 instances, the largest species — has
**zero simple collision primitives**, and R-COLLIDE names it as *the* blocker
on unit 6. That finding is TRUE, it is a real defect, and it is **not the
blocker.**

Measured before anything was changed: **all fourteen `FT_*` foliage types read
`NoCollision`.** 219,659 trees and 13,515 rock instances were pass-through, and
so were the three tree species whose MESHES carry a perfectly good
vendor-authored trunk capsule (ConiferPine 2 sphyl, SpruceSub 1, SpruceSapling
1). **Authoring the missing capsule alone would have changed nothing
observable, and the session would have ended reporting a fix.**

Root cause at two source lines:

    InstancedFoliage.cpp:640   UFoliageType's constructor:
                               BodyInstance.SetCollisionProfileName(NoCollision)
    InstancedFoliage.cpp:1822  UpdateComponentSettings copies the foliage
                               type's BodyInstance onto the component
                               UNCONDITIONALLY — no "if changed" guard —
                               overriding the MESH's own BodySetup

and `place_foliage` contains **no occurrence of the string "collision" in any
form**. Nothing was set wrongly. Nothing was set at all.

**THE GENERAL RULE: A DEFAULT YOU NEVER NAMED IS A DECISION YOU NEVER MADE.**
Every other silent-default defect here had a value somebody typed — `t.MaxFPS`,
`CullDistance` 0, `sections_per_component`. This one had no value anywhere, so
no grep for a wrong number could find it and no review of the recipe would
notice an absence. The fix is therefore structural: `collision` is now a
REQUIRED key on every instanced species (schema v1.23), refused on grass, with
16 `prove_gates` probes holding the refusal. **An optional field with a
sensible default reproduces exactly the failure being fixed.**

The gate was positive-controlled before it was satisfied: on the unmodified
recipes it refused exactly 14 species — 4 in `alpine_8k`, 10 in `alpine` —
matching the 14 `FT_*` assets one for one, with zero errors on the two grass
species.

## TWO OBJECTS, AND ONLY ONE IS ON THE PATH

`Free/_measured/mesh_collision.json` reports `collision_profile` = `BlockAll`
for all six meshes. That artefact is correct and its number is useless for this
question: it reads the MESH's `BodySetup.default_instance`, while the runtime
component is overwritten from the FOLIAGE TYPE at `:1822`.

Non-negotiable 0 warns against two instruments that share a source. **This is
the mirror case: two instruments that describe DIFFERENT OBJECTS, one quoted as
an answer about the other.** `measure_foliage_collision` now prints both in one
table so the substitution cannot be made silently again.

## THE PLAN'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS SELF-CONTRADICTORY

`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 asks for `collision_enabled = QUERY_ONLY` together with
`collision_profile_name = BlockAll`. Those cannot both hold:

    BaseEngine.ini:3104            BlockAll declares CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics
    InstancedFoliage.cpp:806-812   UFoliageType::PostLoad -> BodyInstance.FixupData
    BodyInstance.cpp:4567          FixupData -> LoadProfileData, on EVERY load
    BodyInstance.cpp:4509          LoadProfileData -> UCollisionProfile::ReadConfig,
                                   which writes the PROFILE's CollisionEnabled,
                                   ObjectType and responses INTO the body instance

A foliage type saved as `BlockAll` + `QueryOnly` reads back correct **in the one
session where it cannot fail** and silently becomes `QueryAndPhysics` on the next
start. Fixed by making the contradiction unrepresentable: a project profile
`FoliageBlockQueryOnly` whose own `CollisionEnabled` **is** `QueryOnly`.

**AND THE OBVIOUS SHORTCUT WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE.** Leaving the profile as
`Custom` stops `ReadConfig` running — and inherits the response container
`NoCollision` left at construction, which `BaseEngine.ini:3103` shows sets
**`Visibility=Ignore` and `Camera=Ignore`**. Trees would have blocked movement
while being invisible to visibility traces: line of sight, AI perception,
weapon traces. **A walk test would have passed it.**

## `CustomNavigableGeometry = No` DOES NOT MEAN "KEEP IT OUT OF THE NAVMESH"

Per `NavRelevantInterface.h`, `No` means the custom callback is not called *but
the default collision export still runs*; `DontExport` is the value that
excludes. For an ISM the custom callback is `DoCustomNavigableGeometryExport`
(`InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:5435-5438`), which exports **per-instance
transforms** — the path that makes 63,981 instances navmesh obstacles at all.
`Yes` is the engine default (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:868`) and is correct. The
plan's `No` reads like a safety measure and would have removed the per-instance
export. **NOT APPLIED**; left at `Yes`, now declared rather than inherited, and
flagged for unit 8, which is the first thing that can test it against a built
navmesh.

## SIZING THE CAPSULE: THE OBVIOUS INSTRUMENT READ THE WRONG MESH

`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` is Nanite, and both
`ProceduralMeshLibrary.get_section_from_static_mesh` and GeometryScript's
`RENDER_DATA` LOD return the **Nanite fallback proxy**:

    SOURCE_MODEL    76,343 verts   z -0.58 .. 2731.07    x -375 .. 302
    RENDER_DATA      7,005 verts   z -10.50 .. 2901.53   x -511 .. 459

The fallback overstates the mesh by **6.6% in Z and ~36% in X**, and its low-Z
bands hold **1 to 8 vertices each**, giving radii scattered 7–63 cm with no
cylinder in them. That is "I could not look", not a radius, and it was one
sentence from being written down as one. `build_scale` is `[1,1,1]`, so these
are **different meshes, not one mesh in two unit systems** — checked, because a
6.6% gap invites exactly that assumption.

From `SOURCE_MODEL`: max **37.13 cm** in the 0–20 cm root flare, 28.6–34.6 cm
from 0.2 m to 3.2 m, r_p50 21–24 cm throughout. Declared **38.0 cm**. Physical
check: DBH 46–74 cm on a 29 m Norway spruce, which is right.

**AND A TIGHT REFERENCE CLASS WOULD HAVE BEEN 2x WRONG.** The three sibling
spruces' vendor capsules fit `r/h ~ 0.030` across 4.5 m, 16.7 m and 22.1 m —
three points, `r ∝ h^0.85`, a good fit. Extrapolated to 29.12 m: **78 cm**.
This mesh measures `r/h = 0.0120`. The vendor capsules are GAMEPLAY-FATTENED
VOLUMES, not trunks. **A tight fit across three samples says the samples agree
with each other, not that they measure the thing you want.**

## `FHitResult` IS OPAQUE IN 5.8 PYTHON, AND THE TEST GOT BETTER FOR IT

Enumerated after `component` raised: `component`, `distance`, `location`,
`time`, `normal`, `item` are *"protected and cannot be read"*; `hit_component`,
`hit_actor`, `impact_point`, `face_index`, `blocking_hit` are *"failed to find
property"*. **A trace tells Python hit-or-miss and nothing else.**

That forced a better instrument. A horizontal trace on alpine ground hits the
landscape readily (a 16 degree slope rises 86 cm over the 3 m approach), so
"something was hit" was never evidence. Every trunk trace now runs **twice —
the second time with every `InstancedFoliageActor` in `actors_to_ignore`** —
and counts only when the first HITS and the second MISSES. Terrain is hit by
both and counts as nothing. The capsule radius is measured by stepping the line
sideways until foliage stops being hit, which needs no distance field.

**That geometric method then recovered capsules it was never told about:**
implied unscaled radii of 55–63 / 45–57 / ~12–24 cm against the vendors'
62.79 / 52.81 / 16.30 cm. A measurement that independently reproduces three
numbers from a different source is worth more than the one it was built for.

## THE LAST DEFECT WAS A SAVE NOBODY ASKED FOR — AND IT IS PASS 1'S SHAPE AGAIN

With the foliage types cold-verified `QUERY_ONLY` / `FoliageBlockQueryOnly` and
the editor world proven to stop a trace on a trunk, **PIE still found zero
foliage hits across all four species over 4,659 loaded instances.** Measuring
the two worlds side by side:

    editor world components   QUERY_ONLY    FoliageBlockQueryOnly   BLOCK
    PIE world components      NO_COLLISION  NoCollision             IGNORE

`UpdateComponentSettings` runs at LOAD, so after the restart memory was
correct — **and a load-time fixup does not dirty the package it corrected.**
`get_dirty_content_packages()` returned **0** while 1,093
`InstancedFoliageActor`s held corrected components. The external actor packages
on disk still carried the OLD serialized `BodyInstance`, World Partition
streams PIE from those packages, and the game got `NoCollision`.

**A normal save would have written nothing and reported success.** The fix is
`save_foliage_actors.py`, saving with `only_dirty=False` — which is the entire
reason it exists rather than calling `save_dirty_packages`. 1,093 submitted,
**1,073 modified on disk**, confirmed by `git status` rather than by the tool.

This is Pass 1 wearing new clothes: **the artefact on disk disagreed with the
live editor, every asset-level check was green, and only a different
representation — the PIE world — could see it.** The difference is that this
time the question was asked in the same session rather than three days later.

## THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONE NUMBER THAT IS NOT PINNED

    Conifer         5/6 trunk hits    6/6 negative controls missed
    ConiferPine     6/6               6/6
    SpruceSub       5/6               6/6
    SpruceSapling   5/6               6/6

The one non-hit per species is a line with terrain on it, counted as neither
answer. Our own Conifer capsule brackets 0.1–1.4 cm **below** `38.0 x scale` on
3 of 4 samples — consistent with `align_to_normal: 0.15` tilting the capsule
axis (up to ~6 cm of lateral shift at the 1 m trace height on a 24 degree
slope) plus 2–5 cm offset granularity. **Consistent, not independently pinned,
and it should not be quoted as a verified radius.**

## A LESSON THAT EXISTED AND DID NOT FIRE

`ue_exec.py --timeout N` is a fixed DISCOVERY WINDOW, always spent in full.
That was written into this file **earlier the same day**, with the words "Use
12–15", and this session passed 120–180 anyway and paid minutes per call. The
narrative could not stop the hand that types the flag. Fixed where it fires:
the argument's help text now says so, and any value above 60 prints a note at
the point of use. **A lesson whose only home is a story is a lesson that
depends on somebody having read the story recently.**

# 2026-08-17 — UNIT 8: THE NAVMESH BUILDS, AND THE SAVE DEFECT CAME BACK IN SIX HOURS

**Session goal:** `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 8 — build ONE 1024 m navmesh chunk,
measure it, then decide. Built, measured, verified by query, both abort bars
passed by a wide margin.

    wall clock      30.0 s   (commandlet execution 20.18 s)     bar 30 min
    peak commit     19.6 GB  of a 223.4 GB limit                bar 200 GB
    packages        9.45 MB across 4 chunk actors + 9.56 MB navmesh actor

## THE PLAN WAS 7/7 THIS TIME, AND CHECKING IT WAS STILL RIGHT

Unit 6 taught that this plan's citations cannot be assumed, so every line of
unit 8's config table was opened first. All seven were exact —
`TileNumberHardLimit = 1 << 20` at `RecastNavMesh.cpp:551`, the ini defaults
at `BaseEngine.ini:3052-3063`, `NavigationDataBuilderLoadingCellSize =
102400*4` at `WorldSettings.cpp:122`, `bWholeWorldNavigable`'s commented-out
`UPROPERTY` at `NavigationSystem.h:368-371`, and `MaxTileGridWidth` with
**zero hits across all of `Engine/Source`**, exactly as the plan claimed.
One line number off by one.

**A plan being right seven times does not retire the check.** Two engine
facts it did NOT carry were both traps, and both were found by the same
reading:

- `GetClampedTileSizeUU` (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:75-81`) CLAMPS `TileSizeUU` to
  `CellSize * 1024`. A larger declared value is not the value that builds.
- `ARecastNavMesh::PostLoad` (`:963-1015`) FORCES `TileSizeUU` and
  `AgentMaxSlope` back to the class default when the voxel cache is on, with
  a warning and nothing else. Writing them onto an INSTANCE is silently
  reverted; writing them into config moves the CDO too, so the comparison is
  1600 against 1600 and cannot fire. **That is why these are ini values.**

## THE AGENT DOES NOT COME FROM THE NAVMESH

`AgentRadius=34` / `AgentHeight=176` written into
`[/Script/NavigationSystem.RecastNavMesh]` produced a CDO reading 34/176 and
an ACTOR reading **35/144**. Every other value on the actor was correct,
which is what made it convincing.

    NavigationSystem.cpp:2874-2875   NavData->SetConfig(SupportedAgents[0]);
    NavigationSystem.cpp:4729        Instance->SetConfig(NavConfig);

`SetConfig` overwrites the navmesh's agent dimensions from
`UNavigationSystemV1::SupportedAgents`, which was EMPTY — verified, no entry
anywhere in engine or project config — so `FNavDataConfig`'s fallbacks stood.

**THE CDO READ-BACK WAS GREEN OVER A VALUE THE BUILD WOULD NOT HAVE USED.**
Third time in two sessions that reading the object which ACTS rather than the
object which was WRITTEN found a real defect: foliage type vs component, mesh
BodySetup vs foliage type, and now navmesh CDO vs navmesh actor. The tool now
reads both and names the source line in the mismatch.

## AND THEN THE SAVE DEFECT CAME BACK, SIX HOURS LATER, IN A DIFFERENT SUBSYSTEM

With `SupportedAgents` declared and the editor restarted, the actor read
34/176 — correct — and the first headless build still produced a navmesh that
was **removed while it ran**, 166 times:

    LogNavigation: Warning: NavData RegistrationFailed_AgentNotValid, NavData
    instance contains navmesh that doesn't support any of expected agent types
    ...will be removed. This warning will disapear once the map is saved.

The actor was auto-created BEFORE `SupportedAgents` existed, so its
SERIALIZED config was still 35/144. `SetConfig` had corrected it in MEMORY at
load — which is exactly what the applier read and reported OK — and nothing
wrote it to disk. The commandlet loads from disk.

**In-memory correct, disk stale, consumer reads disk.** That is unit 6's
foliage-collision defect, the same shape, hours later, in an unrelated
subsystem. The same fix applies for the same reason: the load-time fixup does
not dirty the package it corrected, so `save_dirty_packages` writes nothing
and `only_dirty=False` is required.

**The general rule, now twice paid for: A LOAD-TIME FIXUP LEAVES NO TRACE
THAT IT HAPPENED. Whenever the engine corrects something on load, the
correction is in memory only, the package is clean, and anything that reads
the file — a commandlet, a cook, World Partition streaming, another
process — gets the stale value.** The tell is an engine message saying "this
will disappear once the map is saved"; that sentence means the disk and the
session disagree right now.

## A BUILD TOOL WHOSE EXIT CODE MEANS NOTHING

The commandlet exits **1 on both the broken and the healthy run.** The single
"error" is `LogHttpListener: Error: HttpListener unable to bind to
127.0.0.1:8000` — the IncrediBuild port conflict this project already
recorded, entirely unrelated to navigation. Warnings fell 166 → 2 between the
runs and the exit code did not move.

So the runner reports the exit code and REFUSES to conclude anything from it,
printing "read the log before concluding anything about cost". Success is the
log plus a projection query, never the return value. This is the
save-that-returned-True class arriving from the other side: a tool reporting
failure over work that succeeded.

## THE VERIFICATION AGREED WITH SOMETHING IT WAS NOT FITTED TO

    PlayerStart          (354600, -321400, 31139.5)
    projects to navmesh  (354600.0, -321400.0, 31020.1)
    difference           119 cm

`recipes/character.json` declares `spawn.height_above_ground_cm = 120`. The
navmesh surface under the spawn and the spawn's own declared offset agree to
**one centimetre**, by two completely different routes — a Recast voxelisation
of collision, and a number typed into a recipe weeks earlier. Corroboration
of that kind is worth more than either measurement alone.

Negative control: **0 of 4** points in other 1024 m cells project. The navmesh
is bounded by the declared volume rather than global, which is what makes
"it projected" a statement about this chunk.

## A COVERAGE NUMBER IS A PROPERTY OF THE QUERY

The first verification read **7/25** points projecting inside the cell, which
looks like a navmesh full of holes. It was the QUERY: a fixed z=33000 with a
±20 m tolerance cannot reach columns in a cell whose terrain spans 143 m.
Widening the tolerance to 120 m gives **25/25 on the same navmesh**. Nothing
about the navmesh changed. Had that 7/25 been written down it would have
started a hunt for a defect that does not exist.

## FOUR CHUNK ACTORS FOR "ONE CHUNK", AND IT IS ARITHMETIC

The declared volume IS cell (3,-4): its X and Y bounds are the cell
boundaries themselves, so it touches cells 2 and -3 along its edges and the
builder creates chunk actors for all four. Their sizes say which is real —
9526.6 KB against 76.7 / 74.0 / 4.2 KB.

## WHAT WAS NOT ESTABLISHED, STATED PLAINLY

The builder iterated **81 loading cells** to produce navmesh in one, so the
20 s is NOT one sixty-fourth of a whole-world build — most iterations had
nothing to do. Extrapolating a world figure from it is the
misleading-denominator class and is not done here.

What the config change DOES establish is that a whole-world build is legal at
all: at `TileSizeUU` 1600 and 1.5 layers a world-sized volume needs **388,622
tiles** against the 1,048,576 hard limit, where the engine defaults needed
~1.99M and would have silently CLAMPED. The standing 1.89× overflow is now a
`prove_gates` refusal rather than a note — and it was never reachable before,
because there were zero bounds volumes and therefore no navmesh grid at all.

## A UNIT ERROR I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT THE SAME HOUR

I named the recipe key `min_region_area_uu2`. `RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5267`
computes `rcSqr(MinRegionArea / CellSize)` — divide by cell size, and only
THEN square — so the engine property NAMED `MinRegionArea` is a LINEAR uu
dimension, and 400 discards islands smaller than 400×400 uu = 16 m², not
400 cm². Renamed to `min_region_dimension_uu`, with the derivation in the
refusal message.

That happened in the same session that logged a lesson about values arriving
meaning something other than they read. **Writing the lesson does not
inoculate the author against the defect; only checking the source does.**

# 2026-08-17 — THE HERO FACE NEEDED AN INSTRUMENT BEFORE IT NEEDED A FIT

Ryan ruled out both cheap capture routes before I could reach for them, and
the reasoning is the whole lesson: hand screenshots are out because
**framing drift between shots is indistinguishable from joint movement**, and
offline rasterisation is out because **it renders exported geometry, not the
assembled post-import character**. So the first deliverable of a face-fitting
pipeline is not a fit. It is a camera that cannot lie.

Building it produced five failures, and every one of them was found by
looking at an artefact rather than by reading a return value.

## THE FIRST WORKING RENDER WAS THE BACK OF THE HEAD

Four exposure sweeps, a near-clip check and a post-process bypass all failed
to explain a pure-white 2048 square frame. The cause was none of them:
`SceneCaptureComponent2D.always_persist_rendering_state` was FALSE, so every
`capture_scene()` began with **no rendering history**, and the MetaHuman
face's virtual textures (`MID_MI_Face_Skin_Baked_LOD*_VT_*`) never left their
white fallback. Setting it True and taking ten captures:

    before   mean 254.85   min 239   nonwhite 0.027
    after    mean 161.90   min   0   nonwhite 1.000

Converged by 10 frames, stable through 120.

**AND THE FIX IMMEDIATELY EXPOSED THE NEXT ERROR, WHICH NO STATISTIC WOULD
HAVE.** The now-real frame had mean 161.7, std 92.8, full 0-255 range — every
number said "a photograph" — and MediaPipe still found no face. A 512 px
preview settled it in one look: **the back of a head, in silhouette, ears
either side.** Azimuth 270 was behind the subject, and it had been *selected*
by the search because every candidate frame was white and rejected for the
wrong reason. Non-negotiable 10 exactly: inspect the artefact before running
a statistic on it.

## A LIGHT RIG THAT WAS NEVER BUILT, AND SAID IT WAS

The same frame was a silhouette because the three-point rig was ~10 lux
against Alpine8K's 130,000 lux sun. I had written:

    _c.set_editor_property("intensity_units", _u.LightUnits.LUX)
    _c.set_editor_property("intensity", intensity)

`ELightUnits` has **no LUX member** — `DirectionalLightComponent.cpp:1509`
returns `ELightUnits::Unitless /* Lux */`, because a directional light's
units are fixed and there is nothing to select. The AttributeError was raised
**while evaluating the argument**, so the intensity line beneath it never
ran, and the builder's report listed the actor as created with a note beside
it. A note is not a refusal. The frame that then passed the gate was lit by
the level's own sun, and I would have recorded that as "the rig works".

**A PROPERTY SET IS NOT A PROPERTY LANDED.** Both builders now read the
intensity back and RAISE on mismatch, which is non-negotiable 8 applied to
the cheapest possible case.

## `Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)` — THE THIRD INSTANCE IN THIS PROJECT

The manifest stores the locked camera as `[pitch, yaw, roll]`, and I passed
those three positionally into `unreal.Rotator`, which takes **roll first**
(PythonStub:66750). The camera came out pitched -90 degrees — looking at the
ground — and the light rig had its pitch in the roll slot the whole time.

This is recorded twice already: once as `Rotator(0.0, YAW, 0.0)` setting
PITCH 135 and putting a camera 88 cm below its pawn, once as the 2026-08-12
finding in its own right. **It recurred anyway, in a file written by an
author who had read both entries the same day.** What caught it was not
memory: it was the read-back assertion, which printed

    camera rot.pitch read back -90.000000, manifest says 0.000000
    camera rot.yaw   read back   0.000000, manifest says -90.000000

and refused to capture. That is the shape of the general defence — the
argument order cannot be remembered reliably, so nothing is allowed to
depend on remembering it.

## THE CAMERA MUST NOT BE A FUNCTION OF THE SUBJECT

The stage builder derives the camera from `get_actor_bounds`, which is right
for searching the framing and catastrophic for everything after: a joint edit
changes the head's bounds, the camera moves, and camera movement is exactly
the confound Ryan ruled out. The comparison instrument (`capture_shot.py`)
therefore **sets the transform absolutely from the manifest and reads it
back**, and reads no property of the subject at all. Preferring a state that
cannot express the bad value over a check that catches it — non-negotiable 3.

## A NOISE FLOOR AT n=2 UNDERSTATED ITSELF BY 3x

Two captures of the unchanged character gave per-landmark p90 **0.00240**
interpupillary units. Rerunning the identical test gave **0.00374**. At n=4,
comparing all six pairs:

    a-b  p90 0.00758      a-c  p90 0.00559      a-d  p90 0.00301
    b-c  p90 0.00305      b-d  p90 0.00514      c-d  p90 0.00450

The worst pair is **3.2x the best**, and the original n=2 answer was near the
bottom of that spread. **The bar adopted is the WORST pair, not the mean** —
a floor that averages away its own bad case is a floor a real delta can hide
under. Final: p90 0.00758 IPD = **0.057 cm**, max 0.0114 IPD = 0.086 cm, via
a pinhole scale of 0.01745 cm/px labelled APPROXIMATE because the irises sit
nearer than the orbit centre the distance is measured to.

This reproduces the project's standing finding that a noise floor is a
property of a scene and its settings and is not a constant — here at n=2 vs
n=4 rather than across worlds. **Against this bar the axis test's 2.0 cm
joint move should read ~0.27 IPD, about 35x p90.** If it does not, the DNA
write did not reach the mesh, and that is the question the test exists to
answer rather than a threshold to be relaxed.

# 2026-08-17 (later) — THE FIRST DNA WRITE, AND THE PREMISE IT REFUTED

The mission brief fixed Pass 1 as "joints-first likeness fitting: edit ONLY
neutral joint translations". Before writing anything I read the engine source
and predicted the opposite of the brief: `USkelMeshDNAUtils::UpdateJoints` is
commented *"Updates bind pose using joint positions from DNA"*
(SkelMeshDNAUtils.cpp:79) and ends with

    InSkelMesh->GetRefBasesInvMatrix().Reset();
    InSkelMesh->CalculateInvRefMatrices();

so the inverse-bind matrices are recomputed FROM THE NEW BIND POSE while the
stored vertex positions are untouched. My reasoning: at the reference pose the
skinning matrix is NewRef * inverse(NewRef) = identity, so a joints-only write
is invisible.

**I put it to a render and the render refuted me.** The head left the frame
entirely. The step I got wrong is that the COMPONENT does not pose from the
mesh's reference skeleton — it poses from the USkeleton asset
(`Face_Archetype_Skeleton`). Change the mesh's bind pose alone and the two
stop cancelling, so the skin flies. **A source reading is a hypothesis. This
one was specific, mechanical, and wrong at exactly one step, which is the
kind of wrong that reads as certainty.**

## THE REAL FINDING: THE EXPORTED DNA IS NOT IN THE MESH'S SPACE

The write was innocent, and a control proved it. Applying the **unedited**
canonical DNA — the same file the character was exported to — does the same
thing:

    spine_04 (the DNA root, parent to itself)
      DNA file            (0, 120.0077,   4.3415)
      mesh ref skeleton   (0,   4.3415, 120.0077)

An exact Y/Z swap, to four decimals on both non-zero components. The subject's
bounds swap with it: extent [18.72, 10.86, 26.28] becomes
[16.21, 26.20, 10.73]. **The DNA is Y-up; the mesh is Z-up; and `UpdateJoints`
applies `GetNeutralJointTranslation` RAW, with no conversion.** So does
`UpdateBaseMesh` — `Vertex.Position = FVector3f{ GetVertexPosition(...) }`,
no swizzle either.

My +2.0 cm edit landed perfectly through all of this: joint 804 FACIAL_C_Jaw
went -0.106097 -> 1.893903 on X, self-verified against a re-load of the
written file. The DNA write path is sound. **It is the APPLY that is in the
wrong coordinate system.**

## WHY THAT IS A ONE-WORD BUG, AND THE WORD IS THE FUNCTION NAME

`DNAUtils.h` declares two families that differ only in verb:

    LoadDNAFromFile(Path, FDNAConfig)     <- what I used. Raw.
    // To be used as legacy (returning FLegacyDNAReader)
    ReadDNAFromFile(Path, Layer, MaxLOD)  <- the swizzling one

and `DNAReader.h:39-44` says `FLegacyDNAReader` *"applies the legacy Maya->UE
coordinate swizzle on geometry queries regardless of FDNAConfig"*. Load
versus Read. Nothing in either name says which one moves the head.

**Stated plainly: the legacy adapter is NOT yet confirmed to be the fix.** Its
joint conversion is `(x, -y, z)` and its rotation conversion `(-y, -z, x)`
(LegacyDNAReaderAdapter, GetNeutralJointTranslation / GetNeutralJointRotation),
and `(x, -y, z)` is not the Y/Z swap that was measured. So there are three
candidate readers and the measurement does not yet pick one:

    file    LoadDNAFromFile          measured WRONG for this asset
    legacy  ReadDNAFromFile          conversion does not match the measurement
    mesh    GetDNAReader(SkelMesh)   the DNA the mesh already CARRIES

The third is the live hypothesis: `export_dna` plausibly writes a DCC-space
file for a Maya round trip, and the mesh's attached DNA is the one in the
mesh's own space. **A DNA DECLARES ITS OWN AXES** — `FCoordinateSystem` of
`EDirection` {Left, Right, Up, Down, Front, Back}, `DNACommon.h:47,268` — so
this does not have to be inferred from a magnitude at all. The wrapper now
takes a `ReaderSource` and reports what the reader declares.

## THE POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED FIRST, AND ITS FAILURE WAS THE INSTRUMENT
## TELLING ME SOMETHING TRUE

The first control nudged the subject actor 0.2 cm sideways — about 0.027 IPD
against a p90 floor of 0.0066, which should have been 4x. It read **0.9x the
floor**: indistinguishable from noise.

That is not a broken instrument. The landmark frame is IRIS-CENTRED and
IPD-SCALED, so a rigid translation of the whole head **cancels out of it
exactly**. The metric is translation-invariant by construction — which is
precisely the property that makes it immune to the framing drift that ruled
out hand screenshots in the first place. An X-scale cancels too, because the
IPD that normalises the frame is itself measured along X.

**The control has to be a SHAPE change.** A Z-scale of 1.02 reads 5.4x the
floor, MOVED, and scaling back returns to 1.1x. **A control that fails can be
the instrument working correctly on the wrong stimulus, and the way to tell
is to know what your metric is invariant to.**

## TWO SAFETY RESULTS WORTH KEEPING

**The restore route is not the one the plan assumed.** The axis test's
restore arm re-applies the canonical DNA — which, given the above, would have
"restored" the damage rather than undone it. What actually restores is
`EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.reload_packages([pkg], ASSUME_POSITIVE)`:
nothing was ever saved, so the bytes on disk are still the assembled hero.
Probes came back to (-0.1066, 3.985, 162.3585) and bounds to
[18.724, 10.859, 26.277], exactly baseline. **Never INTERACTIVE** — a modal
blocks the game thread, which is the only channel that could report it.

**A probe was dirtying the package.** `ApplyDNAToSkeletalMesh` called
`Modify()` and `MarkPackageDirty()` unconditionally, so a read with every
stage switched off left a Save Content modal waiting at the next editor
close. Now guarded on whether any stage will actually mutate. A read-only
call that dirties is the same class as a check that consumes the value it is
verifying.

# 2026-08-17 (later still) — THE SANCTIONED DNA PATH, AND THREE FALSE READINGS BEFORE THE TRUE ONE

Ryan ruled `import_from_face_dna` and closed the hand-derived conversion
route, on reasoning worth keeping: UpdateJoints failed the identity round
trip on all three readers, so deriving a swizzle to make it agree with the
mesh would be **calibrating the instrument to the answer**, and even a
perfect result would be a coincidence we would then trust. He also required
one cheap check before accepting the body-type lock the manifest warned
about.

## THE CHECK PAID FOR ITSELF: FACE-ONLY IMPORT EXISTS

The reflected docstring for `import_whole_rig` says that when unchecked
*"the head DNA file will only be used for neck alignment"*. **The code says
otherwise.** `MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem.cpp:6647-6656`, the false
branch:

    FFitToTargetOptions FitToTargetOptions{ AlignmentOptions, true,
                                            !bIsolateHeadFromBody };
    const bool bFitted = FitToFaceDna(InMetaHumanCharacter, InFaceDna, ...);
    if (bFitted) { CommitFaceState(...); }

The SAME `FitToFaceDna` as the whole-rig branch, and `FitToFaceDna` itself
(`:6504-6520`) calls `FaceState->FitToFaceDna(...)` then `ApplyFaceState`.
That is a genuine parametric fit of the face. What `bImportWholeRig` adds is
`CommitFaceDNA` — baking the rig, which is what fixes the body type.

**So the import runs face-only and NOTHING is locked.** A docstring is a
claim; the code is the contract. This is the second time in two days that a
reflected doc has been wrong about this subsystem in a way that would have
cost a permanent, irreversible decision.

## THE RENDER LOOP DOES NOT NEED AN ASSEMBLE

`import_from_face_dna` moves the parametric STATE. The assembled
`/Game/MetaHumans/...` meshes only move on a full Assemble — which needs a
rig, writes 252 packages, and has hung this editor on memory once. Far too
heavy for a compare loop.

`assemble_for_preview` plus `spawn_meta_human_actor(keep_transient=True)`
give a transient 875-bone Face mesh, and its bounds are IDENTICAL to the
assembled mesh's — origin `[0.0, 2.697, 250151.053]`, extent
`[18.724, 10.859, 26.277]`. So pointing the stage at it keeps the locked
camera, the locked lights and the measured floor without re-framing anything.

## THREE FALSE READINGS, IN ORDER, AND WHAT EACH ONE WAS

The identity arm read **0.68x (pass)**, then **7.50x (fail)**, then
**0.35x (pass)**, then finally **1.13x (pass)** once the instrument was
fixed. Every number was correctly computed. Three of them were about
something other than the import.

**0.68x** — the baseline happened to be captured from an already-settled,
already-preview-assembled state, so the import genuinely changed nothing.
Right answer, lucky conditions.

**7.50x** — the baseline was taken straight after a restore. **A freshly
reloaded character renders a FACETED, UNRESOLVED PREVIEW**: pointed crown,
polygonal facets, an asymmetric open mouth. It resolves into a proper head
after further assembles. The frames settled it in one look; the statistic
never could have. I was one sentence from recording "importing the unedited
canonical DNA changes the face" as a finding about the DNA pipeline, when it
was a finding about my own capture procedure.

**0.35x** — a real result: the import IS idempotent. Importing the canonical
DNA onto an already-imported state changes nothing. But it was measured to
test a hypothesis (idempotent-but-not-identity-from-disk) that turned out to
be the wrong explanation for the 7.50x.

**1.13x** — the true one, with baselines that are required to reproduce.

**THE RULE THIS BUYS: A CAPTURE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT UNTIL IT REPRODUCES.**
Baselines and post-import renders now shoot repeatedly, re-assembling
between, until two CONSECUTIVE renders agree inside the noise floor, and
exit 9 rather than return an unsettled frame. On the passing run the machine
printed its own working:

    baseline  settle 1: 7.66x floor   <- rejected
              settle 2: 0.86x floor   <- accepted
    after     settle 1: 0.43x floor   <- accepted
    delta     0.00947 IPD = 0.0709 cm = 1.13x floor   PASS

The noise floor already had a homogeneity gate that would have caught this.
**A single baseline capture had no such check** — the guard existed and did
not cover the place the defect appeared, which is non-negotiable 4's sweep
problem in miniature.

## THE COLD SESSION HAS ITS OWN CONVERGENCE, AND IT IS NOT THE WARM-UP

Separately and earlier: the first noise floor taken after a stage build split
into two clusters — p90 **0.0722** across them against **0.0032** within, a
22.6x spread — and an immediate re-run gave **0.0078** across all six pairs
at a 2.18x spread. A spread like that is a STEP, not noise: something changed
mid-run, and the worst pair would be measuring that change rather than the
instrument. The floor now settles first and REFUSES above a 4x pair spread.

**And a floor must contain every operation the comparison contains.** The
arms run an `assemble_for_preview` between the two compared renders, so the
floor now does too. It came out at 0.00835 against 0.00919 without — which
also establishes that the preview assemble is deterministic.

## A UNIT I INVENTED IN MY OWN REPORT

I printed `compare_face_state`'s tolerance as centimetres. **It is not a
distance.** The API documents it only as "vector norm" over vertices AND
vertex normals, and normals are unit-ish quantities whose differences do not
map to a length. It read NOT-within-1.0 on a face whose render had moved
0.043 cm — and 1 cm of surface would be over 57 px at this scale, unmissable.
Same contamination class as the 2026-08-03 sampler claim: an unverified unit
in our own output, in the one place that is supposed to be checkable.

## THE FINDING THAT REACHES THE STRATEGY

Measured with the settling instrument, both arms sit AT the floor and are
indistinguishable from each other:

    identity, UNEDITED canonical DNA          1.13x floor
    +2.0 cm on FACIAL_C_Jaw X, joints only    1.26x floor

Each rejected an unresolved first baseline on the way — 7.66x and 7.73x —
which is the same artefact that, before the fix, had produced a confounded
7.50x against 7.48x. **The joint edit contributes nothing the import does not
already do.**

That is consistent with what `FitToFaceDna` does: it fits the parametric face
state to the DNA's GEOMETRY. A neutral-joint-translation edit leaves the
geometry untouched, so there is nothing for the fit to see.

**So "joints-first" is invisible through the sanctioned path as well, for a
different and more fundamental reason than it was through UpdateJoints.**
Pass 1 must edit VERTEX POSITIONS — `DNACalibSetVertexPositionsCommand`,
which ships in 5.8 and needs a wrapper beside the existing joint-translation
one. That is a change to the ruled strategy and is Ryan's to make.

# 2026-08-17 (night) — GEOMETRY MOVES THE FACE. THE FIRST REAL EDIT.

Ryan rescoped Pass 1 to GEOMETRY-FIRST and approved the
`SetVertexPositions` wrapper. This is the first DNA edit in this project
that has ever changed the rendered face, and it is measured, not asserted.

    EDIT   1,661 of 24,049 vertices of head_lod0_mesh, -2.00 cm in DNA Y
           (down), selected by a declared box in the DNA's OWN space
    RENDER 7.09x the noise floor, both settles clean (0.30x, 0.33x)

## THE ATTENUATION, WHICH IS THE POINT

    region        dx_cm     dz_cm    |d|_cm
    chin         +0.031    -1.299     1.299
    jaw_L        +0.076    -0.890     0.894
    jaw_R        -0.038    -0.793     0.794
    cheek_L      -0.105    -0.498     0.509
    cheek_R      +0.101    -0.424     0.436
    nasion       +0.024    -0.343     0.344
    mouth        +0.052    -0.117     0.128
    forehead     -0.073    -0.044     0.085
    nose_tip     +0.041    -0.028     0.050
    eye_inner_L  -0.038    -0.010     0.039

    CHIN vertical -1.299 cm against a commanded -2.00 cm
    ATTENUATION    0.650

**0.65 is the first entry in the gain table.** Ryan's reasoning for staying
on the fit path predicted exactly this: the model's resistance is not a
blocker, it is a measured gain term, and the loop calibrates against it.
To land 2.0 cm of chin, command about 3.1.

**THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS BUILT INTO THE SAME MEASUREMENT.** Forehead
0.085 cm, nose tip 0.050, eye 0.039 — all at or below the floor of 0.083.
Nothing moved where nothing was commanded, and the falloff is monotone from
chin outward. That is what makes this a regional edit rather than a global
one, and it is the discriminating half of the result: a fit that had simply
rescaled the head would have moved the forehead too.

## THE HARD BOX LEAVES A SEAM, AND THE FRAME SHOWED IT

The render has visible vertical streaks on the chin. The edit applied a
UNIFORM delta with a HARD CUTOFF at the box boundary, so the vertices just
inside moved 2 cm and their neighbours just outside moved none. The fit
smooths this but does not remove it.

`FDNACalibSetVertexPositionsCommand` takes an optional per-vertex MASK
(`SetMasks(TArrayView<const float>)`), which is the mechanism for a feathered
falloff. **The next edit uses a mask; a box is a selection, not a brush.**
Recorded from the frame rather than anticipated — the statistic was clean and
would never have shown it.

## WHAT THE REFUSALS COST TO PROVE: NOTHING, AND ALL FIVE FIRE

Exercised live before first use, as ruled:

    missing input file        REFUSED
    in-place overwrite        REFUSED
    mesh index out of range   REFUSED   "MeshIndex 9999 is outside [0, 50)"
    degenerate box            REFUSED
    box selects nothing       REFUSED   and it names the DNA's declared axes

The last one matters most: a box that selects nothing would otherwise write a
DNA byte-identical to its input and report success — the false audit trail
that this whole geometry route replaces. And because the box is in the DNA's
space and not UE's, "selects nothing" is the failure a caller will actually
hit, so the refusal prints the declared axes rather than just complaining.

## A SELF-VERIFY THAT CHECKS THE UNTOUCHED VERTICES TOO

DNACalib replaces every position of the mesh at once, so read-all /
modify-some / write-all is the only correct shape. Verifying only the 1,661
selected vertices would not establish that the other 22,388 were carried
through rather than defaulted, so the wrapper re-reads the written file and
checks a sample of UNSELECTED vertices as well. It reported
"self-verified 1661 selected and 512 untouched vertices".

## A NOISE FLOOR BELONGS TO ITS SESSION, AGAIN

This session's floor came out at p90 **0.01114** IPD = 0.0833 cm, against
0.00835 in the previous editor session and 0.00758 before that. Same stage,
same script, same subject — different process. Every arm is judged against
the floor measured in its own session, which is R13's calibration class
applied to a landmark instrument instead of a GPU timing.

## AN ARGUMENT PARSER READ A COORDINATE AS A FLAG

`--box-min "-12,148,4"` exits 2 with no message: argparse takes a value
beginning with `-` as an option. `--box-min=-12,148,4` works. Trivial, and
worth the line because the failure is silent under `2>$null` and looks like
the tool doing nothing.

# 2026-08-17 (late night) — THE HARD BOX WAS MEASURING ITSELF

Ryan ruled feathering BEFORE gain calibration, on reasoning that turned out
to be worth 66%: a hard-box edit **changes the regional attenuation it is
supposed to measure**, because seam vertices drag their unmoved neighbours
through skinning and the fit. A boxed number is the attenuation OF A BOXED
EDIT. Calibrating gains against seamed edits would have baked the selection
artefact into every entry in the table.

**Same region, same -2.00 cm command, the only change being the mask:**

    selection            weighted   core    chin moved   attenuation   x floor
    hard box                1,661   1,661     1.299 cm      0.650         7.09
    + 2.5 cm smoothstep     6,703   1,661     2.155 cm      1.078        21.16

**0.650 -> 1.078.** The feathered chin slightly OVERSHOOTS its command where
the boxed one fell 35% short, and the signal is three times larger. The
render confirms the mechanism: the vertical streaks on the chin are gone and
the elongation is smooth and continuous.

**Gain-table entry #1 is 1.078, and it carries its mask.** Attenuation is a
property of (region x mask), not of region alone, so the manifest stores the
box, the band, the falloff shape, the command and the measured result
together. The boxed 0.650 is kept beside it marked PROVISIONAL BY
CONSTRUCTION — a gain number without its selection method is not a gain
number.

## THE MASK SEMANTIC WAS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED

`FDNACalibSetVertexPositionsCommand` takes a per-vertex mask, and I inferred
that `Interpolate` lerps: result = original + (new - original) * mask. That
is an inference about someone else's code, so the wrapper offers every vertex
`original + Delta` with mask = weight and then **re-reads the written file and
checks against `original + Delta * weight`**. It reported "self-verified 6703
weighted (against original + Delta*w) and 512 zero-weight vertices". A
different semantic would have failed loudly instead of producing a
differently-shaped edit that still looked plausible.

## A PREVIEW ACTOR'S BOUNDS ARE POLLUTED, AND THE NUMBER SAID SO

Rendering the hero for a look, `get_actor_bounds` on the spawned MetaHuman
preview actor returned extent Z **250,090** — half a million centimetres.
A component (Niagara, or a groom) does NOT follow `set_actor_location` and
stays at the world origin, so the bounds span from the origin to the actor.
The head "centre" computed from that lands at Z 500,168 and the camera aims
at empty sky.

This project's record already carried "the preview mesh's components sit at
world origin and do not follow set_actor_location" from 2026-08-16, filed
under a different symptom. **Derive the head target from the actor's own
LOCATION plus a known head height, never from its bounds** — and the tool now
reports `bounds_are_polluted` rather than quietly using them.

## WHAT THE HERO PREVIEW SHOWS

Three angles at 60/90/120 degrees, full preview actor with everything
visible: body, clothing, and the stubble groom reading clearly on the jaw.
**The HAIR groom does not render** — he reads bald. `GroomComponent` is
present and the beard shows, so the components work; this is consistent with
the standing note that all four groom BINDING assets failed to build
("guide roots are not close enough to the target mesh"). Not investigated
here; recorded so nobody reads the bald head as a missing selection.

# 2026-08-18 — THE FIT CONVERGED ON A BEARD

The likeness loop was built, run to convergence, and was measuring the wrong
thing the entire time. The number fell 88% and the face got worse. Both of
those are true and they are the same finding.

## THE DEFECT, AND IT WAS IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN RECORD ALL ALONG

`manifest.json` carries, written by an earlier session:

    _reference_image_choice: "The BALD frontal is the SHAPE input, per
    hero/reference/README.md: hair adds false volume at the cranium and a
    beard adds it at the mandible, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHERE THIS PIPELINE
    MEASURES. The haired frontal is Ryan's ruled APPEARANCE target and is
    used for grooming decisions, not geometry."

`paths.reference_image` obeys it and points at `hero_face_bald_frontal.jpg`.
**`fit.reference_image`, which I added when adopting Ryan's "Hero Example
Pic", points at the haired and bearded image.** Every jaw and cheek target
the fit chased was partly stubble.

MEASURED, bald target against bearded target, same instrument:

    jaw_width     +0.570 cm        chin_height   -0.514 cm
    cheek_width   +0.202 cm        eye_spacing   +0.128 cm

**About 1.29 cm of a 2.616 cm starting residual was BEARD, not skull.** And
the consequence is visible in the result: measured against the CORRECT
target the fitted hero's jaw is 0.482 cm TOO WIDE and his chin 0.343 cm TOO
LONG. The loop did exactly what it was told and widened a face to match
facial hair.

**A rule that exists in the file you are editing does not enforce itself.**
The manifest stated the constraint, in the same document, forty lines above
the field that violated it. I read the file to add a block and did not read
the block already there. This is non-negotiable 9 -- before writing "as
recorded in X", open X -- failing in the smallest possible radius: X was
open.

**AND IT WAS NOT FOUND BY ANY GATE.** Every instrument agreed the fit was
converging, because the fit WAS converging, on the target it had been given.
It was found by a design review reading the project's own records.

## WHAT THE SESSION ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, WHICH IS A LOT

The loop is real: measure a reference, edit MetaHuman geometry through
UE's own sanctioned import, render on a locked calibrated camera, re-measure,
correct the gain, iterate. 2.616 -> 0.311 cm, monotone. Recipes R-HEROCAP,
R-HEROIMPORT, R-HEROGEOM, R-HERODNA.

Five loop defects were found by the loop contradicting itself, and every one
is worth more than the residual:

1. **THE RULER MOVED.** Edits reaching the eye band changed the IPD the
   frame normalises by -- +2.7% from geometry, +1.37% from a parametric
   probe -- so regions nobody commanded appeared to move.
2. **AND THE FIX WAS TO STOP NORMALISING THE RENDER AT ALL.** IPD scaling
   is a technique for comparing faces at UNKNOWN scale. That is the
   reference photo. It was never the render: the camera is locked and the
   head sits at a fixed distance, so render pixels are absolute at
   0.01745 cm/px. I inherited the technique for one side and applied it to
   both, which made the ruler a function of the thing being edited. Frozen
   at 429.027 px, the loop went monotone immediately.
3. **THE GAIN UPDATE WAS INVERTED.** gain is defined by command = want/gain,
   so it must EQUAL the observed response; I wrote gain/response, which
   shrinks the gain when the render over-moves and makes the next command
   larger.
4. **A GAIN FROM A SUB-FLOOR MOVE IS NOISE.** A 0.029 cm "move" under a
   0.078 cm floor drove a gain to its clamp.
5. **STATE DID NOT SURVIVE THE PROCESS.** Run as single-iteration calls, the
   cumulative reset to zero each time and the loop oscillated, each call
   correcting a state it had not produced.

## THE RULING, DELEGATED TO THE FABLE MODEL

Ryan delegated the design ruling, as on 2026-08-15. Summarised; full text in
the session record.

- **Ratio fitting is FINISHED and demoted to a regression guard.** Seven
  scalars are widths at three heights plus a chin drop; "round face vs long
  narrow face" is a CONTOUR property that no combination of them expresses.
  New objective: the face-oval contour, radially compared, weighted down
  where hair occludes it.
- **Image-space losses REJECTED as drivers.** They are dominated by hair,
  stubble, albedo and lighting, so an optimiser pointed at them pushes
  GEOMETRY to fake grooming -- the wrong variable absorbing the residual.
- **Return rank: grooms > skin/eyes > presentation lighting > geometry >
  second view. EXECUTION order is geometry-first-then-FREEZE**, because
  groom bindings bind to the mesh and all four already failed once; moving
  the skull after rebinding re-buys that failure.
- **Depth is HAND-AUTHORED from art direction and MEASURED on a second
  locked azimuth.** A single frontal reference cannot constrain projection,
  and synthesising a profile or inferring shape from shading would invent a
  ground truth that does not exist -- the reference is a generated portrait,
  not a photograph of someone who has a profile.
- **Whole-rig import NOT invoked**, and the reasoning is the sharp part:
  whole-rig buys EXACTNESS IN REPRODUCING A DNA, and there is no DNA that
  expresses the likeness to reproduce. The bottleneck is authoring the
  target, not the model's fidelity to it. Criterion re-bound to the new
  objectives.
- **The road correction: an ATTENDED MetaHuman Creator session as the
  AUTHOR, with this loop demoted to VERIFIER** -- which is what it is
  genuinely excellent at. Same shape as the two prior times the attended
  route turned out to be the diagnostic rather than the fallback
  (MetaHumanCoreTech; Save Face Textures).
- Also flagged: the base head is round, young and short-faced, so every
  iteration fights that prior with sub-centimetre deltas. A preset blend
  moves the prior in one act.

## THE THING WORTH KEEPING FROM ALL OF IT

An objective function is a claim about what matters, and it is the least
tested claim in any fitting pipeline. This one was tested by exactly one
thing: opening the resulting picture and looking at it beside the target.
Every number said success.

# 2026-08-18 (later) — TWO WRITES, ONE DURABLE AND ONE ALREADY BEING DONE FOR US

## A WRITE THAT LANDS ON TRANSIENT STATE IS A WIN FOR EXACTLY ONE RENDER

The groom colour was going to be set on the material. The materials on the
MetaHuman preview actor are TRANSIENT --
`/Engine/Transient...MI_WI_Hair_M_Layered_None_2_Hair` -- recreated by every
`assemble_for_preview`, which the likeness loop runs on EVERY iteration.
`hairMelanin` set there takes, renders correctly, and is erased by the next
assemble. It would have photographed as a success and evaporated.

The durable surface is the INSTANCE PARAMETERS, and it exists:

    read   MetaHumanCharacterInstanceBlueprintLibrary
             .try_get_instance_parameter(instance, item_path, name)
    write  MetaHumanCharacterInstanceParameterBlueprintLibrary
             .set_float_instance_parameter(param, value) -> bool

    per groom item: Melanin, Redness, Roughness, Whiteness, Lightness,
                    DyeColor  (+ ombre and highlight sets on Hair)

Applied Melanin 0.92 / Redness 0.28 / Whiteness 0.00, 12 of 12 writes
returning true, proven by render.

**This is the MCP-authored-scene-state class in a new costume.** That entry
says scene state authored outside the recipes does not survive a rebuild.
Here the rebuild is `assemble_for_preview` and it happens every two minutes.
What caught it was ENUMERATING THE DURABLE SURFACE FIRST rather than reaching
for the material that was already in hand -- the standing "names from the
asset" rule doing work it was not written for.

## THE BINDING WAS NEVER STALE, AND THE FIT LOOP NEEDS NO REBUILD STEP

Ryan ruled one bounded test before gain calibration, on reasoning worth
keeping even though the answer went the other way: **if the groom bindings
were built against the MetaHuman archetype head, then every geometry edit
re-breaks them, and gain calibration is about to edit the head many more
times.** That failure would have arrived mid-calibration, intermittently,
and the presence manifest would have caught it without explaining it.

Read directly, before building anything:

    Hair      target_skeletal_mesh  /Engine/Transient/FaceMesh_68   true
    Eyebrows  target_skeletal_mesh  /Engine/Transient/FaceMesh_68   true
    Beard     target_skeletal_mesh  /Engine/Transient/FaceMesh_68   true

    binding objects themselves: /Engine/Transient...GroomBindingAsset_51/52/54

**The bindings are TRANSIENT and rebuilt by every `assemble_for_preview`
against the CURRENT mesh.** That is why the GroomBindingAsset numbers keep
changing between probes. There is nothing stale to rebuild; the engine has
been doing it continuously.

Consequences, both better than the outcomes the ruling anticipated:

- **Binding staleness is eliminated as a cause of the hair failure.**
- **No binding-rebuild step is needed in the fit loop, and no compounding-
  degradation risk exists on this path.** The design concern that justified
  the test is closed rather than budgeted for.

**And it sharpens the remaining lead rather than blunting it.** Hair and
Beard now have IDENTICAL binding configuration -- same source mesh
(`SKM_Groom_Head_Legacy02`), same target, same 100 interpolation points,
same matching section, same LODs, same binding type -- and one renders while
the other does not. The difference is not in the binding's configuration. It
is inside the groom asset or the binding's BUILT data, which is exactly where
`enable_global_interpolation` (True on both failing hairs, False on the
working beard) lives.

**The cheapest decisive test cost one read and no build.** The ruling asked
for a rebuild; the rebuild would have produced a binding identical to the one
already there, rendered nothing, and been recorded as evidence against a
hypothesis that the read had already refuted. Ask the artefact what it IS
before building a replacement for what you assume it is not.

# 2026-08-18 (later still) — GAIN CALIBRATION HAS A CEILING, AND THE INSTRUMENT FOUND IT

Gain calibration was ruled to begin. It ran, it did not converge, and the
reason is a property of the system rather than of the tuning. Three findings,
in the order they surfaced.

## 1. THE STAGE REBUILD WAS SILENTLY WIPING THE MEASURED NOISE FLOOR

`build_capture_stage.py` REPLACES `manifest.capture` wholesale when it locks
the framing, and took `noise_floor` and `presence` with it. Nothing
complained, because every consumer fell back to a hardcoded default:

    fl_p90 = fl["per_landmark"]["p90_ipd"] if fl else 0.01

The real measured value is ~0.0104. **The default sat close enough to the
truth that the loop ran uncalibrated for an unknown number of iterations
while reporting numbers that looked calibrated.** A silent fallback to a
plausible constant is worse than a missing key: a missing key fails, a
plausible constant produces confident output.

Fixed both ends -- the rebuild PRESERVES what was measured and says so, and
the fit loop now REFUSES rather than defaulting.

## 2. A GUARD AGAINST LEARNING FROM NOISE BECAME A TRAP AGAINST LEARNING

`temple_width` sat at +0.024..+0.039 IPD for eight consecutive iterations,
never closing. Its gain was 5.614, which makes the command about a fifth of
the wanted move; that command lands below the noise floor; the sub-floor
guard then HOLDS the gain rather than learning from noise -- so the region
could never recalibrate and drifted at a constant offset forever.

    too-high gain -> tiny command -> sub-floor -> gain held -> too-high gain

Fixed by requiring a MINIMUM MEASURABLE COMMAND: a region outside the
deadband gets a command of at least 2x the floor even when the gain asks for
less, because a command too small to measure teaches nothing.

**Every guard that suppresses an update needs an escape, or it becomes a
fixed point.**

## 3. THE REAL CEILING: THE FIT STOPS REPRODUCING AS EDITS ACCUMULATE

With the lock-in fixed, the commands became measurable and the responses were
absurd:

    jaw_width     commanded +0.150 cm, render moved +1.526    ratio 10.2
    cheek_width   commanded +0.150 cm, render moved +0.755    ratio  5.0
    temple_width  commanded +0.150 cm, render moved +0.569    ratio  3.8

A 0.15 cm nudge moving the face 1.5 cm is not a gain. `FitToFaceDna`
re-solves the whole parametric state on every import, so a small local edit
perturbs the global solution by more than the edit.

**Measured directly, and this is the finding:**

    state                                  floor p90   spread   gate
    edited (cumulative 0.3..0.7 cm)         0.27 cm     5.52    REFUSED
    canonical (restored)                    0.0698 cm   3.10    passes

Two captures of the UNCHANGED character differ by 0.27 cm at the edited
operating point and 0.07 cm at canonical. **The rig did not change; the state
did.** Sub-centimetre accumulated edits degrade the fit's own reproducibility
about fourfold, until it exceeds the 0.15 cm deadband the loop is trying to
hit.

**So the loop is not failing to converge on a target it could reach. It is
converging on a target that moves by more than the tolerance, because the
thing being measured has stopped being repeatable.** No gain, damping or step
policy fixes that: the ceiling is the parametric fit's stability under
accumulated geometry edits, not the controller.

**The homogeneity gate is what caught it**, refusing to write a floor from a
non-homogeneous run rather than averaging one out of it. That gate was added
two days ago for a different reason -- an unsettled cold session -- and it
found this. A gate that refuses on a condition it was not written for is the
cheapest evidence that the condition is real.

## WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ROUTE

The fable ruling's road correction now has hard evidence under it: the
automated geometry loop is an excellent VERIFIER and a poor AUTHOR, and the
measured reason is that its measurement stops being valid exactly where
authoring would need to go. Large shape moves belong in an attended
MetaHuman Creator session or a preset blend, with this loop measuring the
result and guarding regressions -- which it does reproducibly at 0.07 cm
when the state is one the fit holds stably.

# 2026-08-18 (night) — THE WHOLE-RIG ARM HOLDS ITS OWN RULER, AND THE TEST COST ONE DUPLICATE

The fit path's ceiling was not a tuning problem: `FitToFaceDna` re-solves the
whole parametric state on every import, so the RENDER stopped reproducing at
edited states — 0.27 cm against a 0.0698 cm canonical floor, a 4x degradation
that swallowed the loop's 0.15 cm deadband. The standing ruling escalated to
`import_whole_rig=True` on one test. It ran tonight and it passed.

    state                                         floor p90    spread   gate
    0  scratch, parametric canonical (control)     0.0463 cm    1.98    passes
    A  whole-rig, UNEDITED canonical DNA           0.0837 cm    3.82    passes
    B  whole-rig, feathered -2.00 cm chin DNA      0.0559 cm    1.97    passes

    chin  commanded -2.0000 cm -> rendered -1.9613 cm, ratio 0.981
          fit path, the SAME DNA BYTES:  -2.1553 cm, ratio 1.078

**The edited-state floor is canonical class under an edit four to six times
larger than the accumulation that broke the fit path.** Numbers in
RECIPES R-HEROWHOLERIG.

## THE PART THAT IS METHOD, NOT RESULT

**THE TEST WAS BUILT SO THE EXPENSIVE THING WAS THE EXPENDABLE THING.**
Whole-rig import advertises a PERMANENT per-asset body-type lock, which makes
it the kind of decision that cannot be un-made — so it was taken on a
duplicate whose entire purpose is to absorb it. Nothing at any point could
reach `MHC_AlpineHero` or its master, and both are byte-identical on disk
afterwards. A permanent cost stops being a risk when it lands on something
built to be thrown away.

**THE TWO ARMS CONSUMED THE SAME BYTES, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED.** The edited DNA was regenerated from the canonical through the
manifest's own `chin_jaw` region and came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the prior
session's edit (sha256 `ff9e44b1…`, 6703 weighted / 1661 core both times). So
the 0.981 and the 1.078 are the same input through two engine paths, not two
experiments that happen to be comparable. Regenerating rather than reusing the
file cost one minute and turned an inherited artefact into a proven one.

**A FLOOR IS A PROPERTY OF ITS MANIFEST, AND `--noise-floor` WRITES.** The
scratch measurements went into a COPY of the manifest, because the tool writes
`capture.noise_floor` into whatever file it is handed. Measuring a scratch
state against the canonical manifest would have overwritten the working
character's calibration with a number belonging to a different asset — and,
being plausible, it would never have announced itself. The silent-fallback
lesson from earlier the same day, one step upstream: a number in the right
field, from the wrong subject.

## THE PART I WILL NOT LET READ AS CLEAN

**TWO MEASURES MOVED FROM OUTSIDE THE EDIT.** `brow_height` -0.125 cm and
`nose_bridge` -0.211 cm, both 2-4x the floor, both far above a box that tops
out at Y 160.5 while the eyes sit at Y 165.6+ and the edit self-verified 512
zero-weight vertices. Pose moved with them — roll -0.06 -> +0.60 deg, ipd
429 -> 422 px.

The obvious explanation is a head pitch, and **the measurement refutes it**: a
pitch foreshortens chin and brow TOGETHER, and here the chin lengthened 15%
while the brow shortened 6%. What fits instead is the LANDMARK MODEL
re-fitting to an out-of-distribution long jaw — MediaPipe solves a canonical
face, so a 2 cm elongation is not a local edit as far as the instrument is
concerned. **The ruler is a model too, and a big enough edit moves it.** That
bounds the ratio at ~0.1-0.2 cm rather than at its 0.013 cm frame spread, and
it is recorded as unresolved instead of averaged away.

**AND THE ADVERTISED COST DID NOT SHOW UP WHERE IT WAS LOOKED FOR.**
`fixed_body_type` reads False on the scratch after TWO whole-rig imports,
identical to the untouched master. That is a reading, not a conclusion: the
asset was dirty and unsaved and the lock may live where that flag does not
report. Reporting it as "the lock is absent" would be the config-file class
all over again — the file is not the state — so it is logged as measured and
neither confirmed nor refuted.

## WHAT IS PROVEN AND WHAT IS NOT

Proven: a whole-rig import of the CANONICAL DNA reproduces the parametric face
to 0.005 cm on every named measure, an order below the floor — a far stronger
identity result than the 1.05x p90 headline. Proven: one 2 cm edit renders
1:1 and leaves the measurement reproducible.

**Not proven: accumulation.** The fit path's ceiling appeared under CHAINED
edits, and this test chained one. The cheap next test is a second edit onto
the edited DNA and a third floor, and until it runs the claim is exactly as
narrow as the experiment.

# 2026-08-19 — DEPTH-2 HELD, AND THE UNDO IS WHAT KILLED THE EDITOR

The accumulation test ran. The floor held, one ratio did not match, and then
`--restore` fataled the editor. Three separate things, in that order.

## THE ACCUMULATION RESULT

    state                                        floor p90    spread   gate
    0  scratch, parametric canonical              0.0463 cm    1.98    passes
    A  whole-rig, UNEDITED canonical DNA          0.0837 cm    3.82    passes
    B  depth 1, chin -2.00 cm                     0.0559 cm    1.97    passes
    C  depth 2, + jaw +-1.00 cm per side          0.0942 cm    2.85    passes

    fit path, same rig, prior session
       edited at cumulative 0.3..0.7 cm           0.27   cm    5.52    REFUSED

Depth 2 reads 1.13x the whole-rig canonical floor where the fit path read
3.9x its own canonical and was refused. **The instability was the fitter, not
edited geometry in the assemble path** — which is the question the test was
built to answer. Stated with its limit: four floors at n=4 span 0.046..0.094,
a 2x range, and this project's own record is that floors move ~1.5x between
measurements at small n. No degradation TREND is established either.

## A RATIO THAT MISSED, AND THE DNA'S OWN BOUNDS SAID WHY BEFORE ANY RERUN

    edit 1  chin  commanded -2.0000 cm  ->  rendered -1.9626   ratio 0.98
    edit 2  jaw   commanded +-1.0 per side, so +2.0000 in the WIDTH
                                        ->  rendered +1.3959   ratio 0.70

0.70 is not 1.0, and the tempting reading is that the second edit in a chain
lands weaker than the first. **The DNA disagreed, and it cost one read.**
`read_dna_meshes` on the two files shows the head's widest vertices moving
**0.1876 cm per side for a 1.0 cm command** — 19% — because the jaw box holds
558 core vertices inside 3372 weighted ones and the extremes sit deep in the
feather band.

So the same mask delivers 1.00 at its core, 0.19 at the head's widest point,
and whatever its own weight is wherever the JAW landmark happens to sit. The
manifest already says this in one line — *attenuation is a property of
(region x mask), NOT of region alone* — and a chained-edit conclusion was one
step from being drawn against a number that never had 2.0 cm available to it.
**A ratio is only a statement about a path when the mask under it is known.**
The discriminating control is the same jaw edit at DEPTH 1: same mask, no
chain. It is unrun, because of what happened next.

## THE UNDO IS NOT SAFE ON THIS PATH

    05:02:14  LogUObjectGlobals: Reloading 1 Package(s):
                Asset Name: /Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero_Scratch
    05:02:21  Unhandled Exception: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x470
              PythonScriptPlugin -> python311 -> UnrealEditor-Core

`sanctioned_import.py --restore` — destroy the preview actor,
`remove_object_to_edit`, then `reload_packages(..., ASSUME_POSITIVE)` — has
run clean many times on the FIT path. On a character that has taken a
**whole-rig** import it fataled the editor seven seconds into the reload.

**LOCATION ESTABLISHED, MECHANISM NOT.** The callstack is unsymbolised and
nothing here identifies what still held a pointer. What is measured is that
the reload is where it died and that whole-rig is the only variable that
changed. Candidate worth testing first: whole-rig runs `CommitFaceDNA`, so the
committed rig may be referenced by something the reload swaps underneath.

**WHAT IT COST: NOTHING THAT WAS NOT REBUILDABLE, BY DESIGN.** The scratch's
depth-2 state lived only in memory and is re-derivable from a tracked asset
plus three recorded calls; every measurement was already on disk; the working
character and the master were never in the write path and are byte-identical.
The expendable thing is what the crash reached. That is the whole reason it
was built expendable — and it is the second time this project has been glad a
destructive experiment had somewhere safe to happen.

**THE OPERATIONAL RULE THAT FOLLOWS:** on the whole-rig path, do not reach for
`--restore` as the undo. The undo is a fresh duplicate from the tracked
source. Restore is for the parametric path, where it is proven.

## AN OBSERVATION THAT IS NOT A FINDING, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD LATER

The log carries `LogMetaHumanCharacterEditor: Error: Vertices do not match
between current data and gold data`, 328 times, **first seen 2026-08-18
07:49** — before any of this work. Max difference reads 2.049 then and 18.198
at the depth-2 import. It is tempting to read that growth as the accumulation
signal. It is NOT attributed: the errors predate the whole-rig arm entirely,
nothing here establishes what "gold data" is compared against, and a number
that grows with the size of a deliberate edit is exactly what a comparison
against an unedited reference would print.

# 2026-08-19 (night) — THE ENGINE ERROR WAS OURS, AND THE ADVISOR HELD THE LOCK

Three findings, and the first one is a warning about how to read a log.

## THE "ENGINE-SIDE ERROR" ON EVERY WHOLE-RIG IMPORT IS OUR OWN DIAGNOSTIC

The import logs, as an **Error**, four times per run:

    LogMetaHumanCharacterEditor: Error: Vertices do not match between current
    data and gold data. Max difference = 18.1982937 for vertex 7

Sitting a line above `ImportErrorCode.SUCCESS`, that is alarming, and an
outside reader was right to refuse to let it pass unexplained. It is emitted
at `MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem.cpp:2567`, inside **`CompareFaceState`**,
whose "gold data" is simply **character 2 of the comparison**. The call is
OURS: `sanctioned_import.py` compares the working character against the master
across four tolerances, and every failing tolerance logs a line.

**What settles it is that the number never moves:**

    parametric fit-path imports  03:00..03:26  1.12 .. 1.32 cm  vertex 869/58703
    whole-rig IDENTITY (unedited canonical DNA)  18.1982937  vertex 7
    whole-rig depth 1 (chin -2 cm)               18.1982937  vertex 7
    whole-rig depth 2 (+ jaw)                    18.1982937  vertex 7
    whole-rig jaw-only, a different session      18.1982937  vertex 7

Identical to seven decimals across four different edits — **including the
import whose render reproduced the face to 0.005 cm.** A quantity that does not
respond to the thing it supposedly measures is not measuring it. What it
compares is a whole-rig-COMMITTED face state against a PARAMETRIC one, and
those differ by construction.

**Two consequences.** `compare_face_state` is useless as a check on a
whole-rig-imported character and must never be quoted as one — the sanctioned
import's own "vs master" line reads `NOT within 1.0` on a perfect identity
round trip. And an ERROR in a log is not evidence of a fault in the operation
next to it.

**THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM MADE IN THE ENTRY ABOVE.** That entry says the
gold-data figure "grows with the size of a deliberate edit, which is what a
comparison against an unedited reference would print". It does not grow. It is
a constant, and the same constant appears on an import that changed nothing.
The instinct to leave it UNATTRIBUTED was right; stopping at "not attributed"
instead of asking whether it fired on THIS import was the defect, and the
question cost one grep.

## THE MUTATE-A-COPY TRAP, CAUGHT BY A POSITIVE CONTROL RATHER THAN BY LUCK

Testing whether whole-rig had locked the body, the first probe read Height
back UNCHANGED after `set_body_constraints` — which looks exactly like a lock.

It was not. Iterating a UE struct `Array` in Python yields **copies**, so
mutating the loop variable and passing the same list back changes nothing, and
the setter reports no error. Rebuilding the array by index, with a
NEVER-IMPORTED duplicate as the positive control in the same run:

    control  (duplicate, NEVER whole-rig imported)  178.196 -> 182.0   TOOK
    locked   (scratch, THREE whole-rig imports)     178.196 -> 182.0   TOOK

So the write path works, and the body parameter still moves after three
whole-rig imports. **The advertised permanent body-type lock has not been
observed on any surface we can read.** Stated as measured, not concluded: a
read-back is the field the setter wrote, and the mesh-side check returned
EMPTY — the preview actor was not found — which is *I could not look*.

This project paid for this exact trap once before, on `Masculine/Feminine`,
where a +-2.0 swing produced byte-identical bounds INCLUDING the baseline. The
difference tonight is that the control was in the same run, so a null result
could be told apart from a dead instrument.

## THE ADVISOR HELD THE LOCK, AND ITS REASONING OUTLIVES THE DECISION

Depth 2 passed on the floor — 0.0942 cm, gate accepts, against the fit path's
0.27 cm refusal — and the jaw ratio missed its stated bar at 0.70 against
~1.0. The depth-1 jaw control then showed the same mask delivering **0.58**
with no chaining at all, so chaining RAISED delivery and the miss is the mask.

The ruling was still HOLD, and the reason is worth more than the outcome:
**converting a failed criterion into a pass by reinterpreting its bar is the
moved-bar pattern**, refused here once before on the unit-2 step-height bar,
where the reasoning was also correct and the change was still held for
ratification. When the letter of a gate fails while its spirit passes, on an
advertised-permanent operation, unattended: fail closed and hand back a
sharper boundary instead of an irreversible act.

The supporting ground was stronger than the principle. **A pre-authorisation
is a decision taken on the evidence available when it was written**, and by
the time the lock came up its risk map was stale by three findings made after
it: the proven undo now fatals the editor on exactly the asset class the lock
produces, so the lock's falsifier did not exist; the lock's advertised cost is
unmeasurable in either direction; and the gold-data line was unexplained at
that moment. Two of the three are now closed — by this entry's first two
sections — which is the shape a held decision should take.
