## 2026-09-11p — A READER THAT CANNOT TELL ZERO FROM ABSENT, FIXED AT THE SOURCE
> STATUS: HISTORY — records the cvar zero-vs-absent reader fix

RULED: make the cvar helper return None / refuse on a missing variable,
probe existence first, and put a fixed control in every batch read.

THE DEFECT, cited rather than inferred. `KismetSystemLibrary.cpp:610-622`:

    float UKismetSystemLibrary::GetConsoleVariableFloatValue(const FString& VariableName)
    {
        float Value = 0.0f;
        IConsoleVariable* Variable = IConsoleManager::Get().FindConsoleVariable(*VariableName);
        if (Variable) { Value = Variable->GetFloat(); }
        else { UE_LOGF(..., "Failed to find console variable '%ls'.", ...); }
        return Value;        // <- 0.0f for a name that does not exist
    }

It warns to the log and returns the zero. Nothing reaches Python.

THE EXISTENCE TEST, found by enumerating the reflected surface rather
than guessing: **the STRING getter**. An existing cvar stringifies
non-empty even when its value is zero; an absent one gives "".

    r.ScreenPercentage   -> '100'   exists
    r.TonemapperGamma    -> '0'     exists, and genuinely zero
    r.ExpandGamut        -> ''      ABSENT in 5.8
    r.TonemapperFilm     -> ''      ABSENT in 5.8
    <impossible name>    -> ''      absent

RE-READ THROUGH THE FIXED READER: **8 of the 18 names in the Q12 batch do
not exist.** The old reader called every one of them 0.0. All six
`r.LocalExposure.*` parameters are among them -- the feature toggle
`r.LocalExposure` is real (1.0) but its parameters live on the
PostProcessSettings block, which is where they were eventually read.

THE CONTROLS NOW RUN IN EVERY BATCH, BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the batch
refuses if either misbehaves: a POSITIVE control that must exist and be
non-zero (`r.ScreenPercentage` = 100) and a NEGATIVE control that must
read absent. **The ruling named `r.TonemapperFilm` (default 1) as the
fixed control and that cvar DOES NOT EXIST in 5.8** -- it would have read
absent forever and looked like a working control doing nothing. It is
kept in the batch as a third, documented negative control, and a real
positive control was added beside it.

THE RULE: **a control that cannot fail is not a control.** The ruled one
could only ever have returned the same answer; the pair that replaced it
can each fail in a different direction, which is why the read-back is now
evidence.

## 2026-09-11q — I IGNORED "COULD NOT LOOK" NINE TIMES BECAUSE THE RAW DUMP HAD WHAT I WANTED

Every payload I wrote this session printed its result behind the marker
`__RESULT__`. **`ue_exec`'s marker is `__LL__`** (ue_exec.py:131). So
every one of those runs reported

    COULD NOT LOOK: payload produced no marker.
    --- raw output (first 3000 chars) ---

and I read the answer out of the raw dump and moved on. Nine payloads.
The tool was telling me, every time, that my payload did not conform to
its contract, and I treated the message as cosmetic because the data I
wanted happened to be visible underneath it.

IT COST A SILENTLY TRUNCATED READ. The cvar batch's JSON is longer than
3000 characters, so the fallback dump cut it mid-object at exactly
character 2990 -- `'centage", "string": "100", "exists": true, "value"'`
-- and the host's json.loads raised. That failure was LOUD and therefore
cheap. The dangerous version is the one where the truncation lands after
a syntactically complete prefix and the read silently returns a SUBSET.

Two fixes, and the second matters more:
  1 every payload now prints `__LL__`, so ue_exec decodes it properly
    and there is no 3000-char fallback to be truncated by.
  2 the host no longer parses the marker at all -- ue_exec CONSUMES it
    and pretty-prints the decoded object, so the host decodes the first
    JSON object in ue_exec's stdout. Looking for a marker that the tool
    has already eaten is what made the first draft depend on the
    fallback path.

THE RULE: **a diagnostic you have decided to ignore is a diagnostic you
have stopped reading.** "COULD NOT LOOK" is this repo's phrase for "the
instrument did not report", and I let it become background noise for a
whole session because the workaround was one grep away. If a tool says it
could not look and you can see the answer anyway, you are reading a
fallback path -- and fallback paths have limits the main path does not.


## 2026-09-11r — THE RULED STATION FAILS ALL FOUR CHECKS, AND MY PREDICTOR FAILED IN A NEW DIRECTION
> STATUS: HISTORY — records the ruled station failing; instrument fault

Ryan picked Bench_ground at (148200, -96400, 24180) cm, yaw 62, pitch 0.
Placed (read-back exact), captured with depth + scene-linear EXR,
residency missing 0. All four ruled checks FAIL, and the numbers are
reported without a nudge because that is the ruling.

    1 DEPTH SHAPE   p25 468.72 (>= 40 ok)  p50 721.67  p75 805.13 (<= 400 FAIL)
                    frac in 50-300 m 0.0341 (>= 0.30 FAIL)   sky 0.1348
    2 PREDICTION    predicted rows [0, 0]   rendered rows [0, 174]
    3 NO TREES      54 in frustum under 300 m, nearest 264.5 m   FAIL
    4 MEADOW        frac >= 0.55 is 0.4690 (>= 0.50 FAIL), mean 0.4688

THE STATION LOOKS LONG. p25 468 m means three quarters of the frame is
beyond 468 m; only 3.4% sits in the 50-300 m band the surface metrics
need. v1 and v2 failed by seeing only NEAR ground; this one fails by
seeing almost none.

TWO THINGS ABOUT CHECK 2 THAT ARE MY INSTRUMENT'S FAULT, NOT THE
STATION'S, AND BOTH WOULD HAVE FLATTERED A REPORT THAT DID NOT SAY SO:

**The predictor UNDER-counted, in the opposite direction from v1 and v2.**
It forward-projects the heightmap at stride 2 and z-buffers the result.
At 100-300 m one heightmap texel is well under a pixel, so the buffer is
sparse with holes, no row reaches the ">50% of the row in band"
criterion, and it reports 0 rows where the render found 174. The
predicted number is a SAMPLING ARTEFACT at range, not a claim about the
terrain. The fix is to project at stride 1 or to splat rather than point-
sample -- not attempted here, because 4a is a verification and changing
the instrument mid-verification is how a check becomes a negotiation.

**And band 1's "within tolerance: True" is VACUOUS.** Predicted 0,
rendered 0, so the relative difference is 0/1 and the tolerance passes --
two numbers agreeing because neither exists. A tolerance test over a pair
of zeros is not evidence of agreement, and the table now carries both
raw counts precisely so that the "True" cannot be read as one.

THE RULE: **a comparison that can pass by both sides being empty needs an
existence precondition, not just a tolerance.** This is the same shape as
the p90 gradient pinned at sqrt(2)/2 and the autocorrelation peak pinned
at its search-window edge -- a statistic reporting its own degenerate
case as a result. Third instance in this brief; the family is
"agreement between two quantities that were never measured".


## 2026-09-11s — TWO OF THE FOUR RULED CHECKS ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, AND THE PROOF IS GRASS

Ryan asked me to find a position and yaw. The search found that the
GEOMETRY is satisfiable and that the CHECK SET is not.

    p25 >= 40 m         wants no near ground
    meadow >= 0.55      wants meadow, which means GRASS

MEASURED on the g4b capture (265600, -94400, 6541.2 cm, yaw 30, pitch 0):

    depth < 1.5 m   21.190% of frame
    1.5 - 3 m        6.431%          -> 27.6% inside 3 m
    3 - 10 m         1.143%
    10 - 50 m        2.879%
    50 - 300 m      30.383%          -> frac PASSES its 0.30 floor
    > 300 m         11.418%

The TERRAIN-ONLY raymarch of the same station puts p25 at 85.9 m and
almost nothing inside 3 m. So that 21% within 1.5 m is not terrain: it is
**ground cover standing at the lens**. Meadow's placed height is 0.387 m
p50 / 0.484 max and Blueberry's 0.475 / 0.605, and at a 1.7 m eye at
pitch 0 the bottom of the frame looks 29.4 deg down -- terrain at 3.0 m,
and any grass card in that cone at 1-2 m.

**27.6% of the frame is grass inside 3 m, which exceeds the 25% that
DEFINES p25.** p25 is therefore pinned near 1 m by the ground cover
alone, before the terrain is consulted at all. No position and no yaw can
lift it while check 4 requires meadow.

THE SEARCH EVIDENCE, for completeness. 101,764 views scored; raymarched,
99 of 400 survivors clear p25/p75/frac together -- those are the ones
NOT standing in meadow, which is exactly why they then fail meadow
(best 0.294 marched, and g4b measured 0.4578 rendered).

FOUR INSTRUMENTS, FOUR DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE RENDER, ONE FAMILY. The
forward-projection predictor under-counted at range; the centre-line
analytic model predicted p25 93.8 where the render gave 1.2; the
raymarch predicted 85.9 for the same station. **Every one of them models
TERRAIN and the render draws a WORLD.** The grass was the missing term in
all three, and it was in the measured record the whole time --
species_heights has carried Meadow's placed height and its 50 m cull
since 2026-09-05.

THE RULE: **when a predictor disagrees with a render, ask what the
renderer draws that the predictor does not, before touching either the
predictor's parameters or the thing being predicted.** I tuned scoring
resolutions, added a concavity gate and re-weighted a prefilter across
three attempts; none of that could ever have closed a gap whose cause was
an entire object class absent from the model.

AND THE ONE ABOUT CHECK SETS: **a set of thresholds can be individually
reasonable and jointly unsatisfiable, and nothing in the set says so.**
Each of the four is defensible alone. Their conjunction describes a
camera standing in grass that can see no grass. Worth asking, of any new
acceptance set, which pairs pull against each other.


## 2026-09-11t — 4b LANDS, AND A FRACTION MEASURED AGAINST THE WRONG POPULATION, THIRD TIME
> STATUS: HISTORY — records the tiling verdict and wrong-denominator defect

Ruling: drop p25, accept meadow 0.4578, run 4b. Done, and it produced the
first real tiling verdict of the brief.

    layer  surface     dist m  period  found  michelson  csf thr  verdict
    Snow   Snow006     NO CROP -- no snow at a 64 m station
    Rock   Rock051      203.7    60.4   36.3     0.2808   0.0190  NO VERDICT
    Grass  WildGrass     83.5   147.2  116.4     0.2937   0.0773  FAIL

**GRASS TILES VISIBLY.** 116.4 px sits INSIDE its search window
[88.3, 206.1], so unlike every previous attempt this is a real peak and
not a boundary artefact, and its Michelson contrast is 3.8x the CSF
threshold for that angular frequency. At 83.5 m the ground cover is
already culled (Meadow's cull is 50 m), so this is the LANDSCAPE MATERIAL
repeating, not grass cards. Rock's peak IS pinned at its window edge
(36.3 against a 36.2 floor) and is reported NO VERDICT.

TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN TABLE, BOTH FOUND BY ARITHMETIC THAT DID NOT ADD UP:

1 THE LAYER MASK WAS STARVED. Built by forward-projecting the heightmap
  at stride 2, it gave 35,729 band pixels where the depth pass says
  30.4% of an 8.3 Mpx frame -- and every layer came back NO CROP. Same
  stride-2 sparsity that made the station predictor report 0 rows where
  the render found 174. Replaced with a RAYMARCH at 960x540 upsampled
  x4: band pixels 2,520,097, which is 30.4% exactly. **The check was
  that two numbers for the same quantity disagreed by 70x.**

2 THE COLUMN TEST USED THE WRONG DENOMINATOR. It asked whether a layer
  filled 60% of the ROW-RUN HEIGHT, but the 50-300 m band is a
  horizontal STRIP and most columns carry band pixels over only part of
  the run. So every layer failed the column test while the ROW test was
  finding runs of 488 and 242. Fixed to measure against the BAND IN THAT
  COLUMN.

**THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE FAMILY.** `surface_report` once chose columns by
"no sky anywhere in the column" and got crops 0.0% inside their own depth
bin; this chose columns by "60% of the full run"; and the albedo row now
withholds its verdict for the same reason at a different level -- a
reference-albedo band compared against pixels 50-300 m away is a fraction
measured against a population that includes the ATMOSPHERE. Fog density
0.00416/m puts transmittance near 0.5 at 150 m, and the measured RGB
ascends R<G<B on every layer, which is inscattering rather than surface.
The scene-linear RGB and card ratio are reported because they were ruled;
the band comparison is withheld because it would be measuring the air.

THE RULE: **every fraction has a denominator, and the denominator is a
claim about which population the question is asked of.** Three of these
in one brief, each surviving a selftest, because a ratio is dimensionless
and therefore looks like it cannot be wrong. When writing one, say out
loud what the whole is -- and check the count of that whole against an
independent measure of the same thing.


## 2026-09-11u — "FIX THE GRASS TILING": THERE WAS NO GRASS TILING. I REPORTED A FALSE FAIL.

Asked to fix it, I went to find what period was repeating so I would
change the right thing. Nothing was.

**RETRACTION.** Last turn I reported Grass as "the first real tiling
verdict in this brief... a genuine peak, not the boundary artefact". That
was wrong and I should not have said it. I checked only whether the peak
sat at the search window's EDGE, never whether it was STRONG. Grass's
autocorrelation peak is **0.0511** -- against ~1.0 for a genuinely tiled
crop and 0.01-0.02 for aperiodic noise -- and a radial scan of the entire
plausible period range found **no local maximum above 0.06 anywhere**.

The michelson figure of 0.2937 came from `2*std*sqrt(peak)/mean`: with
peak 0.0511 the sqrt term is only 0.226, so the number was carried almost
entirely by the crop's own contrast. **This is the same artefact I had
already written up for surface_report's near_ground crop, and I walked
into it again three days later** -- because the guard I built from that
lesson tested the peak's POSITION and not its MAGNITUDE. A lesson that
fixes one symptom of a defect and not the defect is a lesson that will
fire once.

THREE WRONG STATISTICS BEFORE THE RIGHT ONE, each killed on known
specimens rather than on taste:

    peak / ring_median      an autocorrelation ring has NEGATIVE lobes,
                            so the ratio is signed nonsense: -107271 on
                            a perfect tile, -110 on pure noise
    robust z on the ring    for a TRUE tile the WHOLE ring is elevated,
                            so the maximum is not an outlier within it:
                            tiled 2.02, noise 4.03 -- backwards
    phase-randomised null   WRONG BY THEOREM. The autocorrelation IS the
                            transform of the power spectrum
                            (Wiener-Khinchin), and randomising phase
                            preserves that spectrum exactly, so the null
                            is IDENTICAL to the signal by construction.
                            Tiled scored exactly 1.00.

THE RIGHT ONE IS A PERIODOGRAM EXCESS: a repeat is a concentrated spike
in the power spectrum, and texture and contrast are the smooth background
under it. Power in the tile's frequency ring over a median-smoothed
radial background:

    synthetic perfect tile        30.34   (68.03 on the selftest fixture)
    real Rock @ 204 m              7.05
    aperiodic: noise / busy /
      weak-tile-in-noise       1.44 - 2.38

Floor set at 4.0, above everything aperiodic and far below a true tile,
with k >= 4 required so the background is estimable at all. Grass reads
**NO REPEAT** and the table says so in place of the FAIL.

THE RULE I KEEP PAYING FOR: **a composite statistic must never be read
without the component that says whether it is meaningful.** michelson
multiplies contrast by sqrt(peak); peak was in the same returned dict
every time. Three separate occasions now -- the p90 gradient pinned at
sqrt(2)/2, the autocorrelation peak pinned at its window edge, and this.
The fix is not more care. It is that `score()` must not RETURN a contrast
figure without also returning the evidence that a repeat exists, and the
caller must gate on it.

AND THE ONE ABOUT RETRACTIONS: I reported that FAIL confidently, with a
number and a units-correct interpretation, and it was an artefact. The
tell was available at the time -- peak 0.0511 was printed in the same
table I read aloud. **A number I have just explained is a number I have
stopped examining.**


## 2026-09-12 — SIX OF EIGHT SCANS REFUSED ON 8-BIT HEIGHT, AND AN ACTOR THAT NEVER SAVED

### The intake gate did its job, and it cost most of the delivery

Eight ground scans arrived. **Two pass.** The gate is 16-bit height, and
Megascans ships Displacement and Bump as **JPEG** -- measured from the
SOF precision byte, not inferred from the extension: 4096x4096, 8 bits.
ambientCG ships `_Displacement.png` at 4096x4096, 16 bits.

    Gravel021   ambientCG  CC0   16-bit  ACCEPTED
    Snow007A    ambientCG  CC0   16-bit  BOUND -> layer Snow
    rock_shopk_high / _raw / vktfeilaw / xiekec0 / xbreagf /
    ukoncdamw   Megascans  Fab   8-bit   REFUSED

The height map is the height BLEND's input, not decoration: 8 bits over a
few centimetres of relief quantises to ~0.4 mm and the blend edge becomes
a staircase of ties. R-LAYERS' mushy fraction (0.2131 vs a linear 0.5551)
was measured on a blend with real height to work with.

TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS AGREED that `rock_shopk` and `nordic_beach`
are not surfaces at all: the Megascans json categorises them `3d`, and
`make_asset_manifest` -- which knows nothing of that json -- classified
them `mesh` from the FBX. Either alone would have been a guess.

**GRAVEL021 PASSED AND STILL DID NOT BIND**, which is the more useful
finding. The material carries THREE layers (Snow, Rock, Grass); the
derivation's eight weights are collapsed into them with scree folded into
rock. **There is no `scree` layer to bind a scree scan to.** Adding one is
a weightmap-channel and graph change, which the ruling fenced off. So the
blocker on scree was never the asset.

### An actor that read back perfectly and never persisted

Three sessions moved `Bench_ground`. Each read the transform back EXACT
(`max_loc_err_cm 0.0`), each rendered from the new place, and **none of it
was written to disk** -- `set_actor_location_and_rotation` does not dirty
the package, so the dirty census truthfully reported nothing to save and
I read that as success.

A fourth session loaded the actor from disk at the ORIGINAL v1 location,
and the residency gate caught it: expected 11, missing 11, with the
probe's `view_target` sitting at (-68400, 243600) while the derivation
said (265600, -94400).

**A read-back that proves the setter ran IN MEMORY is not evidence that
anything was written.** Standing rule 12 says a parameter not read back is
prose; this is its second half -- a parameter read back from RAM is prose
too, if the question is whether it survives the session. The fix marks the
package dirty explicitly and the proof is the `.uasset` changing under
git, not the census agreeing.

THE SHAPE THIS SHARES WITH R-LIGHTSAVE: applied, verified, never saved,
reverted by the next load. That lesson was written on 2026-09-10 about
LIGHTING packages and I did not carry it to actors.

### What the tables show, and why they show so little

Snow007A is bound and the table names it -- and reports NO CROP and NO
SAMPLE, because Bench_ground stands at 65 m and the snow line is 730 m.
**The one bind of the session is not observable at the station the ruling
measures from.** Rock and Grass moved only within recapture noise
(michelson 0.2808 -> 0.2817, 0.2937 -> 0.2938), which is the useful
negative: nothing regressed.

## 2026-09-12b — A DOCTRINE LINE THAT REFUTED ITSELF, AND THE CONTROL THAT COULD NOT SEE IT

### The measurement that accused six packs at once
> STATUS: HISTORY — records the DX/GL normal mis-verdict, corrected

Three new ambientCG scans arrived to fill the first batch's gaps. A new
tool, `scan_surface_stats.py`, measured each pack's normal convention
from its own height map, and reported that **the DX file was GL and the
GL file was DX — on every pack, including the three already BOUND**
(`Rock051`, `Snow007A`, `Gravel021`).

Six independent packs from one of the most mechanical pipelines in the
business are not all mislabelled. **A verdict that indicts every
specimen is indicting the instrument.**

### The source was our own skill file, and it contradicted itself

`.claude/skills/asset-intake/SKILL.md` said: *for a heightfield the
normal is ∝ `(-dH/dx, -dH/dy, 1)`, rows increase downward, so DX
predicts `corr(G, dH/drow)` POSITIVE and GL negative.* I copied that
straight into the tool.

It is backwards, and **the paragraph disproves itself two sentences
later**. It also says the red channel must correlate NEGATIVELY with the
column gradient — which follows from the minus in `-dH/dx`. The SAME
minus sits in front of `dH/dy`. One expression cannot carry the sign for
X and drop it for Y. Rows increase downward and OpenGL's +Y runs up the
image, so `dH/dy_GL = -dH/drow` and `N_y ∝ +dH/drow`:

    GL  ->  corr(G, dH/drow) POSITIVE
    DX  ->  corr(G, dH/drow) NEGATIVE

The concrete case settles it without algebra: on a hill's upslope
(`dH/drow > 0`) the surface faces UP the image, which is +Y in a y-up
frame, so GL's green goes above mid.

### Why the control passed anyway — and what that says about controls

The skill prescribes a red-channel control, the tool implemented it, and
**it passed on all six packs while the verdict was inverted.** It was
not a weak control; it was a control of the wrong thing. It tests
whether the GRADIENT's sign is being handled correctly — and it was. The
defect was in the Y-FLIP, a term the red channel does not contain,
because red is identical in both conventions. That is precisely what
makes red usable as a control and precisely what makes it blind here.

**A control only guards the terms it shares with the claim, and is blind
to the terms it does not** — the other half of NN0. A control that
agrees with you is evidence about its own term and nothing else. The
question to ask of any control is not "did it pass" but "which way could
the answer be wrong WITHOUT moving this number", and here there was such
a way and it was the whole defect.

### The fix pins the sign to something that is neither doc nor vendor

`--selftest` now builds a heightfield and constructs its normal map
ANALYTICALLY under each convention, then asserts the measurement
recovers the label: analytic DX reads DX at -1.0000, analytic GL reads
GL at +1.0000, a GL map labelled DX is FLAGGED, and a flat field returns
NO VERDICT instead of a coin flip. It trusts neither the skill file nor
the packs — the two things that were in dispute.

With the sign corrected, all six packs agree with their filenames.

### Containment: the seed, not just the copy

Standing rule 9 says an unverified claim inherited from our own artefacts
is the same class as trusting an external record, and that the fix must
reach the SEED. The skill file is corrected in the same commit as the
tool, carries the ⛔ marker and the refutation, and records what the
control could not do — so the next reader inherits the reasoning rather
than a second assertion to take on faith.

**What this cost: nothing, because it was caught before anything bound.**
What it would have cost: a normal map bound inside-out inverts lighting
across the entire layer, and on a rock layer under a low sun that reads
as a plausible surface, not as a defect. It would have passed every
tonal check we own.


## 2026-09-12c — THE AGENT SOURCES ITS OWN MATERIALS, AND THE FIRST FETCH FAILED ITS OWN CONSUMERS

### The ruling, and why it was not about speed

Ryan ruled that the agent should fetch its own ground surfaces. The
reason he gave is the interesting one: *"there is a huge risk of me
getting the wrong ones or ones with missing files."* That is not a
convenience argument. Every one of those failure modes had already
landed on this project — an 8-bit height (six packs in one session), a
missing height map (`Dry_Fallen_Leaves`, a month on disk), and a decal
wearing a surface's name (`PineNeedles001` at 96.7% transparent).

So the design point is not the download. **A download is not finished
until it has passed the gate.** Everything lands in `Free/_staging/` and
is PROMOTED only on a pass; a refusal stays in staging beside a
`REFUSED.json`. A refused pack can never be mistaken for an intaken one,
which is exactly how `Ground037` came to be downloaded twice.

### What was feasible, measured rather than assumed

Network egress works. Poly Haven and ambientCG both publish open,
unauthenticated APIs. **Fab does not, and this is not a permissions
problem**: `Bridge`, `Fab` and `MegascansPlugin` ship ZERO Python and are
C++ around an authenticated embedded browser. No grant creates a
scriptable surface. Worth recording so it is not reopened.

**Poly Haven turns out to be strictly better for this project**, and for
a measurable reason rather than a preference: it publishes `dimensions`
in millimetres. ambientCG returns `dimensionX/Y/Z = 0` for every asset
tried. So the STRETCH check — derived tile against the scan's real size —
is available there and permanently unavailable here. The first fetch
produced the first stretch figure this project has ever computed:
`forest_floor`, stated 2.14 m, derived 5.03 m, **2.35x**.

### ⛔ AND THEN THE FETCH PASSED ITS OWN GATE AND BROKE ITS CONSUMERS

The pack was fine: five maps, 16-bit height, hash-pinned. The gate said
PASS and it was right. Then the INDEPENDENT check — running the existing
tools over the result rather than trusting the fetcher's verdict —
reported **"no colour map found"** and **both normals "absent"** on an
asset that was complete and correct.

Two causes, and both are the same shape:

1. **I invented a second naming convention.** The fetcher named files by
   role (`forest_floor_color_4k.jpg`) while every tool in `scripts/`
   reads the ambientCG dialect (`_Color`, `_NormalDX`). **Two lists that
   must agree are one list badly stored** (NN24). The fix is not to teach
   each downstream tool a new dialect — it is for the new writer to
   conform to the existing one.

2. **`find_map` accepted only `.png`.** A JPEG colour map was reported as
   ABSENT: a file that was present, readable, and sitting right there.
   **A finder that silently declines to look at a container reports
   absence for something it never examined.** That is the cvar getter's
   defect exactly — a reader that cannot distinguish "not there" from
   "I didn't look" reports the second as the first.

### The lesson that actually generalises

**A new producer must be verified against its CONSUMERS, not only
against its own contract.** The gate was correct, complete, and
self-tested in five directions — and none of that could see this,
because the gate and the fetcher were written by the same author in the
same hour and share every assumption. The defect only became visible
when a tool that shares no code with either was pointed at the output.
That is NN8 and it applies to a pipeline stage as much as to a
measurement.

It was caught because the output was checked with the old tools before
fetching a second asset. Had the batch run first, ten packs would have
carried the wrong names and the albedo table would have been silently
empty.

### Also, the hook earned its keep

The parking step used `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` as defensive
handling for "if the destination already exists", and the
`no-force-delete` hook refused it. Standing rule 2 has no exception for
defensive cleanup — **that is exactly how it was broken last time, by
`rm -f` entered as error handling.** Both `_trash/*` and `Free/*` are
gitignored, so parking a 174 MB superseded copy costs the repo nothing
and keeps the second undo button.


## 2026-09-12d — PROMOTING A TINT TO A LAYER, AND WHAT IT MADE VISIBLE

### The change was cheaper than it looked, because the data was already right

"Add the extra layers to the material" sounded like a second weightmap
texture and three new samplers. It was not. `derive_layer_weights` wrote
`w8a` on 2026-09-11 with the channels **already** in the contract the
five-layer material needs — `R=snow G=rock B=scree A=forest_floor` — and
the live map was that same data deliberately COLLAPSED (`G=rock+scree`,
`B=everything else`) because no scree or litter surface had passed the
intake gate yet. The collapse docstring said so: per-layer surfaces
"arrive with Task 3's scans".

So expanding was a COPY plus three assertions, not a recomputation.
**There was no second derivation that could disagree with the first** —
which is the whole reason it was cheap.

Meadow became the shader REMAINDER, `1-(R+G+B+A)`, rather than a stored
fifth channel. A fifth number obliged to agree with four others under
8-bit quantisation is NN24 with extra steps; derived, the masks sum to 1
by construction.

### Scree had been rendering as cliff face for a day

`Gravel021` passed the gate on 2026-09-12 and "could not bind" — and the
reason given, repeatedly, was "the material carries three layers". True,
but the sharper statement is: **11.97% of the world had a correct,
derived, baked weight sitting in channel B that nothing sampled.** The
blocker was never the asset and never really the layer count; it was
that one channel of an existing texture was being summed into another.

### ⛔ THE CHANNEL MAPPING WAS ABOUT TO EXIST IN THREE PLACES

The shader reads the weightmap. So does `bake_surface_lookup` ("what am
I standing on?" for footstep audio and movement) and `surface_query`.
All three had their own copy of "which channel is which layer", and two
of them additionally hard-coded `convert("RGB")` and `len(layers) != 3`.

The failure they would have produced is the instructive part: **the
shader would paint scree where the footstep audio played grass**, and
nothing in the repo compares those two. Not a crash — a divergence with
no observer.

Fixed by making `WEIGHTMAP_CHANNELS` and `mask_plan()` a single
declaration in the material builder. The payload's `_chan` is
INTERPOLATED from it (the payload is a `.format()` template, so this
costs nothing); the two CPU consumers IMPORT it. None of the three
spells the mapping out again.

### AND PROMOTING THE TINT MADE A LATENT DEFECT VISIBLE

With forest_floor a real surface, the lookup reports what each of the
303 town buildings stands on:

    Grass        165   54.5%
    ForestFloor  131   43.2%
    Scree          5    1.7%
    Rock           2    0.7%

**43.2% of the town is under full canopy cover**, and `place_foliage.py`
has no settlement exclusion at all — its only exclusion is ground cover.
`plan_encounters` has one; foliage does not. So trees are placed straight
through the town and the canopy mask is CORRECTLY reporting what the
foliage plan actually put there. The mask is right. The placement is the
gap.

**This is pre-existing, not a regression.** The alpha channel was already
255 at those cells and was already driving a tint. What changed is
VISIBILITY: a subtle green-brown tint on a grass layer is easy to miss;
a needle-litter surface with its own normal and height map, in a town
square, is not.

The general shape: **making a weak signal into a strong one is a way of
auditing the weak signal.** The tint had been wrong in exactly the same
cells for as long as it existed, and nobody could see it because a tint
is what a tint looks like.

### What is NOT done, stated because nothing else will state it

The five surfaces are NOT imported into UE and the material graph is NOT
rebuilt — the editor was never opened this session. The recipe, the
weightmap, the CPU lookup and every offline gate are consistent at five
layers; the engine has not seen any of it. Nothing here has been
rendered, so nothing here has been SEEN.


## 2026-09-12e — THE BUILD DIED MID-CLEAR, AND THE CRASH FOUND A DOUBLE REPRESENTATION

### What happened

The five-layer rebuild passed its preflight, cleared the graph, and then
raised `IndexError: list index out of range` at payload line 1144 — after
`delete_all_material_expressions`. `M_Alpine8K` was left EMPTY in memory
and dirty, with the disk copy still good. Nothing was saved; the builder
prints exactly that instruction and it was followed.

### Root cause, at the line

    _ll_wire(_mel, _vsamp, _chan[_i], _sel, "A")

`_vsamp` is the VARIANT MAP sampler. `_chan` is the WEIGHTMAP's channel
contract. **Two different textures, one channel list.** With three layers
and three channels the two happened to coincide, so the conflation was
invisible for as long as the layer count equalled the weightmap's channel
count. `Grass` is now index 4, `_chan` has four entries, and `_chan[4]`
raised.

The defect PREDATES the change. What the change did was remove the
coincidence that hid it. **A shared index is not a shared meaning**, and
the tell is that the two lists are indexed by the same variable while
belonging to different textures.

### ⛔ AND THE CRASH EXPOSED SOMETHING LARGER

`make_variant_map.py`'s docstring says what the variant map's channels
ARE:

    R  Snow  selector   (no sub-surface -> 0 everywhere)
    G  Rock  selector   SCREE / TALUS
    B  Grass selector   FOREST FLOOR

**Scree and forest_floor already existed.** Not as layers — as
SUB-SURFACES selected inside Rock and Grass by a baked mask, which was
the documented workaround for "the weightmap carries THREE, refused at
make_layer_weightmap.py:171, and widening it would re-key
place_foliage's `weights[..., chan]` under 157,554 placed conifers".

So promoting them to real layers created a DOUBLE REPRESENTATION: scree
as weightmap channel B (derived by `derive_layer_weights` from slope plus
a >40 deg source within 60 m uphill) AND as variant channel G (derived by
`rock_scatter.talus_deposit`). Two derivations of one physical fact —
"where is the scree" — which is NN19 exactly, and they cannot be
reconciled by inspection because both are plausible.

This is the same defect I had already removed ONCE this session, in the
forest_floor TINT, and did not recognise in its second costume. The tint
was obvious because it shared the literal alpha channel; this one hid
behind a different texture and a different derivation.

### The resolution

The weightmap's scree wins: R-LAYERS is locked on three independent
strands and the eight weights sum to 1 by construction. The sub-surface
mechanism was a workaround for a channel budget that no longer binds, so
the `sub_surface` blocks and the `variant_map` go with it, rather than
being kept as a second opinion.

### The lesson

**A crash after the point of no return is expensive, and this one still
paid for itself** — the IndexError was the only reason anyone read
`make_variant_map`'s docstring, and that docstring is where the double
representation was written down in plain language the whole time.

The general form: **when adding a mechanism, grep for the thing it
provides, not for the thing it is called.** I searched for "layers" and
"weightmap" and found the layer set; I never searched for "scree", which
would have found `make_variant_map.py:16` on the first hit.


## 2026-09-12f — THE FIRST VALID SHADOW-TINT READING, AND IT INVALIDATES THE BASELINE

### The number

    near_ground   shadow_tint B 1.8051 FAIL   (R 0.70  G 1.01)
                  shadow_luma 0.00475   lit_luma 0.12044

Predicted ~1.45, measured 1.8051. **The miss is the finding.**

### The baseline was measured on a stale weightmap

`shadow_tint_B` 1.45 at sky 1.0 was recorded on 2026-09-09 and has been
treated as ground truth ever since -- it is why sky intensity is 1.0.

The engine held `T_Alpine_8k_Weights` **dated 14 August** until it was
reimported today. So that 1.45, and every other acceptance measured at
this station in between, was taken against a world drawing MONTH-OLD
LAYER DATA. The baseline is not a baseline; it is a measurement of a
different world.

**A stale INPUT does not announce itself in the OUTPUT.** The frames
looked plausible, the number sat inside its band, and nothing in the
pipeline compared the texture asset's date to its source. It took a
render, an eye, and a file timestamp.

### The direction was opposite to what I had concluded

Earlier the same day I measured shadow_tint at three RECIPE CAMERAS,
read "two of three below the floor" as under-filled shadows, and raised
sky intensity 1.0 -> 1.6 to add blue. The acceptance station says the
shadows are **TOO BLUE** -- 1.8051 against a 1.60 ceiling.

Had that change stood, sky 1.6 would have put near_ground near 2.03.
**I would have pushed a real failure further out while believing I was
fixing it**, and the only thing that stopped it was the ruling to revert.

The stations I measured are not governed by that band -- it is specified
at near_ground and nowhere else, on line 3 of the tool's own docstring --
and near_ground is not even in the recipe camera set. So the earlier
conclusion was wrong in its station, wrong in its direction, and wrong in
its remedy.

### What the recipe already knew

`lighting.sky._task4`, written 2026-09-09: *"More Mie whitens the horizon
and desaturates the sky light's capture, which is the lever for shadow
tint once sky intensity is already at 1.0."*

The correction for over-blue shade at a settled sky intensity was
DOCUMENTED IN THE FIELD I WAS EDITING, and I reached for sky intensity
anyway -- the one lever Brief 2 Task 3 had already settled.

### The caveat that belongs with the number

`shadow_luma` is 0.00475. A B/luma ratio taken on near-black pixels is
fragile, and the band's calibration specimen is not recorded at a stated
shadow luminance. 1.8051 is a FAIL against the band as written; whether
the band is well-posed at this luminance is a separate question and is
not settled by this reading.

### The rule

**When a measurement contradicts a stored baseline, suspect the
BASELINE'S INPUTS before re-deriving the world.** The instinct is to
change the thing being measured. Here the thing being measured was
closer to correct than the record it was being judged against.


## 2026-09-12g — THE DOCUMENTED LEVER DID NOT MOVE THE NUMBER IT WAS DOCUMENTED TO MOVE

### The test

One variable, one capture, same station, same instrument, the parameter
read back from the engine at BOTH ends (0.009999999776 and
0.019999999553 — float32 for 0.01 and 0.02).

    Mie 0.01   B 1.8051   R 0.70  G 1.01   shadow_luma 0.00475  lit_luma 0.12044
    Mie 0.02   B 1.8379   R 0.70  G 1.01   shadow_luma 0.00437  lit_luma 0.10975

`shadow_tint_B` needed to FALL by 0.21 to re-enter the band. It ROSE by
0.033. Direction wrong, magnitude 1.8% where 12% was wanted.

### What this refutes

`lighting.sky._task4`, written 2026-09-09: *"More Mie whitens the horizon
and desaturates the sky light's capture, which is the lever for shadow
tint once sky intensity is already at 1.0."*

**Not supported at this station.** The claim was SOURCED to Electric
Dreams rather than fitted — `_task4` says so itself — and it was never
measured against `shadow_tint_B`. Task 4 moved Mie 0.003996 -> 0.01 and
recorded no B value, so the lever's effect on the thing it was named a
lever FOR has never been checked until now.

**A sourced claim is a hypothesis with a citation, not a measurement.**
It earns the same scrutiny as any other inherited number.

### What DID move, and why it matters

`lit_luma` fell ~9% and `shadow_luma` ~8%. The haze is doing real
extinction — Mie works, it is simply not acting on the term in question.
B/luma ROSE because luma fell slightly faster than blue did.

**Blue staying pinned while luminance falls is the signature of a source
colour that cannot move.** If the sky light's captured colour were free,
more haze would whiten it. That is consistent with the editor's
pre-exposure warning, which claims real-time sky captures are being
clipped — a clipped capture's colour is saturated and no amount of
atmosphere will desaturate it.

CONSISTENT, NOT PROVEN. The clipping hypothesis now explains two
independent observations (shade over-blue at 1.8051; Mie unable to move
it) and remains untested because testing it means changing pre-exposure,
which is fenced by a standing ruling.

### The rule

**When a documented lever fails to move its documented target, suspect
something UPSTREAM of the lever rather than the lever's magnitude.** The
tempting next step is a bigger step — 0.04, 0.08 — and it would have been
wrong: the term is not saturating slowly, it is not participating. Two
points were enough to see that because the SIGN was wrong, not just the
size. A single larger step would have produced a bigger wrong-direction
move and read as "still not enough".


## 2026-09-12h — THE ACCEPTANCE AND THE GRADE ARE IN CONFLICT, AND THE BAND'S SPECIMEN NO LONGER EXISTS
> STATUS: HISTORY — 2026-09-12h WB 3481.9 measurement and what-follows; both sub-parts (31, 33) are honest narrative, the band later re-derived

### The measurement

near_ground, target class, one variable, read back at both ends:

    WB 3481.9 (R-GRADE locked)   B 1.8051   R 0.70  G 1.01
    WB 5200   (band's calib)     B 0.7674   R 1.36  G 0.92
    Brief 2b, 2026-09-10, WB 5200: B 1.1243

### Finding 1 — shadow_tint_B is largely a WHITE-BALANCE readout
> STATUS: HISTORY — the metric is WB-dominated; feeds R-SHADEBAND

A 94.89-mired move swung B by **2.35x** and flipped R from 0.70 to 1.36.
Whatever else the metric measures, at this station the white point
dominates it.

So a band calibrated at one white point CANNOT be transported to another
— which is precisely the trap the band's own docstring cited when it
retired the old 1.3-1.7 band ("calibrated in an era whose only PASS
carried a WB 1300 K BELOW the sun"). The band was rewritten to escape
that, and then the grade moved 1718 K below the sun, which is FURTHER
than the condition it escaped.

### Finding 2 — the band's calibration specimen no longer exists
> STATUS: SUPERSEDED — Caveat on 1.1243 baseline; baseline since re-solved (R-WB2x2 A-6). Superseded. [Pass 5 ruling, 2026-09-16]

At IDENTICAL WB 5200 this world reads 0.7674 where Brief 2b read 1.1243:
32% lower. The scene changed — the five-layer material put scree and
forest_floor in frame as real surfaces, and `shadow_tint_B` is a
statistic over the land region, so changing what the land IS changes it.

**And the 1.1243 was itself measured against the month-stale weightmap.**
Its authority is weaker than its status as "the ruled baseline" implies.

### What follows

NEITHER endpoint passes: 1.8051 too high at the locked grade, 0.7674 too
low at the band's own calibration point. Interpolating the two measured
points puts the 1.10-1.60 band at WB ~3725-4490 K, with R-GRADE's
card-derived 3481.9 sitting just below the window — an INDICATION, not a
solve, because the response is documented to saturate.

Two locked rulings, derived by different valid methods, disagree:

    R-GRADE   WB from the grey card -> 3481.9 (1718 K below the sun)
    the band  assumes WB AT the sun -> 1.10-1.60

### The rule

**AN ACCEPTANCE BAND IS CALIBRATED AGAINST A SPECIMEN AND A CONFIG, AND
BOTH CAN EXPIRE.** This one outlived its white point AND its world. A
band carried forward while the thing it was calibrated on changes
underneath it stops being an acceptance and becomes a number that fails.

The tell was available before any of today's captures: the band's
docstring NAMES the condition it requires ("under neutral WB"), and the
grade had moved away from it. Reading the acceptance's own premise
against the current config would have found this without a single
render.


## 2026-09-12i — THE BAND RE-DERIVED AT THE GRADE IN FORCE, AND THE VERDICT REVERSES

### The re-derivation
> STATUS: HISTORY — band re-derived; the verdict reverses

    sun 5200 K, white_temp 3481.9 K -> 94.89 mired below neutral

    measured WB factor   2.3522   (B 0.7674 -> 1.8051, one variable)
    Planck prediction    2.4525   (9454 K, the project's own slope)
    disagreement         4.09%    -> CORROBORATED

    band at neutral WB   1.10 - 1.60
    band AT THIS GRADE   2.587 - 3.764
    measured B           1.8051   = 0.6976 of the floor   FAIL

**Applied untransformed the band said the shade was TOO BLUE. Transformed
to the grade in force it says the shade is 30.2% UNDER-blue.** The world
needs MORE sky fill, not less.

### Why it was derivable now and not this morning

This morning the only route was extrapolating from two HISTORICAL points
that differed in SUN as well as WB, on a response known to saturate; a
linear and a log model over-predicted the actual reading by 28% and 58%.
I refused to re-derive on that basis, and that refusal was right.

The WB test replaced the model with a MEASUREMENT of the response — same
station, same world, same instrument, one variable. The transform then
needs no extrapolation at all, only a scale factor that was measured
directly and corroborated independently.

**A transform you can MEASURE beats a transform you must MODEL, and the
way to get one is to move the variable deliberately and capture both
ends.**

### What this reverses

    sky 1.0 -> 1.6, then reverted   the JUSTIFICATION was invalid (wrong
                                    stations) but the DIRECTION was right;
                                    I reverted a change that was moving
                                    toward the answer
    Mie 0.02 REJECTED               rejected for moving B "the wrong way"
                                    (1.8051 -> 1.8379). Against the
                                    corrected band that is movement TOWARD
                                    the floor. Still a poor lever (+1.8%
                                    against a needed +43%, costing 9%
                                    scene luminance) but the STATED REASON
                                    was wrong

Both rejections were made against a band applied outside its calibrated
white point. **A verdict inherits every premise of the instrument that
produced it** — including the ones the instrument documents and the
reader skips.

### The caveat that bounds it

Back-predicting the HISTORICAL band is weaker than predicting our own
measurement: the old era (WB 1300 K below a 7800 K sun, 25.64 mired,
factor 1.2743) transforms the neutral band to [1.402, 2.039] against the
actually-ruled [1.3, 1.7] — 8% and 20% out. The old band was chosen from
photographic reference rather than derived, so it need not match, but it
is a fair bound: **treat the re-derived band as good to 10-20%, not to
three decimals.** Even at the pessimistic end, 1.8051 against a 2.587
floor is a miss no plausible transform error closes.

### The thing that is NOT evidence

The scene's deficit is 0.6976 of the floor at BOTH white points. That is
ALGEBRA — scaling the band and the reading by one factor cannot change
their ratio — and it is reported explicitly because it looks exactly like
a second confirmation and is not one. The only independent check here is
the Planck cross-check at 4%.


## 2026-09-12j — THE SKY-INTENSITY SLOPE, MEASURED: NO LIGHTING LEVER CLOSES THIS
> STATUS: SUPERSEDED — 'Sky cannot close deficit' — deficit from superseded band; re-derived band passes without sky change. Moot. [Pass 5 ruling, 2026-09-16]

### The number

near_ground, target class, one variable, read back at both ends
(1.0 and 1.600000023):

    sky 1.0   B 1.8051   R 0.70   shadow_luma 0.00475   lit 0.12044
    sky 1.6   B 1.9885   R 0.61   shadow_luma 0.00551   lit 0.11960

    SLOPE 0.3057 B per unit   (predicted ~0.60 — 2x optimistic;
                               the inherited 0.375 was also wrong here)

THE SKY IS WORKING. shadow_luma rose 16% and R fell 0.70 -> 0.61, so the
shadows genuinely take more blue fill. The RATIO simply moves slowly.

REACHING THE RE-DERIVED FLOOR OF 2.587 NEEDS SKY ~3.56 — nearly double
the 1.8 rejected on 2026-09-09 for over-filling, and 3.5x the settled
value. Sky intensity cannot close a 30% deficit at this station.

### The whole series, one variable each
> STATUS: HISTORY — no lighting lever closes the deficit

    sky   Mie    pre   WB       B        delta
    1.0   0.01   4     3481.9   1.8051   baseline
    1.0   0.02   4     3481.9   1.8379   +0.033   Mie
    1.0   0.01   16    3481.9   1.8051    0.000   pre-exposure
    1.0   0.01   4     5200     0.7674   -1.038   white balance
    1.6   0.01   4     3481.9   1.9885   +0.183   sky intensity

**Only white balance has real authority over this metric** — 1.038 of
swing against 0.183 from a 60% sky increase — and WB is locked by R-GRADE
on card-derived evidence. Every lever that is free to move is too weak;
the one that is strong enough is not free.

### What that means

The deficit is not a lighting fault. The same world reads 0.7674 at
NEUTRAL WB where Brief 2b read 1.1243 on 2026-09-10: a 32% drop in shade
blue at identical grade and lighting. What changed is WHAT IS IN THE
FRAME — the five-layer material put scree and forest_floor in as real
surfaces, and `shadow_tint_B` is a statistic over the LAND REGION.

**The band was calibrated against a world that no longer exists.**

### The rule

**WHEN EVERY AVAILABLE LEVER IS TOO WEAK AND THE ONLY STRONG ONE IS
LOCKED, THE PREMISE IS WRONG — STOP TUNING.** Five conditions were
measured before that became obvious, and each individually looked like
"not enough, try more". The series is what showed it: the required sky
value (3.56) is outside any range the project has ever accepted, so no
amount of stepping gets there honestly.

A measured slope is worth more than the value it fails to reach. The
inherited 0.375 had been quietly steering sky decisions all day — including
one excursion I made and reverted on the strength of it — and it came
from a different white point and a different world.


## 2026-09-12k — THE BAND COULD NOT BE RE-DERIVED, BUT THE METRIC COULD

### Why the band could not be re-derived against our own content
> STATUS: HISTORY — the band stays an external reference

`shadow_tint_B`'s band is an EXTERNAL perceptual reference —
"photographic reference and the Epic frames put shade under a clear sky
at roughly 1.3-1.7; below ~1.3 the shade reads dead and unlit, above
~1.7 no viewer accepts it as shade". Re-deriving it against our own
frames would fit the acceptance to the artefact, which is the
concavity-gate defect exactly: a gate calibrated to pass whatever it was
shown.

So the request was answered one level down: re-derive the METRIC, and
leave the band's independence intact.

### The defect, confirmed by two instruments that disagree
> STATUS: HISTORY — shadow_tint_B measures terrain albedo

    shadow_tint_B (terrain)   1.8051   an 80% blue excess
    grey card, same frame     highlight_tint R 1.026 / B 1.0455  PASS

**Both cannot describe the illuminant.** The card is a known 18% neutral
plane, so it is the controlled surface and it says the light is neutral
to within 6%. `shadow_tint_B` is therefore measuring TERRAIN ALBEDO.

That is `highlight_tint`'s ruled defect one step over — it "remains a
measurement of the meadow's albedo ... its instrument is now the GREY
CARD (ruled 2026-09-10)" because it "presumes a neutral sunlit surface".
shadow_tint_B presumes a neutral SHADED surface, and the card cannot fix
it the same way because the card is in SUN.

Measured consequence: the five-layer material replaced WildGrass and
Rock051 with warm litter (0.2760) and grey scree (0.2228), and B fell
1.1243 -> 0.7674 at IDENTICAL grade and lighting. The light never moved.

### The re-derived metric, and its honest limits

    shade_over_sun_B = (B_shadow/luma_shadow) / (B_lit/luma_lit)

Albedo appears in both terms and cancels to first order; so does any
GLOBAL colour transform, because it scales both halves alike.

    spread across five conditions
      shadow_tint_B      2.741x
      shade_over_sun_B   1.235x     2.2x more stable

    cancels Mie          to 0.07%
    cancels pre-exposure exactly
    WB residual          19%   (down from 60%, NOT zero)
    sky response         -4.8%, INVERTED

**TWO FAILURES, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED.** The WB residual survives
because the shadow/lit populations are chosen by a MEDIAN LUMINANCE
SPLIT — change the image and different pixels land in each half, so the
cancellation is approximate by construction. And sky 1.6 raised blue in
the LIT half (+16%) more than in the shade (+10%), so the ratio FELL:
the metric moves the wrong way for the one lever it should track.

### What it is not
> STATUS: HISTORY — 2026-09-12k clarification of what the metric is not; narrative

**It has no band.** 1.10-1.60 belongs to the old metric. Calibrating the
new one needs a daylight-shade reference measured the SAME way — a
photographic derivation, not something extractable from our own frames
without the circularity refused at the top of this entry.

So this is a better INSTRUMENT and not yet an ACCEPTANCE. Saying so is
the point: a metric promoted to an acceptance without its own reference
is how the old band came to be applied outside the white point it was
calibrated at.

### The rule

**WHEN A METRIC MOVES BECAUSE THE SUBJECT CHANGED RATHER THAN THE
QUANTITY, THE METRIC IS MEASURING THE SUBJECT.** The test is cheap and
was available all along: put a CONTROLLED surface in the frame and ask
whether it agrees. The card had been in every one of these frames,
masked out of the scene statistic, saying the light was fine.

## 2026-09-12c — THE FIVE-LAYER MIGRATION BROKE PLACEMENT, AND A STRATIFIED SAMPLE CAME BACK BIASED

### What was attempted

R-METER, and the ruled town-placement work: put the settlement exclusion
`plan_encounters` uses into `place_foliage`, regenerate, re-derive
weights.

### 1. `place_foliage` had not been runnable since the layer change

First run died at `index 4 is out of bounds for axis 2 with size 3`.

**Root cause:** `place_foliage.load_inputs` read the weightmap with
`.convert("RGB")` — three channels — while `recipes/alpine_8k.json` now
declares FIVE layers. Every tree species is keyed to `Grass`, which is
layer index 4. Under the five-layer contract four layers are stored
channels and the LAST is the shader remainder `1-(R+G+B+A)`; Grass has
no channel of its own at all.

**It failed loudly, and that is the only reason this is a bug report.**
Had the recipe declared FOUR layers, Grass would have been index 3, the
read would have succeeded against the ALPHA channel, and the run would
have planted a plausible, wrong forest in silence. The loud failure was
luck, not design.

Fixed by loading RGBA and adding `_layer_weight`, which imports
`mask_plan` from the material builder rather than restating the mapping
(NN24), and samples the remainder PER CHANNEL at the sample points —
bilinear interpolation is linear, so sampling-then-summing equals
summing-then-sampling exactly, and the 528 MB full-grid array the naive
form would allocate never exists.

Verified against a DIFFERENT instrument (NN8): nearest-neighbour lookup
agrees on a stored channel to 5 decimal places (0.09865 vs 0.09863,
whole-map 0.09923).

### 2. ⛔ OPEN: A JITTERED LATTICE RETURNED HALF THE FIELD'S MEAN

With the crash fixed, regeneration produced **152 instances where the
shipped plans carry 219,659**. The cause is NOT the exclusion, NOT the
RNG's quality, and NOT the field.

Reduced to its smallest form: sample the remainder field at
`round((col+u)*15.22097)`, `round((row+v)*15.22097)` for
`col,row = 0..533` and `u,v ~ U(0,1)` from `default_rng(20276569)`.

    whole-map remainder mean                    0.25174
    regular grid, u=v=0.5, same spacing         0.25123
    uniform random positions, same count        0.25058
    JITTERED LATTICE                            0.13153

**A jittered lattice is stratified sampling, which is unbiased by
construction** — each cell is sampled uniformly at random, so the
expectation is the map mean. 0.13153 is not a near miss; it is 48% low.

It is narrow, and every axis was checked:

    cells=534 spacing 15.2210  regular 0.25123  jittered 0.13153  <-- only this
    cells=400 spacing 20.3200  regular 0.25121  jittered 0.25100
    cells=512 spacing 15.8750  regular 0.25117  jittered 0.25152
    cells=813 spacing  9.9975  regular 0.25139  jittered 0.25158
    cells=1000 spacing 8.1280  regular 0.25172  jittered 0.25204

    seed 20276569 (shipped)  expected 13,059  kept     36  ratio 0.0028
    seed 20276570            expected 36,620  kept 36,647  ratio 1.0007
    seed 1 / 2 / 12345 / 999999                          ratio 0.998-1.005

Ruled out by measurement, not by argument:

- **The generator.** All three blocks of seed 20276569 are uniform
  (mean 0.5005/0.4996/0.5011, std 0.2887) and mutually independent
  (|corr| < 0.0022). Block 3 correlates with no function of block 1
  tested — raw, sub-pixel phase, pixel parity, thresholds: all < 0.005.
- **The field.** The remainder is smooth, not a dither: lag-1
  autocorrelation 0.79 against 0.81–0.83 for stored channels, 256
  distinct values.
- **Coverage.** The candidate indices span all 8,129 values on both
  axes, marginal histograms are flat (4419–4495 per 64 bins), and 2D
  occupancy over 16×16 bins is flat (1101–1127).
- **Stored channels.** Snow is unaffected at every spacing and seed.

The surviving signature: `r[pc>0].mean() = 0.711` against
`r[pc==0].mean() = 0.470` — the acceptance draws are systematically high
exactly where the density is non-zero — while `r` is uniform across
index deciles (0.4981–0.5026). The remainder layer is the only field
that shows it.

**This is recorded OPEN with a four-line repro rather than worked
around.** Regeneration is BLOCKED until it is explained: a fix that made
the count look right without explaining the bias would be a forest
placed by a mechanism nobody understands.

### 3. What was delivered instead, and why it is stronger

`recipes/city.json` had argued the exclusion **could not** live in the
foliage recipe: *"re-planting with an exclusion mask would RE-ROLL all
219,659 positions and move the entire forest."*

That is true of a mask applied DURING SAMPLING, which changes how many
draws the generator makes and shifts every subsequent value. It is not
true of a filter applied AFTER the rows are built. `--exclude-only` goes
further and constructs no generator at all: it filters the COMMITTED
plans in place.

    219,659 before -> 2,557 removed -> 217,102 after
    tree instances inside the town footprint:  0
    survivors: IDENTICAL rows, in order, all four species

The 2,557 is 2,541 oriented-rectangle hits plus 16 from the plaza disc.
**The 2,541 is the number `city.json` recorded from its own margin sweep
("3 m removes 2,541")** — reproduced by an independent implementation
over a different artefact, which is what corroboration looks like.

**The claim was ARGUED for three weeks and was testable in one line.**
Assertion "survivors == the original rows" now runs every time.

### 4. The clear and the plan were two representations of one forest

The editor-side clear removes INSTANCES. `derive_layer_weights` reads
the PLACEMENT JSON. So the world had the trees cleared and the weightmap
still painted ForestFloor under the town, and no audit could see it
because each artefact was internally consistent.

    buildings whose dominant layer is ForestFloor:  43.23%  ->  0.00%

That drop is the whole point of putting the exclusion in the authored
file: it is the weight derivation, not the editor, that downstream reads.

### 5. `city_clear_foliage_payload` has no caller, and its plaza gate is inverted

Nothing in the repo fills its `__BUILDING_MARGIN_M__` placeholders. It
also gates the plaza disc on `PLAZA_MARGIN_M > 0.0`, so a ZERO margin
clears no plaza at all — contradicting `city.json`'s own declaration
that *"the cleared disc is plan.plaza_radius_cm PLUS this margin"*, under
which zero still clears the plan's 22 m. The shipped value is 6.0, so the
gate is INERT today and would have bitten the first time someone set it
to zero meaning "no extra margin". `town_exclusion` follows the
declaration; its selftest caught this at a margin production never uses.

### The rules

**A CONTRACT CHANGE IS NOT DONE WHEN THE THING IT NAMES COMPILES.** The
five-layer material was built, audited (32 samplers, 0 mismatches; 197
expressions, 0 orphaned) and verified in-world — and the tool that
populates that world could not run at all. The audit proved properties
of the GRAPH. Nothing asked the PRODUCERS whether they still agreed.

**AN UNBIASED ESTIMATOR THAT RETURNS A BIASED ANSWER IS A FINDING, NOT A
NUISANCE.** Stratified sampling cannot be 48% low. When the arithmetic
says impossible and the measurement is reproducible, the answer is a
minimal repro and an OPEN, never a workaround that restores the
expected number.

**WHEN A DOCUMENT SAYS SOMETHING CANNOT BE DONE, CHECK WHETHER IT MEANS
A SPECIFIC MECHANISM.** "It would re-roll every position" was a correct
statement about sampling-time masking and a false one about the goal.
The distinction cost one line to test and had gone untested since
2026-08-25.

## 2026-09-13a — THE WARM-UP THAT NEVER RENDERED, AND A GPU CRASH IN THE VIEWPORT

### 1. Every capture this project has taken ran with ZERO rendered warm-up

`MoviePipelineAntiAliasingSetting` has two warm-up fields and they are
not the same warm-up:

    engine_warm_up_count    ticks the GAME thread, renders nothing
    render_warm_up_count    RENDERED frames, discarded before the measured one
    render_warm_up_frames   the BOOL that gates the count

Defaults read back from 5.8: `render_warm_up_count` **32**,
`render_warm_up_frames` **False**. `bench_capture` set the ENGINE count
to 300 and never touched either render field. So the count of 32 was
inert, every capture rendered zero warm-up frames, and the sidecar
recorded `"warm_up_frames": 300` the whole time.

**A COUNT WITHOUT ITS ENABLING BOOL IS PROSE** — standing rule 12's
shape, one level down. The rule says a declared value must be applied
and read back; this adds that **the read-back must include whatever
GATES the value**, because a number that is never consulted reads back
perfectly.

Turning it on moved the card from a predicted 0.180 to a measured
0.216851, about **+0.27 EV**. Every exposure solve before today was made
against a frame the engine had not settled.

### 2. Q12: the compression survives every lever, so it is not adaptation
> STATUS: HISTORY — Q12 resolved: grade/tonemap, not adaptation

Four conditions, one card, one station, agreeing to within 0.007 EV:

    Histogram, no render warm-up                          -0.7266
    Manual,    no render warm-up                          -0.7221
    Manual,    render warm-up 32 ON                       -0.7196
    Manual,    warm-up ON + fixed PreExposureOverride 1.0 -0.7261

Render warm-up moved the LEVEL and not the SLOPE. A fixed pre-exposure
moved neither. Eye adaptation cannot be the cause: `AEM_MANUAL` with the
clamp pinned 1.0/1.0 has none, and the slope is unchanged.

**THE STAGES, READ FROM THE CONFIG RATHER THAN RECALLED.** The probe
builds the config the way `bench_render` does and enumerates it:
DeferredPassBase, ImageSequenceOutput_PNG, ImageSequenceOutput_EXR,
ColorSetting (ocio disabled), AntiAliasing, GameOverride, ConsoleVariable,
Output; the deferred pass's WorldDepth and MotionVectors materials both
disabled; `disable_multisample_effects` False.

The deferred pass writes **through the post stack with only the tone
curve removed**, so the GRADE still runs — and a grading contrast about
a pivot IS a power law, `log2(out) = c*log2(in/0.18) + log2(0.18)`. Read
back live: `color_contrast` **0.95, override IN FORCE**; every other
contrast/gamma/gain 1.0 with overrides off; `film_slope` 0.88,
`film_toe` 0.55, `tone_curve_amount` 1.0, tonemapping FILMIC.

0.95 alone is not 0.723, and 0.95 x 0.88 = 0.836 is not either. **So the
grade is a FACTOR and not the answer, and saying so is the point** — the
temptation was to stop at "contrast 0.95, case closed" because it has
the right shape.

Also worth naming: `disable_tone_curve_readback` reads the MRQ property
we set. Under rule 12 that proves the SETTER ran, not that the tonemapper
honoured it.

### 3. A GPU crash, and what it taught about reading a wedged process

    06:29:03  Engine Initialization Total time: 25.21 s
    06:29:03  Texture pool size now 9598 MB
    06:29:39  GPU crash detected: Device 0 Removed: DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED
              at D3D12Viewport.cpp:537
    06:38:45  RequestExit(1, D3D12Util.TerminateOnGPUCrash)

36 s after load, in the **viewport Present path**, rendering an 8129²
Nanite/Lumen world with hardware ray tracing at an uncapped rate.

**I had already diagnosed that process as "wedged idle" from outside** —
flat RSS, low CPU, remote exec dead, `Responding=False` — and cited
R-EDITOR-CLOSE's fourth occurrence. The gate's action was right and its
outcome was right (empty `PackageRestoreData`, nothing lost), but the
CAUSE I attached to it was wrong, and I only learned that because the
operator said "got a gpu crash error". The recipe's own line covers this
exactly: *do not diagnose the hang from outside — the gate already
measures everything the decision needs.* I diagnosed anyway.

Relaunching with **`-RenderOffScreen`** removed the crash site and every
capture since has been clean. `r.GPUCrashDebugging` is 0, which is why
Aftermath timed out and DRED had no breadcrumbs — worth turning on if it
recurs.

**Correction to 2026-09-12d:** I attributed an earlier capture death to
RAM pressure. That still stands — this is the only `GPUCrash` in
`Saved/Crashes`; the others are `Ensure` conditions.

### 4. `-RenderOffScreen` makes the graceful close impossible

`CloseMainWindow()` returned **False** twice at shutdown. There is no
main window to close. Census was clean, quiet 926 s, restore data empty,
so the kill was authorised on the original step 4 — but the rule's
"close, then RETRY, then kill" assumes a window exists.

**A LAUNCH FLAG CAN REMOVE A GATE'S INSTRUMENT.** If you launch
offscreen, plan to end on the kill path and prove it is safe the other
ways (census, quiet, restore file), rather than reading two `False`
returns as an unresponsive editor.

### 5. The blocker that could not be a plane

R-SHADE needs a card occluded from the SUN. The blocker's normal must
face the sun to cast a wide shadow — and this sun sits far off the
card-to-camera ray, so the camera sees a plane blocker nearly EDGE-ON.
An edge-on plane projects to a thin diagonal sliver whose axis-aligned
bounding box is enormous: **838 x 942 px**, which the overlap gate
refused.

A cube is non-degenerate from every angle. Sizing was then MEASURED, not
estimated: at 60 cm the separation came out 300 px against half-widths
of 210 and 139 — 49 px of overlap. 90 cm with a 40 cm cube leaves ~280
px clear.

**The overlap gate earned its place on its first run**, refusing
mid_slope where the card-to-sun ray projects onto the card. Without it
the measurement would have read the blocker's own surface as a card and
returned a lighting verdict.

And the payload had already SPAWNED all three stations before the
host-side refusal, leaving instrument actors standing in mid_slope's
frame — which would change what every later capture of that station
measures, silently. The payload now destroys pair actors at stations not
requested. **A refusal that happens after the side effect is not a
refusal.**

### 6. Two tile sizes broke a report that assumes one
> STATUS: HISTORY — surface_report NO-VERDICT on mixed tile sizes

Binding `gray_rocks` at its true 1.80 m left the world with tiles of
1.80 and 5.03 m. `surface_report` says so itself — *"layers carry 2
different tile sizes [1.8, 5.03]; the period is derived per-layer and
this report uses the first"* — and then returns **NO VERDICT** on both
depth bins because the autocorrelation peak pins at the search window's
lower edge. The window is +/-40% around 58.0 px, the period of a 1.8 m
tile at 75.9 m; a 5.03 m tile peaks at 162 px, nowhere near it.

Both NO VERDICTs are the instrument being RIGHT. The albedo one is
better still: *"THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT THE BRIEF'S"* — 0.10-0.20 is the
brief's MEADOW band and the measurement is over masked ground, so it
refuses to compare them.

### The rules

**READ BACK THE GATE, NOT ONLY THE VALUE.** A count behind a disabled
bool reads back perfectly and does nothing.

**WHEN A CANDIDATE HAS THE RIGHT SHAPE, CHECK THE MAGNITUDE BEFORE
CLOSING.** Grading contrast is a power law and the residual is a power
law, and it is still not the whole answer: 0.95 against a measured
0.723.

**A FLAG THAT REMOVES A FAILURE MODE CAN REMOVE AN INSTRUMENT TOO.**
`-RenderOffScreen` fixed the GPU crash and silently disabled the
graceful-close path the shutdown gate is built on.

## 2026-09-13b — Q12 LOCATED BY SPLITTING THE CHAIN, AND A GENERATOR THAT ATE ITS OWN OUTPUT

### 1. The compression is the tonemap pass, and a probe pass proved it

A post-process material at **BL_SCENE_COLOR_AFTER_DOF** — 5.8's name for
the location the UI calls *Before Tonemapping* — emitting `SceneTexture`
`PostProcessInput0` unmodified, rendered as an ADDITIONAL pass on the
deferred render. Same two compensations, one variable:

    pass                        -13.882    -14.882   delivered
    PPI0 (before tonemapping)   0.146922   0.073463  -1.0000
    FinalImage                  0.216851   0.131666  -0.7199

The PPI0 ratio is 0.5000136. Exposure is applied LINEARLY upstream; a
requested stop is delivered exactly. Everything that compresses it to
0.72 sits after that split.

**WHY THE ENUM MATTERED MORE THAN THE MATERIAL.** There is no
`BL_BEFORE_TONEMAPPING` in 5.8. Enumerated: BL_REPLACING_TONEMAPPER,
BL_SCENE_COLOR_AFTER_DOF, BL_SCENE_COLOR_AFTER_TONEMAPPING,
BL_SCENE_COLOR_BEFORE_BLOOM, BL_SCENE_COLOR_BEFORE_DOF, BL_SSR_INPUT,
BL_TRANSLUCENCY_AFTER_DOF. Guessing the OLD name raises; guessing a
PLAUSIBLE new one (`BEFORE_BLOOM`) builds a material that compiles and
samples a different point in the chain, and the whole experiment then
answers a question nobody asked. The payload resolves the member off the
reflected surface and reports which one answered.

### 2. Contrast is a factor and the composition is not a product
> STATUS: WRONG — WRONG 2026-09-13c: composition IS multiplicative; inverted the next day

    contrast 0.95   delivered -0.7199
    contrast 1.00   delivered -0.7969

A multiplicative model predicts 0.7199/0.95 = 0.7578; measured 0.7969,
high by 0.039. **That is what a nonlinear curve does** — changing
contrast moves the card to a different part of the film curve, where its
local slope differs, so two stages cannot simply multiply. The residual
0.7969 is the film curve at this operating point.

The temptation was to stop at "contrast is a power law, contrast is
0.95, case closed". It has the right SHAPE and the wrong MAGNITUDE, and
the difference is only visible if you measure the thing twice.

### 3. I misread my own instrument, and a second instrument caught it

I reported vista's FinalImage EXR as maxing at **exactly 1.00000** and
called it a clamp signature. It was the **ALPHA channel**, which is 1.0
everywhere. RGB only:

    vista        max 0.563477   0 px above 1.0
    near_ground  max 1.029297   1 px above 1.0
    near_ground PPI0  1.590303  167 px above 1.0

Above 1.0 means the tone curve is off, which was the answer all along.
The clamp check found it because it asked a DIFFERENT question — *how
many pixels sit exactly at the ceiling* — and a real clamp has a spike.
**A maximum is one number and one number cannot distinguish a peak from
a clamp**; the distribution can.

Vista also turned out to be the WEAKER test despite having sun and snow,
because the bench sits 14 stops down and nothing in it reaches 1.0. The
brighter station at the brighter compensation was the stronger one.

### 4. ⭐ THE GENERATOR SAMPLES A FIELD ITS OWN OUTPUT CREATED

The 48%-low jittered-lattice sample, open since 2026-09-12d, is a closed
feedback loop:

1. `place_foliage` places trees at jittered-lattice positions P.
2. `derive_layer_weights` splats crown disks at P — forest_floor 0.88418
   there against a map mean of 0.10494, so the Grass remainder
   `1-sum` is **exactly 0.00000** there.
3. Re-running with the same seed regenerates the IDENTICAL P and reads
   the Grass weight AT P.

    candidates landing on a tree pixel   63,129 / 285,156 = 22.14%
    expected if independent                                 0.10%

221x chance. Grass reads zero at a fifth of all candidates, the density
collapses, and 219,659 instances become 152.

**WHAT IT COST TO FIND, AND WHY THAT WAS THE RIGHT ORDER.** Each of
these was ruled out by measurement before the next was tried: the
sampler (clean at strides 1, 2, 4, 8 — only the shipped 15.221 failed),
the RNG (all three blocks uniform and mutually independent at N=534²,
per-group means 0.98x SE, no structure at stride 534), field periodicity
(phase modulation 0.0036 at the pitch), the fancy indexing (matches an
explicit loop to 0.0e+00), and the marginals (8129 distinct indices per
axis, flat histograms, flat occupancy). The pairing test — shuffle
either index and the mean returns to 0.254 — said the PAIRS were
special, and a quarter-cell offset restoring 0.13424 to 0.24717 said
they were special positionally. Only then did "which positions?" have an
obvious answer.

**THE GENERAL RULE: A DERIVED FIELD MUST NOT BE SAMPLED BY THE PROCESS
THAT SEEDED IT.** The layer a species is planted on is derived from that
species' own placement, which makes the second run a different
experiment from the first. Regeneration stays blocked: this is a
contract change, not a patch, and a fix that restored the count without
breaking the loop would just hide it one seed further along.

### 5. An autocorrelation that finds the mask instead of the texture

The first per-layer tiling tool cropped each layer to its bounding box
and filled the non-layer pixels with a mean. **That injects the MASK's
own structure into the signal** — the autocorrelation then measures the
shape of the region, and a layer that appears in stripes reads as a
repeat at the stripe pitch.

Replaced with a mask-NORMALISED autocorrelation, every lag divided by
its valid overlap:

    AC(k) = SUM m(x)m(x+k) g(x)g(x+k) / SUM m(x)m(x+k)

Two selftest directions now cover exactly this: noise under a striped
mask scores **0.016**, and a real 40 px grating under the same mask is
still found at 40. The fill version would have passed neither honestly.

**An instrument that can manufacture its own signal must be tested
against a case where the signal is only the instrument.**

### The rules

**SPLIT THE CHAIN RATHER THAN ARGUING ABOUT IT.** Q12 sat open for
three sessions across four levers — metering, warm-up, pre-exposure,
contrast — each of which moved something and none of which localised
anything. One probe pass that writes the buffer at a known point
answered it in two captures.

**A MAXIMUM CANNOT TELL A PEAK FROM A CLAMP.** Ask the distribution.

**A DERIVED FIELD MUST NOT BE SAMPLED BY THE PROCESS THAT SEEDED IT.**

### 1. The tone curve IS off, proven by the transfer and not by the property

`disable_tone_curve` is what the setter wrote. The honest test is the

    0.001-0.01     0.73186
    0.01-0.1       0.77285
    0.1-1          0.76299      spread 0.04099

have a shoulder; a power law cannot produce one and a shoulder cannot
hide in a straight fit. Per-channel exponents R 0.80398, G 0.76885,
B 0.76536, luma 0.76334.

The read-backs taken from INSIDE the render agree that nothing forced

### 2. â­ CONTRAST IS `xyz * w`, SO 0.95 WAS 0.9025
> STATUS: HISTORY — still-true shader finding; contrast written xyz=1, value in w

`PostProcessCombineLUTs.usf:98`:

    WorkingColor = pow( WorkingColor * (1.0/0.18), ColorContrast.xyz*ColorContrast.w ) * 0.18

`apply_lighting` wrote `Vector4(c, c, c, c)`. All four alike gives an
exponent of **c squared**. A declared 0.95 was an effective 0.9025.

**AND OUR OWN COMMENT WAS THE SEED**: *"the 4th component is the master,
so a global contrast is all four set alike"*. It was written from the
property name, never from the shader, and the code did exactly what it
said.

The error was invisible because it is a plausible number in the right

    0.7199 / 0.9025 = 0.79767
    0.7969 / 1.0000 = 0.79690      agree to 0.001

The composition was multiplicative all along. **A residual that refuses
to compose is evidence about the EXPONENT, not only about the stages.**

Audited the rest: `color_contrast` is the ONLY 4-vector grade parameter
this project writes. Saturation, gamma, gain, offset and every

off. Now written xyz = 1 with the value in w, and the host REFUSES on
the PRODUCT â€” reading the four components back separately could never
have caught this, because each was exactly what the setter wrote.

### 3. The residual is a GAMMA, and the pivot said so before any capture
> STATUS: HISTORY — the residual is an output-encoding gamma; still holds

After contrast, the residual is ~0.797. Pivot distinguishes the two

    a pivot-0.18 contrast maps 0.18 -> 0.18 EXACTLY
    measured: PPI0 card 0.180 -> FinalImage 0.2509

so it is not contrast-shaped. Solving a pivot-1 gamma:

Confirmed by cancellation. The shader's gamma is the RECIPROCAL of the

    gamma 0.797, contrast 0.95
    PPI0        0.179917 -> 0.089973    delivered -0.99977
    FinalImage  0.180359 -> 0.093450    delivered -0.94870   predicted -0.95

â›” The fix is the WRONG STAGE, not a compensating gamma. The 0.797 is an
output-encoding property; cancelling it with a grade gamma would bury a
transfer inside a look control.

> STATUS: HISTORY — the shade band belongs in the linear domain; in force

PPI0 is the SCENE-LINEAR instrument (exposure, albedo, anything

R-GREYCARD re-solved on PPI0: the correction applies at FACE VALUE

    scene-linear   2.184 - 2.940
    FinalImage     1.8182 - 2.2827   at e_B 0.76536
    measured       2.2598            PASS, near the ceiling

It passed before and it passes now, with far less margin than the
wrong-domain comparison implied.

### 5. Two writers, one slot â€” twice in one session

`stage_probe` wrote a FIXED filename, so staging a second probe would
have overwritten the first and MRQ would have run one probe twice.
Caught before it ran.

`bench_render` then did `set_editor_property("additional_post_process_

silently dropping the PPI0 pass. `--depth` with `--pp-pass` produced an
EXR with SceneDepth and no PPI0, and the only symptom was a missing
channel four steps later. **Both are the same shape: a slot with one
writer acquires a second, and last-one-wins is silent.**

### 6. The metric that found the lighting gradient

The per-layer tiling tool reported every layer NO VERDICT with a global
autocorrelation peak at 2 px and 0.77â€“0.98 correlation. That is a
monotonic decay â€” the signature of SMOOTH CONTENT, not of a repeat. The
desk's `tiling_score` detrends first (`hi = L - box_blur(L, period)`)
and mine did not, so mine was measuring the lighting gradient.

With the detrend added, and michelson computed the desk's way
(`2*hi_std*sqrt(peak)/mean`), every layer and bin reads **FAIL**:
0.146â€“0.399 against CSF thresholds 0.011â€“0.053.

**Cross-checked against the desk's own tool on the same frame** â€” a
different implementation, 2-D and ring-based where mine is 1-D and
