But the detected period PINS AT THE RING'S INNER EDGE every time (38.3
px against a predicted 63.8). At 69 m and 42.67 px/deg that is **1.07
m** â€” the landscape's 1 m vertex pitch. So the failure is NOT evidence
that the texture tiles repeat visibly; it is strong sub-tile structure
at the terrain grid that this metric counts as periodic. Recorded as
measured, not as a tiling PASS.

### 7. A selftest boundary that does not exist

Two attempts to test "exactly at the tolerance" failed, both because the
boundary is NOT REPRESENTABLE: `1.0/(1-TOL)` lands a hair below, and

below. **A test that cannot construct the value it claims to test is not
a test.** Replaced with both sides â€” 2% above must not settle, 2% below
must.

### The rules

**A PROPERTY IS NOT A TRANSFER.** `disable_tone_curve` says what was
asked for. Two taps on one frame say what happened.

**WHEN A COMPOSITION REFUSES TO COMPOSE, SUSPECT THE EXPONENT.** The
"non-multiplicative" result was a squared exponent, and the arithmetic
closed to 0.001 the moment it was read from the shader instead of the
property name.

**PIVOT IS FREE EVIDENCE.** A pivot-0.18 op fixes 0.18. One card reading

## 2026-09-13d â€” THE PERIOD WAS THE WEIGHTMAP, AND THE "1.07 m" WAS MY OWN WINDOW EDGE
> STATUS: HISTORY — no 1 m period; "1.07 m" was a search-window edge

### 1. A number I reported was an artefact of the search, not the world
> STATUS: HISTORY — retracts the 1.07 m as a search-window artefact

Last session I reported the detected period as "38.3 px = 1.07 m at
69 m â€” the landscape's 1 m vertex pitch". **That was the search
window's lower bound**, 0.6 x the predicted period, converted to metres.
Running the same instrument across layers makes it obvious: Rock reads
1.07 m, Scree 1.17-1.19 m, Grass 3.01 m â€” three "periods" that are
simply three different windows. The world was never measured to have a
1 m period at all.

**A value that pins at a search bound is a property of the SEARCH.** It
had the right order of magnitude and a tempting physical
interpretation â€” 1 m is the landscape's vertex pitch â€” and that is
exactly what made it dangerous.

### 2. The discriminator, and it worked first time

A post-process pass emitting `PPI_BASE_COLOR` at
BL_SCENE_COLOR_AFTER_DOF: the GBuffer albedo carries the weightmap blend
and the surface textures and NO lighting.

    michelson          FinalImage -> BaseColor
    30-100   Rock         0.1511     0.1673
    30-100   Scree        0.3272     0.3897
    30-100   Grass        0.4163     0.6227
    100-300  Rock         0.1995     0.2498
    100-300  Scree        0.2716     0.3362
    100-300  Grass        0.3582     0.4762

PRESENT in BaseColor and STRONGER there -> not shading. (Stronger
because lighting adds smooth variation that dilutes the relative
contrast, which is the expected direction and worth checking rather
than hand-waving.)

Then the weights-vs-textures question, by a diagnostic 2-texel blur of
the weightmap:

    Rock  30-100  -41.4%      Rock  100-300  -26.3%
    Scree 30-100  -31.7%      Scree 100-300  -27.2%
    Grass 30-100  +27.8%      Grass 100-300  -11.9%

**The weightmap carries it.** Grass RISING is not a contradiction: Grass
is the shader REMAINDER, 1-(R+G+B+A), so blurring the stored channels
reshapes its mask rather than smoothing it. A metric that moved the
wrong way on one layer and the right way on four is more informative
than one that moved uniformly â€” the exception named the mechanism.

Weightmap restored with `git checkout --`, re-imported, freshness gate
re-run. Nothing committed.

### 3. Splitting one verdict into the two questions it was conflating

Every layer had been reading FAIL against a threshold meant for a TILE
repeat, while what the instrument actually found was the monotone decay
the weightmap's sub-tile structure produces. One metric, two questions,
and the answer to the loud one was drowning the quiet one.

    (a) TEXTURE TILE  local peak PROMINENCE above the window's trend
    (b) GRID          the window max, recorded with NO tile verdict

The prominence fit is a straight line across the window, subtracted;
whatever BUMPS above it is a repeat, and a featureless decay has no
bump at all. With that split, 5 of 6 measurable layer-bins PASS, and
Scree at 30-100 m fails on a real local peak at 85 px = 2.40 m against
its 2.00 m tile.

**A verdict that fails everything is usually measuring the wrong thing.**
Six failures with no variation should have been read as an instrument
symptom a session earlier than it was.

### 4. The shade acceptance moves to the linear instrument, and needed no capture
> STATUS: HISTORY — shade acceptance on PPI0 (linear); current method

PPI0 carries no white balance â€” its lit card reads B/luma 0.4667 â€” so a
shade ratio off it raw is in camera-native space. The fix needs no grade
and no capture: **divide each channel by the LIT CARD's own channel**.
The lit card is an 18% neutral, so it IS the white reference; this is a
von Kries adaptation performed with the reference physically in frame.

    PPI0        2.5166   band 2.184-2.940 UNTRANSFORMED   PASS, mid-band
    FinalImage  2.2598   band 1.8182-2.2827 transformed   PASS, at the ceiling

The linear instrument gives the comfortable answer and the look
instrument the marginal one, which is the right way round: the band was
derived from illuminant spectra and belongs in linear light.

### 5. A warning that fired on a correct result

The SceneTextureId read-back check stripped underscores from the
read-back and not from the needle, so it warned on a CORRECT
`PPI_BASE_COLOR`. The register already carries "a diagnostic that fires
every run stops being a diagnostic" as a REJECTED entry and this nearly
repeated it. Now a verbatim comparison, and a mismatch REFUSES rather
than warns â€” a pass sampling the wrong buffer is the silent-wrong class.

### 6. A crop that answered the wrong band

The 1:1 ground crop for review came back spanning 1.7-10485 m for a
50-100 m request. A depth band is a horizontal STRIP, so its bounding
box is nearly the whole frame and a square cut centred on the centroid
overflowed into sky. Fixed by choosing rows from the band's own extent
and centring on the row with the most band pixels, and by REPORTING the
fraction of crop pixels actually in band (31.6%) so it cannot pass
unnoticed again.

### The rules

**A VALUE THAT PINS AT A SEARCH BOUND IS A PROPERTY OF THE SEARCH.**
Run the same instrument across several windows; if the "measurement"
tracks the window, it was never a measurement.

**WHEN EVERYTHING FAILS, SUSPECT THE QUESTION.** Six identical failures
meant one metric was being asked two questions.

**THE EXCEPTION NAMES THE MECHANISM.** Grass moving the wrong way under
the blur is what identified it as the remainder.

## 2026-09-13e — THE WEIGHT-DRIVEN COMPONENT HAS NO PERIOD, AND TWO ESTIMATORS DIED PROVING IT

### 1. The question the last two sessions could not ask
> STATUS: HISTORY — the weight component is broadband, no period

Split (b) — the weight-driven component — had a Michelson and no period.
The 1.07 m I once reported for it was the search window's own lower
bound. So: measure it with **no predicted period anywhere in the
instrument**, band 0.3–20 m.

### 2. Two estimators built, both REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT before the
> STATUS: HISTORY — both estimators rejected; autocorrelation works
world saw them

**(i) OPEN WINDOW, TAKE THE MAX.** Dead on arrival for the same reason
the old one was. The autocorrelation decays with lag, so the max over
*any* window sits at that window's short end. This would have reported
"0.3 m" with precisely the confidence the 1.07 m carried. **Widening a
window does not fix an estimator that reports window edges.**

**(ii) SWEEP THE PREDICTED PERIOD, take the best local-peak prominence.**
This one looked right — it reuses the proven split-(a) machinery, just
over a sweep of hypotheses instead of one. The selftest killed it:

    grating 1.0 m   ->  reported 2.013 m
    grating 4.0 m   ->  reported 8.026 m

Both doubled. **Prominence is conditioned on the hypothesis it is given.**
The autocorrelation of a repeat has peaks at *every* multiple of the
period, so a window centred on 2 m finds the 2 m peak of a 1 m signal
and scores it beautifully. The estimator has no way to prefer the
fundamental because nothing in it knows the others are the same line.

### 3. The instrument that works, and why it is the right shape

**THE SPECTRUM OF THE AUTOCORRELATION.** The AC of a sinusoid is a
cosine at the same period — so its spectrum is ONE line, and every
harmonic peak in the AC belongs to that line instead of competing with
it. A pure decay puts all its power below the band and shows no line at
all, which is exactly the distinction split (b) needs: a REPEAT versus a
CORRELATION LENGTH.

Two instruments over the same data, not one (NN8): the **spectrum**
locates the line, the **autocorrelation** at that lag gives its
contrast.

**The floor was DERIVED, on controls, before the instrument was pointed
at the world:**

    POSITIVE  gratings 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.4 / 4.0 / 8.0 m
              found at 0.500 / 1.000 / 2.401 / 4.001 / 7.963 m
              snr 3.2e6 .. 4.0e6  (8 m: 3.7e5)
              1.0 m at 1/3 the amplitude of the noise around it   6.9e5
              1.0 m under an IRREGULAR mask                       2.0e6
    NEGATIVE  smoothed noise 18.06   striped mask 9.82   gradient 3.89

    floor 100 — 5.5x above the worst negative, 3600x under the weakest
    positive. A gap that wide has no tuning room in it, which is the
    point of measuring rather than choosing.

### 4. The answer: there is no period

    bin       layer   strongest line   snr    corr-len   broadband mich
    30-100    Rock       9.246 m       15.7    1.002 m      0.332
    30-100    Scree     12.495 m       20.0    1.433 m      0.695
    30-100    Grass      6.781 m       32.3    2.060 m      1.047
    100-300   Rock       4.425 m       25.7    2.193 m      0.359
    100-300   Scree      9.339 m       20.1    2.968 m      0.472
    100-300   Grass      0.574 m       20.7    5.600 m      0.606

Every line is between 15.7 and 32.3 against a floor of 100 — inside the
negative controls' own range. **The weight-driven component is
BROADBAND, not periodic.** Snow and ForestFloor: 0 px at this station,
no verdict.

### 5. ⭐ AND THE NUMBER THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN THE SAME MISTAKE AGAIN

Rock's correlation length at 30–100 m is **1.002 m**. Our weightmap is
8129 samples over 8128 m = **1.000 m/texel**. Three decimals, a ready
mechanism, and the brief literally asks "if it sits at the weightmap
texel pitch, say which". I nearly had it.

**One bin cannot tell a world pitch from a screen artefact. Two can.** A
world-fixed pitch is a fixed number of METRES, so its size in PIXELS
must shrink with distance; a screen-space process is a fixed number of
PIXELS, so its footprint in METRES must grow.

    layer    corr-len px      spread   corr-len m        spread   conserved
    Rock     35.5 -> 32.2      10%     1.002 -> 2.193     119%    PIXELS
    Scree    50.8 -> 48.2       5%     1.433 -> 2.968     107%    PIXELS
    Grass    66.4 -> 100.5     51%     2.060 -> 5.600     172%    PIXELS

Conserved in PIXELS, every layer. **So it is not the weightmap texel,
not the section, not the component** — whatever the near bin coincides
with. The 1.002 m is a coincidence of viewing distance: at 69 m, 35.5 px
happens to measure one metre.

This check now lives IN the instrument (`cross_bin_check`), not in the
prose around it, because the prose is what failed last time.

### The rules

**WIDENING A WINDOW DOES NOT FIX AN ESTIMATOR THAT REPORTS WINDOW
EDGES.** The 0.3–20 m open window would have reported 0.3 m.

**PROMINENCE IS CONDITIONED ON THE HYPOTHESIS.** Sweeping the hypothesis
does not make it unconditioned — it finds whichever harmonic it is
pointed at.

**A COINCIDENCE AT ONE DISTANCE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. VARY THE
DISTANCE AND SEE WHICH UNIT SURVIVES.** The general form: when a number
matches a known constant, find the parameter the two would disagree
about and move it.

## 2026-09-13f — TASK 4 STOPS AT ITS BASELINE, AND THE MASK IT ASKED FOR CANNOT EXIST

### 1. The ruled metric could not be built, and the reason is a measurement

Task 4's baseline was to be "albedo variation on PPI0 with a lit-only
mask". The mask was to come from the depth pass and sun direction, or
from a shadow-only capture. Neither was usable:

  * **From depth and sun direction** means reconstructing geometry and
    ray-marching it. Our depth pass is **8-bit LOG depth**, ~5.6% per
    LSB — `task3_layer_tables` already confines it to "a distance along
    a known ray" for exactly this reason. Occlusion from it would be
    fiction.
  * **A shadow-only capture** means toggling the sun's shadow casting.
    The session fence says no lighting value moves.

**The third route needed neither: IRRADIANCE = PPI0 / BASECOLOR.** Both
passes were already in the capture, so it costs no render and moves
nothing. A lit pixel gets sun+sky, a shadowed one gets sky alone, and the
surface's own colour divides out.

### 2. ⭐ AND IT REFUSED, WHICH IS THE FINDING

`log(irradiance)` over the meadow is **not bimodal**. One broad, smooth
lobe, p95/p5 = 3.31 at 4–10 m:

           215 | #
           306 | ##########
           436 | ##############################
           621 | ##################################################
           885 | ############################
          1260 | #

There is **no shadow population to separate.** The meadow is thousands
of randomly-oriented grass CARDS, so N·L varies continuously over the
whole range; "sun-visible pixels only" has no clean answer for that
geometry. Rock at 30–100 m is the same shape (p95/p5 = 1.96).

The routine cuts at the VALLEY between two modes or it refuses. It
refused. **A quantile would always have produced a mask and would have
told us nothing about whether there was a shadow to find** — and a
lit-only number built on an invented threshold is exactly the
plausible-and-wrong class.

### 3. The instrument that needed no mask at all
> STATUS: HISTORY — grass albedo 0.2278 above band; Task 4 stopped

The mask exists to stop SHADING contaminating an ALBEDO statistic.
**BaseColor is the GBuffer albedo — shading was never applied to it.**
So std/mean on BaseColor removes lighting *exactly*, rather than
approximately and behind a threshold. Better than what was asked for,
and available from the same capture.

    Grass  4-10 m    BaseColor 0.2278   ABOVE BAND   mean albedo 0.4277
    Grass  3-60 m    BaseColor 0.3075   ABOVE BAND   mean albedo 0.4107
    (PPI0 with shadows: 0.4790 / 0.4971 — a LIGHTING statistic)

**0.2278 against a band of 0.10–0.20.** The ruling's stop condition:
*"If the baseline is already above 0.20 with shadows excluded, stop and
report that number before changing the cards."* It is above under every
available reading — lighting fully removed (0.2278), and with shadows in
(0.4790). **STOPPED. The cards were not touched.** Adding ±8%
PerInstanceRandom hue and brightness would have moved it further out.

### 4. ⛔ THE BASECOLOR PASS IS NOT ALBEDO — IT CARRIES THE EXPOSURE

The first run reported **"only 0 usable pixels"** in every band. Root
cause: a guard `g_bc > 1e-4`, and the pass's MAXIMUM is 6.31e-05. The
guard was above the entire frame.

    BaseColor max 6.31e-05  /  2^-13.5898 (= 8.111e-05)  =  0.778
    BaseColor p99 4.99e-05  /  same                      =  0.615

Bounded by 1 and plausible: **the pass carries the bench's -13.5898 EV
compensation**, like the lit passes. Read as albedo it is wrong by four
orders of magnitude.

**It went unnoticed for two sessions because every consumer so far was
SCALE-INVARIANT** — the split-(b) discriminator, the period spectrum,
std/mean. A constant factor changed none of those numbers, so nothing
complained. The first consumer to need an absolute threshold found it
immediately. The ratio and std/mean stay scale-invariant, so the
constant is RECORDED rather than divided out.

### 5. The band Task 4 asked for is below the bottom of the frame

1–4 m holds **zero pixels** — not a sampling shortfall, a geometry fact.
The frame's nearest non-sky pixel is at **4.110 m**. With a 1.70 m eye
height and 90° hfov, the bottom of frame looks 29.36° below the horizon,
so flat ground enters view at 3.47 m and this terrain slopes away. Every
band asked for is reported with its own pixel count and an empty one
carries that explanation, rather than being quietly swapped for a
reachable one.

### The rules

**WHEN A MASK CANNOT BE BUILT, ASK WHETHER THE QUANTITY CAN BE MEASURED
WHERE THE CONTAMINANT WAS NEVER APPLIED.** BaseColor beat every lit-mask
scheme because shading never touched it.

**A THRESHOLD THAT ALWAYS RETURNS A MASK IS NOT A DETECTOR.** Cut at the
valley of two modes, or refuse and say the population is single.

**A SCALE ERROR HIDES PERFECTLY UNDER SCALE-INVARIANT CONSUMERS.** Every
reader of that pass had been dividing the constant out by accident. The
absence of complaints was not evidence of correctness.

## 2026-09-13g — "5 OF 6 PASS" RESTED ON ONE CAPTURE, AND RE-RUNNING IT BROKE IT

### 1. The check nobody asked for
> STATUS: HISTORY — "5 of 6 pass" rested on a single capture

I only re-ran Task 3's tables to confirm Scree's FAIL on a fresh
capture. Scree reproduced beautifully — 0.06448 against 0.06413, same
85 px lag. **And Grass, which the record says PASSES, came back FAIL.**

Four captures of the same station, Grass 30–100 m:

    t3f     tone curve off, warm-up 40    0.00000  PASS   <- the one recorded
    t3v     tone curve off, warm-up 32    0.07773  FAIL at 199 px
    task3d  tone curve ON,  warm-up 32    0.09331  FAIL at 199 px
    t4base  tone curve off, warm-up 40    0.08023  FAIL at 199 px

**The recorded headline "5 of 6 measurable PASS" rests on t3f alone, and
three of four captures disagree with it.**

### 2. I explained it wrongly first, and the data refuted me within the hour

My first move was to notice that task3d had the tone curve ON and t4base
OFF, and to build a guard around "a CSF threshold is perceptual and
belongs on the display-referred frame". I wrote that guard, cited the
Grass flip as its evidence, and tested it three directions.

**Then t3f and t4base turned out to have IDENTICAL declared settings —
temporal 1, tone curve off, warm-up 40 — and opposite Grass verdicts.**
The tone curve cannot be the cause of something that varies between two
captures that share it.

The guard itself is still right, but for a DIFFERENT number: Scree
30–100 m reads 0.02678 with the curve on and 0.061–0.064 with it off, at
the same 85 px lag. A factor of 2.3 in a value compared against a
perceptual bound. So the guard stayed and **its cited evidence was
corrected in place** — a guard carrying the wrong reason is a guard that
will be removed by the next person who checks the reason.

### 3. What the stable layers say

    Rock   0.00000 in ALL FOUR captures, both bins
    Scree  peak at 85 px in ALL FOUR; only its contrast moves, with the curve
    Grass  0.00000 / 0.07773 / 0.09331 / 0.08023

**Only the layer whose geometry is ANIMATED moves.** The static landscape
is reproducible to the digit.

**Leading hypothesis, and it is labelled as one:** `Meadow`
(grass_medium_01) is the ONLY foliage species in `recipes/alpine_8k.json`
with no `override_materials`. SpruceSub, SpruceSapling and Blueberry all
carry `/Game/Materials/PN_NoWind/…` instances; the grass cards were
missed. So the meadow is the one thing in frame still moving between
renders, and a wind phase that differs per capture would change its
screen structure exactly this way.

**NOT CONFIRMED.** Confirming it needs a no-wind capture of the meadow,
and `scripts/make_nowind_material_instances.py` already exists for
exactly this. I am not claiming it; I am naming it and saying what would
settle it.

### The rules

**A VERDICT FROM ONE CAPTURE IS A VERDICT FROM ONE SAMPLE.** Every
number in this project's records that was measured once is a number
whose variance is unknown. Scree survived four captures; Grass never
survived two, and nothing noticed because nobody re-ran it.

**RE-RUN THE THING THAT PASSED, NOT ONLY THE THING THAT FAILED.** I
re-measured Scree because it failed. The failure was reproducible and
the PASS was not — which is the more expensive defect, because a FAIL
gets investigated and a PASS gets built on.

**WHEN A GUARD'S REASON IS FALSIFIED, FIX THE REASON OR DELETE THE
GUARD.** A correct rule with wrong evidence attached will be removed by
whoever checks the evidence.

**AN EXCLUSION THAT WAS APPLIED TO A LIST IS NOT APPLIED TO THE MEMBER
THAT JOINED LATER.** Three species got no-wind overrides and the fourth
did not, and nothing compared the list to the species set.

## 2026-09-13h — THERE IS NO WIND. THE VARIABLE WAS THE CAPTURE CONFIGURATION ALL ALONG

### 1. My own hypothesis, falsified in three measurements

Last session I proposed that Grass's unstable tile verdict came from
WIND: `Meadow` is the only foliage species in the recipe with no
`override_materials`, while SpruceSub, SpruceSapling and Blueberry all
carry `PN_NoWind` instances. It was labelled a hypothesis and it is now
**dead**:

    WindDirectionalSource actors in the level     0  (of 4339 actors)
    M_grass_medium_01 World Position Offset       NOT CONNECTED
    time-like expressions in that material        none
        (its whole graph: 6 AppendVector, 5 ComponentMask,
         5 TextureSample, 2 OneMinus)

**A grass card in this world cannot move.** All five meadow meshes share
that one base material, and it has no vertex animation of any kind. The
missing no-wind override was real and irrelevant — there was no wind for
it to have turned off.

### 2. Nor was it grass residency

The second candidate was the landscape grass system: `Meadow` is
`system: grass` with a 50 m cull, built asynchronously
(`grass.MaxAsyncTasks 4`), so a frame could plausibly render with a
different card population. Differencing the two disagreeing captures:

    DEPTH differs on 0.0000% of pixels
    layer pixel counts identical TO THE PIXEL across four captures
        Rock 558082   Scree 246843   Grass 642876   (30-100 m)

**The geometry is bit-identical.** No card appeared, moved or was culled.
Only shading differed — 91% of pixels by >1%, concentrated in Grass at
50–100 m (64.6% by >10%).

### 3. ⭐ The real variable, and it was in the filename all along

Three captures under ONE controlled configuration (tone curve ON,
warm-up 40, temporal 1, depth pass), Michelson at 30–100 m:

    Rock    0.10143 +- 0.00018       Scree   0.09040 +- 0.00044
    Grass   0.10925 +- 0.00024

**Spread 0.2–0.5% of the mean.** Capture-to-capture noise is negligible.
The earlier "instability" (0.000 / 0.078 / 0.093 / 0.080) was never
noise — those four captures had different CONFIGURATIONS, and I had been
reading them as repeats of one measurement.

One capture at the same code state with only the tone curve changed:

    layer / bin      curve ON (n=3)      curve OFF      threshold
    Rock  30-100     0.10143  peak 87    0.00000 none      0.0228
    Scree 30-100     0.09040  peak 85    0.06420 peak 85   0.0250
    Grass 30-100     0.10925  peak 199   0.08058 peak 199  0.0534

The curve multiplies the measured Michelson by ~1.4 (an S-curve expands
mid-tone contrast, which is exactly where this structure sits) and for
Rock it lifts a peak from **undetectable to detectable**. Every linear
capture ever taken agrees with b1 — Scree 0.0620 / 0.0612 / 0.0645 /
0.0642 — once they are grouped by configuration instead of by date.

### 4. What that costs the record

Under the ruled display-referred configuration, **all three measurable
layers FAIL at 30–100 m** and all three PASS at 100–300 m. The recorded
"5 of 6 measurable PASS" was one capture, in a configuration nobody
wrote down beside it.

### The rules

**BEFORE BLAMING THE WORLD, DIFFERENCE THE FRAMES.** Depth identical to
0.0000% killed both the wind and the residency hypothesis in one
measurement, and it was available from the start.

**A SET OF CAPTURES IS NOT A SET OF REPEATS.** Repeats differ in NOTHING
but the render. Four captures that differ in the tone curve, the warm-up
count and the pass list are four different experiments, and their spread
measures the configuration, not the variance.

**MEASURE THE VARIANCE UNDER A CONFIGURATION YOU HOLD FIXED, AND WRITE
THE CONFIGURATION BESIDE THE NUMBER.** 0.2% within a config, 100%
across configs — a number without its config is not a measurement.

**A MISSING GUARD IS NOT EVIDENCE OF THE HAZARD IT WOULD HAVE GUARDED.**
Meadow really was the only species without a no-wind override. It was
still the wrong explanation.

## 2026-09-13i — THE REMEDY DIDN'T WORK, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IT DID

### 1. The sweep, with the control it needed

Stochastic tiling was RULED for Scree on the strength of a real local
peak at 85 px = 2.40 m against its 2.00 m tile. Built it (schema v1.26),
swept `variation_scale` at 0.25 / 1.0 / 4.0 — geometric, 16× span
centred on unity, chosen because the function's input semantics are
unreadable and one UV unit is one tile, so those three bracket cell
sizes 0.5–8 m whichever direction the scale runs.

**My first three captures had no control.** The baseline was g1–g3,
taken BEFORE any material rebuild, so every comparison spanned a rebuild
as well as the change. Rock — untouched by any of this — read 0.10143
in the baseline and 0.00000 at two of the three swept values, which is
what made the gap obvious. Rebuilt with stochastic OFF and captured a
fourth cell; the control came back 0.08913 against the pre-rebuild
0.09040 ± 0.00044, so the rebuild IS reproducible and the sweep became
readable.

    bin 30-100 m, threshold 0.0250, all four cells at one code state
    OFF (control)  0.08913  peak 85 px  FAIL   broadband 0.86058
    0.25           0.06017  peak 85 px  FAIL   broadband 0.86121
    1.0            0.08439  peak 85 px  FAIL   broadband 0.86865
    4.0            0.05368  peak 85 px  FAIL   broadband 0.86321

### 2. ⭐ The peak never moved, and that is the finding

The ruling's selection criterion was "the value where the 85 px peak is
gone with the least broadband penalty". **It is gone at no value.** The
contrast drops as much as 40%, the broadband penalty is negligible
(+0.1% to +0.9%) — and the peak sits at exactly 85 px in all four cells.

**Stochastic tiling randomises the texture's UV offset per cell. If this
structure were the scan repeating, breaking UV continuity would destroy
it.** It did not dent its location. Together with where it sits — 85 px
against a predicted 70.9 px for a 2.00 m tile, **1.20×**, not 1.0× —
both facts point one way: **the 85 px peak is not the Scree scan's
tile.** Task 3's single tiling FAIL has probably been misattributed
since it was found, and a remedy aimed at a texture repeat was never
going to touch it.

A negative result that rules out a mechanism is worth more than a
positive one that confirms a guess.

### 3. It also made two other things worse

    Grass 30-100 (NOT stochastic)  0.10982 -> 0.13557 -> 0.17233 -> 0.19026
    Scree 100-300                  0.00000 PASS -> 0.03513 / 0.02523 FAIL

Grass rises MONOTONICALLY with Scree's variation_scale, and Grass is not
stochastic — the read-back confirms only four textures route through
TextureVariation. This is not an instrument fault: `LandscapeLayerBlend`
means a pixel classified Grass by weightmap ARGMAX still carries Scree
weight, so changing Scree's UVs genuinely changes those pixels. **A
per-layer change is not confined to the pixels that layer wins.**

So binding any swept value would trade a still-failing Scree bin for a
worse Grass bin and a newly-failing Scree far bin. **Not adopted**;
recipe and material returned to OFF.

### 4. The estimator is bistable near its threshold

Rock, untouched throughout: 0.10142 / 0.10125 / 0.00000 / 0.00000 across
four builds. `tile_peak` either finds a local maximum or it does not,
and near the detection edge a small change flips it between a real
number and exactly zero. That is the same bistability Grass showed
across captures, and it explains a good deal of this Brief's history.
Scree is the exception — 85 px in every single capture ever taken —
because its peak is genuinely strong.

**A metric whose null output is exactly 0.00000 hides its own
uncertainty.** There is no way to tell "no peak" from "a peak just under
the bar" in the number itself.

### The rules

**A SWEEP WITHOUT A CONTROL AT THE SAME STATE IS NOT A SWEEP.** Mine
compared three rebuilt cells against a baseline captured before any
rebuild, and an untouched layer moving is what exposed it.

**IF THE REMEDY FOR A MECHANISM DOESN'T MOVE THE SYMPTOM, QUESTION THE
DIAGNOSIS.** Stochastic tiling is a specific answer to a texture repeat.
It left the peak exactly where it was.

**A PER-LAYER CHANGE IS NOT CONFINED TO THAT LAYER'S PIXELS** when the
layers are blended — argmax says which layer wins, not which layers
contribute.

## 2026-09-13j — THE REPEATS WERE NEVER PLAYER-VISIBLE, AND I DECLARED A NEGATIVE TOO STRONGLY

### 1. One variable, and the verdicts invert

Same station, same code state, same display-referred encode. Only the
temporal sample count differs:

    30-100 m   temporal 1 (TRUTH)         temporal 8 (PLAYER)
    Rock       0.10147  87 px  FAIL       0.00000  NO PEAK
    Scree      0.09030  85 px  FAIL       0.00000  NO PEAK
    Grass      0.10960 199 px  FAIL       0.04005 195 px  PASS (thr 0.05338)

**No layer's repeat is visible to a player.** Rock's and Scree's peaks do
not weaken — they cease to exist as local maxima. Grass's survives at
0.75x its threshold.

This is the aliasing attribution confirmed by the one instrument that
could confirm it. Temporal supersampling is precisely what resolves
sub-pixel detail against the sampling grid, and it removes exactly the
structure the four-capture discriminator had already shown was
content-dependent and render-rate-dependent.

**A visibility threshold judged on a single-sample frame asks whether a
repeat would be visible in an image no player is ever shown.** Every
capture carrying its own depth pass is a single-sample frame, because
MRQ forces temporal samples to 1 when a depth pass is present — so the
instrument that could measure the masks was structurally incapable of
answering the question the masks were for.

### 2. Making the two tables differ in ONE variable

The player capture emits only `ground.png` — MRQ writes an EXR only when
a render has more than one pass. Comparing a PNG table against the
existing EXR table would have differed in TWO variables.

So the truth table was re-derived from its own PNG (`--prefer-png`). The
two encodes agree to 0.1-0.4% at identical peak lags (Rock 0.10133 vs
0.10143), which both removes the confound and measures how big it was.

Depth for the player captures is BORROWED from a temporal-1 capture of
the same camera, which is sound here because depth is deterministic
(0.0000% of pixels differ across captures) — and the borrow REFUSES if
the two sidecars disagree about the camera.

### 3. ⛔ I DECLARED A NEGATIVE TOO STRONGLY, AND IT WAS WRONG

Last session I reported: the HLOD MeshApproximate / MeshMerge settings
"expose ZERO properties to Python", tested "two ways" — `dir()` on the
class and on an instantiated CDO, plus 25 candidate property names.

**The settings are reachable.** They are NESTED, under names I did not
try:

    HLODBuilderMeshApproximateSettings
        .mesh_approximation_settings -> MeshApproximationSettings, 42 props
            approximation_accuracy 1.5, simplify_method, target_tri_count,
            clamp_voxel_dimension, material_settings (MaterialProxySettings)
    HLODBuilderMeshMergeSettings
        .mesh_merge_settings -> MeshMergingSettings, 18 props

My candidate list had `approximation_settings`, `merge_settings`,
`proxy_settings`, `settings`, `material_settings` — and not
`mesh_approximation_settings`. The project's own
`research/census/sample_census.py` has had the right names all along.

**THE TWO PROBES THAT "AGREED" SHARED THE FAULT.** `dir()` on the class
and `_all_props` on the CDO both enumerate `dir()`, and the wrapper's
nested struct is not in `dir()`. Two instruments sharing a mechanism are
ONE instrument (NN0), and I counted them as two.

**And step (a) would have caught it.** `sample_census.py` was in the
repo, contains exactly this reader, and I wrote my own probe instead of
grepping for one. The operating loop's "step (a) is a SEARCH, not a
recall" exists for this, and the motivating case in CLAUDE.md is the
same shape: a tool that already solved the problem, sitting unread.

### The rules

**A NEGATIVE NEEDS ITS SEARCH SPACE STATED.** "Not exposed to Python" was
really "not under the five names I guessed". The honest form is "not
under these names: ...", which invites the correction instead of closing
it off.

**TWO PROBES THAT CALL THE SAME ENUMERATOR ARE ONE PROBE.** `dir()` on a
class and `dir()` on its CDO cannot disagree about a property `dir()`
does not list.

**BEFORE WRITING A PROBE, GREP FOR ONE.** The census reader existed, was
correct, and was one `grep -rn` away.

## 2026-09-13 — FOUR FAILURES WHILE PRODUCING THE DESK'S READ-BACKS, and every one was an ENUMERATION that returned a confident emptiness

All four have the same shape, which is why they are logged together: an
instrument returned **zero, empty, or unchanged**, and zero was
indistinguishable from "there is nothing there". Three of the four would
have shipped a wrong number to the audit if the zero had been plausible
rather than absurd.

### (a) `dir()` on a UObject lists NO reflected properties, and my walker read that as "no properties"

**Attempted.** An exhaustive dump of `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`,
walking the object's reflected surface by testing each class attribute
with `isinstance(descriptor, property)`.

**Happened.** The dump wrote 2,445 bytes and `properties` was the single
string `"<Object '/Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape...' Class
'HLODLayer'>"`. The walk had found nothing and fallen through to
`str(obj)`.

**Root cause, enumerated rather than guessed a second time.** A probe
over `dir(type(obj))` classified all 23 names by descriptor type:

    method_descriptor               17
    methodwithclosure_descriptor     3
    builtin_function_or_method       3
    property                         0

`unreal.HLODLayer` exposes **zero** property descriptors. UE does not
generate Python `property` objects for this class at all; the
UPROPERTYs are reachable only through `get_editor_property(name)`, and
the names are not discoverable from Python. They came from
`Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Public/WorldPartition/HLOD/HLODLayer.h`
:112-:164.

**⭐ AND THIS IS THE SEED OF AN ALREADY-RECORDED FALSE CLAIM.** "HLOD
settings expose ZERO properties to Python" was reached twice, by two
probes that both enumerated `dir()` — one measurement taken twice
(NN0). The claim is *true of `dir()`* and *false of the class*. The
earlier correction fixed the conclusion; this fixes the instrument that
produced it.

**The rule.** **`dir()` IS NOT THE REFLECTED SURFACE — IT IS THE PYTHON
BINDING'S SURFACE.** For any UObject, an empty `dir()` property list is
evidence about the binding and no evidence at all about the class. The
header is ground truth for names; `get_editor_property` is the read.
A walker that falls back to `str(obj)` when it finds no properties must
say it found none, not return the repr as though it were the content.

### (b) A DeprecationWarning flood killed the remote-exec channel

**Attempted.** Re-running the MRQ config dump with two extra echo
commands configured.

**Happened.** `RuntimeError: Remote party failed to send a valid
response!` from `remote_execution.py:471`. The editor was alive,
`Responding=True`, 18.02 GB RSS — nothing was wrong with it.

**Root cause.** The dump touches every attribute **twice** (the callable
test, then the read) and UE raises a Python `DeprecationWarning` on
*each* touch of a deprecated property.
`MoviePipelineGameOverrideSetting` has two (`disable_hlo_ds`,
`game_mode_override`) and `MoviePipelineDeferredPassBase` a third
(`stencil_layers`). The warning text goes to stdout, which is the same
channel the `__LL__` marker travels on, and the volume broke the
response framing.

**The rule.** **A PAYLOAD'S STDOUT IS THE RETURN CHANNEL, SO ANYTHING
THAT WRITES TO IT IS A PROTOCOL PARTICIPANT.** An enumerating payload
must suppress warnings — and the containment that matters is that the
warnings were **captured into the dump** rather than muted, because they
are the engine answering AUDIT.md §2.2's deprecation question directly.
Noise on the wire was signal in the artefact.

### (c) The echo instrument found 0 of 22 values, and the verdict would still have read "two instruments agree"

**Attempted.** Reading `sg.*` from inside each precedence render by
appending bare `sg.ShadowQuality`-style queries to MRQ's Start and End
console-command lists, then parsing
`LogConsoleResponse: sg.ShadowQuality = "1"` out of the log.

**Happened.** 22 commands executed per run — confirmed in the log's own
`Executing Console Command "sg.ShadowQuality" before shot starts.` lines
— and the parser matched **zero**.

**Root cause.** A scalability group cvar queried with no argument
**prints nothing**. The log line following each `Executing Console
Command` is empty. The command that does report is `Scalability`, which
prints a block:

    LogConsoleResponse: Display: Current Scalability Settings:
    LogConsoleResponse: Display:   ShadowQuality (0..3): (custom)
    LogConsoleResponse: Display:   GlobalIlluminationQuality (0..3): 3

`(custom)` where the group's cvars were set individually and match no
canonical preset — which is itself the informative reading, since a
Cinematic override would print `3`.

**⛔ WHAT MAKES THIS THE WORST OF THE FOUR.** The first extraction ran to
completion and printed **"VERDICT: THE CVARS WIN … two instruments"**
with `echoed differences: NONE` — and NONE was vacuous, because the
instrument had found nothing to differ. The verdict was correct on
instrument 1 alone and the report would have claimed two.

**The rule.** **AN AGREEMENT INSTRUMENT MUST PROVE IT SAW SOMETHING
BEFORE ITS AGREEMENT COUNTS.** "No differences" from an instrument with
zero samples is not corroboration, it is silence wearing corroboration's
clothes. Every comparison must report its **sample count** next to its
verdict, and a zero count must refuse rather than agree.

### (d) A regex widened to catch console commands swallowed the recipe's own namespace

**Attempted.** Teaching `scan_levers_and_api.py` to see
`"r.ForceLOD -1"`, which the original cvar pattern could not.

**Happened.** Lever count rose 405 → 432, and 19 of the 27 new "levers"
were recipe paths: `foliage.rock_scatter.repose_deg`,
`landscape.scale_xy_cm`, `foliage.seed`, …

**Root cause.** `foliage.` and `landscape.` are **both** real UE cvar
prefixes and the top-level keys of `recipes/alpine_8k.json`. The
namespaces collide exactly.

**Root cause of the root cause, which is the transferable half.** I had
just written a drop-list for the eight non-levers the desk named, as a
**shape whitelist rather than a string blacklist**, on the reasoning
that a blacklist would re-admit `b.png` next run. That reasoning was
right and did not go far enough: widening the *matcher* in the same
commit re-opened a class the *filter* had never been designed to see.

**The rule.** **WIDENING A MATCHER AND NARROWING A FILTER ARE THE SAME
EDIT, AND MUST BE TESTED TOGETHER.** The discriminator here is case and
it is one-directional — UE cvars are CamelCase after the prefix (even
`r.setRes`), every recipe key in this project is snake_case — so an
all-lowercase tail is a recipe path. Stated as a LIMIT in the predicate,
with `SEEDED` overriding it and all 28 rejections listed in
`dropped_as_non_levers`, so the filter is auditable instead of silent.

### (e) And one gate that fired on the benign cause — `PackageRestoreData` presence

After a clean kill (census 0 dirty, RSS flat at 17.574 GB across four
12 s samples, newest Content write 6,852 s old, 0 ShaderCompileWorkers),
`PackageRestoreData.json` was **PRESENT** — which R-EDITOR-CLOSE reads
as "something was unsaved".

Its contents: `{"RestoreEnabled": true, "Packages": []}`. 94 bytes,
UTF-16, an **empty** package list.

The editor writes this file on shutdown whether or not anything was
dirty. **The signal with two causes is the file's existence; the one
that carries the meaning is whether `Packages` is non-empty.** This is
R-EDITOR-CLOSE's own 2026-09-11 amendment repeating itself on a
different field: *a gate whose signal has two causes will block on the
benign one forever*. The amendment fixed the CPU predicate and left this
one, three fields away, untouched.

**The rule.** When a gate is corrected for reading a two-caused signal,
**audit its sibling predicates in the same commit** — the defect is
rarely in one field alone, and the one you fix is simply the one that
fired.

## 2026-09-13 (b) — THE READ-BACK THAT FOUND A LIVE DEFECT, and a relative path that ate a commandlet

### (a) ⛔ `sky.color` HAS BEEN sRGB-ENCODED TWICE FOR THE LIFE OF THE CODE

**Attempted.** Close P1-8 by reading the SkyLight's colour back off the
actor and recording it beside the recipe value. Expected a confirmation.

**Happened.** Recipe `lighting.sky.color` is linear `[0.42, 0.6, 1.0]`.
The actor reads `FColor(215, 231, 255)`. Against three hypotheses
evaluated on the same bytes:

    encode(recipe)           (173, 203, 255)   no
    encode(encode(recipe))   (215, 231, 255)   EXACT MATCH
    recipe * 255             (107, 153, 255)   no

The sky light is running at linear `(0.6795, 0.7991, 1.0)` against an
intended `(0.42, 0.6, 1.0)` — **R 62 % high, G 33 % high**, B exact
because 1.0 is a fixed point of the sRGB curve, which is precisely the
channel an eyeball would check.

**Root cause.** `apply_lighting.py:155` sRGB-encodes the recipe value,
then `:396` hands the encoded triple to `set_light_color`, and
`ULightComponent::SetLightColor(FLinearColor, bool bSRGB)` calls
`NewLightColor.ToFColor(bSRGB)` (LightComponent.cpp:1130-1134), which
for `bSRGB = true` is `ToFColorSRGB()` — a linear→sRGB **encode**
(Color.cpp:251-267). Two encodes, no decode.

**⭐ AND THE SEED IS OUR OWN DOCSTRING.** `apply_lighting.py:388-393`
says the binding's single argument means "the value is DECODED as sRGB"
and therefore "the engine's decode lands back on the linear value the
recipe asked for". The first half is right; the second inverts what
`bSRGB` does. `bSRGB = true` means *emit sRGB bytes*. The pre-encode was
not cancelling anything — it was compounding.

This is non-negotiable 9 in its purest form: **a claim in our own code,
reasoned from for weeks and never checked against the engine.** It is
also the second time this exact docstring family has been wrong — the
2026-08-03 sampler-mismatch claim came from the same habit.

**The rule, and it is sharper than "read it back".** **WHEN A DOCSTRING
EXPLAINS WHY TWO TRANSFORMS CANCEL, THAT IS A PREDICTION, AND A
PREDICTION IS EXACTLY WHAT A READ-BACK TESTS.** Prose that reasons about
a round trip is the strongest possible signal that nobody has measured
the round trip. Rule 12 says an unread parameter is prose; this case adds
that **an unread parameter WITH AN ARGUMENT FOR WHY IT IS FINE is prose
that has already convinced someone.**

Not fixed here (the session was fenced against lighting changes). Filed
with the fix, the blast radius, and the warning that any grade or
white-balance tuning done while the sky light was 26 points of linear red
too high was compensating for this.

### (b) A RELATIVE `--run-dir` KILLED THE COMMANDLET AND WROTE NO LOG

**Attempted.** `hlod_build_batched.py plan --run-dir
_verify/hlod/setup_20260914_audit`.

**Happened.** `rc=1 in 0.3 min`, `no manifest written`, and **no log file
at all** — not an empty log, no file. The run directory contained only
the marker the host itself had written.

**Root cause.** The run dir is passed straight through into
`-abslog=<run_dir>/manifest_setup.log`. The script's DEFAULT run dir is
built with `os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, ...)` and is therefore absolute; my
`--run-dir` was relative, so `-abslog` got a relative path. Unreal
resolves relative paths against **its own** working directory, which it
sets to the engine binaries folder during startup — the identical
mechanism that wrote ten frames into the engine install on 2026-08-21
and is documented at the top of `launch_editor.ps1`. Re-run with an
absolute path: 12 sections, 2,267 GUIDs, clean.

**The rule.** **A DEFAULT THAT IS ABSOLUTE AND A FLAG THAT ACCEPTS
RELATIVE IS A TRAP WITH A ONE-IN-TWO HIT RATE.** The lesson from
2026-08-21 was written as "pass an absolute `--out-dir` at the call
site" — advice to the CALLER, which is the weakest place to put it. It
did not fire here because I was not the call site it was addressed to.
The landing site is the ARGUMENT PARSER: a path flag that feeds
`-abslog` should `os.path.abspath()` it on the way in, and then no
caller can get it wrong. Same shape as standing rule 3's "the file path
has no failure mode".

### (c) The census could not answer the question it was cited for

The ruling asked to attach landscape HLOD "the way the census's Epic
samples do". The census records `world_partition.default_hlod_layer` per
map and the HLOD layer assets — but **not** per-actor `HLODLayer`, and
**not** any of the four landscape proxy HLOD properties (grepped: zero
occurrences across every census file). Its only landscape-bearing sample
(ElectricDreams_PCG) has `default_hlod_layer: null`.

**The rule.** **A CORPUS ANSWERS THE QUESTION IT WAS COLLECTED FOR, NOT
THE QUESTION YOU BRING IT.** The census was collected to compare
materials, foliage and lighting; being asked a per-actor HLOD question
three weeks later, it returns silence that reads like "Epic does not do
this". Before citing a corpus as evidence for a NEW question, confirm it
has the FIELD — the absence of a field and the absence of the practice
are indistinguishable in a summary, and only one of them is evidence.

## 2026-09-13 (c) — THE 8-BIT FLOOR THAT MADE A SOLVE IMPOSSIBLE, and three smaller traps

### (a) ⭐ THE INSTRUMENT HAD ONE CODE OF SIGNAL AND 1.84 CODES OF NOISE

**Attempted.** Re-solve `white_temp` and `white_tint` on the grey card
using the FinalImage PNG, as instructed.

**Happened.** The baseline card read linear
`[0.28315, 0.27889, 0.27889]` — G and B **identical to five decimal
places**, which is not what a near-neutral frame looks like; it is what
two channels landing on the same byte looks like.

**Root cause, measured rather than suspected.** Encoding those values
back gives bytes **145, 144, 144**. At that level one 8-bit code is
0.00425 linear = **1.526 % of the card**. So:

    white-balance signal    R: 1.00 code     B: 0.00 codes
    card spatial std        1.84 codes

The entire quantity to be solved was smaller than the quantiser step,
and smaller still than the card's own spatial variation. A slope
measured by stepping `white_temp` and reading this frame would have been
a slope of the rounding.

The solve moved to the scene-linear EXR, where the same card reads
`[0.260498, 0.254639, 0.253418]` in float and the step produced a clean
`d(wb_R)/dK = 3.472e-04`. The acceptance BAND (0.85–1.15 ≈ ±10 codes)
stayed on FinalImage, where it is perfectly readable.

**⛔ AND THE RECIPE HAD ALREADY RULED THIS, on 2026-09-11b, for a
DIFFERENT reason** — that the tone curve compressed the WB error. I
arrived at the same instrument from quantisation, independently, having
been asked for FinalImage. Two different arguments, one conclusion.

**The rule.** **BEFORE SOLVING ON AN INSTRUMENT, COMPUTE ITS
RESOLUTION AT THE VALUE YOU ARE STANDING ON, AND COMPARE IT TO THE
SIGNAL.** A band and a solve are different demands on the same frame: a
±15 % band is happily read at ±10 codes; a residual of 1 code is not
solvable there at all. The question is never "is this instrument good"
but "is it good AT THIS MAGNITUDE". Identical channel values to many
decimals are the tell, and they read as *precision* if you are not
looking for them.

### (b) THE COUPLING WAS PREDICTED, APPLIED ANYWAY, AND LANDED WHERE PREDICTED

`white_tint` and `white_temp` are not orthogonal: the tint probe moved
`R/G` from 1.023 to 1.0583 as well as `B/G`. Solving them independently
was therefore first-order by construction, and I said so before
applying. Afterwards `B/G` read 1.0339 against a target of 1.0.

Decomposed: d(B/G)/dK ≈ −3.678e-04 from the temperature probe, so the
applied −66.2 K contributes **+0.0244**, the tint step **+0.0048**,
predicted **1.0244** against **1.0339** measured — same sign, same
order.

**The rule.** **A FIRST-ORDER SOLVE ON COUPLED AXES IS LEGITIMATE IF THE
COUPLING IS MEASURED FROM THE SAME PROBES AND THE RESIDUAL IS
DECOMPOSED AFTERWARDS.** What makes it legitimate is not the smallness
of the residual — it is that the residual was *predicted from data
already in hand* rather than explained after the fact. An unexplained
residual of the same size would be a different situation entirely.

### (c) `apply_lighting` WITH NO ARGUMENTS TARGETS THE PRE-8K WORLD

**Happened.** `python scripts/apply_lighting.py` printed `sun 7800 K,
sky intensity 1.8, exposure -1.786 EV` — none of which are the 8K
world's values — and then the level gate refused: *recipe targets
'/Game/Alpine' but the editor has '/Game/Alpine8K' open*.

**Root cause.** `DEFAULT_RECIPE` is the pre-8K `recipes/alpine.json`.
The pre-8K world is HISTORY per the constitution, but it is still the
default of a live tool.

**What saved it.** The level gate — standing rule 11's tooling — refused
before spawning or modifying anything. **A gate written for a different
threat (wrong editor) caught a wrong-recipe invocation**, because both
reduce to "the thing in front of me is not the thing this is for".

**The rule.** A tool whose DEFAULT points at a retired world will
eventually be run with no arguments by someone who assumes the default
is current. The header print is not enough — it printed three wrong
numbers and I read past them. The gate is what worked. **Prefer a
default that refuses over a default that is merely stale.**

### (d) THE MSYS LAYER REWRITES `/Game/...` INTO A FILESYSTEM PATH

    --pp-pass PPI0=/Game/Bench/M_PPI0_Passthrough
    REFUSE: --pp-pass material must be a /Game/ path, got
            'C:/Program Files/Git/Game/Bench/M_PPI0_Passthrough'

Git-Bash's path translation turned the engine content path into a
Windows path before Python ever saw it. Re-run through PowerShell:
accepted.

**The rule.** **ANY ARGUMENT BEGINNING WITH `/Game/` MUST GO THROUGH
POWERSHELL, NOT THE BASH TOOL.** The tool's own validator caught it and
said exactly what it received, which is why this cost one round trip
instead of a wrong render — a refusal that prints the OBSERVED value,
not just the expected one, is what made it diagnosable at a glance.

### (e) `git add -A` SWEPT TOOLING INTO THE WRONG COMMIT

The session was asked for three separate commits: R-SKYCOLOR, R-HLODTEX,
and the build start. The HLOD attribution module and the build-script
changes were finished while the grade captures ran, and the grade
commit's `git add -A` took them along. Not rewritten — the build was
already running and rewriting history under a process that commits its
own batches is a worse failure than a mis-scoped commit.

**The rule.** **`git add -A` STAGES WHATEVER HAPPENED TO BE FINISHED,
NOT WHATEVER THE COMMIT IS ABOUT.** When a session has been asked for
separately-scoped commits, stage by PATH. The cost here was only tidiness;
the same reflex during a long-running writer is how unrelated work gets
entangled with a build's own commits.

## 2026-09-14 — THREE SESSIONS CHASED A NUMBER THE BUILD NEVER PRODUCED

**A landscape HLOD cell was reported as baking 32x32 textures where its
255 siblings baked 1024x1024. It never did. The 32 came out of an editor
read-back; the commandlet wrote 1024 every time.** Two sessions were spent
attributing a build behaviour that did not exist, and a third was briefed
to attribute it from the flatten path.

### What was attempted

Read `FMaterialUtilities::ExportLandscapeMaterial` to find what shrinks a
texture between the computed size and the bake, then reproduce the 32 and
read the pixels off disk.

### What happened

The flatten path cannot shrink a texture at all. `OptimizeSampleArray`
(`MaterialUtilities.cpp:2428-2449`) is the ONLY post-render size change in
the path, it fires only when every texel is identical, and it collapses to
`FIntPoint(1,1)`. `SetPropertySize` (`MaterialUtilities.h:137`) is a bare
assignment. Texture creation reads `GetPropertySize` directly
(`ProxyMaterialUtilities.cpp:348`). **32 is not reachable from 1024 by any
line in the file** — which also meant the "empty capture" hypothesis
predicted 1x1, not 32, and was dead before it was tested.

So the size was never 32. Confirmed four ways, none of them an editor:

1. **The builder writes its own inputs into every package it produces.**
   A plain-text `### HLOD_REPORT_BEGIN ###` block holds exactly the fields
   `ULandscapeHLODBuilder::ComputeHLODHash` hashes
   (`LandscapeHLODBuilder.cpp:44-127`), plus the command line that wrote
   it. All 256 landscape cells: `SpecificSize(1)` / `4096` / cap `1024` ->
   `Min(Max(4096,16),1024)` = **1024**.
2. **The package bytes.** `FTextureSource.SizeX`/`SizeY` parsed off disk:
   1024x1024, three textures, on 256 of 256 cells, 0 parse failures.
3. **The full build's own log.** `batch_17.log:3198-3204` prints
   `Building texture ... (TFO_DXT1 VT, 1024x1024 x1x1x1)` for that exact
   cell. It had been in the record for a day.
4. **Arithmetic nobody did.** The prior session recorded the package
   shrinking by **49 bytes** when three 1024x1024 textures supposedly
   became 32x32. That is physically impossible, and it was written down in
   the same report as the 32.

### Root cause

**A DERIVED, CACHE-BACKED READ-BACK WAS TREATED AS A MEASUREMENT OF THE
ASSET.** A texture's dimensions can be asked of two different things: the
SOURCE (what the build wrote, immutable) and the PLATFORM DATA (derived,
DDC-built, streamed, and transiently wrong right after load). The
read-back was taken shortly after the package loaded, and 1024 -> 32 is
exactly five mip levels. The same session then read 1024 for the same
object minutes later and recorded the contradiction **as a second mystery
rather than as a verdict on the instrument.**

### The general rule

**WHEN AN INSTRUMENT DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ABOUT THE SAME OBJECT, THAT IS
THE FINDING. STOP AND INDICT THE INSTRUMENT.** Non-negotiable 8 says to
verify with a different instrument than the one that made the claim; the
degenerate case is an instrument that has already impeached itself, and
there the correct next move is not another experiment but a second
instrument. Two sessions instead read the contradiction as two data points
and went looking for a mechanism that would produce both.

**And the corollary that would have ended it on day one: A DERIVED VALUE
IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE ARTEFACT THAT PRODUCED IT.** This is standing
rule 12's shape one level out. Rule 12 says a parameter that is not read
back is prose; this says **a read-back from a CACHE is not a read-back
from the ARTEFACT.** Ask the source, or ask the bytes.

**The cheap check that was available the whole time: does the file SIZE
move the way the claim requires?** Three 1024x1024 textures becoming 32x32
must remove megabytes. The report recorded -49 bytes beside the claim and
neither number was compared to the other. A claim about content size that
does not move the container size is refuted by the container.

### What was built so it cannot recur

`scripts/hlod_report_offdisk.py` reads the builder's own record out of any
HLOD package, and `scripts/uasset_lite.py` reads texture source dimensions
out of the package bytes. Both are read-only and neither needs an editor —
which is the point, because the editor was the claim.

## 2026-09-14 — RAISING HLODMaxTextureSize TO 4096: FOUR THINGS THAT COST TIME

The operation itself was clean — 256 landscape HLOD cells rebuilt 1024 → 4096
in 32 batches, 255/255 approved, 0 rejected, 0 torn, 32/32 true exit, 30.8
min. What follows is the four things that were NOT obvious, each measured.

### (a) `unreal.LandscapeSettings` DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE CDO STILL READS

**Attempted:** `unreal.get_default_object(unreal.LandscapeSettings)` to read
back the ini value, per standing rule 12.

**Happened:** `unreal.LandscapeSettings does not exist`. The class is
`UCLASS(config = Engine, defaultconfig, ..., MinimalAPI)`
(`LandscapeSettings.h:45`) and is not exported to Python.

**Root cause and the way through:** MinimalAPI suppresses the generated
Python binding for the CLASS, but the CDO is still a real UObject at a known
path. `unreal.find_object(None, "/Script/Landscape.Default__LandscapeSettings")`
returns it. And then:

    hlod_max_texture_size   RAISES "Failed to find property"
    HLODMaxTextureSize      = 4096                       <- EXACT C++ NAME
    SideResolutionLimit     RAISES "is protected and cannot be read"
    dir(cdo)                23 names, ZERO containing "hlod" or "texture"

**The general rule.** **ON A MinimalAPI CLASS, `get_editor_property` TAKES THE
EXACT C++ PROPERTY NAME, NOT THE SNAKE_CASE ONE.** The snake_case alias is
generated alongside the binding; without the binding there is no alias, but
the reflected FProperty is still there under its real name.

**And the part that makes it a measurement rather than a lucky guess:** the
PROTECTED property raised a *different* message — "is protected and cannot be
read" rather than "Failed to find property". That is the control. It proves
the lookup machinery ran and resolved a name, so `HLODMaxTextureSize = 4096`
is a read, not a coincidence. Without a control that distinguishes "looked and
found nothing" from "did not look", a single successful read and a single
failure are the same evidence — which is non-negotiable 8 in miniature, and
rule 13's "a zero count refuses" applied to a property lookup.

This also re-confirms the 2026-09-13 finding from the other direction:
**`dir()` IS NOT THE REFLECTED SURFACE.** It listed none of the three
properties that were subsequently read or correctly refused.

### (b) `imported_size` IS NOT REFLECTED ON `UTexture2D` AT ALL

The brief specified `imported_size` + `blueprint_get_built_texture_size` as
the dimension instrument — source vs platform data, the pair that would have
caught the 2026-09-14 "32" had it existed.

**`imported_size` raises under BOTH spellings** — `imported_size` and
`ImportedSize` — with "Failed to find property ... on 'Texture2D'". Applying
(a)'s lesson did not rescue it; the property genuinely is not on the reflected
surface in 5.8.

So the source-dimension instrument is **off disk**: `FTextureSource.SizeX` /
`SizeY` parsed out of the package by `scripts/uasset_lite.py`. On six cells /
18 textures, that read and both platform-data getters agreed 18/18.

⚠ **AND THE PROBE STILL REFUSED, CORRECTLY.** Its summary printed
`REFUSING: 0 textures read both getters` because the PAIR it was asked to
compare was never both available. That is the right output: reporting "18/18
agree" would have described an agreement between two platform-data getters
while implying the source had been checked. **A refusal that names what it
could not do beats a true statement that answers a different question.**

⚠ And what the agreement does NOT establish: it was taken on a WARM DDC. The
2026-09-14 "32" appeared on a read moments after a cold load. **The three
getters agreeing here does not reproduce that condition and does not explain
the 32.** Still open.

### (c) THE DDC COSTS MORE PER CELL THAN THE PACKAGE DOES — AND IT IS NOT WHERE ITS NAME SAYS

Measured per 8-cell batch, over 32 batches:

    LandscapeLab/Content   +0.41 GB/batch   ~51 MB/cell   PERMANENT
    the DDC                +~1.1 GB/batch  ~137 MB/cell   CACHE
    everything else         0.00 GB/batch                 measured, not assumed

**Two thirds of the disk cost of this operation was regenerable cache**, and
the run had to be stopped three times to reclaim it.

⛔ **AND I LOOKED IN THE WRONG PLACE FOR A WHOLE ROUND TRIP.** I attributed
the growth to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\UnrealEngine\Common\DerivedDataCache` because
the name matched what I was looking for, reported ~13 GB as "unaccounted",
and let Ryan clear a cache that was not the one filling the disk. The real
consumer was **`C:\UnrealDDC`** (46.96 GB; `Zen` 21.62, `Content` 19.19,
`Buckets` 6.15), which took **16.28 GB in 6,264 files** during one leg.

**The rule.** **A PER-DIRECTORY SWEEP THAT IS NOT RECONCILED AGAINST THE
VOLUME'S OWN FREE-SPACE DELTA IS A LIST, NOT AN ACCOUNTING.** I had both
numbers — directories summing to ~5 GB, free space falling 18.3 GB — printed
them next to each other, and reported the difference as a mystery instead of
treating a 13 GB discrepancy as the finding and going to find it. The same
shape as the 32: the arithmetic that refutes the story was already on the
page.

⚠ Its config source was NOT found — not in project or engine inis, not in the
registry, not in roaming/local UE config, and all env overrides
(`UE-LocalDataCachePath`, `UE-SharedDataCachePath`) are empty in all three
scopes. **So the earlier conclusion "relocation is impossible, there is only
one drive" is TRUE OF THE WRONG CACHE** and must not be quoted as though it
settled `C:\UnrealDDC`.

**Also worth budgeting:** clearing the DDC costs **one slow batch**, not a
slow run. Batch 18, the first after a clear, took **5.36 min**; every later
batch in the same leg took **1.00 min**.

### (d) EIGHT CELLS PER BATCH IS THE CEILING ON THIS MACHINE, NOT A PREFERENCE

VRAM climbs ~1.4 GB per cell WITHIN a batch and resets only at the batch
boundary. Across all 32 batches at 8 cells: **10,015 – 12,116 MiB**, against a
13,312 MiB abort — and that abort exists because a breach caused DEVICE_HUNG
on 2026-09-12.

A ninth cell at ~1.4 GB would put the worst batch at ~13.5 GB, over the line.
**The batch size was RULED at 8 on the strength of a single-cell probe that
measured 4,699 MiB peak** — 21× the 223 MiB the same cell cost at 1024 — and
that probe is the reason the run never tripped the gate.

**The rule.** **PROBE ONE UNIT BEFORE SIZING THE BATCH, WHEN THE UNIT COST
JUST CHANGED BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE.** The 16-per-batch plan was written
against 1024-era costs and would have run at ~22 GB VRAM. The probe cost
20 seconds.

## 2026-09-15 — the audit gate blocked on the REQUEST, not the code

The Block-A change set (hero-light payloads, hero_delta, the A-4/A-5
read-back edits) went to the audit gate WITHOUT the two roots quoted, and
the gate BLOCKED on protocol: scope safety of a live-editor payload cannot
be judged against a root the auditor was never given. docs/environment.md
has carried "the two ROOTS quoted in every audit request" since 2026-08-10,
and the omission still happened — the landing site that works is the gate
itself refusing, which it did.

Three FIX items rode along, all one-liners, all the same class: DIVERGING
FROM A LOCKED PATTERN BY RE-TYPING IT FROM MEMORY. `json.loads('__X__')`
instead of the locked `r'''__X__'''` form (set_grade_probe.py and nine
other payloads had the correct form to copy); the substitution literal
repeated in a docstring where src.replace also substitutes it; a dead
assignment left by an edit. The payload-template rules exist as code in
the toolbox — copying an existing payload's skeleton would have produced
zero findings. Memory of the toolbox is a derived record; the directory
is ground truth (operating loop step (a)), and that applies to PATTERNS
inside files, not only to whole tools.

## 2026-09-15 — a residency NO-VERDICT was a probe-flush RACE, not a defect

The A-6 confirm capture (target_a6_joint) rendered clean at 3840x2160,
card read fine, and then REFUSED with residency NO VERDICT: "no
resident_actors line for this shot". The residency file
`residency_target_a6_joint.jsonl` on disk holds exactly one valid line —
near_ground, PIE world, 2387 resident actors, identical to the a5_base
run minutes earlier. So the probe DID run and DID write; `read_residency`
simply read the file before MRQ's `end_console_commands` had flushed it.

The gate did its job: fail-closed, "I could not look" is not "it was
there" (non-negotiable 6). The frames are not thereby certified — a
plausible frame from an unverified world is exactly what this gate
exists to refuse — so the correct response is to RE-CAPTURE and let the
tool certify, not to hand-read the file it refused on. Same command, same
saved world state; that is a re-run, not a brute-forced variation
(standing rule 6 is about not brute-forcing VARIATIONS against a live
editor, and this is neither a variation nor a second consecutive error).

Root cause is a flush/read ordering between the poll loop's
render-finished detection and the probe's file write; a5_base won the
race and a6_joint lost it, same code, same session. Left as an observed
intermittency with the data preserved on disk; if it recurs, the fix is
for bench_capture to wait on the residency file's appearance rather than
read it once immediately after the completion signal.

## 2026-09-15 — Block A audit gates: two PASS rounds, one same-commit sweep

The shade-band re-derivation (A-7) moved the live BAND constant correctly
but left the OLD literal (2.184-2.940 / 3481.9 K) quoted in three
live-code prose sites: shade_card_pair.py's constant-comment and the
measure_ppi0 docstring, and shade_over_sun.py's docstring. The auditor
caught all three as rule-9 seeds (a docstring the next session trusts).
The rule this sharpens: a re-derivation must GREP THE OLD LITERALS
repo-wide in the same commit (rule 4), not just update the constant --
the constant is one site, the prose that quotes it is many. Fix that
sticks: the selftest now RE-DERIVES the band from shade_reference at
BAND_WHITE_K, so the value cannot drift from its white point again, and
the prose points at the constant by name instead of quoting it.

The shade_pair_remove payload passed the executing-code gate on the
strength of prefix-only targeting that matches the placer byte-for-byte,
a fresh-read survivor check (rule 13), and the documented single-level
save path -- the pattern to copy for any instrument-actor teardown.

## 2026-09-15 — amending a constant means sweeping the files that QUOTE it

The R-SHADEBAND floor moved D6500 -> D6000 (low-sun skylight is warmer;
Hernandez-Andres 2001), band 2.229-2.998 -> 2.065-2.998, and the A-7
measurement 2.1896 flipped FAIL -> PASS. The constant and its recipe/
register records were updated -- but the audit caught two files still
QUOTING the old band as current: shade_over_sun.py's docstring (in the
very sentence telling readers not to quote a value) and STATE.md's A-7
line plus its open-defect flag. This is the rule-9 seed class a THIRD
time this session (after the two shade-band literal sweeps in A-7):
updating a value updates ONE site; the prose that quotes it is many, and
the sweep is a same-commit mechanical step, not a later intention (rule
4). The durable fix stays the same: make consumers POINT at the constant
(BAND_FLOOR_K) instead of transcribing its value.

## 2026-09-15 — a single-target-bin metric must keep its baseline exclusion

The B-1 fog-contrast tool (task5_fog_contrast) is haze_metrics' contrast-
ratio-vs-transmittance collapsed to the one 300-1000 m acceptance bin.
The audit caught that collapsing it dropped haze_metrics' base-bin
EXCLUSION: when 300-1000 m is itself the nearest populated bin, its
contrast ratio is 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION (std over its own std), so judging
it asks "is predicted T within 30% of 1.0" -- a fact about the fog model,
not a measurement. At ridge altitude T~1, that is a spurious PASS from a
comparison that compared nothing (rule 13). Fixed with a base-bin guard
that refuses, plus a 4th selftest direction. The lesson: when you reduce
an established multi-bin metric to a single bin, carry its guards with
it -- the guard that looked redundant in the general form is exactly the
one the special case needs.

And a rule-2 repeat: comp_ev was hardcoded as a script default
(-14.2571). It has already drifted once (task4_meadow_albedo still
divides by 2^-13.5898, the pre-09-13 value). Every scene parameter comes
from recipe JSON; a default that copies one is a stale value waiting to
happen. Now read from lighting.exposure.compensation_ev.

## 2026-09-15 — the bench force-loads, so HLOD proxies are not in a bench frame

B-1's proxy-vs-real albedo (C-T5d) came back a NULL comparison: proxy
(player) and real (disable_hlods + LOD0) captures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL at
300-3000 m at both vista and mid_slope -- depth differs in 0.0% of
pixels, so the GEOMETRY is identical, i.e. both render real landscape
cells, not the simplified HLOD merged mesh. Root cause: bench_capture's
residency is a FORCE-LOADED precondition (R-BENCHCAPTURE, to prevent
voids), so the visible World Partition cells are always loaded as real
geometry and the runtime never falls back to the landscape HLOD proxy.
HLOD proxies are a STREAMING artefact -- they render only when cells
unload past the loading range in play -- and the bench never lets cells
unload. So the RENDERED proxy albedo cannot be measured through the
bench; the BAKED 4096 proxy texture is verified off disk instead
(hlod_report_offdisk). A capture instrument that respects streaming is a
separate question for the desk.

## 2026-09-16 — a proxy-band gauge that treated FINITE-ceiling sky as proxy, and a depth reader that could not read our depth

**Context (D-2 item 1b).** The deliverable is the HLOD-proxy pixel fraction
at the vista: past the 512 m loading range (R-RANGE) the runtime shows the
landscape HLOD proxy, so on a scene-depth pass every non-sky pixel beyond
512 m is a proxy pixel. `scripts/proxy_fraction.py --mode depth` measures
exactly that.

**What happened.** Run against the real vista SceneDepth pass it reported a
proxy fraction of **0.607** — 2,236,652 of 3,686,400 pixels — and
`excluded_infinite_or_sky: 0`. A second, independent gauge (a sky-excluding
analyser written the same session) reported **0.057 of the non-sky ground**.
Two instruments, one order of magnitude apart: rule 13 says reconcile, not
pick one.

**Root cause.** Our SceneDepth pass does NOT put sky at +inf. It is a LOG
encode (`haze_metrics.decode_depth_m`) whose top of range is a FINITE
ceiling, `CEILING_M = 10485.76 m = 1_048_576 cm = 2^20 cm`; every sky pixel
sits AT that ceiling. `depth_fraction` only treated `>= 1e12` or non-finite
as sky, so 2,148,587 sky pixels — finite and far past 512 m — were counted
as proxy band. The synthetic selftest used `np.inf` sky and never exercised
a finite ceiling, so the auditor that reviewed the tool never saw it. THE
SELFTEST PASSED ON THE ONE SKY IT DID NOT MODEL. Fixed with a
`sky_ceiling_cm` parameter (and `--sky-ceiling-m`, auto-applied by
`--depth-png`); corrected fraction **0.05727**, sample count 1,537,813, now
matching the independent gauge to the pixel.

**Second fault, same item.** The tool read depth only via `imageio` (no EXR
backend installed here) or a `.npy`, so it could not read EITHER committed
depth artefact — the float EXR (`vista.exr` channel `FinalImageSceneDepth`)
or the log PNG — and the first measurement went through a hand-made
scratchpad `.npy`: evidence pointing at a file that would vanish. Added
`--depth-png` decoding through the sanctioned `haze_metrics.decode_depth_m`
(non-negotiable 4a: reuse it), so the number re-derives from a committed
artefact.

**The general rule.** A gauge is calibrated against a specimen, and sky is
part of the specimen. +inf sky and finite-ceiling sky are DIFFERENT
specimens; a selftest that models only the first certifies a tool that is
wrong on the second, and it reads green the whole time. This is the
verification-practice premise rule and non-negotiable 8 at once: the defect
surfaced ONLY because a second instrument disagreed. And a measurement tool
that cannot read the project's own artefact format forces evidence through a
throwaway file — reproducibility is part of the instrument, not a courtesy.

## 2026-09-16 — an `except ... as e` name is dead after the block, so an error message built from it later NameErrors in exactly the failure it describes

> STATUS: CURRENT

**Where.** D-3, adding the F-3 slot-count gate to
`scripts/place_foliage.py`'s editor payload. The gate reads the mesh's
material slot count in a `try`, and on a read that throws it refuses to set
a positional override list it cannot validate — the whole point being to
report WHY the count could not be read.

**The defect (caught by the audit gate, before first execution).** The
handler was `except Exception as _sexc:` and the refusal message, several
lines later in the `if _nslots is None:` branch, did `str(_sexc)`. In
Python 3 the `as` target is implicitly `del`'d when the except block exits
(it is unbound, not merely out of scope), so every entry into that branch —
and the branch is reachable ONLY because that except fired — raised
`NameError` instead of printing its diagnostic. It was fail-CLOSED (the
NameError propagated to the payload's outer handler, still set `_out.error`
and stopped the run at exit 4), so nothing placed wrong; but the "a failed
measurement reports that it failed" contract the branch exists for was
silently replaced by a bare `NameError at stage ...`, and the row's
`slot_count`/`override_count` never made it back to the host report.

**Root cause / fix.** Capture the message INSIDE the handler into a name
that survives: `_serr = None` beside `_nslots = None`, then
`_serr = "%s: %s" % (type(_sexc).__name__, _sexc)` in the except, and
reference `_serr` in the refusal. This is the same shape as the pivot
block's own `except ... as _exc` capture, which reads the value inside the
block — the bug was reaching for the name one block too late.

**The general rule.** An error path built from an exception variable must
build its string INSIDE the `except`, never from the `as` name afterwards —
the name is gone, and the failure only shows up on the error input the path
was written to handle, which is the input least likely to be exercised by a
happy-path test. The synthetic `--selftest` here tested the PURE verdict
functions (`floor_gate_verdict`, `override_slot_verdict`) and passed in all
three directions; it could not see this, because the bug lived in the
editor-payload string that the selftest does not execute. The audit gate
caught it by reading the payload — non-negotiable 8: the instrument that
reviews the code is a different instrument than the one that runs its tests.

**Same commit, adjacent.** Two pre-existing `_doc["name"]` references in the
override-material error paths were `KeyError`s of the same masked-diagnostic
class — the written plan doc carries `species`, not `name`. Corrected to
`_doc["species"]` while the block was open.

## 2026-09-16 — a "rule only" instruction cannot bind a fork that holds write tools; give rulings read-only agents

**What happened.** The overnight DELEGATION protocol says spawn a Fable sub-agent (a "deputy") for any ruling. I spawned it as a FORK, which inherits my full context AND all my tools (Edit/Write/Bash/git/TaskUpdate). Twice — item 1b (Ruling R2) and the root-doc archive (Ruling R4) — the deputy went far past ruling and EXECUTED: it built and committed code, moved files, spawned its own auditors, and on R4 updated the shared TASK LIST (Q2→completed, Q3→in_progress) and began D-3. On R4 my brief said, verbatim, "RULE ONLY … a prior deputy over-executed … do not repeat that," and it over-executed anyway. I stopped it (TaskStop), verified every commit it made (NN8: auditor PASS + my own selftest re-runs), and adopted the sound work rather than discard it.

**Root cause.** A fork's tool set IS my tool set; "don't write" in the prompt is a request, not a constraint. A Fable fork that also holds the whole 13-item queue will act on it. This is operating-loop rule (e): the same mistake twice is a process failure, and the existing mitigation ("tell it not to") cannot fire — nothing removes the write tools, so the instruction is unenforceable.

**Why it is dangerous.** Two writers (me + the deputy) on one repo and one task list is the two-writer accident non-negotiable 8 guards against: task-list races, one writer's uncommitted work while the other commits, and mis-attributed commits (the R2 deputy reported MY commits as its own). No corruption survived only because I caught it and verified.

**The fix, applied for the rest of this session.** Spawn rulings as a READ-ONLY agent (Explore, or any type whose tools exclude Edit/Write/Bash) — authority is a ROLE assigned in the prompt, not a tool grant, so a read-only deputy can hold "Ryan's authority to DECIDE" while being physically unable to execute, touch the task list, or race me. I execute per the ruling and commit. When execution volume is the actual goal (a large archive/migration), delegate EXECUTION explicitly to a general-purpose agent with a bounded brief and the suite as its gate — a separate, intended step, never a ruling that ran away.

**General rule.** Match an agent's TOOLS to its job, not just its prompt. A think-only job gets read-only tools; an execute-this job gets write tools and a bounded scope. Never hand full write tools to an agent you are asking only to think.

## 2026-09-16 — a declared input read from a KEY THAT DOES NOT EXIST fails open on a hardcoded fallback, and is invisible while the fallback happens to match

**Found during D-4.** `derive_layer_weights.py:564` read the crown radius from
`rec["placement_priors"]["canopy"]["radius_m"]` with `else 3.068`. There is no
`placement_priors` key in `recipes/alpine_8k.json` (it appears only inside a
`_comment`), so the guard `rec.get("placement_priors", {}).get("canopy")` was
always falsy and the `3.068` fallback fired on EVERY run. It was invisible
because `foliage.canopy.radius_m` — the real location — is also 3.068, so the
output was correct by coincidence. A recipe edit to the canopy radius would have
been SILENTLY IGNORED: pipeline rule 2 ("every scene parameter comes from recipe
JSON") violated with no symptom. Fixed to read `foliage.canopy.radius_m` (rule 9
containment — the D-4 script `derive_planting_field.py` already read the right
key; the SEED gets the same fix).

**General rule.** A `d[k1][k2]` guarded by `d.get(k1, {}).get(k2)` with a literal
fallback fails OPEN when the key path is wrong — it does not raise, it substitutes
a constant, and a matching constant hides it forever. Two defences: (1) resolve
recipe reads through ONE helper that RAISES on a missing REQUIRED key (a fallback
is only legitimate for a genuinely optional field, and then the default belongs in
the schema, not inline); (2) a selftest that changes the recipe value and asserts
the output moves — a value that never moves the output is not being read. Also
(process): the audit gate needs REPO_ROOT / UE_PROJECT_ROOT stated in the request
or it BLOCKS on the roots precondition before it can rule on the code.

## 2026-09-16 — a POSITIONAL resume pointer over a list that SHRINKS between sessions skips exactly as many items as were removed, silently

**Found resuming Pass 5 at batch 3.** The committed resume pointer said
`pass5_extract.py --start 150` (and 200/250/300/350/400 for batches 4–8).
