But `--start` indexes the CURRENT unapplied list, and `pass5_mark_applied`
had removed 17 findings (batches 0–2's APPLY rows) from that list after the
pointer's indices were conceived — the pointer was written against the
405-item list, the tool now slices a 388-item one. Following it would have
ruled original findings 167–216 as "batch 3" and left original 150–166
UNRULED FOREVER, while every downstream count (merge validation, ledger
totals) stayed green: the merge tool validates a deputy's output against the
batch FILE, not against coverage of the ledger, so nothing downstream could
see the gap. Rule 13's shape again — an instrument that would have reported
"405 ruled" while 17 were never examined.

**Caught before damage** by noticing the extractor printed "of 388 unapplied"
where the pointer assumed 405, then measuring coverage directly: the ruled
set occupied current positions 0–132 in one contiguous run, 133–387 unruled
— so the correct batch-3 start was 133, not 150. The pre-extracted
batch_004–008 files on disk (made at pass-5 start, `total_unapplied: 405`)
still align with the unruled slices exactly and remain valid inputs.

**General rule.** A resume pointer into a MUTABLE list must be keyed, not
positional — record WHICH items (stable keys) are done, and resume as "the
next N not yet done", never "index K". Fix applied at the tool:
`pass5_extract.py --skip-ruled` filters the pool by `findings_rulings.json`
keys before slicing, so `--start 0 --count 50 --skip-ruled` is always "the
next 50 unruled" no matter how the ledger has shifted; the trap is documented
in the tool docstring. Sibling of the 09-13 lesson (an index is a DERIVED
record; the keyed set is ground truth).

## 2026-09-16 — three lessons from the consumed-field freshness build (E-4)

**1. A note cannot bind to the hash of the file it lives in.** The
DIVERGENT-BY-RULING binding was first specified against the artefact's
whole-content hash — but the divergence note is INSIDE the artefact, so
writing the note moves the hash it binds and the binding can never
converge; my first implementation chased its own tail through two
re-measures before the shape was obvious. The fix is structural: bind to
the PAYLOAD hash (every key except the metadata keys), which moves
exactly when the DIVERGENCE does. General rule: any self-referential
attestation (a stamp, note, or waiver stored in the thing it attests)
must hash the attested SUBSET, never the whole container.

**2. A new instrument bolted beside an old one must mirror the old one's
input tolerance, or every harness that feeds synthetic inputs breaks.**
consumed_stamp REFUSED on inputs that were not repo-relative paths;
the whole-file stamp had always SKIPPED them — and the gate provers
pass absolute scratch paths by design, so both prover suites crashed at
exit 1 (which reads exactly like refusing gates and tests nothing —
their own docstring's trap). Mirror the sibling's predicate, and make
"all inputs skipped" the ABSENCE of the instrument ({}), never a crash
and never a false verify.

**3. Producer metadata churn is itself an input-stability problem.** The
town plan's stamps/waivers/notes changed three times in one evening, and
each change re-staled every plan that whole-file-stamps the town plan as
an input — a chain the whole-file instrument cannot express. Plans that
consume another PLAN should consumed-stamp the fields they read (the
exclusion geometry), so metadata edits to the upstream plan can never
stale them. Caught live when encounters_all went red twice in one hour
for edits that changed no geometry.

## 2026-09-16 — an archival "unreferenced" check that greps one language's call sites is not a reference check

**Found by the Pass-3 forge.py reading, hours after the archival it
indicts.** Item 1e archived 52 scripts under the criterion "uncalled AND
untested AND unnamed", verified by grepping for importers — PYTHON
importers. `scripts/trellis/_forge_generate_body.py` passed that check
and was archived while `scripts/trellis/run_forge.sh:45` still invokes
it through WSL: every fresh forge run would have died at stage 3,
masked as a TRELLIS/GPU failure, sending the debugger into the WSL
environment instead of at the archival. Restored by git mv the same
window; a sweep of all 45 archived entries against .sh/.txt/.json/.md
referencers found two more hits, both prose, both repointed.

**General rule.** A reference check's scope must match the repo's CALL
SURFACES, not its majority language: shell scripts, payload .txt files,
JSON configs and doc-embedded commands all invoke scripts here. Before
archiving anything, grep the basename across EVERY text file class in
the repo — and a checker that reports "no importers" must say which
surfaces it searched, so the absence claim carries its scope (rule 10's
shape: "no Python importer" was reported as "unreferenced").

## 2026-09-16 — O_EXCL makes lock CREATION atomic, not the payload WRITE; the zero-byte window is a steal path

**Found by the auditor of the Pass-3 resource_guard fix, in my own
just-written fix.** I replaced a non-atomic check-then-write lock with
`os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL)` + a payload write, believing O_EXCL closed the
race. It closes the CREATE race — exactly one process creates the file —
but the winner's file is 0 bytes until its JSON flushes a few
instructions later. A rival hitting FileExistsError in that window reads
an empty file, `json.load` raises, the lock reads as "unreadable →
reclaim", and the rival STEALS the live holder's lock. Both then hold —
the interleaved-mutation outcome the lock exists to stop.

**Why the three-direction proof missed it.** The suite tested "garbage
lock reclaimed" and "live second acquire refuses" SERIALLY; this defect
lives only in the window BETWEEN them — a rival arriving in the 0-byte
gap. A race that exists between two tested states is invisible to tests
that each hold one state still.

**The fix.** An unreadable lock is not proof of a dead holder: re-read
once after a short sleep before reclaiming. A live payload lands in the
gap; a genuinely garbage lock is still garbage. General rule: atomicity
of a multi-step publish (create THEN fill) is only as strong as its
slowest step being atomic — and a reader that treats "I could not parse
it yet" as "it is dead" converts a timing gap into a correctness bug
(non-negotiable 6 again, at microsecond scale).

## 2026-09-16 — correcting a claim's comment while leaving its PRINT copy is a seed-and-copy miss (rule 9)

**Found by the rock_scatter Pass-3 auditor.** I corrected the embed
comment (F7: the displacement is along the BLENDED up-axis, the surface
normal only at align=1) but left the identical wrong "along the surface
normal" claim in the run-REPORT print — the copy every operator actually
reads on every run, more visible than the comment. Rule 9's containment
("fix the SEED as well as the copy") applies within one file too: a
claim usually has more than one voice — a docstring, an inline comment,
and a printed line — and correcting the quietest one while the loudest
keeps lying is worse than not touching it, because the file now
contradicts itself and the reader trusts whichever they hit first.

**General rule.** When a wrong claim is corrected, grep the DISTINCTIVE
PHRASE of it across the whole file (and its seed file) before calling it
done — "surface normal" in print strings here — so every voice of the
claim moves together. A correction that leaves a louder copy standing is
an incomplete fix, not a partial one.

## 2026-09-17 — a python -c payload in double quotes with backticks in it gets eaten by the shell (rule 3's class, new surface)

**Found this session, caught immediately.** Updating the Pass-3 worklist
result string with an inline `python -c "..."`, the result text contained
the literal `` `or "no tiled token"` `` (quoting a code fragment). Bash saw
the backticks inside the double-quoted argument and ran `or "no tiled
token"` as command substitution — "or: command not found" — and spliced its
empty output into the string, so the stored worklist result lost that
clause. The Python still ran (the mangled string was just shorter), so the
corruption was silent except for the stray shell error. Rewritten cleanly by
running the update from a Write-authored `.py` file instead.

**General rule.** This is standing rule 3's shell-quoting hazard on a new
surface: rule 3 already routes COMMIT MESSAGES through a file
(`git commit -F`) for exactly this reason, but the same hazard bites any
`python -c "..."`/`bash -c` whose payload contains backticks, `$(...)`, or
unescaped `$`. For any non-trivial inline payload — especially one carrying
prose with code fragments — Write it to a `.py`/`.sh` file and run the file.
The file path has no failure mode; remembering which characters the shell
eats does. (Also: a data-mangling that leaves the program's exit code 0 is
invisible to the exit check — verify the WRITTEN value, not just that the
writer ran; rule 12's shape, at shell scale.)

## 2026-09-18 — Pass 3 reading: five recurring self-report defects across the script corpus, and the one now mechanized

> STATUS: CURRENT

**What this was.** A claims-vs-behaviour audit of all 178 in-scope scripts:
for each, does what the docstring / comments / printed messages / field
names / exit-code contract CLAIM match what the code DOES. ~648 findings
CONFIRMED-at-source and fixed (41 HIGH), one commit per script, offline suite
GREEN 29/29 at every batch boundary. The point of THIS entry is not the count
— it is that the same five shapes recurred across dozens of unrelated scripts,
so a fresh session (and any new script) will reintroduce them unless the
shapes themselves are named. The per-script commit messages are not where the
next author looks; this is.

**The five recurring shapes, each with its root cause and the rule it implies:**

1. **NN13 zero-sample fail-open — the commonest, and the most dangerous.**
   A probe/verifier/pilot sets `ok = True` (or returns 0, or prints PASS) at
   the tail of a `try`, unconditionally — so a run that found ZERO items to
   check (no PostProcessVolume, no texture sample, no HLODLayer asset, no
   station, zero packages scanned) reports success having verified nothing.
   Seen in: local_exposure_probe, meter_warmup_probe, read_grass_card,
   read_hlod_settings, read_layer_tiling, read_rvt_and_mipbias,
   read_shadow_state, read_stochastic_binding, survey_shots
   (`len(filed) == len(stations)` is `0 == 0`), verify_kit_closure (closure
   PASS over 0 scanned), task4_shadow_lever (`any([])` is False).
   *Rule:* success must be GATED on a non-zero sample count with an explicit
   refusal below it. "No differences / no dangling / all resolved" computed
   from "nothing was examined" is silence wearing agreement's clothes
   (non-negotiable 13). A zero count REFUSES.

2. **Rule-12 read-back that is never COMPARED (verification theatre).**
   A value is set, then re-read into a `readback` dict that is only REPORTED,
   never compared to what was requested — so a clamped/ignored/wrong write
   still reports success. Seen in: make_scenetexture_passthrough (domain/
   location/scene_texture_id collected, `ok=True` set regardless — the read
   proved nothing), set_color_gamma (the delivered product `xyz*w` read back
   but never checked against the requested G). Sibling: a "read-back" via
   `load_asset(PATH)` on a RESIDENT asset returns the SAME in-memory object,
   so it verifies the in-memory struct write-back (real, via fresh struct
   copies) but NOT disk persistence — the docstrings that called it a
   "save+reload" overclaimed (task4_shadow_lever, hlod_set_approx_accuracy,
   hlod_set_proxy_budget).
   *Rule:* a read-back must be COMPARED to the expected value AND come from a
   different instrument than the one that made the claim. `load_asset` is not
   a disk round-trip; `save_*`'s bool return is the disk evidence.

3. **save-return discarded (a save that can silently not happen).**
   `save_asset` / `save_loaded_assets` / `save_packages` / `save_current_level`
   / `write_triangle_mesh` all return False on failure WITHOUT raising, and
   the return was thrown away while success printed. Seen across many payloads
   and both trellis mesh scripts, and — after the audit "finished" — in TWO
   payloads it never reached (hlod_set_approx_accuracy, hlod_set_proxy_budget),
   found only because this shape was mechanized (below).
   *Rule:* capture the bool and require it; it is the only disk-persistence
   signal. **This is now enforced by `scripts/check_save_verified.py` in the
   offline suite** — see the RECIPES anti-spec.

4. **`except: pass` that DROPS a field instead of marking it ABSENT.**
   A per-property read wrapped so a failed read silently omits the key, making
   "missing" indistinguishable from "not read" — the exact missing-vs-zero
   confusion these probes claim to avoid. Seen in: meter_warmup_probe (x2),
   read_rvt_and_mipbias, read_shadow_state, read_stochastic_binding,
   read_grass_card. *Rule:* on a failed read, record `"ABSENT"` / `"UNKNOWN"`,
   never drop the key.

5. **mutate/identify-by-label, and unvalidated MODE — rule 8.**
   Selecting an actor to move/mutate/restore by `get_actor_label() == X`, first
   match wins, no disambiguation — and labels collide in this project (two
   landscapes carried identical proxy labels). Seen in: move_station_diagnostic,
   task4_shadow_lever (sun by label). Adjacent: a single scalar restore value
   that cannot restore heterogeneous originals (landscape_force_lod restoring
   two landscapes from one HOME), and a MODE string not validated so an
   unrecognised mode silently takes a destructive branch (landscape_force_lod).
   *Rule:* identify by property signature, refuse on >1 match, validate the
   mode, and refuse a single-value restore across heterogeneous targets.

**A sixth, non-mechanizable, worth stating:** a "prove" harness whose
negative controls counted ANY non-zero exit as a correct refusal
(prove_gaea_reader) — so it "proved the gates work" whenever the tool merely
crashed. A negative control must assert the SPECIFIC failure reason (here, the
gate's own exit code), or it proves only that something went wrong.

**General rule / what changed process-wise.** Of the five shapes, exactly one
is statically decidable — the discarded save-return (shape 3) — so it is now a
suite gate (`check_save_verified.py`), and it caught two live cases on its
first run. The other four need judgement (is this the empty case? is the
read-back compared? is this a label or a signature?), which is why the audit
needed a reading pass and cannot be fully replaced by a linter. When writing
ANY new probe/verifier/mutator, walk these five before committing; when
reviewing one, they are the first five questions. The completeness test for a
future reading pass: could a fresh author reintroduce shape N without this
entry firing? For shape 3, no — the gate fires. For 1/2/4/5, only this entry
does.

## 2026-09-19 — the HLOD save-cost pilot RAN, and it answers the 2026-09-07 open question: the hang was the BULK save, not per-package cost

The 2026-09-07 lesson ("'one cell first' meant the assignment too") ended with a
gap it could not close: the whole-world HLOD assignment saved 2,796 external
actor packages in one bulk operation, the save spun ~5 cores for 90 minutes
writing nothing, and I killed it *"and I still do not know why it does not
[complete]."* The next attempt was to assign one cell, save it, and MEASURE the
per-package cost before scaling. This session did exactly that.

### What was measured

Fresh offscreen editor on `/Game/Alpine8K` (rule-7 MATCH, world fully loaded:
4337 actors), the Pass-3-fixed `hlod_setup_layers.py` (which now actually saves
each touched package one at a time, timed, and re-reads), bounded by CENTRE_CM /
RADIUS_M. Per-package `save_packages([pkg], False)`, one at a time:

    StaticMeshActor (props)     n=17  mean 0.012 s   max 0.027
    InstancedFoliageActor       n=41  mean 0.0115 s  max 0.014
    LandscapeStreamingProxy     n=21  mean 0.564 s   max 0.832

79 packages, 0 failed, times stable within each class. Whole-world projection
(counts x mean): props ~17 s + foliage ~13 s + proxies 256x0.564 ~144 s ≈
**~3 min**, dominated by the 256 landscape proxies (~65x a prop/foliage package).
Evidence: `_verify/hlod/save_cost_pilot_2026-09-19/RESULTS.md`.

### The root-cause refinement

The per-package save is CHEAP and the whole world projects to ~3 minutes. So the
90-minute 09-07 hang was NOT the intrinsic cost of saving 2,796 packages — it was
the **BULK save call** (one operation over the whole set) doing something
pathological, exactly the shape R-EDITOR-CLOSE and save_level already distrust
about `save_packages` over large sets. The pilot's fix — save one package at a
time — sidesteps it. The general rule the 09-07 entry reached for ("I had no
estimate for the save") is now discharged: the estimate exists, next to the
operation, like every other large op in this repo.

### What this does and does NOT license

DOES: prove the save PATH works (it had never actually saved before the Pass-3
fix — STATE 2026-09-18), and prove a whole-world assignment+save is affordable.
DOES NOT: authorise the whole-world assignment itself. Two things are still open
and were deliberately not settled here — (1) the projection is a projection, not
a full-world run (I measured 79, not 2,796; linearity is inferred from stable
per-package times), and (2) the assignment POLICY is unsettled (`_Landscape`
ruled REDUNDANT in STATE 3c; FoliageApprox-for-all-foliage). A full assignment
wants its own session with a named restore tag. The pilot's 79 assignments were
therefore fully reverted (read-back: 0 target-class actors layered) and the
byte-churned OFPA packages `git checkout`-restored, leaving the world unchanged.

### Process note

The reversibility discipline mattered: assigning HLOD layers dirties real OFPA
packages in the shipped world, and a cost pilot must not leave a half-applied,
unsettled policy behind. Assign -> measure -> revert -> verify-clean -> restore
byte-churn is the shape for any "measure the cost of mutating N of the shipped
world" pilot.

## 2026-09-19 — a carve guardrail computed from the SAME coordinate source as the cut cannot detect a wrong map (NN rule 0), and a zero-change write still re-encodes (rule 13)

The Brief-4 T3 carve tool (`scripts/carve_water_notches.py`) is an irreversible
off-disk edit of the 8129² heightmap. Its first draft passed its own dry run —
and the audit gate caught two latent defects BEFORE the `--write`, both instances
of law that already exists, firing exactly as intended:

1. **`subset_ok` (changed pixels ⊆ declared notch discs) was built from the same
   `(cx, cy, R)` as the cut, in the same loop.** A wrong 2033→8129 coordinate map
   would relocate BOTH the cut and the mask together, so the guardrail would still
   report PASS while the cut landed in the wrong place. This is non-negotiable
   rule 0 (instruments sharing a source are ONE measurement) in a new costume: a
   guardrail is only a guardrail if it is computed from a DIFFERENT source than
   the operation it guards. Fix: an INDEPENDENT per-lip check — the 8129 terrain
   at the mapped lip must agree with hydro's 2033-measured `lip_elev_m` (a field
   that does NOT drive the cut, which uses `outlet_level_m`). It read 1.29 m max,
   decisively validating the map; a transposed or 4×-off map would read hundreds.

2. **A zero-change run printed "guardrails PASS" and, under `--write`, would
   re-encode the 104 MB PNG as a no-op** — the rule-13 zero-sample class (silence
   wearing agreement's clothes). An empty `pool_ids` or a truncated set would cut
   nothing and report success. Fix: refuse the write when `n_changed == 0` and
   require the expected lip count.

General rule for the next gate I write: **the check must not share its inputs
with the thing it checks, and "nothing happened" is a refusal, not a pass.** Also
recorded: the audit REQUEST must carry both ROOTS (`docs/environment.md`) or the
gate blocks procedurally before reading any code — the first submission omitted
them and was correctly refused. The tool was hardened, the I;16 round-trip
isolation-tested (the one path a dry run never exercises), then the carve ran
clean (47 px, sub-decimetre; the fill-to-level premise held). Evidence:
`_verify/brief4/carve_2026-09-19/RESULT.md`; the anti-spec belongs in a
R-WATER-CARVE RECIPES lock owed when the whole carve lands.

## 2026-09-19 — Brief 4 T4: wet_shore is a footprint-DILATION ring, not a global elevation band
> STATUS: CURRENT

`derive_layer_weights.py`'s `wet_shore` layer was hardcoded zero pending
Brief 4's water level. T4 implemented it. The load-bearing decision, made
before any code: **wet_shore is the damp shore of a specific water BODY,
not proximity to a water SURFACE.** A naive `|h - level| <= band` band
paints a contour line clear across the map — every mountainside at 180 m
would read as Lake A's shore. The fix is to gate the 4 m vertical band by
ADJACENCY to the lake's connected footprint (a dilation of it), so only
the actual shoreline qualifies. The selftest's discriminator is a region
at the SAME elevation but far from the lake reading ZERO — a global band
would light it up; the ring does not (measured 0.000).

**The footprint came from the tool of record, not a second flood-fill
(NN24).** The lake footprints already exist as a hydrology derivation
(`hydro_derive.level_slice` on the committed 4x heightmap). Re-flood-
filling at the shipped 8129 grid would be a SECOND lake-extent derivation
that need not reproduce the hydro figures — connectivity at the fine grid
can split or merge basins the 2033 analysis fixed. So `load_lake_footprints`
reuses `level_slice` and upsamples the 2033 mask to 8129 by EXACT vertex
indexing (`np.round(np.linspace(...))`, step 0.25, 4k->k exact), with the
footprint used only as an adjacency LOCALIZER — the precise damp band is
cut from the shipped heightmap, so the resolution gap is immaterial. A
POSITIVE CONTROL refuses if a footprint area drifts from `water.json`'s
`area_ha`; on the real run it reproduced 125.5 / 13.6 / 49.6 ha EXACTLY.

**Three defects the auditor caught before first execution**, all fixed:
(1) `os.path.join(REPO, user_prefix)` SILENTLY discards REPO on an absolute
prefix (and `..` escapes it) — a resolve-and-check `commonpath` guard was
added, not a trusting join; a different-drive prefix raises `ValueError`,
which is wrapped to fail closed. (2) PIL `resize(..., NEAREST)` is
pixel-center resampling, NOT the vertex-aligned mapping the docstring
claimed — up to one 4x cell (~4 m) off at edges; a docstring number that
overstates precision is a rule-9 defect even when output impact is nil, so
it became an exact index upsample. (3) A "declared zero" message that fires
BOTH for pointer-absent AND pointer-present-with-zero-lakes makes a
zero-sample run read as intent (rule 13) — now the second case REFUSES.

**The `--expand` refusal was amended, and the amendment is load-bearing.**
The shipped weightmap stores four channels (snow/rock/scree/forest_floor)
and derives meadow as `1 - their sum` in the shader; wet_shore/dirt_path/
gravel fold into that remainder. The old assertion `remainder ==
gravel+meadow` and the `wet_shore == 0` refusal were both correct only
WHILE wet_shore was zero. With a real wet_shore the identity is
`remainder == wet_shore+dirt_path+gravel+meadow`; dropping wet from that
sum false-passes exactly when wet is zero, so adding it is not cosmetic.
`dirt_path` STAYS required-zero — its zero is a structural fact (streets
are actors), not a pending mask. wet_shore renders as grass at blockout
(no shore surface / no free channel); promoting it to a stored layer is a
MATERIAL-PASS item, recorded in R-LAYERS5 WHAT IS NOT DONE. The shipped
PNG is byte-identical whether or not wet_shore is populated.

Proof: selftest 24/24 (was 16; specimens C wet_shore + D `--expand`,
three directions each with counts); real derive positive-control EXACT,
wet_shore 0.02% (~26k cells), dirt_path 0; `_expand_check` on the real
scratch weightmaps passes with gaps 0.00392 / 0.00784 (1/255, 2/255).
Evidence: `_verify/brief4/t4_wetshore_2026-09-19/`. Anti-spec locked in
RECIPES R-LAYERS5 REJECTED.

## 2026-09-19 — THE FIRST 8129 PUSH DIED IN THE TRANSPORT WINDOW, AND THE ENGINE'S OWN LOG LINE SETTLED THE UNKNOWN

**What was attempted.** Brief 4 T5a: `push_heightmap.py --recipe
recipes/alpine_8k.json --push --timeout 25` — the first-ever push against
the 8129 world (every proven push was 2017). Pre-flight was clean:
encoding confirmed, orientation identity, 1280/1280 vertices in
tolerance, render-target check 2304 texels across 9 blocks.

**What happened.** The push stage failed with `RuntimeError: Remote party
failed to send a valid response!` and the tool correctly reported
"terrain state UNKNOWN, do NOT save". The editor log shows the staging
stages ran (`AssetCheck: /Game/Debug/M_PushHeight Validating` 21:27:05,
`T_PushHeight_Source` thumbnail/autosave 21:27:15) — the 8129² staging
texture import plus the M_PushHeight compile alone outlast a 25 s
transport window that the 2017 world never stressed.

**Root cause, at a source line.** Two independent facts: (1) the remote
transport gives up at the caller's timeout while the editor-side payload
keeps running — the response is LOST, not the work; (2) the engine
prints `"Took %f seconds to import heightmap from render target."` at
`LandscapeEdit.cpp:8175` on EVERY RT heightmap import. The editor log
contained ZERO such lines, so the import never executed — the payload
died or refused after staging, and its refusal JSON was lost with the
transport.

**The general rule.** An exit-5 UNKNOWN after a push is settled by an
instrument the transport cannot lose: grep the EDITOR LOG for the
`LandscapeEdit.cpp:8175` import line. Line present = the write happened
(then verify against the source); line absent = the write never ran
(then a re-run cannot double-apply). The dry-run re-run that R1
prescribes samples only the trusted region (x,y <= 1008) and CANNOT see
a localized change like the 47-px carve — on the 8129 world the log
grep is the settling instrument, the dry-run is only corroboration.

**Also observed, same run.** The FIRST pre-flight export after editor
launch returned ALL ZEROS (`raw R range 0.0 .. 0.0`) with only 0.5 GB
system RAM free, and the tool compared those zeros against the source
and reported "median 9793 units difference" — a nothing-read wearing a
measurement's clothes (standing rule 13's exact shape, this time inside
an instrument that DID report its sample count but not its emptiness).
The second run read real values. A raw-R range of 0.0..0.0 on a terrain
whose minimum is above zero is a FAILED READ, not a flat terrain.

## 2026-09-19 — A UNIT-MISMATCHED FILTER ADDED TO A RULED TOOL PASSED ITS SELFTEST BECAUSE THE SELFTEST NEVER CALLED IT

**What happened.** Brief-4 T7 added a candidate filter to the RULED
`derive_ground_station.py` (water exclusion + a near-centre radius) to
re-derive Bench_ground on Lake A's shore. The radius centre was built as
`cx = ox + col*px_m` (METRES, because load_terrain returns cm/100) and
compared against a candidate in CENTIMETRES — off by 100x. It mostly
REFUSED (radius shrank ~100x) but admitted a narrow wrong-location band,
and I ALSO passed a 4 m-grid col/row to an arg the code treated as the
native 1 m grid (a second, independent 4x error). The "A's shore fails,
bands 30/12" finding I recorded came from that doubly-broken run.

**Why the guard did not fire.** `selftest()` called `evaluate()` directly
and never `search()`, so it exercised none of the new filter — it passed,
and would have passed with the bug present. The auditor caught it (W1/W2);
the committed Bench_ground was safe only by luck (the final run used
`--exclude-water` alone, the one path without the bug).

**Root cause + fix.** The filter now takes a WORLD-CENTIMETRES centre
(`--near-world-cm`), removing both the metres/centimetres slip and the
which-grid ambiguity; the mask read was already cm-correct and matches
`plan_encounters.WaterMask`. A selftest case now exercises `keep()`
directly: centre kept, 500 m kept at r=600 / rejected at r=400, a masked
cell rejected. Re-run correctly: A's shore within 800 m gives best forward
rise 21.4 m, bands below the 160-row floor — the conclusion (A's basin rim
cannot host the concave surface-metrics station) STANDS, now on a sound
measurement.

**The general rule.** A filter added to a ruled tool needs a selftest case
of ITS OWN. A selftest that exercises only the untouched function proves
nothing about the addition and passes regardless — the same
instrument-distrust the gates get (non-negotiable 8): verify with a
different instrument than the one that made the claim, and a selftest that
never runs the new code IS the claim. And prefer WORLD units at a tool's
boundary over grid col/row, which carries a silent which-grid question.


## 2026-09-19b — Brief 4 T6: a nav REACHABILITY collapse was the MEASUREMENT, not the navmesh — HLOD proxy collision intercepted the ground trace

**Happened.** The post-water reachable lattice (`city_reachable_lattice_payload.txt`, box ±406400 cm, step 6000, 18496 cells) read **2802 of 18496 reachable / 11375 projecting** — a 72% collapse from the 2026-08-27 R-NAVGRID baseline of **10146 / 15573**. The water carve removes ~1.5 km² (≈417 cells), nowhere near 7344. 64 nav-chunk actors were resident and the build's maxTiles matched the baseline, so "the navmesh is fine" and "the number is right" could not both be true.

**Refused, not recorded (rule 13).** A re-measure that does not reproduce the prior value is not a measurement. The 2802 was held as a refused read while the cause was found, never written to the spec.

**Root cause (measured).** A read-only diagnostic (`_t6_nav_diag_payload`) showed sample points hitting `WorldPartitionHLOD` as their ground surface. The 4096 HLOD proxies gained collision in the 2026-09-14 rebuild; the 2026-08-27 nav baseline PREDATES that collision, so the lattice's ground trace (a vertical `line_trace_single`) never had to contend with it. A trace that stops on the proxy returns a wrong ground height, and `project_point_to_navigation` (extent 500 cm) then misses the navmesh below — so both coverage and connectivity read low. STATE T5a had already noted the proxies intercept traces (`collision_nohit_probe.py`); the lattice payload simply predated that world condition.

**Fix + confirmation.** Ignore `WorldPartitionHLOD` actors in the ground trace (the real landscape stays resident via `load_all_world_partition_regions`). With them ignored: **2802 → 9810 reachable, 11375 → 15068 projecting** — reproduces the baseline minus the water delta (10146 − 9810 = 336 cells = 1.21 km², ≤ the 1.5 target). Post-water reachable = **35.32 km²** (was 36.53). Folded into `city_reachable_lattice_payload.txt`.

**The general rule.** When a build-derived instrument's result collapses, suspect the READ before the world: a trace or projection whose premise (what surface it hits) was silently changed by an *unrelated* later build will read a plausible wrong number. The baseline that a rule-13 check reproduces was captured under the OLD world; if the world gained collision geometry since, the instrument must exclude it to stay comparable. And a "navmesh is fine" claim from resident-chunk-count + maxTiles is projection, not reachability (`reachability.py`'s own distinction) — only the path query separates them, and here even the path query was reading through the wrong ground.

## 2026-09-19b — Brief 4 T10 close-out: a waiver `to` hash from a file the same run rewrites, a compact dump that reflowed pretty plans, and four prior-session failures owed a home

**restamp ordering (auditor F-1).** `restamp_consumed.py` computed the `_verified` waiver's whole-file pair for `_all` and THEN, later in the same run, rewrote `_all` with its own new waiver — so the recorded `to` hash was dead on arrival: `check_plan_freshness` recomputed `_all`'s actual hash and `waiver_covers` saw `to != actual` → `_verified` read STALE on run 1, converging only on run 2 (the docstring claimed idempotent). Fixed by processing `_all` BEFORE `_verified` so the pair binds to `_all`'s final bytes. *Rule:* bind a whole-file waiver pair only after every plan the run mutates has been written; a `to` from a file you will rewrite is not a measurement of the committed artefact.

**restamp compact dump.** The driver wrote every plan with a bare `json.dump(doc, fh)` (compact, no indent), which reflowed the pretty-printed plans (`_all`, `_verified`, roofbias, at indent 2/1) into 25k-line whitespace-only diffs and diverged from their producers' serialization. Fix: sniff each file's existing indent (second-line leading spaces) and trailing newline and match it, keeping the json default `ensure_ascii=True` (all the producers use it — the files carry backslash-u escapes). *Rule:* a tool that re-writes an artefact it did not originally produce should preserve that artefact's serialization, or every touch is a whole-file diff.

**Four Brief-4 editor-phase failures, root-caused there, logged here (the close-out they were owed).** (a) `place_foliage`'s `DEFAULT_RECIPE` is the pre-8K `recipes/alpine.json` — already covered above (the lighting-tool entry); always pass `--recipe recipes/alpine_8k.json`. (b) `_VEG` gate had no `card` grass key, so the live recipe's card species was ungated — the suite corpus is `prove_gates.py` fixtures, which never validate the LIVE recipe, so the gap was invisible to the suite (fixed with the card key). (c) `ue_exec --set GO=1` is a LITERAL `__GO__` text substitution in the payload, NOT a Python global — a payload written `if GO:` expecting a global silently ran as a dry-run twice before the placeholder was used (commit b6ca4f0b). *Rule:* `--set NAME=VALUE` substitutes `__NAME__`; a payload that reads a bare name gets a NameError or, worse, a stale global. (d) `build_navmesh_chunk --extra=-noxgecontroller` needs the `=`: `--extra -noxgecontroller` makes argparse read `-noxgecontroller` as an option and reject it; the `=` form binds it as the value. (e) `capture.py` run offscreen during the editor phase INVALIDATED in a retry loop — World Partition streamed out and the editor working set dropped to ~5 GB — and was killed. This session was measurement-only (no scene mutation), so rule 4 did not require a capture (the water capture was taken in the T5 editor phase); the offscreen-capture invalidation stands as a known limit to revisit if a capture is genuinely needed offscreen.


## 2026-09-19b — Brief 4 T10: the SUITE runs check_plan_freshness `--reproduce`, which the plain STAMP/consumed pass does not satisfy — three residual reds the restamp missed

The plain `check_plan_freshness` went green after the restamp, but `run_offline_suite` stayed red: the suite's "every plan against its inputs" check runs `--reproduce`, a STRICTER instrument that re-runs each producer and compares payloads. Three carve-induced `--reproduce` reds the STAMP/consumed reconciliation did not touch:

- **foliage ×4 read PRODUCER REFUSES** because `place_foliage` takes no `--out` (the T9 rewire), yet the checker's `"--out" not in src` skip-heuristic misfired: the string "--out" appears in a place_foliage DOCSTRING (`:397`), so the checker ran it with `--out` and argparse said "unrecognized arguments: --out". Fixed in `reproduce()` by mapping that argparse error to CANNOT REPRODUCE (benign — the checker's limit, the STAMP + the RULED `_stamp_waiver` carry freshness), symmetric with the existing "required arguments" branch. Auditor hardened it: anchor the match to `"unrecognized arguments: --out"` (the arg the checker itself supplied, not a grandchild's stderr) and report the argparse line rather than assert the docstring-prose cause. *Rule:* the `--reproduce` skip cannot be inferred from a substring in the producer's source; an argparse usage error about an arg THIS checker supplied is the checker's limit, classified benign, while STAMP/consumed/HISTORY still drive the verdict.

- **_all read DIFFERS** — the FROZEN pre-water pool reproduces to a smaller water-excluded set (deterministic, 69420bbea09e → cda86f9d6549 across two runs). The STAMP `_stamp_waiver` covers the HISTORY path but NOT `--reproduce`; that needs a `_divergence_note` (the `divergence_ruled` mechanism town_plan already uses). Added one bound to the observed payload pair.

- **_verified went STALE after the _all note was added** — the SAME class as the restamp auditor's F-1: adding `_divergence_note` to `_all` moved `_all`'s file hash, expiring `_verified`'s whole-file waiver pair (bound to `_all`'s old hash). Re-running restamp (which processes `_all` before `_verified`) rebound the pair to `_all`'s final bytes. *Rule again:* any metadata write to a plan moves its file hash and expires every downstream whole-file waiver bound to it — re-run the restamp AFTER the last such write, in dependency order.

Net: `run_offline_suite` NO FAILURES across 31 checks; `--reproduce` reports 8 fresh + 2 DIVERGENT-BY-RULING (town_plan, _all). The general lesson: the plain freshness pass and the suite's `--reproduce` pass are DIFFERENT instruments — reconciling one does not reconcile the other, and the SUITE is the acceptance.


## 2026-09-19b — perf_standalone.py now captures VRAM + residency (T11 rule-12 gap closed), and a `--only` verification run clobbers the same-date artefact

T11 flagged that `perf_standalone.py` declared no VRAM/residency, so its numbers could not answer whether the water pushed VRAM toward the DEVICE_HUNG ceiling. Amended:

- **VRAM peak** by polling `nvidia-smi memory.used` through the dwell, peak over the steady-state window (a MARGIN_S-wider *superset* of the timing tail — conservative for a ceiling check, not the identical window; the first draft's "same window" comment was wrong and was corrected, auditor LOW-1/2), vs the 13,312 MiB abort ceiling. A SYSTEM instrument, so it needs no UE CSV column to exist; a box without nvidia-smi records `vram = null` with the reason, never 0 (rule 13).
- **In-engine cross-check** via `r.GPUCsvStatsEnable 1` + a best-effort CSV column reader. On this 5.8 build it DOES emit `GPUMem/LocalUsedMB` etc., and it agreed: plaza `GPUMem/LocalUsedMB 4921.2` (this process) vs nvidia-smi 5094 (whole-GPU), the gap being other consumers — two independent instruments (non-negotiable 8). The reader targets GPU/VRAM/streaming-qualified `*mem*/*mb*` columns only; a bare `mem.*mb` alt was dropped because it also matched system-RAM columns (auditor LOW-3), and a matched-but-unparsable column set returns `{}` so the ABSENT note attaches (auditor LOW-4).
- **Residency** is read from the log as WP streaming-active evidence (Initialize + GenerateStreaming) plus the declared loading range. A steady-state resident-cell COUNT is NOT reachable via startup-only ExecCmds in `-game`, so it is declared as a limit, not faked.

Live plaza verification: VRAM peak 5094 MiB, +8218 headroom, station ok (GPU p90 9.494 unchanged) — the amendment did not disturb the timing capture.

**The gotcha, logged so it does not recur:** `perf_standalone.py`'s outdir is `standalone_<today>`, so a `--only plaza` verification run wrote a 1-zone `perf_standalone.json` OVER the committed 4-zone T11 artefact in the same date dir. Restored from HEAD; the plaza VRAM proof was copied to `_verify/perf/vram_amendment_2026-09-19/` first. *Rule:* a partial (`--only`) perf run shares the date-keyed outdir with a full run — copy the partial result out to a distinct path before it, or it silently replaces a complete artefact (the tool's own no-overwrite guard only fires when NOTHING was measured, not when LESS was).

## 2026-09-19 — Brief 5 Task 0 baseline: the audit caught three defects before a single live run

Building the foliage-hide A/B into `perf_standalone.py`, the auditor (given roots on resubmit — the first pass BLOCKED because I omitted REPO_ROOT/UE_PROJECT_ROOT, which are mandatory in every audit request) found three HIGH defects by reading engine source, before anything touched `-game`:

- **The read-back regex could not match the engine's echo.** A bare-cvar query prints `name = "value"` with the value QUOTED (`ConsoleManager.cpp:3230/:3247`); my `([-\d.]+)` capture cannot start at the `"`, so it parsed 0 of 3 cvars every run and `_honoured` was False even when the hide was honoured — the exact 0-of-N-parsed motif of standing rule 13. Fix: quote-tolerant `\s*=\s*"?([-\d.eE+]+)"?`, numeric `_honoured`, and a `_parsed_n` count beside the verdict.
- **`r.ShowFlag.Foliage` is not a registered cvar.** Show-flag cvars register as `ShowFlag.<Name>` with no `r.` prefix (`ShowFlags.cpp:1116`). The `r.` form logs "Command not recognized", which trips `command_not_recognized` -> `station_ok=False` -> the A/B poisons its own verdict. Fix: `ShowFlag.Foliage 0`.
- **Same-day A/B runs shared one sidecar.** `outdir` is date-keyed and the sidecar was always `perf_standalone.json` — the second run overwrites the first's VRAM/read-back/verdict (only the tag-named CSVs survived). This is the SAME class as the LESSONS gotcha directly above (a `--only` run replacing a complete artefact). Fix: fold the tag into the sidecar filename.

**The general point:** every one of these was invisible to a dry-run and would have produced a plausible-looking but wrong A/B — a `_honoured:False` over an honoured hide, a SUSPECT verdict over a good station, or a silently clobbered result. They were caught only by reading the engine source the code assumed, which is the audit gate doing exactly its job. Two-altitude: narrative here; the perf tool has no RECIPES recipe, so the fixes live in-code with the finding IDs (F1/F2/F3) in the commit.

Census read-back finding: every tree species is culled INSIDE its detail band (detail ring 238-1149 m vs the 512 m streaming-clamped cull), so a live instance is only ever seen at detail; shape/blob are HLOD's job. And the foliage-hide A/B measured live foliage at 0.116 ms (treeline) / 0.286 ms (plaza ground-cover) — removing 10,860 / 126,386 GPUScene instances barely moved GPU p90. Live foliage instancing is near-free on this GPU; the forest's GPU weight is HLOD proxy + landscape. The frustum test was validated by plaza's ~25.4% visible/in-cull ratio across four independent species (= the 90/360 azimuth fraction), so treeline's visible=0 is real angular exclusion, not a bug.

## 2026-09-20 — Brief 5 overnight: two bare-cvar read-backs the log would not echo, and an HLOD A/B that could not conclude

Two `-game` read-backs came back empty and the read-back machinery correctly refused to call them honoured (rule 13, safe direction):

- **`grass.DensityScale`** (density sweep) and **`r.HLOD` / `wp.Runtime.HLOD`** (HLOD A/B) all returned None from the bare-name query echo, while `foliage.DensityScale` and `grass.Enable` echoed fine (`name = "value"`, quote-tolerant regex from audit F1). `command_not_recognized` was False in every case, so the commands were accepted — the values simply did not print in a form the log-parse could capture. Same shape as the earlier `grass.DensityScale` None in the foliage-hide run. Root cause not fully pinned (a bare query for some cvars appears to route to a channel the `-AbsLog` capture does not carry, or prints without the `= value` form); recorded as a tool read-back gap, not a cvar failure.

- **Consequence for item 3d (HLOD GPU share): INCONCLUSIVE, reported as such.** `--hide-hlod` left GPU p90 unchanged (treeline 7.24 vs 7.229; plaza 9.457 vs 9.441) AND the lever read-back was 0/2. That is exactly the ambiguity rule 13 exists to force into the open: an unchanged GPU with an unconfirmed lever cannot be reported as "HLOD costs ~0 here" — it could equally be "the startup-`-ExecCmds` HLOD disable never applied." The number stays owed to a dedicated pass (editor actor-hide, or a console timing that fires warm and is verified). NOT recorded as a measured zero.

**The item-2 density finding stands on an independent instrument despite the grass echo gap:** foliage.DensityScale read back at 2/4, and GPUSceneInstanceCount (a second instrument) showed no rise — placed HISM foliage is capped at its authored count, so DensityScale>1 is a no-op on trees regardless of what the grass echo did. The verdict did not rest on the unparsed value.

General point (sibling to audit F1/rule 13): a read-back that returns nothing must fail toward "unconfirmed", and a measurement whose lever is unconfirmed must not be dressed as a result — even when the raw number (GPU p90 unchanged) looks like a clean zero. The perf tool did both correctly here; the lesson is to keep the HLOD share on the owed list rather than let 7.24≈7.229 read as "HLOD is free."

## 2026-09-20 — HLOD GPU share: measured negligible, and how the instrument had to change twice to say so

The item-3d HLOD share was INCONCLUSIVE because the `-game` disable lever never applied: `wp.Runtime.HLOD 0` / `r.HLOD 0` passed via startup `-ExecCmds` were logged `LogEngine: Warning:  wp.Runtime.HLOD 0` — the engine's list of DEFERRED/unprocessed exec commands — and GPUScene + GPU p90 were unchanged with no query echo. A startup ExecCmds cvar is not a reliable runtime toggle for World Partition HLOD.

The dedicated pass switched to the **editor actor-hide**, which is verifiable: enumerate the 1042 `WorldPartitionHLOD` actors, `set_is_temporarily_hidden_in_editor(True)`, and read back `is_temporarily_hidden_in_editor()` == 1042/1042 (rule 13 satisfied — the A/B is only valid because the hide is confirmed). But the first GPU instrument, a single-frame `ProfileGPU`, was useless: three vista captures read 6.27 / 6.75 / 10.01 ms — ±3.7 ms of frame-to-frame noise (RT dynamic-geometry build spikes, editor primitives, streaming reactions), and vista even read HIGHER hidden than visible. A single frame cannot measure a sub-ms share.

The fix was a **steady editor `CsvProfile` window** (~3300 frames), which averages the noise the way the `-game` p90 window does. Result at vista (the HLOD-dominant far view): GPUTime p90 **7.287 visible vs 7.272 hidden = 0.015 ms (0.2%)**, mean delta 0.002 ms. Hiding every one of the 1042 HLOD proxies changes GPU by ~nothing.

**This refutes the v1 BASELINE inference that the treeline forest GPU is mostly HLOD.** The merged HLOD proxies sit 2.2–3.5 km out, are Nanite, and cover few screen pixels, so they are near-free; the frame is landscape Nanite + atmosphere + shadows. Measurement beat inference — exactly the case rule 9 and the "instrument premise" discipline exist for. Two general points: (1) a lever passed to `-game` via startup ExecCmds must be verified applied, not assumed — the deferred-warning log is the tell; (2) a share smaller than an instrument's own frame-to-frame noise needs a steady window, not a single capture, and the verified actor-hide (not the unverifiable cvar) is what makes the delta trustworthy.

## 2026-09-20 — Brief 5 baseline v3: "measured negligible" was not a measurement — an A/B needs a positive control that the thing was rendering

The desk audited baseline v2 (`research/brief5/BRIEF5_BASELINE_AUDIT.md`) and reverted its two headline conclusions. Both were right to revert, and the reasons are the general lesson.

**The HLOD "RESOLVED — negligible" (the entry directly above) was not a measurement.** Two independent defects, either fatal:
1. The editor actor-hide A/B had **no positive control that the proxies were being drawn**. At full editor residency World Partition keeps an HLOD proxy hidden whenever its source cell is loaded (`WorldPartitionHLODEnabled && !bIsCellVisible`, HLODRuntimeSubsystem.cpp:167), so hiding the (already-hidden) proxies changed nothing — the 0.015 ms delta is the control *failing*, not a measured zero. A delta of zero from hiding something that is not on screen is silence wearing agreement's clothes (non-negotiable 0's sibling: rule 13 catches a read that returned nothing counted as confirmation; this is a *toggle* that toggled nothing counted as "no cost").
2. The "nearest 2.2–3.5 km" distances it rested on were an **artefact**: `get_actor_location`/`get_actor_bounds` are **degenerate for Instanced-layer HLOD actors** (their ISM components are not registered in the editor session — `find_instanced_cell_by_grid.py:5`), so every actor reported the same shared origin and the same three distances regardless of cell. The v3 fix derives the cell centre from the grid index in the actor label (`centre=(idx+0.5)·cellsize`), which is exact and varies per cell.

**The `-game` toggle path is blocked, and the "deferred warning" was a misread.** `wp.Runtime.HLOD` is an `FAutoConsoleCommand` (HLODRuntimeSubsystem.cpp:149) delivered via startup `-ExecCmds` → `GEngine->DeferredCommands` (UnrealEngine.cpp:2552), a one-shot on the first post-init tick. It *does* run (BugItGo in the same batch executed; `LogCheatManager: BugItGo to:` at :10008), and each command is echoed as `LogEngine: Warning: <cmd>` — which v2 read as "deferred/never applied". The real proof it had no effect is the **render-side counter**: as-is vs `wp.Runtime.HLOD 0` runs are byte-identical on GPUSceneInstanceCount / SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances / ActorCount/WorldPartitionHLOD / GPUTime. The one-shot fires before the far cells stream, and there is no post-settle re-fire inside the fence (an ini/asset/Python change would be needed). Verdict: **INCONCLUSIVE**, not "resolved".

**The "density is cheap" number was measured where there is no density on screen.** v2's foliage-hide deltas were taken at treeline (0 visible live trees) and plaza (903, mostly grass) of 185,385. v3 derives a `forest_floor` station (densest cluster, heading swept for the most in-frustum trees; max **1844** — 5000 is unreachable at 90° hFOV / 512 m cull, reported honestly) and measures **0.185 ms, 11.4× the station's own noise floor**, spent in LumenReflections + shadows + base pass (not Nanite raster). And the definitive read-back: **all four FoliageTypes have `enable_density_scaling=False`**, so `foliage.DensityScale` (a scalability opt-in lever) cannot even *test* this forest — "no budget crossing" should have read "this lever cannot test it" (audit B3).

**What v3 measured that stands:** the noise floor (min_detectable 0.060/0.040/0.016 ms; GPUScene is deterministic across as-is runs, refuting v2's "streaming variance"); the forest foliage cost above; the HLOD proxy *composition* (Instanced = INSTANCING at lowest LOD, Merged = MESH_APPROXIMATE — not "merged Nanite"); and the switch distances (billboard/imposter engage at 88–128 m, all far above the 40 px detail floor — so the mesh becomes a card while the tree is still hundreds of px tall). The GPU *share* of those proxies stays open (item-8 `-game` MRQ).

**Tooling failures this session, logged before retry:** (1) `derive_forest_station.py` first ran an O(positions × headings × 185k) pure-Python scan and timed out at 300 s; root cause = no vectorisation and no 512 m pre-filter; fixed with numpy (64 s). (2) The editor payload's final `print("__LL__"+dump[:4000])` would truncate the JSON and make `ue_exec` decode-fail on a *successful* run (a false failure); the auditor caught it before first execution, fixed to a compact always-valid status object (the full result is on disk anyway). Both are the same shape as prior lessons: measure/scale before brute-forcing, and never let a success path emit output an instrument will read as failure.

## 2026-09-21 — Brief 5 T1-T3: a blunt lever's cost is not the targeted change's cost, and the _SRC backup must gate the mutation

Two lessons from the forest ladder work.

**A blanket `foliage.ForceLOD 2` measured +2.9-3.5 ms, but the actual hold cost +0.042 ms.** T1's arm B forced LOD 2 on EVERY foliage instance to prove the lever changed the render (positive control) and to bound the cost. Read literally, +2.9 ms says "holding geometry busts the 12.5 ms budget." But the real T3 fix — pushing only the CARD LOD's ScreenSize past the cull so the card-band trees render their existing LOD G instead of a card — cost +0.042 ms at forest_floor (x2.6 the noise floor), because at that camera few trees sit in the pure 128-512 m card band; the near ones were already geometry. The blunt lever over-stated the targeted change by ~70x. Lesson: a force-everything cvar bounds an upper envelope, not the cost of the surgical edit; measure the edit itself before concluding it is unaffordable. (RHI/PrimitivesDrawn is also not a clean geometry counter here: forcing a mid-LOD on near trees REDUCES their primitives while far cards gain, so it rose at forest_floor and fell at the ring station — the GPU delta was the reliable signal.)

**The pristine `_SRC` duplicate must GATE the mutation, not merely precede it.** The auditor caught a BLOCKER in `brief5_t3_hold.py`: on a failed `duplicate_asset` the code recorded "DUPLICATE FAILED" and fell through to `set_lod_screen_sizes` + save on the original anyway — mutating a vendor mesh with no backup, in a repo where `Content/` is gitignored so git is NOT the undo button (the _SRC dupe is). Fixed to `continue` on a failed duplicate. Also hardened: record + read back the auto-compute flag (rule 12), revert-from-disk on a blocked save so a later save-all cannot persist the refused state, and capture every `save_loaded_asset` bool (the offline suite's "no save-return discarded" check flagged two). The save gate itself — save only when read-back matches AND last-LOD tris + slots are unchanged — the auditor verified correct. General rule: when git cannot undo (gitignored vendor content), the on-disk backup is load-bearing and its creation must be a hard precondition of the edit, checked, not assumed.

## 2026-09-21 — Brief 5 close-out (C): the T3 hold never persisted, and an in-memory read-back is not a persisted value

**The headline: a fresh-editor runtime read-back showed the T3 hold is a NO-OP, and the on-disk `.uasset` mtimes prove the save never happened.** C1 opened Alpine8K in a cold editor and read, from the meshes the placed HISM foliage reference, the render-data LOD ScreenSize array (`StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.get_lod_screen_sizes` returns `RenderData->ScreenSize`, cpp:1003-1008 — the array the runtime LOD selector reads). Both card species still carry the PRE-HOLD value: ConiferPine LOD3 = 0.16821, SpruceSub LOD4 = 0.17, versus the t3_hold targets 0.03818 / 0.02642 — `matches_t3_hold = false` for both. The Mesh LOD Coloration colour read-back corroborates: the 128-512 m band renders ~80% card, whereas a hold that took would render ~0% card there (the card pushed past the 512 m cull).

**Root cause, and it is not DDC / proxy caching / component override — the three the desk asked us to weigh.** It is simpler and worse: the T3 save never wrote the package. The live `.uasset` mtimes predate the T3 run — `ScotsPineTall_01.uasset` 2026-08-02, `spruce_half_01.uasset` 2026-08-14 — while only the `_SRC` backups carry the T3 mtime (2026-09-21 06:29). `t3_hold.json` recorded `saved: true` (from `save_loaded_asset`'s return) and `readback_matches: true` (0.038 / 0.026), but that read-back was taken in the SAME session, in memory, immediately after `set_lod_screen_sizes` — before any write, and the write to the original package never landed. When that editor closed, the in-memory edit was lost. The meshes are gitignored, so git cannot have reverted them; the file was simply never written. Everything downstream inherited the lost value: `tree_lod_probe_t3.json` (captured in the same doomed session) and `alpine_8k.json`'s "recipe == asset; checked by check_recipe_lods.py" note are both STALE — the asset does NOT match the recipe.

**This retroactively explains V1 and V2.** V1's SSIM tie (0.9166 vs 0.9177) and V2's ~0 ms hold cost were both correct measurements of *nothing changing* — because nothing had changed. Two sessions measured the absence of a fix and read it as a small-but-real fix, because the only instrument that would have caught it (a read-back in a DIFFERENT process, or a file mtime) was never used. This is the previous entry's own lesson turned up a level: that entry noted the T3 save gate was "verified correct" by the auditor — and it was, as a gate on the in-memory state — but a correct gate on an unwritten file still ships nothing.

**The general rule (a persistence sibling to non-negotiables 12 and 8): a value is not persisted until it is read back in a DIFFERENT PROCESS, or the file's mtime confirms the write.** The setter's return (`save_loaded_asset` -> true) and a same-session read-back both prove only that the edit exists in memory. For gitignored vendor content — where git is not the record either — the cheapest independent instrument is the `.uasset` mtime: compare it to the run's wall-clock before trusting `saved: true`. Had T3 checked its own two mesh mtimes against its start time, it would have caught the no-op on the spot instead of two sessions later. Consequence for Brief 5: the T3 "hold shipped" claim is false; the imposter tiling (T1 CONFIRMED) is still live in the band; the fix must be re-applied AND verified to survive an editor restart (a write, out of the read-only close-out's scope).

**C2 settled the imposter root cause the other way.** Opened the vendor Showroom demo READ-ONLY: `spruce_half_01` is placed there as `FoliageInstancedStaticMeshComponent` (HISM) + static actors with the SAME `half_01_imposter` material and 5 LODs — identical to our foliage type — and forced to the card (r.ForceLOD 8) at 150 m it renders clean tree billboards with NO square tiling. So H1 (octahedral frame-blend fails under HISM instancing) is DISCONFIRMED: HISM is not the problem. Favoured now: the Alpine8K tiling is scene-specific — the card drawn large and close in the 128-300 m band (because the hold never persisted, so the card is live there), magnifying the low-frame octahedral atlas, plus Lumen HWRT + heavy exposure versus the demo's flat lighting. Lesson: reproduce a suspected asset defect in the VENDOR's own demo before blaming the asset; when it renders clean there under identical placement, the defect is in the integration/scene, not the asset.

**Tooling failures this session, logged before retry (all auditor-caught pre-run, three rounds to PASS):** (1) three `take_high_res_screenshot` calls in one payload share ONE global screenshot config and the single viewport camera / r.ForceLOD, so only the last renders as intended — split to one shot per payload invocation. (2) `SystemExit` is a `BaseException`, not `Exception`, so a rule-11 wrong-level `raise SystemExit` unwound past an `except Exception` handler and the `__LL__` result never printed — catch `SystemExit` explicitly. (3) a legend-completeness gate of `len(cents) >= 4` admitted a legend missing LOD 4, which would silently reclassify spruce card boxes as geometric — require a centroid for every card LOD index. (4) `get_level_viewport_fov` needs a `ViewportConfigKey` arg (LevelEditorSubsystem.h:128, no default); the first C1 run logged the error and the analyzer refused (FOV gate held), fixed to pass `get_active_viewport_config_key()`. (5) the box-median colour classifier collapsed to white under the scene's heavy overexposure (snow blown to 255); fixed by reading the palette from the engine's on-screen legend bar and classifying only SATURATED pixels — the LOD hue survives overexposure where the median does not.

## 2026-09-21 — Brief 5 REPAIR (R1-R4): the persist fix landed, and a persisted value's RUNTIME effect is proved by a cost delta, not by reading the value back

The follow-up write session to the C1 close-out. The T3 hold was re-applied so it reaches disk, then proven live at runtime.

**R1 — the persist fix, and the two-instrument persist gate that worked.** The T3 no-op root cause was confirmed at source: `UStaticMeshEditorSubsystem::SetLodScreenSizes` (StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.cpp:1020-1097) sets auto-compute false (:1060) and writes both `RenderData->ScreenSize[i].Default` and `SourceModel.ScreenSize`, but **never calls `Modify()`/`MarkPackageDirty()`**. So T3's `save_loaded_asset` with its default `only_if_is_dirty=True` saw a clean package, skipped the write, and returned `true`. The fix: `Object.modify(True)` to mark the package dirty, then `save_loaded_asset(only_if_is_dirty=False)` to force the write regardless. The persist GATE is two independent instruments in a DIFFERENT process from the writer: (1) the `.uasset` sha256 AND mtime both change on disk (host-side, before/after the editor closes); (2) a cold `get_lod_screen_sizes` readback in a fresh editor PID equals the targets within 1e-4, with last-LOD tris/slots/num_lods intact and `is_lod_screen_size_auto_computed()` False. Both passed: ScotsPineTall_01 c6ca202c→3b8a0b5a, spruce_half_01 0539bda4→c830a651; cold PID 32556 distinct from apply PID 21944.

**The reflected surface for the auto-compute flag is a METHOD, not an editor property, and our own gate caught the gap.** `bAutoComputeLODScreenSize` is `UE_DEPRECATED(5.7)` (StaticMesh.h:719-722), so `get_editor_property('auto_compute_lod_screen_size')` raises and T3's `get_/set_auto_compute_lod_screen_size()` method form does not exist. The live reflected surface is a getter METHOD `is_lod_screen_size_auto_computed()` (found by enumerating `dir(mesh)` for auto/compute/screen). The first R1 run REFUSED to save because our MAJOR-3 gate (never persist unless auto-compute is confirmed False) read `null` from the two wrong candidate names — a gate catching our own instrument gap before it could ship an unverified write. There is no Python setter, but `SetLodScreenSizes` forces the flag false internally, and the cold readback confirmed it; auto-compute was already False on the pristine vendor meshes (0.168/0.17 were baked as MANUAL values), so persistence was recompute-safe.

**R2/isolated — the visual LOD-coloration instrument is defeated by this scene; a persisted value's runtime effect needed a different instrument.** RenderData readback flipped `matches_t3_hold` False→True (the mesh asset carries the held card ScreenSize on disk and after a load), but that proves persist+load, NOT that the runtime LOD selector uses it. The Mesh LOD Coloration classifier could not settle it: (1) overlapping 2D boxes with no occlusion — ConiferPine (4 LODs, no LOD4) was classified overwhelmingly index-4 yellow (a colour only SpruceSub LOD4 makes) with 0% of its own card, in BOTH the C1 no-op and the R2 hold, so the number does not move with the thing it measures (rule 13 shape); (2) the operator-ordered uncontaminated single-instance read was scene-defeated two ways — the most-isolated instances sit at 508-633 m alpine and render pure white offscreen (those cells are outside the bounded offscreen render region; a ring_station_v1 control rendered 1.12M saturated px, proving render works and the LOCATIONS do not), and the dense rendered band has ZERO zero-intruder or frontmost target boxes (depth overlap + white LOD0 Norway Spruce, 54599 instances/1 LOD, filling boxes). General rule: an offscreen editor renders only a bounded region near the streaming source; and a per-instance VISUAL LOD read is not obtainable in a dense forest with 512 m depth. When the visual instrument is contaminated, fall to an aggregate behavioural one.

**R3 — the decisive runtime control: cost. A live hold MUST cost something, and it did.** 6 `-game` runs post-persist. forest_floor GPU p90 12.645 ms vs the v3 PRE-hold baseline 11.048 = **+1.597 ms (99.8× the 0.016 ms forest noise floor)**; the geometry-pass control Basepass+ShadowDepths+Prepass = **+1.131 ms (70.7× noise)** — Basepass +0.574, ShadowDepths +0.556 — exactly what a card→geometry conversion in the 128-512 m band predicts (LumenReflections FELL 0.123 ms: the flat card was more reflective than the crown). This is the uncontaminated proof the hold took at runtime; it also retro-explains why the blunt arm-B force (all foliage LOD2) was +2.9 ms while the targeted hold is +1.6 ms (only card-band trees, and only some are in the pure band at forest_floor). **Lesson (a runtime sibling to the C1 persist lesson): reading a persisted value back proves it is on disk and loaded; proving it drives the RUNTIME requires a behaviour/cost delta against a pre-change baseline, because a proxy/DDC path could in principle ignore the new value. The instrument must be the effect, not the input.**

**R5-1 ruling: OVER budget.** forest_floor p90 12.645 > 12.5 ms by 0.145 ms. Per the brief, T4 (intermediate LOD rungs, `derived_ladder.json` target_tris) goes back on the list — LISTED, not run; the hold is NOT reverted (the tiling fix stands; the rungs are a cost optimisation on top).

**check_recipe_lods now can only pass on a cold readback.** It read `tree_lod_probe_t3.json`, a same-session in-memory probe that never persisted, so it passed GREEN over an on-disk asset that still carried the pre-hold sizes. Now it reads `tree_lod_probe_cold.json` and REFUSES (exit 2) unless stamped `cold_readback=True` AND `distinct_from_apply=True`; the two held species are verified against the cold asset, and recipe tree species with `lod_screen_sizes` absent from the cold probe (Conifer, SpruceSapling — not part of the hold) are reported not-verified-this-session rather than silently dropped.

**Audit lessons carried (auditor-caught pre-run, per file):** (R1) a cold-verify that reads a result FILE must move the stale file to `_trash/` (rule 2, not `os.remove`) AND gate on the producer's rc + a per-run nonce echoed in the file — an unrun cold pass plus last run's JSON would pass every distinctness check (rule 13 shape); `json.dump(encoding=)` is a py3 TypeError hiding on error paths; a census must GATE the kill, not just be printed. (R4) a diff built from per-side param maps flags a swallowed getter failure as a VENDOR-ONLY finding — the fix writes an `err:` sentinel per failed getter, records per-kind read counts, and marks a kind UNRELIABLE (names>0, read==0) before the hypothesis flag fires; `ue_exec --timeout` is a discovery window only, so a driver's blocking `subprocess.run` cannot race the payload's JSON write.

## 2026-09-21 — Item 8 (HLOD proxy GPU share): the MRQ StartConsoleCommands channel resolves the v3 INCONCLUSIVE, and the CsvProfiler measures the wrong frame in a -game MRQ render

The v3 HLOD-share verdict was INCONCLUSIVE because `wp.Runtime.HLOD` is an `FAutoConsoleCommand` (HLODRuntimeSubsystem.cpp:149-187) and the only in-fence delivery, startup `-ExecCmds`, fires once before the far cells stream — leaving every render counter byte-identical. Item 8 delivered the command through a `MoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting.StartConsoleCommands` (MoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting.h:72) on a `-game` command-line MRQ render, which fires when the shot begins, after the world has streamed.

**The channel works, and the positive control passed decisively.** `GPUSceneInstanceCount` dropped 1,406,348 → 1,344,921 = −61,427 instances (4.37%) in the HLOD-off arm, IDENTICAL at both stations; `SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances` dropped the same 61,427; `ActorCount/WorldPartitionHLOD` stayed 422 (the HLOD actors remain resident — the command calls `SetVisibility`, it does not unload, exactly as the source lambda says). This is the counter change the startup-ExecCmds path could never produce. Command-line contract verified at source: `MovieRenderPipelineCommandLine.cpp` parses `-LevelSequence=` (:148) and `-MoviePipelineConfig=` (:153); the default `UMoviePipelineInProcessExecutor` (:114) self-exits on completion (:68), and the old "-game forbidden" guard is commented out (:29-37). The scratch assets used a SPAWNABLE camera (LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem.add_spawnable_from_instance, :154) so the sequences carry their own camera and `/Game/Alpine8K` was never saved — the before/after census proved the world + all 14,153 non-scratch assets byte-identical, umap sha256 identical.

**⛔ THE INSTRUMENT TRAP: a `-game` MRQ render renders OFF the main game-loop frame, so the CsvProfiler's per-row `GPUTime` is the near-idle offscreen pump (~0.07 ms), NOT the 4K render.** The first analyser windowed on `GPUTime>0` (which is nonzero on idle frames too) and reported a nonsensical 0.08 ms share with INCOMPLETE-UNSTEADY. The render is captured ONLY on the ~64 rows where a render pass fired: those rows carry real `GPU/Basepass`, `GPU/ShadowDepths`, `GPU/NaniteVisBuffer`, etc. The fix: identify a render frame by `GPU/Basepass > 0.1 ms`, take the per-frame GPU cost as the SUM of the `GPU/*` pass columns on that row, and window on the last 30 render rows (the first ~20+ spike to 3.6 s on shader/Nanite/TSR init and are discarded). General rule, a sibling to R3's "the instrument must be the effect not the input": when a tool renders off the profiled loop, the profiler's frame-time column measures the loop, not the tool — verify the instrument is reading the frames the work is actually on (here, `GPU/Basepass>0`) before trusting its central number, or the window silently measures idle.

**The number.** GPU cost of the render frames, arm A (HLOD on) vs arm B (HLOD off), p90 over the steady window × the A/A noise floor: treeline 49.46 → 48.88 ms = 0.576 ms share (1.2%), ×2.9 floor → MEASURED; vista 49.28 → 48.82 = 0.457 ms (0.9%), ×0.7 its noisier 0.67 ms floor → MEASURED-NEGLIGIBLE. Per-pass drop (treeline): NaniteVisBuffer +0.225, ShadowDepths +0.164, Basepass +0.080 ms — the instanced-proxy rasterization + shadow cost. Two caveats stated (rule 10): the ~49 ms/frame is MRQ's full-quality 4K render, heavier than the ~7-12 ms game viewport, so the transferable figure is the SHARE FRACTION (~1%) not the absolute ms; and the pixel diff — hiding the proxies changes 0.20% of non-sky pixels, ~3× the A/A pixel floor, far below the derived 0.05727 beyond-512 ground fraction — shows the instanced tree proxies are a thin subset of the far field (most beyond-512 m ground is the MESH_APPROXIMATE merged landscape proxy + haze). The HLOD proxy far-forest is cheap by construction, ≈0.5 ms / ≈1% of frame, MEASURED at treeline.

A hardcoded "law" value with no path citation is the same unverified-derivation class as trusting an external record — rule 9 applied to our own artefact. Also caught: the forest_floor live-tree growth uses the PRE-hold card-era rate (0.1003 ms/1000) on a POST-hold baseline, so it is a LOWER bound — the T3 hold's +1.597 ms geometry cost also scales with density and is not in the rate.

**Manual HISM-component creation is unusable in 5.8 Python; use the foliage idiom.** The first P3 payload built a HierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent on a bare spawned Actor. The design-review, reading the reflected stub, found `register_component` has ZERO matches in the surface and `attach_to_component` needs three AttachmentRule args, and a bare `Actor` spawn has no root to attach to. The reliable idiom is the one `place_foliage.py` already uses to place the world's 157k+ instances: `InstancedFoliageActor.add_instances(world, FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh, transforms)`. General rule already on the board (step (a) is a SEARCH): a project that has placed 219k instances HAS a proven instancing idiom — find it before inventing one against the reflected surface.

**PCG-graph authoring from Python IS feasible — feasibility PROVEN.** `PCGGraph.add_node_of_type(SettingsClass)` / `add_edge(node, Name, node, Name)` / `generation_radii = PCGRuntimeGenerationRadii` (radius400… the hierarchical grid ladder) / `PCGStaticMeshSpawnerSettings.set_mesh_selector_type(PCGMeshSelectorWeighted)` with `PCGMeshSelectorWeightedEntry.descriptor.static_mesh` — a real SurfaceSampler→TransformPoints→StaticMeshSpawner graph was built and SAVED (`Content/Scratch/PCG/PCG_ClutterSpike.uasset`). One gap for next time: the Input/Output node pins are NOT labelled "In"/"Out" (PCGInputOutputSettings.cpp) and `AddEdge` is non-raising (PCGGraph.cpp), so edges to/from those nodes silently no-op unless the real pin labels are used.

**THE INFRASTRUCTURE LESSON — a live-editor measurement payload must finish in <120s foreground, or it is lost.** This harness auto-backgrounds a foreground command at 120s and REAPS background commands at turn boundaries. Both P3 measurement runs were killed mid-flight. Because the editor is launched DETACHED (not a tracked background command), it kept executing the payload after its python CLIENT was reaped — so the arm-result JSON printed to a dead remote-exec channel and was lost, and the editor's single Python thread then held remote-exec unresponsive for ~25 min (a 20,000-instance × 18-arm payload with per-class `collect_garbage` in an 18 GB editor). Force-killed; disk-safe (graph already saved, level never saved). The correcting design, staged for a supervised session: run against an ALREADY-LOADED editor a payload sized to finish <120s (base 1000 counts, no per-class GC) in the FOREGROUND, so the client is never backgrounded and captures the marker directly. The item8 driver survived analogous work because each `-game` MRQ render self-exited and its per-render client call stayed under the window; a driver that must hold a client open across a >120s editor operation cannot survive this harness. General rule: under a client-reaping harness, the process that must READ a live editor's result has to outlive the work — either the work is short, or the reader is the detached long-lived process itself, never a foreground/short-background client waiting on it.

## 2026-09-22 — Brief 5 D1a: the two-pass driver run as ONE command was reaped, orphaning an editor

Ran research/brief5/scripts/t4_build_run.py (build + cold, two full editor-load cycles) as a single
background command. The harness KILLED it at a turn boundary (status "killed", not "completed") ~mid
wait_ready — the same >120s host-command reap class already recorded in pcg_cost.json that defeated the
Queue-2 clutter measurement. Because the driver launches the editor DETACHED (Popen) and then died, the
editor (PID 4744, 16 GB, fully loaded) was ORPHANED with nothing to close it.

Root cause: a host driver that needs several minutes (editor launch+load happens twice) cannot survive
the turn-boundary reap, whether foreground or run_in_background. The r_apply.py precedent worked only
because that session's driver happened to complete inside a window; it is not reap-safe by construction.

Recovery (clean, fence held): bootstrap confirmed the orphan responsive + project match (rule 7); dirty
census returned dirty_count 0 (world untouched — the build payload never ran, no Content/Scratch/T4, no
t4_build_editor.json, no PackageRestoreData); killed PID 4744; zero editors after.

Fix for the retry (reap-safe): do NOT run the whole driver as one command. Launch the editor DETACHED so
it persists across turns, then drive it with SHORT (<120s) foreground ue_exec payload calls, one per turn:
(1) snapshot shipped sha; (2) launch detached + poll bootstrap across turns; (3) run brief5_t4_build.py
foreground (<120s); (4) census + kill; (5) relaunch (distinct PID) + run brief5_t4_cold.py foreground.
The editor launch (the slow part) is decoupled from the payloads (the fast part) so no single command
exceeds the reap window. General rule: on this harness, the long-lived process must be the DETACHED
editor, never the host orchestrator.
