Python thread produced no log). The first SpruceSub set_lod_from_static_mesh (or the mesh rebuild it
triggers) never logged a "Waiting for static meshes to be ready SpruceSub_gate" line the way ConiferPine
did. This is the same unresponsive-editor mode that defeated the Queue-2 PCG measurement. The ue_exec
CLIENT had already been reaped at 115 s (the reductions + rebuilds exceed a <120 s window), so the
payload's stdout went nowhere and its result JSON is written only at the very END, after BOTH species --
so a mid-run stall leaves NO on-disk progress record and nothing to diagnose from except the editor log.

Recovery: force-killed the stalled editor (rule 6 -- stop, do not brute-force); zero editors after; no
PackageRestoreData; all four shipped/_SRC meshes sha256-verified BYTE-IDENTICAL (fence held -- the
payload is scratch-only, hard-coded paths); ConiferPine_gate persisted on scratch (gitignored).

Root-cause NOT yet established for the SpruceSub stall (a source line / property is owed before any
retry). It is species-specific (ConiferPine identical code path succeeded), so it is something about
spruce_half_01 -- candidates to check next: the billboard card material under reuse_existing_material_slots,
the mesh's build settings, or an async static-mesh-compilation deadlock triggered by the specific LOD
layout. Two process fixes for the retry, independent of the root cause:
  1. ONE SPECIES PER ue_exec INVOCATION (bounded blast radius; a stall on species B does not cost species A).
  2. INCREMENTAL on-disk progress: the payload must write a per-step marker file, not only a final JSON,
     so a mid-run stall is diagnosable without the (reaped) stdout channel.
Also: the build payload's per-mesh work (reductions + rebuilds) exceeds the <120 s reap window, so it
must not be driven as a single client call spanning both species.

## 2026-09-22 — Brief 5 Daylight Density part 2 (D0b→D3): the revert had to be audited harder than the thing it protects

**Context.** Dry-run → regenerate the forest at the ruled density. Six new/changed
tools, four auditor passes, one live world-mutating regen. Root causes and the
general rules they imply, at two altitudes (RECIPES carries the exact-value
anti-spec).

**1. The audit roots-omission fired again (procedural BLOCK, first D2 audit).**
The audit request omitted REPO_ROOT/UE_PROJECT_ROOT and the auditor refused
before reading any code. This is a repeat (STATE noted it at session start). The
lesson exists; it did not fire because audit prompts are written freehand each
time. The durable fix is a habit, not a note: every audit request now opens with
the two roots quoted from docs/environment.md, and I treat a missing-roots BLOCK
as a process defect, not a one-off.

**2. Recipe/validator drift, same class as the 2026-09-19 `card` fix.** The live
`recipes/alpine_8k.json` carried `lod_screen_sizes` (added by Brief-5 R1) and,
later this session, `density_zone_map`/`density_ceiling`, none of which
`import_heightmap._validate_foliage` accepted — so the first `place_foliage` run
REFUSED. The offline suite validates the synthetic prove_gates corpus, never the
shipped recipe, so a foliage regen is the first thing to re-validate it. Rule:
when a recipe gains a key, the validator's allowed-key set gains it in the SAME
change, or the next regen is the discovery.

**3. The MAX_INSTANCES gate checks the PLANNED total, not the PLACED total.** At
m≈5.48 the plan was 851,046 pre-exclusion; town + water post-filters drop 38,788
to 812,258 placed. The 850k ceiling Ryan set to admit the placed count refused
the planned total by 1,046. The gate measures instances before the exclusions
that never reach the world — over-conservative; recorded, Ryan bumped to 860,000.

**4. THE REVERT LESSONS — a git-tracked world is not automatically git-revertable.**
The D3 driver's whole purpose is to restore the shipped world on any failure. The
auditor BLOCKED it twice on the revert, and every finding was real:
  - **`git checkout <tag> -- <dir>` restores tracked files but cannot DELETE files
    a save ADDS.** Placing 4.4× the foliage populates new World Partition cells,
    and the save writes NEW OFPA packages for them. Checkout leaves those in
    place → a hybrid world (pre-D3 tracked actors + D3's new cells) that loads
    wrong. Fix: enumerate untracked additions under the external-actor/object dirs
    with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` and MOVE them to `_trash/`
    (rule 2, never `git clean -fd`) BEFORE the checkout.
  - **A directory "proof" by index file-count cannot fail.** The first driver
    "proved" restoration by counting `git ls-files -s` lines — which reads the
    INDEX the checkout just rewrote, and a changed-but-same-count tree passes. The
    real proof reads CONTENT: `git diff --quiet <tag> -- <paths>` AND empty
    `git status --porcelain -- <paths>`. This is rule 13 in a new place — a check
    that structurally cannot return "different" is silence wearing agreement.
  - **The exception guard must span the LONGEST phase, and the code must match its
    own claim.** The fix comment said "phases 1-6"; the `try` covered 1-5, leaving
    the up-to-3×1800 s `-game` span — the most likely place for a Ctrl-C — able to
    exit with the world mutated, no revert, no verdict. Caught on the re-audit.
  - **WORLD_PATHS must equal the save's write set.** The first list missed
    `__ExternalObjects__/Alpine8K` and `Content/Foliage` (FoliageType packages the
    placement dirties), both in save_level's allow-list — a dirtied file there
    would have survived revert. Derive the revert set from the save's allow-list,
    not from memory.
General rule: **audit the recovery path harder than the operation.** The operation
is git-revertable; the revert is only as good as (a) what it deletes, (b) what it
covers, (c) how it proves success, (d) whether its guard reaches the whole run.

**5. The result: the 4.4× density upgrade fits the VRAM.** 812,258 trees →
editor peak 5,211 MiB, -game peak ≈4,990 at all three stations, vs the 13,312
DEVICE_HUNG ceiling. Item 8's 8,553 MiB was MRQ full-quality 4K (heavy render
targets), NOT comparable to an offscreen editor + -game; a VRAM figure only
transfers within its measurement class. open_max (the densest post-ceiling bin
outside the discs, 4,943 in-frustum) is the real post-upgrade cost hot-spot and is
now a budget station, measured in D4.

## 2026-09-22 — Brief 5 Daylight Density D4: the density cost model underpredicted by 2.4–3.1 ms; the trees were fine

**Context.** D3 placed 812,258 trees (4.4×) and it fit VRAM (editor 5,211 MiB,
-game ~4,990, ceiling 13,312). D4 measured the GPU frame cost at five stations,
3 runs each, against the ruled lines. Three stations busted the GPU budget and D3
was reverted (proven: cold forest_floor 12.620 ms, in the 12.645 ± 3×0.016 band —
counter moved 15.342 → 12.620). The revert restored the world to the fence tag
(git diff tag..HEAD empty, 6/6 LFS-oid match, working tree clean).

**High altitude — the model failed, not the trees.** The desk cost model
(density_project / zone_map projected_ms) predicted forest_floor 12.90 and plaza
9.882 ms for the ceilinged world. Measured GPU p90 (3-run median): forest_floor
**15.342 (+2.442, 152× min_detectable)**, plaza **12.939 (+3.057, 76×)**,
open_max 14.151, treeline 7.261 (−0.252, actually cheaper than predicted), vista
8.235. The per-tree rate the model was built on — v3's **0.100 ms / 1000
in-frustum trees, called an upper bound** — was ~9× low: D4 measured **0.854
(forest_floor) / 0.980 (plaza) ms / 1000 added trees**. The upper bound was not
an upper bound; it was measured pre-hold on cards, in the down-direction
(foliage-hide), and neither the card→geometry hold cost nor the shadow/raster
growth scaled into it. A rate measured in one direction and one LOD regime does
not transfer to 4.4× the trees in the other regime.

**Low altitude — which pass carried it, measured (d4_model_error.json), not
assumed.** The dense per-pass GPU split (GPU/<pass> median, last 1500 frames) at
forest_floor: **ShadowDepths 3.19**, **NaniteVisBuffer 2.20**, Basepass 1.48,
LumenReflections 1.30, Prepass 0.07. open_max: ShadowDepths 2.00, NaniteVisBuffer
1.82, Basepass 1.72. plaza: NaniteVisBuffer 1.85 (buildings), ShadowDepths 1.63,
Basepass 1.25, LumenReflections 1.02. So the two passes that grew are
**ShadowDepths and NaniteVisBuffer** — shadow-depth rendering of 2.56× more
shadow-casters, and Nanite raster of more geometry. This is a MEASURED
correction to the v3 inference that "T4 does not pay because the cost is Lumen +
shadow, not Nanite raster": NaniteVisBuffer is 2.20 ms at forest_floor, a large
raster component, so tri-reduction (T4) DOES pay, and so would shadow-caster /
foliage-shadow-distance reduction. The prior "the paying lever is cull/shadow +
T4" was a hypothesis; the per-pass numbers now say shadow-depth AND Nanite-raster
both carry it, which is a stronger and different statement than "not Nanite."

**Rule.** A cost model built from a single-direction, single-LOD-regime
per-tree rate must be re-measured at the target density and regime before it
gates a build; and the pass that carries a growth is a measurement
(GPU/<pass> split), never an inference from an unrelated station's split.

## 2026-09-23 — Brief 5 T4: neither tri-reduction nor runtime cvars recover the forest_floor headroom; the cost is structural

**Context.** D4 reverted the density upgrade (forest_floor GPU p90 15.34 > 13.0).
The T4 gate opened to buy the headroom back. Step 1 (recalibrate) and step 2
(cvar levers) both say the same thing: there is no cheap lever.

**Step 1 — recalibration killed the T4-rung premise.** The old cost model's
0.100 ms/1000-trees rate was ~9x low; the measured slope at forest_floor is 1.576
ms/unit-m (was 0.185), so the affordable density cap collapses 2.38 -> 1.162. And
the two biggest measured passes are NOT T4-addressable: NaniteVisBuffer 2.20 ms is
Conifer (Nanite, single-representation -- rungs do not touch it) and
LumenReflections 1.30 ms is screen-space. T4 rungs (non-Nanite tri-reduction)
face a >= 3.50 ms untouchable floor at forest_floor, and the reducible non-Nanite
share of ShadowDepths/Basepass is unmeasured. Ryan demoted T4 rungs to BACKLOG
with a numeric entry condition (>= 1.5 ms non-Nanite in ShadowDepths+Basepass).
The lesson: a cost model built from a single-direction, single-LOD-regime
per-tree rate must be re-measured at the target density before it gates a build,
and "which pass a lever can touch" is a per-species/per-representation question
that a station-total per-pass split cannot answer.

**Step 2 — the runtime cvar levers do not pay either (measured).** A/A first, and
the A/A itself was the first finding: the v3 noise floor 0.016 did NOT hold on
this build -- 3-run min_detectable = 0.0737 ms, ~4.6x higher. Every arm verdict
used 0.0737, not 0.016 (rule 13: the instrument's actual noise, re-measured, not
inherited). Then, each arm vs the same as-is baseline at forest_floor:
  - A r.Shadow.RadiusThreshold (0.03/0.06/0.10): DROP. ShadowDepths never moved
    -- the forest_floor trees have a large screen radius, so a small-radius
    caster cull culls none of them.
  - B r.Shadow.DistanceScale (0.25): KEEP but only 0.128 ms (1.7x floor), and
    only at quarter shadow distance -- a large visible-shadow trade for a tiny gain.
  - D r.Lumen.Reflections.MaxRoughnessToTrace: DROP. LumenReflections moved
    ~0.25 ms but the frame p90 gained only 0.05 ms -- a per-pass saving that does
    not surface at the frame's p90 is not a frame saving.
  - E r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge: INCONCLUSIVE. NaniteVisBuffer did not drop;
    the Nanite raster here is not triangle-edge-bound at these distances.
  - F foliage.CullDistanceScale: SKIPPED, INERT by recorded asset state -- all
    live FoliageTypes have enable_cull_distance_scaling=false
    (density_baseline.json:1115), so the cvar is opt-in-gated off; enabling it is
    a FoliageType asset write (out of the cvar-only fence). Same inert-by-opt-out
    class as the density-scaling cvar in D2. Foliage.MinimumScreenSize is not a
    5.8 cvar.
The whole kept stack is 0.128 ms against a ~2.7 ms deficit.

**Rule (two altitudes met).** HIGH: the forest_floor GPU cost is STRUCTURAL --
ShadowDepths, NaniteVisBuffer and LumenReflections are each ~1-2 ms and none is
cheaply reducible by a runtime cvar without a visual trade or an asset opt-in;
"there must be a cheap knob" was the assumption, and two measured passes (T4
rungs, then cvars) refuted it. LOW: the paying arm was B (shadow distance) at
0.128 ms; every other arm dropped or was inert, and a per-pass saving (arm D's
Lumen -0.25 ms) that does not move the frame p90 is not headroom. Also: re-measure
the A/A noise floor per build -- 0.016 became 0.0737 here, and a stale floor would
have mis-ruled every marginal arm.

2026-09-23 | BRIEF 7 PHASE 1 ADDENDUM (height-weighted blend) — implemented the
LB_HeightBlend EFFECT inside the weightmap composite (no LandscapeLayerBlend node
exists), and deviated from the desk lever's "centred height" for a reason the math
forces. Same branch look-p1-material (PR #1 updates). Author-only, no editor run.

WHAT. schema v1.28 `material.height_blend {k, eps}` (default k=4, eps=0.02,
optional; absent or k==0 = off). In the composite, each STORED layer's weightmap
mask (Snow/Rock/Scree/ForestFloor) is scaled w_i' = w_i·(h_i+eps)^k and the four
are renormalised to PRESERVE their sum, so the meadow/Grass remainder
(1-sum(stored)) is byte-for-byte the behaviour it had — only the split AMONG the
stored layers moves toward the higher surface. Reducer height_blend_spec; CPU
mirror _cpu_height_blend + _assert_height_blend_invariants (5 properties);
_validate_height_blend; graph via Add→Power(const_exponent=k)→Multiply→sum-chains
→Divide→Multiply; the per-layer height sample is created ONCE at mask build and
reused as _hA (blend + HeightLerp + displacement — one fetch, three consumers).

DEVIATION, RECORDED (rule 10). The lever wrote "scaled by their centred height^k".
I used the RAW height sample (0..1), NOT the displacement-centred value, because an
EVEN power (k=4) on a height re-centred on its own mean (which straddles 0) folds a
texel far BELOW its mean onto one far ABOVE — a low surface would get the same
boost as a high one, which is not a height blend. Centring is a displacement-only
transform (_centred_height, for the (v-Center)*Magnitude path) and cannot feed
(h+eps)^k. Flagged in the recipe `_height_source` and the PR for the external
review to rule.

THE RENORMALISATION GUARD IS AMPLITUDE-INDEPENDENT, AND 1e-12 WAS TOO LARGE.
norm = S/(S'+eps_norm) with S'=sum(base·(h+eps)^k). The worst-case partition drift
is eps_norm/eps^k (the smallest S'/S is eps^k, at h==0), INDEPENDENT of the actual
weights — so it is a fixed number, not a per-texel wobble. At eps_norm=1e-12,
eps=0.02, k=4 that is 1e-12/1.6e-7 = 6.25e-6, which the real-weightmap prove_gates
scan measured EXACTLY and which failed the 1e-6 partition gate. Dropped to 1e-15
(bound 6.25e-9, below the 1/255 weightmap quantum and any float32-visible level,
still non-zero in float32 at S'==0 so the divide-by-zero guard still fires). RULE:
a divide-by-zero floor added to a denominator is not free — bound its worst-case
effect analytically (here eps_norm/eps^k) and gate against that bound, and prove it
on the REAL artefact, not only synthetic cases: the all-heights-zero config that
exposed the 6.25e-6 drift never appears in the import invariants' hand-picked cases
but does appear in the weightmap scan's stress configs.

2026-09-24 | BRIEF 7 PHASE 1 — the merged material builder FAILS on its first editor run
(NameError: __file__), and the failure was invisible offline. This is a two-altitude BLOCKER.

The Phase 1 material work was authored, reviewed, merged and "offline-verified" but NEVER run
against the editor (the rebuild was declared the gated world run). On the first real run,
make_landscape_material.py died with `NameError: name '__file__' is not defined` at line 131 of
the generated payload -- BEFORE delete_all_material_expressions, so M_Alpine8K is intact (read
back 197 exprs, old graph). No damage; nothing saved.

ROOT CAUSE at the source. The payload body does
`_sys.path.insert(0, _os.path.dirname(_os.path.abspath(__file__)))` then `import ll_must`
(make_landscape_material.py:1772-1773), with a comment asserting "MODE_EXEC_FILE gives us
__file__". But `_run` (line 3916) sends the payload as INLINE TEXT:
`remote.run_command(source, exec_mode=MODE_EXEC_FILE)`. MODE_EXEC_FILE means the command IS A
FILENAME (the engine execs a file, which is what defines __file__). Passing source text runs it
as a statement with no __file__. ue_exec.run() does the same job correctly (ue_exec.py:84-100):
it STAGES the payload to Saved/LLPython/<name>.py, copies ll_must.py beside it, and passes the
PATH. The ll_must refactor updated the payload to import ll_must (needing __file__) but did NOT
update _run to stage -- an incomplete refactor whose only failure site is a live editor, so no
offline gate could see it.

FIX: _run must stage `source` (+ ll_must.py) to a file and pass the path, mirroring
ue_exec.run(). ~6 lines. Because it edits make_landscape_material.py it is gated by the Brief 7
branch rule (author on a branch, PR, wait for "merged, go") -- reported to Ryan, run halted.

RULE reinforced: "offline-verified" is not "verified". A builder whose only execution path is a
live editor has an entire class of bugs (exec mode, staging, __file__, ll_must import) that no
offline suite exercises. The FIRST editor run of any merged-but-never-executed builder is itself
a gate, and must be treated as one -- expect it to fail and protect the world (it did: the clear
is after the preflight, so the crash left the asset intact).

RULE: aerial-perspective COLOUR is the Rayleigh:Mie ratio along the view ray, not a distance knob. A
distance/density lever (height-fog density, AP view-distance scale, extinction, albedo) can only scale how
MUCH of the atmosphere's existing in-scatter colour lands on the far band; if that colour is warm-grey,
more of it is more grey. A hue target needs a lever that changes the scattering spectrum
(mie_scattering_scale down / rayleigh_scattering_scale up) or a different grade -- three ladders
(09-25 fog, 09-25 extinction, 09-26 AP+albedo) spent on distance levers say so. Desk to rule.

2026-09-27 | GITHUB LFS QUOTA -- the repo was recreated and GitHub now holds a SNAPSHOT without the world
(R-GITHUB-LITE, ruled by Ryan: option 2, no external drive).

What happened: every push after the P2 world run was refused with "This repository exceeded its LFS budget".
Two "bumps" changed nothing because the account is on GitHub Free: 10 GiB of LFS storage, every object
version ever pushed counts, and only deleting the repository frees it. Measured: history carried 37.2 GB of
LFS over 43,209 objects -- 22.2 GB of it 42,066 versions of World Partition external-actor packages, ~1,000
per world save. A history rewrite (git filter-repo) needs a second copy of a 64 GB .git; the disk had 13 GB
free. So: scripts/github_lite_snapshot.py builds `github-main` = HEAD's tree minus __ExternalActors__ /
__ExternalObjects__ / _verify/bench (hero binaries KEPT: not cheaply regenerable, and this machine is now the
only copy of everything not on GitHub), one commit per snapshot with a leak gate; Ryan deleted and recreated
the repo; the first push carried 6.05 GB over 419 objects. Local `main` is unchanged: full history, fence
tags, the D3 driver's revert-to-tag, R-EDITOR-CLOSE -- all read local git only.

RULE: the world packages are pipeline OUTPUT (rule 3: the recipe rebuilds the world); GitHub keeps the
recipe, plans, scripts and docs. Never push local `main` or a tag to GitHub -- one world save would refill
the quota. After a commit worth sharing: `python scripts/github_lite_snapshot.py --push`.

RULE (cost): a world save is ~1,000 LFS objects / ~260 MB; any remote that meters LFS will meter that. Budget
the remote by SAVES, not by repo size.

OPERATIONAL: standing rule 2's no-force-delete hook blocks the agent even under an explicit ruling; the
authorised cache deletion (32 GB of DDC / Intermediate / ShaderDebugInfo / Autosaves / Profiling /
Screenshots / old logs / old _trash) ships as scripts/disk_cleanup_20260927.ps1 for the operator's own
prompt (`! powershell -File ...`). The hook is doing its job; the human runs the delete.
